articles.title: Lost Woods - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Guide - IGN

articles.body:
This The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Lost Woods Walkthrough section covers both the Nintendo 64 and Nintendo 3DS versions of Zelda OOT, including the Nintendo Switch Online/eShop version from 2026. We will cover each and every secret, puzzle, boss fight, and item in this guide to the Lost Woods.

The Lost Woods has its name for a reason. There are multiple pathways and going the wrong way transports you straight back to the entrance.

Basically, follow the sound of the music. If it starts to dim, then you are going the wrong way.

Go right, left, right, left, straight, left, right . The correct order takes you to Sacred Forest Meadow, where you must navigate a maze-like area from a top-down view. Most corners are occupied by Mad Scrubs, so keep the shield at the ready.

Head up the stairs at the very end and meet up Saria. She teaches you Saria's Song .

As you walk down the stairs to exit the area Saria was in, you'll see a ladder ahead of you. The ladder allows you to forgo navigating the maze again, but there's a Fairy Fountain nearby! Fall down the first hole after climbing the ladder. You can bottle up fairies which revive you automatically when you fall.

From the Lost Woods entrance, take a right. Straight ahead you will see a wooden target hanging from a tree branch. If you make three bullseyes with your slingshot, a Deku Scrub will reward you with the Biggest Deku Seed Bullet Bag, which increases the number of seeds you can carry by an additional 10, bringing the total to 50.

From the Lost Woods entrance, take a left and then another left. Jump off the ledge and go to the far side of the room, where you will encounter a Business Scrub. After you defeat him, he will offer to increase the number of Deku Sticks you can carry from 10 to 20 for a measly 40 rupees.

There are two Heart Pieces to nab at this point. Return to the Lost Woods entrance by going the wrong way. From the entrance, head left and stand on the smaller stump, in front of the Skull Kid. Play Saria's Song to win his friendship and acquire a heart piece.

Return yet again to the entrance, this time heading right. Stand on the stump in the grotto of the next area and pull out your ocarina to initiate a memory game. Beat the Skull Kids' challenge by replaying their songs. This can be tricky, but you'll get a heart piece after completing the third song.

In Gerudo Valley to the west you can easily obtain two heart pieces with the use of a cucco, Hyrule's easily-excitable chickens. Go over there, pick up the bird and use it to fly to the ledge on the other side of the bridge to the west. Roll into the crate for the first Heart Piece .

If you then fly east, you'll get to a platform beside a waterfall. Go behind the falls and up the ladder, where the other Heart Piece lies.

articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: The Citadel 2 Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

War Assets: Alliance: Ashley Williams / Kaidan Alenko (25 TMS) Asari: Asari Science Team (90 TMS) Asari Second Fleet (90 TMS) Asari Sixth Fleet (90 TMS) Destiny Ascension (70 TMS) Salarian: (these are mutually exclusive based on whether you saved or sacrifice the Council in Mass Effect 1) Salarian Third Fleet (125 TMS) STG Task Force (70 TMS)

Alliance: Ashley Williams / Kaidan Alenko (25 TMS)

Ashley Williams / Kaidan Alenko (25 TMS)

Asari: Asari Science Team (90 TMS) Asari Second Fleet (90 TMS) Asari Sixth Fleet (90 TMS) Destiny Ascension (70 TMS)

Salarian: (these are mutually exclusive based on whether you saved or sacrifice the Council in Mass Effect 1) Salarian Third Fleet (125 TMS) STG Task Force (70 TMS)

As noted in " Priority: Tuchanka ", you'll have been locked out of many Side Quests and interactions on the Citadel by completing that Mission. If these are at all important to you, load a save before that Mission so you can tend to them.

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Tuchanka "

Location: Serpent Nebula - Widow - Citadel

This Mission takes places on the Citadel, so head over there by going to the Serpent Nebula, which automatically takes you to the Widow system.

If you're interested in Search and Rescue, here's everything new that you can find at this point:

Squad Tactics: Liara 's Warp Ammo will be useful for stripping Barriers, and her Singularity will help disable Guardians. Garrus ' Overload Power is great for stripping Shields.

Liara 's Warp Ammo will be useful for stripping Barriers, and her Singularity will help disable Guardians.

Garrus ' Overload Power is great for stripping Shields.

Unique Dialogue: For the most unique dialogue, bring Javik and EDI . If you don't have Javik, go for Garrus and James , a different but equally unique combo. ...and if you don't have Garrus, replace him with EDI . If you have a particularly poor relationship with your Virmire Survivor, bringing along either Garrus or Liara will open up some unique dialogue later.

For the most unique dialogue, bring Javik and EDI .

If you don't have Javik, go for Garrus and James , a different but equally unique combo. ...and if you don't have Garrus, replace him with EDI .

...and if you don't have Garrus, replace him with EDI .

If you have a particularly poor relationship with your Virmire Survivor, bringing along either Garrus or Liara will open up some unique dialogue later.

Shepard's Loadout: Several sections in this level are perfect for Sniper Rifles , and you’ll definitely want to have one on hand to hijack an Atlas. Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will be rather appreciated to deal with this level's Guardians. The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs. If you have the Citadel DLC and / or completed the Omega DLC , a Thermal Scope for your assault / sniper rifle helps see through both their smoke bombs and through walls! Soldiers and Infiltrators will want to have Disruptor Ammo unlocked to strip Shields. Many cutscenes in this Mission will force Shepard and their Squad Mates to use the M-3 Predator Heavy Pistol in cutscenes. You may want to equip it simply so that the cutscenes look more natural, especially with your preferred mod loadout for it.

Several sections in this level are perfect for Sniper Rifles , and you’ll definitely want to have one on hand to hijack an Atlas.

Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will be rather appreciated to deal with this level's Guardians.

The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs.

If you have the Citadel DLC and / or completed the Omega DLC , a Thermal Scope for your assault / sniper rifle helps see through both their smoke bombs and through walls!

Soldiers and Infiltrators will want to have Disruptor Ammo unlocked to strip Shields.

Many cutscenes in this Mission will force Shepard and their Squad Mates to use the M-3 Predator Heavy Pistol in cutscenes. You may want to equip it simply so that the cutscenes look more natural, especially with your preferred mod loadout for it.

The Mission begins with Joker attempting to make his usual entry to the Alliance Dock... only nobody is answering. He checks the emergency comms and connects to Thane (or an automated distress message from Commander Bailey), learning that Cerberus has invaded the station trying to wrest control of it. Shepard tells Joker to fly near C-Sec HQ so they can land there in the shuttle and start a counter-attack.

The shuttle bay is loaded with Shields of all types. Note that there are Shield Pylons at the far end of the room where the enemies first come from that will give everyone Shield boosts. You can destroy these if you are really having trouble with them. The Combat Engineers should also be removed quickly as they will make repairs to other enemies and replace any destroyed Turrets.

Medical Station - 25 XP. Before talking to Commander Bailey, check around the left-hand corner to find an easily-missed Medical Station on the wall.

Talk to Commander Bailey sitting against the wall at the far end of the room. It seems that the Salarian Councillor (who contacted you after Tuchanka) was meeting with the C-Sec Executor to prepare for a big arrest, only for both to go missing. Here you can say...

"I can launch a rescue" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I don't believe this" for +2 Renegade Points .

Continue through two green panel doors and you’ll come open two unsuspecting Assault Troopers. Snipe them and then turn left and go up the short stairs. Two Guardians with combat shields will come at you while an Engineer keeps a Generator active at the top of the stairs. You can destroy the Generator from the bottom of the stairs on the right-hand side. Make sure to go to the back half of this room so that four Assault Troopers spawn in from the windows.

Med Kit - 25 XP. This is just at the top of the stairs on a counter to your right.

Assault Rifle Piercing Mod - See above, next to a Terminal you can Examine, and near a C-Sec Body you can also Examine.

Continue through a few doors and you’ll come upon a locker room with sprinklers gushing water, drenching the area. Get the drop on the two Guardians here and kill them before they turn around with a combination of Squad Powers and sniping, then get to work on the Engineer, who has also dropped down a turret.

Recon Hood - In the left-hand "lane" of the room, on a table underneath a screen cautioning about pressurized Volus suits.

M-76 Revenant - Through a door near the Recon Hood in a bathroom, laying next to a sink.

Locker - 6,250 Credits. Part of a trio of Lockers to the left of the sinks where the Revenant was, near another C-Sec Corpse you can Examine.

Medical Station - 75 XP. To the left of the exit doorway of the drenched room.

Head through the exit doorway into a hallway with two broken windows. Through them you can see a Cerberus Engineer tampering with the elevator controls. Shoot him down, then shoot the lock of the breaker box so you can then Activate the Elevator Door. There's also a Weapon Bench here in case you don't like the Revenant you just picked up, or want to apply new mods.

Sniper Rifle Extended Barrel - This useful Weapon Modification is on a shelf to the left of the Elevator Door's breaker box that was guarded by a Combat Engineer.

Head through the elevator and then exit it to another drenched room filled with the bodies of fallen C-Sec officers. The room here is made up of three lanes: the central corridor, a left-hand corridor, and two right-hand corridors. The end of the middle corridor is blocked by a malfunctioning door, but you can go around it using the back-right corridor. First though, sweep this area for loot.

Pistol Piercing Mod - In the first right-hand corridor will be this mod in the middle section of tables along the right-hand wall. You can also find a Terminal here with some logs to read.

M-25 Hornet - Exit out the other side of the first right-hand corridor to find this Submachine Gun on the body of a C-Sec officer in the central walkway.

Door Control - Not a collectible, but required to access one. From the Hornet's position, face the malfunctioning door nearby, then go right through the doorway into the second right-hand corridor that goes around the malfunctioning door: directly ahead will be a Door Control. Using it won't fix the malfunctioning door, but instead open a door elsewhere in the area.

Pistol High Caliber Barrel - Return to where you got the Hornet, face the malfunctioning door, then turn left to spot a doorway into a side room. Head into the side-room and check the shelves in here to find this Mod.

M-358 Talon - Return to the start of this area and face forward towards the malfunctioning door: turn left to spot a door you can now open, if you used the Door Control described above. In this side room, check under the shelving unit to find this Heavy Pistol. There's also a Datapad on the desk nearby with some lore.

Account Details - 6,250 Credits. All the way back in the corridor where the Door Control was, on a laptop to the left of the shelving unit on the right-hand wall.

Head through the back-right corridor that goes around the malfunctioning door, then get the jump on the two Assault Troopers who just executed a C-Sec officer. When you enter the next area, ignore collectibles for now and just go to the far end of the room, where Cerberus enemies will drop in. There isn’t much cover, so keep a good distance between you and the enemies.

Once they're all dead, return to the entry door and face the way forwards to start looking for loot.

Medical Station - 75 XP. From the starting point, head right through the door into a kitchen area, with the Medical Station directly in front of you.

Credits - 6,250 Credits. From the Medical Station, turn right and go to the far end of the kitchen to find a Datapad with the Credits you want.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Return to the main area and continue forward to the far end where there's a doorway with "Executor" above it. To the right of this doorway is the Medical Station.

Sniper Rifle Piercing Mod - From the Medical Station, head right along the desks to find this mod in the corner, under a large holographic C-Sec sign.

Now go through the doorway and up the stairs to initiate a series of cutscenes where Shepard finds the Salarian Councillor under a cloaking device. They'll then be attacked by an assassin, Kai Leng, however their attempt will be thwarted by either Thane Krios, or Major Kirrahe if Thane died in Mass Effect 2. If Kirrahe is also dead however, Leng will successfully kill the Salarian Councillor.

Either way he escapes and Shepard chases after him, but crashes on the side of the Presidium and has to catch up to the Council on foot.

As you press onwards you'll face two new enemy types, the Nemesis and the Phantom . The Phantoms should always be a priority as they will rush you, cloaking to avoid detection and then dealing SERIOUS melee damage with their swords. Further, they're protected via powerful biotic Barriers rather than Armor of Shields, meaning fewer techniques can be used to strip them. It's best to take these out as early as possible so they don't cause trouble.

The Nemesis enemies are snipers that stay far away, although you may have encountered two of them already if you did the From Ashes DLC . They can target you in under a second with a shield-reducing blast, so ALWAYS stay in cover when you spot one. The best way to eliminate them is to turn your own Sniper Rifle sights in their direction: they're easy to spot when aiming thanks to the large red aiming glare coming from their position.

Leap across the ledge to the next section of the Citadel, where there are a few parked cars making it close quarters for sniping. Pull out your Shotgun here and keep on the move. You should be able to clear out the Nemeses and Phantoms in this manner before moving on. You will hit a dead end at a locked door: follow the waypoint by hopping over the wall, then clamber through a narrow passageway and leap a gap to continue on the perimeter of the structure.

Credits - 6,250 Credits. After leaping across the smoky gap, turn left, climb up the ledge, then turn left again to complete a U-Turn. You'll see some boxes in front of you, one of which is a Datapad with these Credits to Access. This is the last item in the level!

In the next area you'll be fighting an Atlas mech. To hijack it, equip your Sniper Rifle and shoot through the glass and then the pilot without destroying the mech itself. Once you reduce its Shields fully, and its Armor about half way, the glass will shatter. At this point you can shoot out its occupant. Use the mech to kill the few remaining enemies.

Once the Atlas is down, you'll get a new Mission Marker directing you to an elevator up some stairs. Head through and you'll be on your way to the Council. In the elevator shaft, the elevator you are pursuing will appear beside you. Shoot the Power Conduits on its underside and it will plummet below. Equip a Shotgun and take cover: Phantoms will soon arrive, and they are especially dangerous in these close quarters. If you're quick however, you can shoot the Power Conduits to send their elevator plummeting down, taking them out very quickly and efficiently!

You will have to repeat this process once more. Shoot out the devices below another elevator to prevent Cerberus enemies will land on your platform (this also nets you some bonus XP in the process!). After this, leap across the gap to the adjacent elevator when given the chance so you can catch up to the Council.

You'll now have caught up with the Council, but due to Shepard's arrival and them blocking the exit, Udina accuses you of working with Cerberus, something which your Virmire Survivor may be inclined to agree with. This is the culmination of everything you did to gain the trust of your Virmire Survivor: you need to convince them to stand down so that you don't have to shoot them down to get to Udina.

The calculations behind this are explained in detail on the How to Save the Virmire Survivor page, but here we'll break the confrontation down into five Stages.

Right from the get-go you'll be faced with a Dialogue Wheel with an upper-left option and a lower-left option, the wording of which will vary depending on how much your Virmire Survivor trusts you. Here's what can happen here:

Pick the upper-right option and then pull the Paragon Interrupt to earn more trust with the Virmire Survivor, and get +5 Paragon Points .

Pick the lower-right option and then pull the Renegade Interrupt to get +5 Renegade Points .

If you miss either Interrupt, you miss out on Morality Points and your Virmire Survivor will reflect on how you talked to them on Mars.

If you used one of the Interrupts, you'll also get +15 Reputation . No matter which course of action you took, you'll move on automatically to Stage 2 .

The second stage is the Trust Check, which is where your past actions with the Council and your Virmire Survivor are tallied up into points. Your total can be anywhere between +8 and -3 Points. Here's how you can earn or remove points throughout the course of the trilogy:

Locking in a Romance with them in Mass Effect 1 ( +2 Points ).

Mass Effect 1 Council choice : Saved the Council ( +1 Point ). Sacrificed the Council ( -1 Point ).

Both Thane and Kirrahe are dead, meaning the Salarian Councillor died ( -2 Points ).

ROMANCE ONLY: Cheating on them in Mass Effect 2 with anyone except Kelly ( -1 Point ).

Using Paragon responses in the two conversations during Priority: Mars ( +1 Point ).

Visiting them after they first wake up in Huerta Memorial Hospital ( +2 Points ). If you cheated on them, not apologizing for it ( -1 Point ).

If you cheated on them, not apologizing for it ( -1 Point ).

Pulling the Paragon Interrupt during Stage 1 of this confrontation ( +1 Point ).

Your total number of points will result in one of three outcomes:

If you have 4 Points or more, your Virmire Survivor will automatically trust you, skipping to Stage 5 .

If you have between 0 and 3 Points, you'll move on to Stage 3 .

If you have -1 Points or less, your Virmire Survivor automatically REFUSES to trust you, moving you to Stage 4 .

If your Virmire Survivor is still unsure about you, then you'll have to pass a Reputation Check as Udina moves to override the lock. You'll have a Dialogue Wheel with three options: a Charm and an Intimidate option on the left, and a normal white option on the right. The Charm / Intimidate options unlock after filling about 3/5ths of the Reputation bar.

If you pick the Charm option, you'll convince your Virmire Survivor for +15 Paragon Points , and move to Stage 5 .

If you pick the Intimidate option, you'll will convince your Virmire Survivor for +15 Renegade Points , and move to Stage 5 .

If you pick the right-hand option (whether you were forced to or chose to), you've failed to convince your Virmire Survivor, moving you on to Stage 4 .

If you're in this stage, you were unable to convince your Virmire Survivor, and they WILL die no matter what you do. Here you'll be given a Renegade Interrupt:

Pulling the Renegade Interrupt will have Shepard shoot your Virmire Survivor dead.

Ignoring the Renegade Interrupt will have one of your Squad Mates will shoot them instead.

Either outcome will move you on to Stage 5 .

This is the final stage of the confrontation. At this point, the Asari Councillor tries to stop Udina from overriding the door lock, but he shoves her to the floor and pulls a gun on her, after which you'll be given a Renegade Interrupt.

Pull the Renegade Interrupt and you'll shoot Udina dead personally for +5 Renegade Points .

Ignore the Renegade Interrupt, and either your Virmire Survivor or (if your Survivor is dead) one of your Squad Mates will shoot Udina dead instead.

After this you'll have some parting words with your Virmire Survivor if you were forced to shoot them, whose tone will vary depending on how much they trusted you. In any case, Commander Bailey will force himself through the door and announce that Cerberus has begun retreating now that C-Sec is now capable of retaking the station.

The upper-right option gives +2 Paragon Points .

"About time" will give +2 Renegade Points .

With all that over, you'll meet up with Commander Bailey in his office on the Presidium Embassy. If Thane was present to fight Kai Leng, you can answer either...

"Thanks, Commander" for +2 Paragon Points .

"There will be time" for +5 Renegade Points .

You may want to talk to Commander Bailey again to learn about how the Citadel is doing after the Cerberus Coup.

When you go through the doors to the Normandy, you'll be met by your Virmire Survivor if they survived the Udina confrontation. As the scene concludes they mention that Admiral Hackett offered them to join his team, but they would rather be on the Normandy.

If you accept their offer, they'll be the newest occupant aboard the Normandy and become available as a Squad Mate.

If you decline, they'll become a War Asset worth 25 TMS.

Either way, simply having this conversation will give you +2 Reputation .

You'll now reconvene with Admiral Hackett and Admiral Anderson to talk about the Coup. As it turns out, Anderson had a previous run-in with Kai Leng.

Here, you can respond with either... "Thanks for the Intel" for +2 Paragon Points ". "He'll die like all the rest" for +2 Renegade Points .

"Thanks for the Intel" for +2 Paragon Points ".

"He'll die like all the rest" for +2 Renegade Points .

As the conversation ends, you can pick... "I won't fail you" for +2 Paragon Points . "Nobody can stand in our way" for +2 Renegade Points .

"I won't fail you" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Nobody can stand in our way" for +2 Renegade Points .

As Shepard leaves, Liara will approach them with a Side Mission from Asari high command: " Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastary ". If you've been holding out for the full Store Discount, this Side Mission will give you that! (the other half being obtainable via the From Ashes DLC)

You'll now want to do another full sweep of the Normandy for post-coup conversations and email.

CIC - Talk to Traynor to pick up " Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists ", Joker, and EDI for +2 Reputation and the Defense Matrix Bonus Power. When you return to the CIC, you can talk with Anderson again via the Vid Comm room ( +2 Reputation ).

Private Terminal - You'll now have new emails, including "Durlesh Mole", which unlocks " Citadel: Volus Ambassador ". You should also read "Kai Leng's Dossier" to help prevent tragic events later in the game. You'll also have an email titled "Priority: Citadel Shore Leave" if you have the Citadel DLC . We recommend saving this until you've concluded Miranda's storyline, or unlocking " Priority: Thessia " at the earliest.

You'll also have an email titled "Priority: Citadel Shore Leave" if you have the Citadel DLC . We recommend saving this until you've concluded Miranda's storyline, or unlocking " Priority: Thessia " at the earliest.

Crew Deck - Talk to Garrus ( +2 Reputation ), Liara, and your doctor to unlock " Citadel: Medical Supplies ". If Kaidan is on-board, talk to him in the Starboard Observation lounge now to unlock the Reave Bonus Power. If Liara or Garrus shot your Virmire Survivor, they will talk about it.

Engineering - Talk to Javik and Allers, as well as Gabby and Ken if they mentioned the KEI-9 dog in an earlier exchange.

Captain's Cabin - If you read your email, you can now invite up Traynor ( +5 Reputation ), Allers and Vega ( +2 Reputation ). Joining Traynor in the shower will initiate a Romance with her. As well, your responses in the Allers interview will affect the EMS of a War Asset either positively or negatively.

articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Geth Dreadnought Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Geth Dreadnought Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Perseus Veil "

Location: Perseus Veil - Tikkun - Geth Dreadnought

The Geth Dreadnought is in the Tikkun system, the only system you can visit in the Perseus Veil. There are three crosshairs around the star, but the Dreadnought is the one between the star and the first planet, Rannoch. If you have Tali, be sure to upgrade her Powers in the setup screen -- especially Sabotage and Combat Drone.

Squad Tactics: If Tali is present, she is required to come on this Mission. Her Sabotage is an essential tactic against Geth enemies. EDI comes highly recommended thanks to her similar focus on Tech powers, which work great on Geth. If Tali is dead, you can freely pick a second Squad Mate. In this case, Garrus is a good pick for his Overload and Armor-Piercing Ammo powers.

If Tali is present, she is required to come on this Mission. Her Sabotage is an essential tactic against Geth enemies.

EDI comes highly recommended thanks to her similar focus on Tech powers, which work great on Geth.

If Tali is dead, you can freely pick a second Squad Mate. In this case, Garrus is a good pick for his Overload and Armor-Piercing Ammo powers.

Unique Dialogue: EDI will give the most unique dialogue by a long way, being an AI. Javik is also a great pick for his Prothean lore, especially if you completed the Arrival DLC in Mass Effect 2.

EDI will give the most unique dialogue by a long way, being an AI.

Javik is also a great pick for his Prothean lore, especially if you completed the Arrival DLC in Mass Effect 2.

Shepard's Loadout: A Sniper Rifle is of great use against the Geth Hunters aboard the ship, as this level has extremely long sightlines. An Assault Rifle with a Scope mod is a good fallback if none of the sniper rifles are viable for you.

A Sniper Rifle is of great use against the Geth Hunters aboard the ship, as this level has extremely long sightlines.

An Assault Rifle with a Scope mod is a good fallback if none of the sniper rifles are viable for you.

You start the level inside the docking tube, which has been destroyed such that its artificial gravity isn't working. It may be disorienting, but whenever you reach a gap that seams like a dead end, simply walk up the walls of the tube to find a path. You can criss-cross all the way to the Dreadnought in this manner.

When you start, veer to the right to find a View Point where Shepard looks at the Dreadnought, then from there veer left to find a second one where you can look to Rannoch itself. Once you get to the end however, the tube fully breaks off, so you'll have to venture through the ship so that your two Squad Mates can board themselves.

Shotgun Smart Choke - This well-hidden Weapon Modification is found at the beginning. Drop down the ledge, then mantle up onto the light grey block that stretches left-to-right across the room. Go left across it to find the mod on the platform at the end.

Now go to the right-hand side of the room and go left around the rubble. Climb up the ladder in the hole in the hull, then turn right and leap a gap to reach a green panel door. This leads to the room with another airlock your Squad Mates can use to enter the ship.

Geth Data - 1.875 Credits. In this room, turn left at the intersection and go down the ramp towards the airlock. On the right-hand side will be a Terminal with this found on it.

Return to the intersection and go up the nearby ladder, then use the Docking Controls on the terminal to your right. Here you'll be able to pick up the Arc Pistol, which you must do manually; if you forget it, you can buy it at Elkoss Combine after the Mission.

In the next room you’ll be tasked with getting the Operations Center marked on your HUD so you can make a plan of attack.

Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope - After going through the airlock-like space, you can find this mod on the right side of the terminal directly ahead of you, and to the left of a GARDIAN Battery interact point.

When you get to a gap in the path, look for the Bridge Controls to continue through the ship. The first Geth appear after you hit the Bridge Controls: Geth Troopers are the grunts of the Geth forces and are easy to destroy, offering little threat. The Geth Rocket Troopers however fire rockets that will reduce your shield instantly upon contact and stagger Shepard.

Rocket Troopers have Shields as well. Overload and Disruptor Ammo are good choices, and a Sniper Rifle can keep Geth Rocket Troopers at a distance in which you can avoid their rockets. Rocket Troopers are an ideal candidate for hacking, though. You can Sabotage them immediately and let them take out their unwitting cronies.

Geth Data - 2,500 Credits. As you reach the end of this walkway area, keep an eye out for a terminal, at the intersection where you turn right to go to the exit door. On the right-hand side of the terminal will be this item.

Enter the green panel door at the end of the hallway. Here you can move through a few rooms filled with data panels: search this area for loot, as well as three Consoles that will provide interesting discussions, particularly if you have EDI or Javik in your Squad.

Archon Visor - When you head through the first door, go directly forwards to the Signal Console and then look to your left.

Geth Pulse Rifle - This is in the second room you traverse with no enemies just before the Op Center. When you enter the room, turn left, then search the wall on your right-hand side.

In the large Ops Center chamber you will encounter Geth Hunters , cloaked Geth with Shields and a penchant for rushing your position and blasting you with shotguns at close range. If you can’t snipe them from afar, a good Overload attack will take down their cloak. Spraying a Shotgun blast at their shimmery essence can work well too.

Data Console - Return to the entry point of this room and face into the room. Walk down to the central area of the room and check the right-hand corner of the central hologram to find this.

SMG Scope - At the opposite end of the large room from where you enter is a Weapon Mod on the raised area. It’s to the left of the Operation Center Controls.

Geth Data - 1,250 Credits. This is just on the right-hand side of the Operation Center Console.

After accessing the controls and formulating a plan, more Geth will stream into the room. Note that Tali’s Defense Drone Power can help keep the Geth Hunters off your back: it will zap them and make them visible when they near Tali. Stick by her and you can pick them off as they close in.

Head out the door the Geth used to enter the Operations Center and head down the shaft using the various ladders available to you.

Geth Data - 1,250 Credits. After sliding down the second ladder in the shaft, look for a terminal on your left.

Med Kit - 50 XP At the bottom of the shaft will be this Med Ket, to the left of the green panel exit door.

The long hallway you come to that leads to the core has periodic shockwaves that will zap your shields away. You can stay in cover to avoid it, but it’s a good idea to learn the audio cues that mean a shockwave is coming. Fortunately, you can still pop out and shoot Geth while in cover, and standing close behind walls is also enough to protect you.

The tough barrage of Geth in this tunnel should be dealt with at a great distance. Use a Sniper Rifle and Sabotage if you have them. You can climb to the upper area on the right side to get a break from the shockwave, but there are many ways for the enemies to flank you here. Note that your AI Squad will most likely repeatedly stand in the way of the shockwave and perish. To avoid this, place them in cover spots with the D-Pad and hope that they stay put.

Geth Data - 1,250 Credits. On the left side of the shockwave tube is a lower area with a terminal you can Salvage. Keep an eye out on your right for a pair of ladders: go to the bottom of the second one, then head into the lower area down a ramp nearby to find the terminal at the bottom of said ramp.

The Maintenance Override to the shockwave weapon is at the far end of the tunnel. Use them to temporarily disable the cannon so you can pass through its barrel. Inside the tube you must sprint towards the far end, leaping the gaps as you do so. If you don’t get moving right away after the cutscene ends you will automatically get vaporized and you’ll have to start the small segment over.

The next stretch is similar to the last, but shockwaves come in pairs now. Hang far back in cover and pick off the dozens of Geth that come at you. Only proceed from one cover spot to the next when the Hunters are gone.

If you're playing the Wii U Special Edition, you can find an M-597 Ladon after sliding down the ladder to the final section of the main battery hall. It'll be on your right on top of a low metal structure, next to a pair of Thermal Clips.

At the end of the hall is a ramp on the left side that leads to a door you can interface with. This leads to the elevator to the Core.

Geth Data - 1,875 Credits. Before stepping on the elevator, head rightwards around the elevator platform to find a terminal with Geth Data on it.

In the elevator shaft a pair of Geth will fire at you with rockets, destabilizing the lift: you must sprint to reach Tali and clamber up to safety. The next section will be just like the previous shaft (no combat!), only now you'll be climbing up rather than down.

Med Kit - 50 XP. After climbing the first and only ladder, you can find a Med Kit on the corner terminal directly ahead of you.

In the core you'll open up the Reaper Signal Transmitter to find a geth inside. Who this is will depend on your choices earlier in the series:

If you decided not to sell Legion in Mass Effect 2 and they survived the final mission (or you focused entirely on building the Squad in the Genesis 2 DLC), they will be the one in the transmitter.

If not, it will be a replacement known as the Geth VI .

For ease, we'll refer to both of these characters as "Geth Sniper". Either way, pick the upper-right option for +2 Paragon Points , or the lower-right option for +2 Renegade Points .

After the cutscene, make sure to grab the items listed below BEFORE stepping on the elevator with your Quarian. It'll be impossible to get back down here after that!

Assault Rifle Precision Scope - Immediately on your right after the Geth Sniper cutscene, on top of a terminal.

Geth Data - 2,500 Credits. In the opposite corner of the lower area from the Assault Rifle Precision Scope, also on a terminal.

Head up the lift and then make a U-Turn to your left to find the Data Core Override.

The next fight features several Geth Turrets and, worst of all, two Geth Primes . These towering Geth move slowly but fire extremely dangerous projectiles. They also call drones to assist them and pack a powerful set of Shields and Armor that will require you to use your Powers carefully.

Sabotage won’t work well on the Geth Prime, so use it on the Rocket Troopers to turn them against the others. The main problem with this area is poor visibility, so stay on the high ground and, if you find a good cover spot, just take your time eliminating the many threats. You must kill all of the Geth in the area to proceed -- as you do so the Quarian Fleet will begin firing on the Dreadnought.

After clearing the room, you will be forced to make a speedy escape via the Hangar. As you do so many things will blow up. There is a linear path towards the goal, however, so don't worry about getting lost or stuck. At the hangar bay a cutscene will play and the combat portion of the Mission will end.

After a chat with Admiral Hackett, you'll reconvene with the Quarian Admirals, particularly about Gerrel firing at the Dreadnought while you were still on it. Here you can say...

"You are out of control" for +2 Renegade Points . If you pick this, Gerrel protests, and you can then use a Renegade Interrupt to punch him in the gut and order him off your ship, for +5 Renegade Points .

If you pick this, Gerrel protests, and you can then use a Renegade Interrupt to punch him in the gut and order him off your ship, for +5 Renegade Points .

After this, the Geth Sniper will enter the room. Normally the Admirals will be outraged at having a Geth on board, but if you managed to have Legion be present in " Tali: Treason " in Mass Effect 2, they'll be much calmer about it. Admiral Xen in particular expresses interest in studying them, where you can...

Pick "No" for +2 Paragon Points . When Xen presses the issue, you can pull a Paragon Interrupt for +5 Paragon Points .

When Xen presses the issue, you can pull a Paragon Interrupt for +5 Paragon Points .

After this scene, you'll notice that a garbled Distress Call is being picked up by the Normandy. While this will loop forever, after you Examine it and have EDI clear it up, you have until just after the call goes to static to Warn Raan. If you do it in time, you'll get +5 Reputation .

Now it's time to do your usual sweeps of the ship:

CIC - In addition to your Geth Sniper, Raan will have new dialogue if you ask about the Civilian Fleet and Admiral Xen, and Tali has a new greeting. Also talk with Traynor to pick up " N7: Fuel Reactors ", then Joker and EDI. You'll also have an email from Miranda asking to meet at the Citadel, which we'll handle later.

Crew Deck - Talk to Garrus ( +2 Reputation ), your Virmire Survivor, Liara ( +2 Reputation ) plus her Broker Terminal, and your Med Lab doctor. If you're following our guide in order, did " Normandy: Serrice Ice Brandy " in Mass Effect 2, but didn't do the Omega DLC recently, you can talk with Dr. Chakwas now for +5 Reputation and optionally have another drink with her.

If you're following our guide in order, did " Normandy: Serrice Ice Brandy " in Mass Effect 2, but didn't do the Omega DLC recently, you can talk with Dr. Chakwas now for +5 Reputation and optionally have another drink with her.

Engineering - Talk to Allers and Javik ( +2 Reputation ), but be aware that Javik has a walk-in conversation with Tali.

Shuttle Bay - Talk to Cortez and James ( +2 Reputation ).

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Tuchanka: Turian Platoon - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Tuchanka: Turian Platoon Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Tuchanka: Turian Platoon Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

While this Side Mission doesn't expire at all, the one that follows it, " Tuchanka: Bomb ", DOES. "Bomb" expires three Missions after you complete "Turian Platoon", so if you want very unique dialogue opportunities in "Bomb", delay "Turian Platoon" as well.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Weapons: M-9 Tempest Phaeston (if not acquired in " Omega: Aria T'Loak ")

Phaeston (if not acquired in " Omega: Aria T'Loak ")

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Sur'Kesh "

Location: Krogan DMZ - Aralakh - Tuchanka

This Side Mission is unlocked after you complete " Priority: Sur'Kesh ". Once you've done so, then in the aftermath cutscene you'll be asked to meet with Primarch Victus regarding a sensitive matter. Turns out the Turians have lost a platoon on Tuchanka, one lead by Victus' son.

Tuchanka is one of the main worlds for this leg of the game's story, so its system, Krogan DMZ, will be marked with a flashing white on the Galaxy Map. You'll be dropped off in the Aralakh system, and Tuchanka will be the third planet here.

You may have a few spots on Tuchanka you can land on: you'll want to pick the spot labeled "Downed Vessel" But while you're here, you may want to consider getting the following Search and Rescue items from the Krogan DMZ's other systems (although Nith is admittedly optional since it only contains Fuel):

Squad Tactics: James is a fantastic choice for his armor-stripping powers: Incendiary Ammo and Carnage. Garrus is also a good choice for his Armor-Piercing Ammo.

James is a fantastic choice for his armor-stripping powers: Incendiary Ammo and Carnage.

Garrus is also a good choice for his Armor-Piercing Ammo.

Unique Dialogue: Garrus gives the most unique dialogue for this Side Mission. If you don't have Garrus, pick James . EDI provides some alternate dialogue for the start of this Mission. The Side Mission after this one, " Tuchanka: Bomb ", has some very unique dialogue. However "Bomb" expires three Missions after unlocking you complete "Turian Platoon" (with drastic consequences), so if you want this unique dialogue you should delay "Turian Platoon" in order to make that easier on you. You'll want to wait until after " Priority: The Citadel 2 " and / or " Priority: Rannoch ".

Garrus gives the most unique dialogue for this Side Mission. If you don't have Garrus, pick James .

EDI provides some alternate dialogue for the start of this Mission.

The Side Mission after this one, " Tuchanka: Bomb ", has some very unique dialogue. However "Bomb" expires three Missions after unlocking you complete "Turian Platoon" (with drastic consequences), so if you want this unique dialogue you should delay "Turian Platoon" in order to make that easier on you. You'll want to wait until after " Priority: The Citadel 2 " and / or " Priority: Rannoch ".

Shepard's Loadout: This level is primarily made up of tight, enclosed spaces, so bringing a Sniper Rifle is just added weight. Instead, focus on short and medium-range weapons like SMGs, shotguns and assault rifles.

This level is primarily made up of tight, enclosed spaces, so bringing a Sniper Rifle is just added weight. Instead, focus on short and medium-range weapons like SMGs, shotguns and assault rifles.

For those playing the original release of Mass Effect 3 on Xbox 360, PS3 or PC, there's a bug in this Side Mission relating to the Harvesters you fight. If you kill either of the first two Harvesters, then the fourth that shows up at the end will never appear, soft-locking the Mission. If you accidentally do that, use the Restart Mission save file from the Load Screen to try again. Legendary Edition and Wii U Special Edition players don't have to worry: this bug was fixed for those versions.

Unfortunately, due to the bad terrain Cortez isn't able to land anywhere near the crashed Turian frigate, but it does bring one unintended bonus: you're far back enough that the Reaper forces will be unaware of your presence! After landing, Shepard will get Victus' rough position with a signal flare, and the Side Mission begins.

SMG Magazine Upgrade - From the start of the level the path will turn right towards a ladder. Instead of doing that, turn left to find this in the rubble.

Spare Parts - 3,125 credits. From the SMG Magazine Upgrade described above, climb up the ladder and press on through the rubble. Ahead you'll encounter three squatting Husks: kill them quick as you can, then investigate the debris they were squatting in front of for credits.

M-9 Tempest - From the Spare Parts described above, climb up the ladder to find a crashed escape pod with three dead Turians in front of it. Jump across the gap, then check the Turians to find this new weapon.

When you vault over the fallen column ahead on the left, you'll get into a cutscene where Shepard spots some Cannibals up ahead, unaware of your presence. After it's over, press forward and exploit this golden preemptive strike opportunity and neutralize the threats before they notice you. Then, a Harvester shows up.

If you're playing the original release of the game on Xbox 360, PS3 or PC (but not Wii U), killing this first Harvester will cause the final one at the end of the level to not spawn in, soft-locking the Mission! If you do kill it, load the Restart Mission file in the Load Menu.

This bug is NOT present in the Legendary Edition.

The Harvester is a very formidable foe, and demands the utmost respect on the battlefield.

Their main cannons deal huge area, so make sure you're in cover at all times and spread your squad out to minimize splash damage casualties. Infiltrators can work around this issue by using Tactical Cloak, letting them snipe as they please.

Harvesters always keep their distance, sometimes to the point that you can never get up close to them, so you won't have to worry about any melee attacks.

It's very hard to take out Harvesters whilst under enemy fire, so make sure you take out all other enemies before focusing on the Harvester itself.

The only bar a Harvester has is Armor, so use Incendiary / Armor-Piercing Ammo, Incinerate and Carnage to take chunks out of it.

The Harvester is also part of a mechanic unique to this level in particular:

The Harvester will start firing on the Escape Pod, weakening its health and gradually killing the pair of turians at each pod.

You can distract the Harvester by firing at it, where it will attack you instead of the Escape Pod. If you leave it along for too long, however, it will turn its attention back to the Escape Pod.

You DO NOT need to kill the Harvester! It'll fly away once you've taken out half its Armor.

Once the Harvester is down, any surviving Turians will thank you and let you know of another pod just up ahead. To continue, check the right-hand wall for a ladder to climb up.

Sniper Rifle Spare Ammo - When you climb to the top of the ladder, STOP! Look left to find this mod on some rubble.

Spare Parts - 6,250 credits. From the Sniper Rifle Spare Ammo described above, go down the drop up ahead to find a turian body. Continue past him and then look right to find this pile of Spare Parts.

Phaeston - From the Spare Parts described above, return to the dead turian and then go left. Ahead will be a dead Turian with this gun next to him. NOTE: This will not be present if you already picked up a Phaeston during the Omega DLC .

SMG Ultralight Materials - From the Phaeston described above, head forward into the dark noon and turn left to spot this mod under the rubble.

Med Kit - 50 XP. When you drop down the next ladder, directly ahead will be a stone column leaning on the right-hand wall. Check behind the column for this Med Kit.

If you're playing the original release of the game on Xbox 360, PS3 or PC (but not Wii U), killing the second Harvester up ahead will cause the final one at the end of the level to not spawn in, soft-locking the Mission! If you do kill it, load the Restart Mission file in the Load Menu.

Again, this bug is NOT present in the Legendary Edition.

The next area of conflict features all of the enemies, including a Marauder and another Harvester. Take them all down quickly and drive the Harvester away to save the Turians (that'll happen with about 1/3rd of its Armor left). Once the area is good and quiet, head right and down the drop to continue.

Hahne-Kedar Chestplate - After the drop, turn right and vault over the fallen column. This will be sitting on a ledge to your left.

Flight Recorder - From the Hahne-Kedar Chestplate described above, drop down the hole in the ground ahead. You'll see a Datapad up ahead near some rubble, giving you a bit of insight into how the men feel about Victus' leadership.

Shotgun Smart Choke - From the Flight Recorder described above, turn left to spot this on some rubble in the corner ahead.

Junk - 3,125 credits. From the Shotgun Smart Choke described above, turn right and a trio of Husks will be dropped in right in front of you. Mow them down, then check the body of the Turian where the Husks dropped in. Make sure to grab this before dropping down the next ladder!

Resistance ramps up when another Harvester appears, but fortunately it retreats with about a sliver of its health left. You should try and do this where the Harvester first appears at the top of the ramp: driving it away now will prevent it from flying down the ramp and spawning a LOT more Reaper enemies for you to deal with.

Press forward and move downhill through the collapsed ruins: at the bottom you'll finally spot the crashed Turian ship Lieutenant Victus commanded. From there, the path turns right.

Med Kit - After dropping down a short ledge, check the right-hand wall for this Med Kit.

Sniper Rifle Extended Barrel - From the Med Kit described above, drop down the second, much higher ledge, then look left to spot this mod.After scaring off the third Harvester, continue down to find this along the path.

The next area becomes a crucial chokepoint, where a Brute is thrown at your squad along with a bevy of Cannibals and Marauders. There is a Reaper Blackstar available at the base of a column across from the entry point if you're having difficulty with the Brute: it's powerful enough to one-shot it on any difficulty! But you may also want to save it for the Harvester, who'll bookend the encounter.

Once the Harvester and any Reaper stragglers are dead, you’ll meet up with Lt. Victus, who'll explain how exactly his team managed to get pinned down by Reapers. Here, you can pick...

"Bad calls happen" for +2 Paragon Points .

After this, the Lieutenant reveals the exact reason why they came on Tuchanka: a bomb in Cerberus' possession that the Turians were sent to deactivate, which is now in Cerberus' possession. Unfortunately Lt. Victus' men are low on spirit and he'd prefer to abandon the mission, so you'll have to motivate them with...

"Appeal to their honor" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Kick their asses!" for +2 Renegade Points .

Either choice will be successful, and Shepard will return to the Normandy.

Shepard chats with Hackett, and both agree that something isn't right about Cerberus just happening to have a bomb on Tuchanka. After the call is over, Shepard approaches Primarch Victus, who remains tight-lipped about the situation and asks if Shepard would give up information that puts Earth at risk. Here, you can answer...

"Yes. I have to trust you" for +2 Paragon Points .

"No. Earth comes first" for +2 Renegade Points .

Unfortunately neither appeal to him. Hopefully you can learn more when you reunite with the Primarch's son back on Tuchanka.

If this was the first main Mission you completed after " Priority: Sur'Kesh ", you'll now be approached by your STG Doctor saying he's developed a cure. You can get up to +4 Paragon Points or +4 Renegade Points depending on your choices, and unlock " Priority: Tuchanka " too! You still have total freedom to ignore it, however.

After the cutscenes, do another sweep of the Normandy:

CIC - Chat with the Primarch again, your Krogan Leader, Traynor, Joker, and EDI.

Crew Deck - Chat with Garrus and Liara in Port Observation (with an extra discussion when you open the door to leave).

Engineering - Pop by Javik's place for a few comments. Gabby and Ken will have an exchange, and Allers has a news recording you can overhear. If you completed this Side Mission after " Priority: Rannoch ", then you may be able to overhear an exchange between Tali and EDI as well.

If you completed this Side Mission after " Priority: Rannoch ", then you may be able to overhear an exchange between Tali and EDI as well.

Shuttle Bay - Chat with James for a very small comment.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Priority: Rannoch - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Rannoch Mission. Our step-by-step guide will detail everything you need to know
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Rannoch Mission. Our step-by-step guide will detail everything you need to know about uploading the Reaper code, Tap to Reveal , surviving all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and also how to pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

It is imperative that you complete the Side Missions " Rannoch: Admiral Koris " and " Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons " first, as they will be removed after completing this Mission. This is important because they affect your chances for an ideal outcome at the end of this Mission!

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

War Assets: (note that for story reasons, geth and quarian assets are typically mutually exclusive) Geth: Geth Corps (300 TMS) Geth Fleet (300 TMS) Quarian: Admiral Daro'Xen (25 TMS, original 2012 release only) Quarian Civilian Fleet (200 TMS) Quarian Heavy Fleet (200 TMS) Quarian Patrol Fleet (200 TMS)

Geth: Geth Corps (300 TMS) Geth Fleet (300 TMS)

Quarian: Admiral Daro'Xen (25 TMS, original 2012 release only) Quarian Civilian Fleet (200 TMS) Quarian Heavy Fleet (200 TMS) Quarian Patrol Fleet (200 TMS)

Admiral Daro'Xen (25 TMS, original 2012 release only)

Prerequisite: Complete either " Rannoch: Admiral Koris " or " Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons "

Location: Perseus Veil - Tikkun - Rannoch

For this mission, head to the Perseus Veil and then to Rannoch in the Tikkun system. It'll be clearly marked as all worlds with Priority Missions are. Choose to land at the "Reaper Base" near the equator.

Team Tactics: You must bring Tali if she's alive: her Sabotage will once again come in handy, so upgrade it as much as possible. Garrus is a good choice here thanks to his Overload and Armor-Piercing Ammo abilities. If Tali died in Mass Effect 2, you can bring along two Squad Mates of your choosing. In this case, EDI is good replacement for her.

You must bring Tali if she's alive: her Sabotage will once again come in handy, so upgrade it as much as possible.

Garrus is a good choice here thanks to his Overload and Armor-Piercing Ammo abilities.

If Tali died in Mass Effect 2, you can bring along two Squad Mates of your choosing. In this case, EDI is good replacement for her.

Unique Dialogue: If your love interest is available as a Squad Mate, choosing them may give some unique dialogue.

If your love interest is available as a Squad Mate, choosing them may give some unique dialogue.

Shepard's Loadout: If you're playing the original release and just completed " Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons ", note that Shepard's loadout will have been completely reset to just the M-3 Predator pistol! If you forget to switch it back, go to the Load menu and choose the Restart Mission file.

If you're playing the original release and just completed " Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons ", note that Shepard's loadout will have been completely reset to just the M-3 Predator pistol! If you forget to switch it back, go to the Load menu and choose the Restart Mission file.

As you travel to Rannoch, you'll have a conversation with your Geth Sniper, as well as with your Quarian partner. If said Quarian is Tali, then you'll have a very significant scene when you first touch down on Rannoch. This scene is why we suggested you not take Tali with you for Rannoch's two Side Missions. You can say anything you like are there are no Morality Points, but if you have Tali you'll get +2 Reputation .

After the opening cutscenes, you will touch down on top of a steep slope and drop to a valley leading up to the front gate. Send your Squad to one side and remain on the other. Stay in cover and snipe the many Geth Troopers below. There are no surprises here, outside of the sheer numbers of Geth Troopers who spawn here.

SMG High Caliber Barrel - As you approach the bottom of the hill, you'll spot the front gate ahead which will slam shut as you approach it. Walk up to it, then look to your right to spot this Weapon Modification among some Thermal Clips.

The main way into the facility is blocked, so you'll have to improvise and climb up the side of the base's wall. Look to the right of the now-closed entry gate at the bottom of the hill to spot a series of ledges, pipes and ladders. Some ammo can be found on the first ledge.

As you climb up, send your Squad up one ladder and then climb up the other to flank the Geth Rocket Troopers who appear on the distant walkway. We recommend going up the right-hand ladder as you have a better view of the Rocket Troopers who enter the area.

Assault Rifle Piercing Mod - Climb the right-hand ladder as you ascend up the wall of the base and keep right. When you get to the end where the Rocket Troopers were, turn left and leap across the first gap to spot this mod on your right.

Kassa Fabrication Gauntlets - From the Assault Rifle Piercing Mod described above, hop across the next gap to get to the ladder leading to the top of the wall. This armor will be visible on your right, in the corner of the platform.

Climb the ladder to the left side of where you encountered the Rocket Troopers. At the top you can gather ammo and clamber onto some pipes to proceed upwards. In the next area, Geth will appear above and below you. The upper path is safer since you have the high ground, but if you have Sabotage , hack a group of Rocket Troopers on the lower path and let them take out everyone in proximity while you back them up.

Enter the green panel door at the end of the two-tiered hallway to continue.

Reaper Tech - 10,000 Credits - As you pass through the small room behind the green panel door, make sure to check the right-hand side for a terminal with this on it.

Exit the tunnel to find a lone Geth Trooper directly ahead. Shoot them down, then head forward along the walkway to the intersection where it was standing. Here you can use a View Prompt to look down to the bay where the Reaper tech is, just in time for it to be covered up by a Blast Shield. Legion will help you work to getting it open.

SMG Ultralight Materials - At the intersection where the lone Geth Trooper described above was, head down the left route down the ramp, where you can find this mod in the left-hand corner at the dead end at the bottom of the ramp.

Take the right-hand path at the intersection now to progress into the base, where there are numerous Geth Troopers . Stay in cover and snipe them -- Sabotage can capture entire groups of enemies and turn them to your side temporarily here since the area is so cramped.

Assault Rifle Stability Damper - Early on the right-hand path is a low square block you can use as cover. To the right of it is an alcove-like area where this Weapon Mod is located.

Geth will now appear both directly in front of you on the walkway and across a chasm on your left, as pointed out by one of your Squad Mates. Deal with the Rocket Troopers first since they're the most pressing issue, then continue to the end of the walkway once all the Geth are gone.

Geth Plasma Shotgun - As you get to the end of the walkway where the green panel door is, look to your left to find this weapon on some containers next to a terminal.

Data - 5,000 Credits. On the terminal that's next to where you found the Geth Plasma Shotgun.

Data - 10,000 Credits. Continue through the green panel door and you'll quickly find a terminal with this on it at the U-turn.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the left side of the terminal where you found the Data described above.

In the next area, your waypoint shows a Door Override console. Clear the room of Geth first (stay near where you entered so you don’t get flanked), then when everything's quiet, head over and Activate it. Once you do so, you'll have to survive a wave of Geth Rocket Troopers and Geth Pyros.

The Pyros are, somewhat ironically, very susceptible to fire, so take advantage by shooting their fuel tanks with Incendiary Ammo or other fire-based Powers. After hitting a second console, a Geth Prime will arrive with two Rocket Troopers. Try to catch them all with Sabotage in the shaft or a barrage of grenades.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Before heading up the lift to the upper floor, check the corner to the right of it to find this Med Kit. It'll be quite dark, almost black!

At the top of the elevator you will face three Geth Primes in a relatively small area, as well as Geth Turrets in the middle of the room, so as you move about, stay in cover or take them out. Luckily, there are three Geth Spitfire heavy weapons in the area, one right near the entrance, one by a door on the left side, and one on some crates on the right side.

The Geth Spitfires will not completely solve your Geth problem, but combined with Sabotage or explosives to stop the Primes from moving in, they can be a huge help. Just make sure you're in cover, as getting hit will stop the Spitfire from firing and you'll have to spin it up again.

Once the Geth Primes are down, walk to the balcony on the edge of the outer area (in the direction of the sunset), then stand on the upper ledge here to initiate a cutscene, where you'll then pull out the Targeting Laser.

Your target for this is NOT the “Base” marker in the distance, but an open blast door below the ledge you're standing on. Aim from the ledge down at the red light below and hold the FIRE button (usually the right trigger) to summon an orbital strike via the Normandy.

Unfortunately, your target wasn't just Reaper tech, but an entire dormant Reaper, which is now very much awake. Sprint to the left around the Reaper's chamber to escape its death ray, which will initiate a cutscene for a frantic escape manning a turret atop the Geth speeder. You can fire at the Reaper if you want, but it's absolutely not required and won't do anything to harm it.

Eventually, you'll pull over to fight the Reaper Destroyer head-on. This is actually more unintuitive than it looks, so here's a breakdown of how this section works:

To summon an orbital strike, all you need to do it point it at the Reaper's firing chamber when it has the blue circle around it and hold the FIRE button.

After the first strike, the Reaper will turn its attention to Shepard and fire at them, so you'll need to balance using the laser with moving out of the laser's explosive path.

The biggest mistake players make here is also using the left trigger to zoom in for aim. DO NOT USE THE LEFT TRIGGER . It is not required to use the Targeting Laser, and more importantly it slows Shepard's movement, making it almost impossible to move out of the way of the Reaper's laser beam.

The Reaper's laser beam does not track you, so once it starts firing just move far away.

You can still lock onto the target while moving, although in that case the lock will be slower until you stop moving again.

You do not have to do the entire target lock in one go: if you let go of the Fire button, it will simply pause, waiting for you to resume when you're ready. Don't be afraid to let go of the Fire button if it means you can get out of the way more quickly!

The Reaper's laser beam causes explosions as it passes through, so you'll have to be much further away than you might think in order to avoid getting blasted by it.

You don't have unlimited room to maneuver on the cliff: you'll be blocked by walls on the sides. With that in mind, alternate between moving left and moving right with each passing laser beam.

There are four strikes required, including the first one, and each time the Reaper comes closer. After making the last strike, you will enter a slow-motion scene to engage your final shot. Just point, focus and watch the fireworks.

At this point the Destroyer will be downed, but not entirely out, as it will now speak to Shepard. We actually recommend you pick the middle option on the left: Shepard will ask why the Reapers are killing everyone, and you'll get some hints about the subject.

Pick "Help us understand" for no Morality Points, but receive a little bit more hints behind the Reapers compared to the other two options.

Pick "We'll destroy you eventually" for +2 Paragon Points . Pull the Paragon Interrupt after this to verbally lay the Reaper to rest for +5 Paragon Points more.

Pull the Paragon Interrupt after this to verbally lay the Reaper to rest for +5 Paragon Points more.

Pick "You're arrogant for a machine" for +2 Renegade Points . Pull the Renegade Interrupt after this to explosively silence the Reaper for +5 Renegade Points more.

Pull the Renegade Interrupt after this to explosively silence the Reaper for +5 Renegade Points more.

The Geth vs. the Quarians - How to Broker Peace Between Geth and Quarians

Following the destruction of the Reaper will be another one of Mass Effect 3's pivotal story checks that determines the fate of many. Here, it's to convince the Quarians not to attack the Geth. You have an initial wheel that appears to make this choice, but the real one is after that, the Charm / Intimidate options on the left and the two white options on the right.

The two white options on the right will always be available. Here's what they do:

"[Allow the upload] / [Upload the code]" - The Geth will come back online and wipe out the Quarians, and your Quarian partner will then commit suicide. Even a Loyal, Romanced Tali will take her own life, and not even the Paragon Interrupt will be able to save her. If your Geth Sniper is Legion, this will give +15 Paragon Points . If your Geth Sniper is the Geth VI, this will give +15 Reputation .

If your Geth Sniper is Legion, this will give +15 Paragon Points .

If your Geth Sniper is the Geth VI, this will give +15 Reputation .

"[Stop Legion]" / "[Let geth die]" - Your Geth Sniper will attack you, and you can pull up to three optional Renegade Interrupts to shoot the Geth Sniper. They'll die either way, and the Quarians will destroy the Geth fleet and wipe out the race altogether. If your Geth Sniper is Legion, this will give you +15 Renegade Points . If your Geth Sniper is the Geth VI, this will give you +15 Reputation .

If your Geth Sniper is Legion, this will give you +15 Renegade Points .

If your Geth Sniper is the Geth VI, this will give you +15 Reputation .

If you can only pick these white options, there's an extra wrinkle here that may influence who you side with. Your choice at the end of " Legion: A House Divided " in Mass Effect 2 affected the strength of the Geth and Quarian War Assets:

If you rewrote the Geth Heretics, the Geth Fleets have 750 TMS while the Quarian Fleets have 450 TMS.

If you deleted the Geth Heretics, the Geth Fleets have 400 TMS while the Quarian Fleets have 600 TMS.

The Charm / Intimidate options allow you to attempt to convince the Quarians that both wars were entirely their fault and that ceasing their fire will end it, but this is one of the most demanding feats in the entire trilogy because it requires you to pass TWO checks that involve decisions you've made in the past.

First, you need to unlock the Persuasion options to begin with. You must meet all four of these for the options to unlock . The requirements are:

Legion needs to be alive and present (the Geth VI replacement does not count).

The " Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons " Side Mission must have been completed, since it provides the context for why the Quarians are to blame, which forms the basis of Shepard's argument.

Unlocking the options is half the battle, however: you also need to have enough clout, both situationally and diplomatically, for your plea to actually work . Similar to " Priority: The Citadel 2 ", this is done by checking your past actions and awarding points. These actions are:

Mass Effect 2 actions: +2 Points for not presenting the evidence against Tali's father during " Tali: Treason " in Mass Effect 2. +2 Points for destroying the heretic geth in " Legion: A House Divided " in Mass Effect 2, weakening the Geth fleet now. +1 Point for using a Persuasion option to resolve Tali and Legion's post-Loyalty Mission argument in Mass Effect 2.

+2 Points for not presenting the evidence against Tali's father during " Tali: Treason " in Mass Effect 2.

+2 Points for destroying the heretic geth in " Legion: A House Divided " in Mass Effect 2, weakening the Geth fleet now.

+1 Point for using a Persuasion option to resolve Tali and Legion's post-Loyalty Mission argument in Mass Effect 2.

Mass Effect 3 actions: +1 Point for completing " Rannoch: Admiral Koris ", proving your loyalty to the Migrant Fleet. +1 Point for saving Admiral Koris in "Rannoch: Admiral Koris", where he will back Shepard's plea.

+1 Point for completing " Rannoch: Admiral Koris ", proving your loyalty to the Migrant Fleet.

+1 Point for saving Admiral Koris in "Rannoch: Admiral Koris", where he will back Shepard's plea.

If you acquired 5 Points towards this second check, your plea will be successful, resulting in a ceasefire that allows you to have peace between the Quarians and the Geth, letting you get BOTH fleets for the war effort! You will also get the following Morality Points:

If "[Rally the fleet]" was successful, you'll get +15 Paragon Points .

If "[Warn the fleet]" was successful, you'll get +15 Renegade Points .

You'll now be in the Vid Comm room on the Normandy, where you'll be talking with the Asari Councillor. She wants to discuss new information from her government, and Shepard offers to meet her at the Citadel to do so.

After this, Traynor will call to let you know you can talk to talk to Admiral Hackett: make sure to ask about "Allied forces" to check up on the Asari and Salarians, and if the " Tuchanka: Bomb " Side Mission expired, asking about "Krogan and turians" will have new info as well. You can also ask about "Reaper progress" and "Why pick me?".

You'll also have the Quarian and / or Geth War Assets added to Shepard's cause. If you wiped out one of the Rannoch races earlier, you may have lost a War Asset that you earned from a Rannoch Side Mission:

If you wiped out the Quarians, the Admiral Zaal'Koris War Asset from " Rannoch: Admiral Koris " has been lost.

If you wiped the Geth out, the Geth Platoon War Asset from " Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons " has been lost.

Now it's time to do your usual rounds of the Normandy to catch up with everyone.

CIC - Talk to Traynor, Joker and EDI. Unlock the third and final Allers interview by reading your Private Terminal. If Ashley is alive, you'll have a message from her asking to meet at the Citadel.

Crew Deck - Talk to Ashley, Liara, Garrus, and Chakwas if Tali died. If Kaidan is alive, you can find him in the bar lounge with James.

Engineering - Talk to Javik, Gabby and Ken (and Ken again if Tali died), Tali in the drive core ( +5 Reputation ), and Allers.

Shuttle Bay - Talk to James here, if he wasn't in the bar lounge with Kaidan.

Captain's Cabin - Call Allers up for the interview ( +5 Reputation , and... a Codex entry?!). The Persuasion options will add 5 TMS to a War Asset belonging to the the race being discussed (Quarians if they survived, or Geth if either they or both races survived). If you've been flirting with Allers, this is where the Romance scene can happen with her. This won't jeopardize any other Romance in the game, although if Liara has been Locked In, she won't be too impressed (she's the Shadow Broker, remember!).

If you've been flirting with Allers, this is where the Romance scene can happen with her. This won't jeopardize any other Romance in the game, although if Liara has been Locked In, she won't be too impressed (she's the Shadow Broker, remember!).
