articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Thessia Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Thessia Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: The Citadel 3 "

Location: Athena Nebula - Parintha - Thessia

To begin " Priority: Thessia ", travel to the Athena Nebula (close to the Serpent Nebula where the Citadel is), and land on Thessia , the inner-most planet in the system.

Before landing, you may want to grab these Search and Rescue items:

Squad Tactics: Liara is a mandatory squad member. Level up her Warp skill, as well as Warp ammo. A combination of biotics is also a good choice, so Javik or Kaidan are ideal.

Liara is a mandatory squad member. Level up her Warp skill, as well as Warp ammo.

A combination of biotics is also a good choice, so Javik or Kaidan are ideal.

Unique Dialogue: For unique dialogue, Javik will give a huge amount of it in this Mission. If you don't have Javik, Garrus will have to do.

For unique dialogue, Javik will give a huge amount of it in this Mission.

If you don't have Javik, Garrus will have to do.

Shepard's Loadout: The Sniper Rifle Concentration Module makes sniping Banshees much easier, as it briefly slows down time when aiming down the scope.

The Sniper Rifle Concentration Module makes sniping Banshees much easier, as it briefly slows down time when aiming down the scope.

During the next cutscene, you will discuss the situation with Liara, who is very distressed over the Reapers attacking her homeworld. Here you can tell her how she should act in this situation.

The wording will vary depending on if Javik is in your squad or not, but in any situation, the upper-right option will give +2 Paragon Points while the lower-right option will give +2 Renegade Points .

When you arrive, head down the hill of rubble to the outpost. Before talking to Lieutenant Kurin on your left, check among the body bags on the right-hand side for some items. You MUST pick these items up now or else you'll be swiftly moved on to the next part of the level without a chance to go back for them.

Umbra Visor - To find this item, look to the right of the two rows of body bags directly in front of you. It'll be close to a red ammo box.

Supplies - 4,500 Credits. Continue forwards to a light stand at the base of a column to find this.

Now talk to Lieutenant Kurin, but before you can even get a word in, some rockets take out the guard, so you'll have to defend the position. Using the Mounted Turret on the right side of the entrance, destroy the Barrier Engine from the jump, take out all six Brutes, and of course the Husks that attack the Asari. Don’t let the biotic barrier fall, and reload between waves. Pay special attention to the barrier bubble itself -- Husks like to slip past you and attack it.

Once they're all dead, speak with Kurin again, who has been ordered to hold this hopeless position especially for you, although she has no idea who you even are.

Here you can say "What are your orders?" on the left, then reply either... "I sympathize" for +2 Paragon Points . "There's a good reason" for +2 Renegade .

"There's a good reason" for +2 Renegade .

Regardless, you can advance the conversation with... "I'm looking for an artifact" for +2 Paragon Points . "Just follow your orders" for +2 Renegade Points .

"I'm looking for an artifact" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Just follow your orders" for +2 Renegade Points .

The next set of Morality Points depends on if you brought Javik along or not:

If you have Javik, he will read the Asari's memories and give her confidence. If that's the case, you can say either... "We have the Crucible" for +2 Paragon Points . "Listen to him" for +2 Renegade Points .

"We have the Crucible" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Listen to him" for +2 Renegade Points .

If you don't have Javik, you can pick "I've beaten Reapers before" for +2 Renegade Points .

After finishing the conversation with Kurin, you'll be on the bridge with the path behind you blocked. Push forward and take out the Marauders and Cannibals that appear on the far end. Remember that Cannibals like to devour their fallen brethren to bolster their armor (hence the name), so don't give them the chance! Once they're all down, head to the end of the bridge and head right, going over more rubble and around the building into a plaza.

Here, expect multiple Marauders in the area, and dozens of Cannibals. The Marauders here are perhaps best dealt with by assigning your squad to confront one, while you take out another. Use the squad commands (D-pad)! When you get towards the back end of the area, a Banshee will appear through your exit door.

Banshees are Reaper-converted Ardat-Yakshi, and this is the first guaranteed time they appear (you can meet them earlier in " Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastery " or the Leviathan DLC ). They have extremely powerful Barriers, and warp around to make headshots hard. Use Warp or Disruptor Ammo to sap the Barrier, and if you have a Sniper Rifle Concentration Mod, use it to score headshots. Most importantly, keep your distance.

Once all the enemies are down, you can search the area for some loot. Both of these will be near the plaza in the middle of this area.

Med Kit - 50 XP. In the plaza, face towards the Banshee door, then look left close to the plaza for a pile of rubble just up the steps. This Med Kit will be here, underneath a light.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Near the plaza will be a building on the right, whose front door is in the shaded area underneath its very large overhang. The Med Kit will be at the front door.

Now, enter the demolished building via the Banshee door, then turn left to go up the ramp, vault up a ledge and head through a doorway. Turn right and you'll spot an orange panel bypass door at the end of the ruined hallway.

Terminal - 7,500 Credits. Drop down the next ledge to find this in the rubble on your left. This will be just before the orange Bypass door.

In the next area, you will get a View Prompt to look up at a Reaper towering above you, as well as some Asari snipers on the other side of the area. Drop down and take out the Cannibals below you, who are largely unaware of your presence. If you have a sniper rifle, this is a great area to get some practice in.

Broken Shotgun - 3,000 Credits. In this area, head to the lower portions on the right-hand side. Here will be a large, square, two-tiered structure: go clockwise around it and up the steps into the very dark alcove to find this item for some more Credits.

Shotgun High Caliber Barrel - Above the Broken Shotgun will be a balcony. To get up there, you'll need to walk up the ramp made of rubble, where you'll find this mod.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the same balcony as the mod above.

Run up the ramp of rubble made by the collapsed building and talk to the lone sniper, although you'll quickly have to take out some enemies below. Your elevated position is a perfect sniper's nest, which contains the following items:

Sniper Rifle Concentration Module - On the overlook, at the base of the wall directly behind the Asari sniper, Cayla.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Right next to the mod described above.

M-98 Widow - This Sniper Rifle is located to the Asari sniper's left, next to some Thermal Clips.

After you clear the area, head down the ladder and look for the gap in the opposite wall so you can get to Outpost Tykis. Through the wall, head left and vault up the ledges to meet what's left of them. Unfortunately it's impossible to get to the temple without some air support: at this, reply with either...

"We could use their help" for +2 Paragon Points .

After the dialogue, you will have to clear the area in front of you. Just before the stairs up, look down and you will see another Hydra Missile Launcher , which should help you quite a bit in this situation, which is full of Ravagers and yet another Banshee, all with thick Armor. If you choose to, deal with the Banshee first, then the Ravager. Take out the Barrier generator too since it'll give another layer of protection to your foes.

Once all the enemies are dead, head up the hill of rubble.

Assault Rifle Extended Barrel - When you get to the top of the slope, stand still and turn to your right to spot the wreckage of one of the gunships. Check among the rubble for this easily-missed mod, near a Thermal Clip.

Continue to advance, but be very careful because the road ahead is a tough one. You will have to kill Husks, Ravagers, Marauders and bear the brunt of TWO Harvesters. Take out the Barrier Engine first and foremost, stay in cover at all times and maintain a fair distance. Don’t forget about Liara’s Singularity power.

Don't try and take down the Harvesters as they'll simply be replaced: instead focus on all the other Reapers while hiding in the rubble. Once the Harvesters have left, head through the debris and then follow the route left to the entrance of the temple.

SMG Heat Sink Mod - When you reach the entrance to the temple, check the left-hand side to find this mod, lying against an ammo box.

Bypass the Barrier Control on the right to enter the temple.

Med Kit - 50 XP. As you walk in, you can find this Med Kit on the left side of the entry walkway.

Once you're done examining the artifacts, Examine the Statue, where Shepard will realize that the statue contains a Prothean Beacon, like the ones they found on Eden Prime and Virmire. One of your Squad Mates then interacts with one of the plaques, which cracks the statues somewhat. So, your task is to find three more. Here are the artifacts you need to interact with:

The Bust of Janiri - The bust in the middle-right-hand side of the temple.

The Biotic Manuscript - In the corner directly to the left of the Athame Statue's Examine point.

The Shield of Athame - Flanking the side of the main walkway near where you entered the temple.

Once you find all three, return to the base of the statue to Examine it, where you'll have a very unique encounter involving a Prothean memory construct named Vendetta. Make sure to pick left-hand options here if you want a better perspective regarding the Reaper Cycles.

At first Vendetta tries to argue against even helping you, considering the Reapers are already here. To this you can say...

"But we need your help" / "Then help us" for +2 Paragon Points .

"It isn't over yet!" for +2 Renegade Points .

Vendetta then says that the Crucible is not of Prothean design, and that no cycle has ever defeated the Reapers with it (obviously!). To that you can say...

"Give us a chance" for +2 Paragon Points .

"They weren't me" for +2 Renegade Points .

Unfortunately your meeting is interrupted by the coming of Kai Leng, who links you up to a conversation with the Illusive Man.

This is another INCREDIBLY important conversation. Like the one on Mars , you'll influence events later in the game if you don't explore the dialogue here. What you need to do is pick "Whose side are you on?" when it appears , then use either...

You MUST pick the same Morality option that you did on Mars. Oddly the 5 Morality Points awarded are inverted (Charm gets Renegade, Intimidate gets Paragon), but rest assured they are otherwise treated normally.

As the conversation concludes, you can pick...

"You've lost touch" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I used to trust you" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then get in a duel with Leng himself for possession of the Prothean VI.

As soon as you gain control over Shepard, take cover behind a bench. What you should know is that you won’t win this fight, and there's nothing you can do to change its outcome.

What you need to do is to stay in cover all the time, so you can avoid the gunship behind Leng. He generally won’t get near you (although he can incur a one-hit kill on you or a Squad Mate if he does), so you don’t have to worry about that. Just fire your weapon and aim for Leng. If your shield drops, remain in cover, then fire again. Leng has Shields, so Overload and Disruptor Ammo are great assets. A Sniper Rifle is especially useful with the time-stopping Sniper Rifle Concentration Module.

When you drop Leng's Shields to about a quarter, he'll retreat and call a gunship. You can slow his recovery, but you can't stop it, so you may as well let them fully recharge. Once they have, return to attacking Leng and you'll be able to reduce his shields again to nearly zero. But he will retreat and call a gunship, again.

When his shield drops a third time, a new cutscene will start that signals the end of the Thessia Mission.

You are now in a rough spot for Shepard, and some of their crew. After a sad conversation with the Asari Councillor, Shepard retreats to the War Room with their squad, Liara upset that Cerberus was there before you. You can respond with either...

"No, I should have known" for +4 Paragon Points .

"Not good enough!" for +4 Renegade Points .

Shepard is understandably sick of Cerberus beating them and wants to get some payback. Luckily, Specialist Traynor has a lead: she tracked Kai Leng's shuttle as it crossed the galaxy, only for the signal to be blocked when it entered the Iera system in the Shadow Sea cluster. As EDI points out, it's home to Sanctuary and not much more, so with nothing else to go on, that's your next destination. You can respond to this with...

"Great job, let's make it count" for +2 Paragon Points .

"We've got our destination" for +2 Renegade Points .

Here's the various conversations you can have:

CIC - Talk with Anderson on the Vid Comm ( +2 Reputation ), Traynor to pick up " N7: Communication Hub ", then Joker and EDI.

Crew Deck - Talk to Tali ( +2 Reputation ), Ashley, and Garrus ( +2 Reputation ) to unlock the Proximity Mine Bonus Power. If you have Javik, Glyph says Liara is downstairs talking to him.

Engineering - Visit Allers, talk to Kaidan with Engineer Adams, then go to Javik's room if you have him ( +2 Reputation ).

Shuttle Bay - Talk to James for a bit of dialogue.

Crew Deck - Return to the Crew Deck and talk to Tali again, ( +2 Reputation ), then Liara ( +2 Reputation ) to unlock the Stasis Bonus Power. Then talk to Tali yet again ( +2 Reputation ).

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Priority: Horizon - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Horizon Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Horizon Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Armor : Rosenkov Materials Shoulder Guard

War Assets: Alliance Sixth Fleet (90 TMS) Miranda Lawson (25 TMS)

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Thessia "

Horizon is located in the Shadow Sea cluster in the eastern part of the Milky Way. It's the third planet in the cluster's only system, Iera.

Squad Tactics: Garrus is a great choice thanks to his combination of Overload and Armor Piercing Ammo . Ashley is also good if you have her as her Disruptor Ammo will help tear through Cerberus defenses.

Garrus is a great choice thanks to his combination of Overload and Armor Piercing Ammo .

Ashley is also good if you have her as her Disruptor Ammo will help tear through Cerberus defenses.

Unique Dialogue: For unique dialogue, Javik and Liara will tease out the most of it. If you don't have Javik, anyone else can do. If you have your Virmire Survivor , they're at least contextually interesting because of the " Horizon " Mission in Mass Effect 2.

For unique dialogue, Javik and Liara will tease out the most of it.

If you don't have Javik, anyone else can do. If you have your Virmire Survivor , they're at least contextually interesting because of the " Horizon " Mission in Mass Effect 2.

Shepard's Loadout: Bring a Sniper Rifle to deal with Nemeses. A Heavy Pistol with a Scope mod can be used if a sniper rifle isn't viable for you. Bring a Shotgun for dealing with Husks.

Bring a Sniper Rifle to deal with Nemeses.

A Heavy Pistol with a Scope mod can be used if a sniper rifle isn't viable for you.

After a scene with your Squad Mates in the Kodiak shuttle, you'll disembark at Horizon's entrance. Clearly something is VERY wrong: the place is a wreck and there are no signs of colonists anywhere. As you head up the stairs, you'll get a View Prompt that'll reveal the reason why: the Reapers have attacked the facility.

Soon after this you'll be attacked by two Phantoms , and a Nemesis sniper on an upper balcony. Try to kill the Phantoms at a distance while staying in cover to avoid getting shot by the Nemesis' sniper rifle. Once the Phantoms are taken care of, get out your sniper rifle or pistol with scope to take care of the Nemesis.

Parts - 1,500 Credits. Before you head inside, check the right-hand side of this area for a lower section. Among some rubble closest to the entry door to Sanctuary will by a ruined terminal with these Parts.

Head up to the entry door and Bypass it to enter Sanctuary proper.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Standing in the doorway into Sanctuary, look on the right side of the doorway to find this Medical Station.

As you enter, you'll get another View Prompt to look up through the glass ceiling to spy Cerberus shuttles leaving Sanctuary. This area is very large, but we'll help you through it. To make your way through, head left alongside the giant window to find a " Sanctuary " point you can use to prompt a bit of dialogue.

Near the "Sanctuary" point Now head through the office desk area to your right: you'll find many logs here to listen and read if you want, while your goal is to head down some stairs near two crashed Alliance Kodiak shuttles.

Log - On the reception desk under the cluster of holoscreens, close to the "Sanctuary" point.

Log - In the office area, directly across from the reception desk and behind the glass wall.

PDA - On a corner desk in the office area.

Log - On a corner desk in the office area.

Inventory logs - 1,500 credits. In the office desk area described above, on the corner desk that overlook the stairs to the next area and the two crashed Alliance shuttles. The desk will be empty aside from the datapad and a desk lamp.

Log - On an "island" desk, close to the stairs down to the next area.

Head down the nearby stairs to continue.

Log x2 - When you get to the bottom of the stairs, turn left to spot two crashed Alliance shuttles, Check the right-hand shuttle to find these Logs, one on each side of the door.

Through the desks on the right you'll encounter bodies of both Reapers and Cerberus, and will soon get into a fight with Cerberus Troopers. There isn't much cover to utilize here, but since they're Assault Troopers you shouldn't have too much trouble handling them.

Pistol Scope - In the middle of the room is a raised reception desk section with a dead Assault Trooper on it. Check the body for this weapon mod.

The exit is an open doorway on the left side of the room labeled "Pool Maintenance", to the right of the massive holographic Sanctuary sign. Activate the Console directly ahead to hear what you're up against -- and get a glimpse of Miranda Lawson (so long as she didn't die in Mass Effect 2).

Equipment - 1,500 Credits. Turn around after activating the console to find some salvageable equipment on the wall, right next to the doorway you just went through.

Head outside and Activate the Water Pump at the edge of the pool: this will drain all the water, allowing you to head down the ladder. One of your Squad Mates will examine one of the pumps and say it's Reaper Tech, but regardless head through the door on the opposite side of the pool.

There's nothing in the first room, but the second will have some loot:

Equipment - 1,500 Credits. On the right-hand wall of this second room will be an object that looks like one of the Wall Safes from the first and second games, which you can Salvage.

Rosenkov Materials Shoulder Guard - Just to the left of the next door, on top of a wall block thing.

The next room is a command center of sorts. Activate the console in the middle of the room to restore power. Don't worry, the things you see in the cutscene can't hurt you... yet. The tower is now marked on your HUD. Proceed through the now-unlocked door opposite the one you came in with.

There's two lore-related items to find in the next room:

PDA - When you enter, check the orange-lit area on the left to find this on a desk against the railing.

Console - If Miranda is alive, you can find this in the nook area at the back-right corner of the room.

The exit to this room is down a short set of stairs. There are a bunch of Husks behind the door, so get prepared before you head down the stairs.

Logs x2 - On the desks at the bottom of the room where you fought the first Husks of the level.

The open doorway and the regular door near the Logs both lead to the same hallway. It's a Reaper party out there -- there's a Ravager, a Banshee, and a few Marauders shooting at you from a catwalk above. Kill them in that order, ducking back into the room with the Logs for cover if you need to.

The exit is down the hallway to the left into "Incubation Research 02", a room with a Banshee staring menacingly at you through the window and making ineffective attacks on the window. Here you can find some more items:

Log - Immediately to the left of the Banshee window.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the corner desk on the opposite corner of the room from the Banshee window.

Log - To the right of the Med Kit described above.

Exit through the door to the right of the Banshee window for more loot 'n' lore:

Console - Use this glitchy terminal on your right when entering this room to get some current story progress.

PDA - On a desk to the left of the Console described above.

Research Data - 1,500 credits. In the dark corner of the room, past the Console and PDA described above.

Now head up the steps and then go left into a room full of Reaper forces. Ignore the Husks in the pods (they don't come to life) and focus on the Cannibals and Marauders. If you take cover between the two doors, you should be able to destroy the Barrier Engines through either doorway without taking fire, which will make your fight a little easier.

Once the room is clear, head to the tables and consoles in upper section of the room.

M-12 Locust - On a table in the upper area of the room.

Shotgun Blade Attachment - On a table in the area of the room, further down from the Locust.

Log - From the Shotgun Blade Attachment, turn left and down the steps to the lower area. This will be the terminal for the pod with a Husk in it on the right.

Log - In the same spot as the Log described above, only it'll be the empty pod to the right of it.

PDA - From the Logs described above. Head right to the end of the room. Ignore the Console for now and look for this on the desk to the right of it.

Console - To the left of the PDA described above. Required to progress the story!

Close to the PDA, you'll want to examine the Console at the far end to progress the story, and lower a ladder to the next area.

Climb up the ladder and get ready to fight. There's a Marauder fairly close to you -- take him out first. There are also Ravagers and Cannibals farther down the hall. Get up on the raised ledge and peer down the support columns to take out two Barrier Engines with the Sniper Rifle, if you can. There are also some more enemies lurking in the dark on the right of the lit hallway. Once the enemies are clear, make your way through the open doorway at the end of the hall.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Standing in the doorway, it'll be immediately to your right.

Research Data - 3,000 credits. On the left-hand side of this end room are three tanks. The Research Data will be on the one closest to the doorway you entered through.

Log - The terminal of the open pod with the Husk hanging out of it, to the right of the Research Data described above.

Log - A terminal at the back-corner of the room, in front of a window looking into another room.

Once you're done, go through the doorway directly across from the corner window and hop onto the Lift. To get it moving, shoot the box on the right-hand side and Activate it to move the lift across the room. Once it's on the other side, leap across the gap on the left and go through the doorway into the last combat room.

A View Prompt will reveal some Brutes at the far end of the area: there's three in total, on top of a Banshee for good measure, making this a very difficult fight. One of the Brutes is actually pretty close to you, just beyond the burning rubble. Keep your distance and wear them down.

If you're facing down the hall (as you were when you were instructed by the game to look at the Brute), there is ammo in the dark area on the right side of the room, and a med kit in the well-lit area on the left side of the room.

After the area is clear, you'll find a console and a Husk pod that can be activated to get some cool loot.

M-99 Saber - A VERY easily missed weapon. To the left of the steps up to the back end of this room is a blue "Pod Status" hologram. Activate it and use the "Pod - manual override" button prompt, which activates a pod on the opposite side of the room. Turn around and run all the way to the opposite side of the room, then turn right to find a pod with a gun in it. Activate the pod and you can access the gun!

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the upper area on the left-hand side of the room, close to a door lit in white.

Research Data - 4,500 credits. In the very end of the room will be a long desk in front of some blue servers. One of the computers on this desk will have the Research Data.

Open the door at the far end of the room to enter the elevator, which takes you up to the tower, and an important confrontation.

The end of the Mission has you finally meet and confront Miranda's father, Henry Lawson, who holds his daughter Oriana captive. Miranda will also be present if she survived the events of Mass Effect 2, but will be worse for wear here. Shepard will attempt to negotiate for Oriana's life, which is when you'll get a dialogue wheel.

Here's what each of the options do in your possible situations.

Picking the "I can be reasonable" Charm or the "I will hunt you down" Intimidate will convince Henry to let Oriana go in exchange for his life. How well this goes for him depends on if Miranda is present:

If Miranda is present, she'll use biotics to blast him through the window, killing him.

If Miranda isn't present, you'll get a Renegade Interrupt after he lets Oriana go. Pull it to shoot him dead anyway, or ignore it to let him escape with his life.

Picking "I just want Oriana" will fail to convince Henry, and will give you a Renegade Interrupt. What the Interrupt will do depends on if Miranda is present:

If Miranda IS present: Taking Interrupt will have Shepard will shoot Oriana in the leg and separate her from Henry, allowing Miranda to blast him through the window, killing him. Ignoring the Interrupt will have Miranda use her biotics to separate Oriana from Henry. This allows Henry to fatally shoot Miranda, but not before she blasts him through the window, killing him.

Taking Interrupt will have Shepard will shoot Oriana in the leg and separate her from Henry, allowing Miranda to blast him through the window, killing him.

Ignoring the Interrupt will have Miranda use her biotics to separate Oriana from Henry. This allows Henry to fatally shoot Miranda, but not before she blasts him through the window, killing him.

If Miranda is NOT present: Ignoring the Interrupt means Oriana will push them both through the cracked window behind them, killing both of them. Taking the Interrupt will have Shepard shoot Oriana in the leg and separate her from Henry. You'll then have a second Renegade Interrupt. Take it and Shepard will kill Henry. Ignore it and Henry will escape with his life.

Ignoring the Interrupt means Oriana will push them both through the cracked window behind them, killing both of them.

Taking the Interrupt will have Shepard shoot Oriana in the leg and separate her from Henry. You'll then have a second Renegade Interrupt. Take it and Shepard will kill Henry. Ignore it and Henry will escape with his life.

You'll then have a second Renegade Interrupt. Take it and Shepard will kill Henry. Ignore it and Henry will escape with his life.

If Miranda was present in the scene and Henry didn't shoot her, you'll now see the results play out on whether she lives through her Kai Leng injuries, or dies to them. This is determined by another important check which looks through your past actions to determine her fate.

The check that determines Miranda's survival requires you to have cleared at least two separate actions earlier in the story. Fail any one of them, and Miranda will die.

First, you must have either completed one of the following two actions: Completed " Miranda: The Prodigal " in Mass Effect 2 - This ensures that Miranda will be Loyal. However, using the Genesis 2 DLC comic DOES NOT COUNT! Using that will still result in Miranda being Disloyal, due to Shepard always siding with Jack in her and Miranda's argument in Mass Effect 2. Warn Miranda about Kai Leng in your conversation at the Spectre Office - This requires you to have read his dossier at your Private Terminal after " Priority: The Citadel 2 ". You'll know it worked because Shepard mentions Leng by name early in the Spectre Office conversation.

Completed " Miranda: The Prodigal " in Mass Effect 2 - This ensures that Miranda will be Loyal. However, using the Genesis 2 DLC comic DOES NOT COUNT! Using that will still result in Miranda being Disloyal, due to Shepard always siding with Jack in her and Miranda's argument in Mass Effect 2.

Warn Miranda about Kai Leng in your conversation at the Spectre Office - This requires you to have read his dossier at your Private Terminal after " Priority: The Citadel 2 ". You'll know it worked because Shepard mentions Leng by name early in the Spectre Office conversation.

Second, you MUST have attended the third meeting at the Citadel Apartment and MUST have allowed Miranda access to Alliance resources. Denying her, or not attending the meeting at all, will result in her death.

ROMANCE ONLY - If you've Romanced Miranda, you'll have a third check. Breaking up with Miranda during Mass Effect 3 results in her death, irrespective of if you met the first two requirements. Breaking up with Miranda in Mass Effect 2 doesn't kill her, however.

If you passed all the applicable conditions, Miranda will live through the confrontation, as indicated by her being able to walk and talk normally. If not, Miranda will collapse to the floor after you deal with Henry and she'll succumb to her wounds.

Here's what you can do across the Normandy now that you're done:

CIC - Talk with Traynor, Joker and EDI (for the Decoy Bonus Power and +2 Reputation ).

Crew Deck - Talk with your Virmire Survivor, Tali (in the bar lounge for +2 Reputation ), Liara and Garrus.

Engineering - Visit Javik for a very important scene ( Dark Channel Bonus Power and +2 Reputation ). Here he'll ask if it's worth looking into the Echo Shard: for the most positive outcome to his character arc, pick "No, I wouldn't". Also talk with Allers.

Shuttle Bay - Talk with James for some comments from him about Horizon.

Finally, if you did " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ", encountered a Rachni Breeder (NOT the Rachni Queen from Noveria) and decided to spare her, then it's at this point that she and her offspring turn on the Alliance, taking out 100 TMS from the Alliance Engineering Corps.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

Up Next: Priority: Cerberus Headquarters

articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Cerberus Headquarters Mission on Cronos Station, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Priority: Cerberus Headquarters sets the endgame events in motion, and marks the point of no return for the game. Heed the warnings below before you get started!

All Side Missions close after starting " Priority: Cerberus Headquarters ". If your Effective Military Strength is 4,000 (3,100 with Extended Cut DLC) or higher, you will have gotten the Master and Commander Achievement / Trophy, and thus are eligible for the "best" ending.

You'll otherwise want to make sure you've done absolutely everything you want to do before this point, including...

Side Missions - These will award credits, XP, War Assets, and in a few cases character reunions that are required for them to appear in the Citadel DLC.

DLC - All of the DLC offer XP, credits, weapons and mods to help you in the final fight. Leviathan DLC - This DLC introduces some story threads that foreshadow revelations made in the next two Missions, and thus we highly suggest completing it if you have it. Citadel DLC - This DLC can be seen as "an epilogue before the ending", and includes a great many character moments and conclusions not available in the base game. It also has the Armax Arsenal Arena that allows you to grind for credits to buy weapons and their upgrades.

Leviathan DLC - This DLC introduces some story threads that foreshadow revelations made in the next two Missions, and thus we highly suggest completing it if you have it.

Citadel DLC - This DLC can be seen as "an epilogue before the ending", and includes a great many character moments and conclusions not available in the base game. It also has the Armax Arsenal Arena that allows you to grind for credits to buy weapons and their upgrades.

Shopping and Store Guide - This page lists every store and their complete stock throughout the game. Use this to help figure out what you want to buy!

Search and Rescue - This link takes you to a checklist of every Search and Rescue item in the galaxy, including the Leviathan DLC. These will give you credits and War Assets. Remember that you can refuel for free by simply landing on the Citadel!

Unlike the first game, you will be taken back to this point in the game after you've rolled credits, however you will lose anything you picked up after this point.

Due to a conversation that occurs just before the end of " Priority: Earth ", we highly recommend that you have a 100% full Reputation Bar (or are on the verge of it) before starting this Mission. Side Missions and DLC are the ways you can increase it at this point in the game.

Armor : Serrice Council Greaves Delumcore Overlay

War Asset: (note that these are mutually exclusive, based on how you handled the Collector Base at the end of Mass Effect 2) Reaper Brain (100 TMS) Reaper Heart (100 TMS)

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Horizon "

Location: Horsehead Nebula - Anadius - Cronos Station

After " Priority: Horizon ", head to Anadius in the Horsehead Nebula . You'll need about 300 Fuel to get there. Dock with Cronos Station to start the mission: it'll be the only place you can visit in this system. When you dock with it, you'll be taken to the Vid Comm with Admiral Hackett to confirm you want to begin: he'll make it absolutely clear that this will kickstart the final assault.

If you want some very easily-missed dialogue, pick "Let's wait" to Admiral Hackett. Traynor will then say Hackett is available on Vid-Comm, which lets you start a one-on-one conversation with him. Here you can ask "Cerberus" and then "And if the Illusive Man is right?", "Galactic readiness", "Allied forces" and "Reaper progress".

When you're ready to go, dock with Cronos Station with "We go now!" to begin the end of the game. If you have Locked In a Serious Romance, you'll have a scene with them in the Captain's Cabin, which will be interjected with the final dream sequence where Shepard sees themselves burning with the child. After this, Shepard will wake up, and as they plan the attack in the War Room, EDI offers to come along given her familiarity with Ceberus protocols, something which Joker is quite concerned with.

Squad Tactics: EDI is a mandatory Squad Mate, and her Overload is helpful for taking down the Shields of this level's boss. Bringing Garrus for his Overload is helpful. If you Ashley is available, her Disruptor Ammo is also quite useful.

EDI is a mandatory Squad Mate, and her Overload is helpful for taking down the Shields of this level's boss.

Bringing Garrus for his Overload is helpful.

If you Ashley is available, her Disruptor Ammo is also quite useful.

Unique Dialogue: If your love interest is a Squad Mate, you will get unique dialogue if you bring them with you. If nobody applies, Liara is a good choice.

If your love interest is a Squad Mate, you will get unique dialogue if you bring them with you.

If nobody applies, Liara is a good choice.

Shepard's Loadout: A Sniper Rifle is helpful for taking down Cerberus troops from a distance in this large space station. Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods will be rather appreciated to deal with this level's Guardians. If you have the Omega / Citadel DLCs , a Thermal Scope for your sniper / assault rifle is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs.

A Sniper Rifle is helpful for taking down Cerberus troops from a distance in this large space station.

Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods will be rather appreciated to deal with this level's Guardians.

If you have the Omega / Citadel DLCs , a Thermal Scope for your sniper / assault rifle is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs.

After a dramatic entry through the fleet bombardment and into a hangar bay, you start the Mission ducked behind the Kodiak shuttle for cover. On the other side of the shuttle is a hangar full of Cerberus troops shooting at you. Centurions and Assault Troopers will flank you relatively quickly, so start thinning out their ranks before they can get to you.

Once you get to the other side of the shuttle, there are more troops and an Atlas Mech , both of which enter the hangar on your left. Be sure to look up -- there is a Nemesis sniping at you from the second level. Both the Atlas and the Nemesis are on the left side of the docking bay, so take cover accordingly. It's easiest to thin out the troops from cover, then take out the Atlas, and save the Nemesis for last. If you can get past those forces though, there are not 1, but 2 empty Atlas Mech's waiting for you on polar ends, just right and left of the fighter platform sitting back.

As soon as you take out the last enemy, you'll hear an announcement about a security breach (that's you!) and that the Achilles Protocol is being initiated. EDI translates for you: they're going to vent the hangar. Even though there's no timer, if you don't get EDI to an active console to stop the venting, you'll be sucked out into space and fail the mission. Quickly climb up the ladder on the left side of the hangar up to where the Nemesis was, then go through the door on your right and activate the hangar bay compression controls at the window. This stops the timer and prevents a Critical Mission Failure.

After the short cutscene, reinforcements will appear on your left. Take them out, then continue down the hallway and cross over to the other side of the hangar on the second level. Halfway across you'll be greeted by the remainder of the welcome party: Assault Troopers, Centurions, and another Nemesis. Once you're clear, continue to the far end of the catwalk and open the door. In the small room, activate the Rotation Controls to aim the Cerberus fighter inward towards the hangar doors (use the View Prompt to see it in action!).

Medical Station - 75 XP. Across from the Rotation Controls is a doorway into a small, dark room. Check inside this room to find the Medical Station on the wall.

PDA - 5,000 credits. Head for the balcony-like room with the ladder, but instead of using it, head through the next door to find this PDA on some crates, next to a red ammo box.

Head back into the previous room and go down the ladder to return to the ground floor of the hangar. If you need some ammo, you should be able to find some around the hangar.

When you're ready to move on, activate the Clamp Release half way between the ladder on the right of the hangar and the fighter on the rotating platform.

As you can see in the cut scene, an Atlas Mech appears from the gaping hole left by the fighter, accompanied by a few Assault Troopers. Take out the troops before they can get to an unoccupied Atlas Mechs sides of the hangar, then take out the piloted Atlas. If you can, rush to the empty Atlas in the back-right corner: you can hop in and wreak some havoc yourself! Once you're clear, do one more pass for ammo, then head through the hangar doors -- or at least, what's left of them.

M-37 Falcon - On the floor in the rubble just left of the fiery hole in the wall. Pick this up now: if you don't, you can only get it from the Requisitions Terminal in the Normandy's Cargo Bay, where it'll have a 10% markup.

Take the door on the left of the fiery hole -- you can open it even though its panel is orange. When the cutscene is over, take the ladder down to the sublevel as EDI suggests, then take cover immediately. A few Assault Troopers and a Centurion begin attacking, and once you get past them, a Nemesis awaits further down. Once the area is clear, be sure to grab the Med Kit just beyond the ladder before you head up.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Instead of taking the ladder up, head past it to the end of the dead end. On the back wall will be the Medical Station

Terminal - 5,000 credits. To the left of the Medical Station described above.

Back on the main level, EDI will direct Shepard to a Cerberus Video Log terminal to learn more about the Lazarus Project, which is the main reason we recommended that you bring a Love Interest Squad Mate with you. They'll offer moral support for Shepard.

Serrice Council Greaves - After finishing up at the terminal, turn around to spot this armor piece on some crates.

Now head through the door EDI opened up, down the hall and drop down through the opening on your right. Vault over some rubble, then head down the ramp on your right. Down here you encounter the Cerberus Combat Engineers (and their annoying turrets) that EDI warned you about earlier. Everyone is also protected shield generators and pylons, so take those out if you can to make your fight easier.

Note that Sabotage comes in extremely handy here, since you can hack a turret to take out all the enemies around it. Stay far back from groups of enemies so as not to get flanked, and keep an eye out for the Engineers with large, flat packs on their backs so you can kill them first.

Once all the enemies are down, go up the ladder to the upper floor. EDI will need to hack through two doors this time, so as she does so, explore the two rooms you have access to for some goodies:

Cerberus Video Log - To the far left of the exit door with the orange panel on it. This one details the creation of EDI, as well as her follow-up, Eva Coré, who you encountered back in " Priority: Mars ".

Cerberus Audio Log - On the opposite side of the room from the Cerberus Video Log will be an operating table covered in blood with a PDA on it. If Jack survived Mass Effect 2 but you didn't do the " Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation " Side Mission, this PDA will have some very disturbing logs on it.

PDA - 5,000 credits. Enter the next room and check a table on the right-hand side for this PDA.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Found on the left-hand wall among some terminals.

Exit the room via the door EDI is tending to: after Shepard says it's okay for Hackett's fleet to fire upon the station, it'll be opened up. Head through it and and then turn right.

Go past the blue doorway and instead go through the green panel door on your right, next to a smashed window. You'll find some loot in here:

Med Kit - 50 XP. As you go around the left-hand side of the room, you'll find this Med Kit at the bottom of the wall.

Delumcore Overlay - This Body Armor piece is just past the Med Kit on your right, just before the next green panel door. This is the final piece of armor in the game!

Cerberus Video Log - Head through the door to find this video log, which will detail Kai Leng's meetings with the Illusive Man throughout the game.

Once you're all done, return to the blue doorway and go through it to enter the next area.

This room features the remnants of the Reaper-Human from the Collector Base at the end of the previous game . What's actually left in the room depends on a decision you made in Mass Effect 2 (or the Genesis 2 DLC comic if you used that instead):

If you destroyed the Collector Base, or you started a new game in Mass Effect 3, the Human Reaper Heart will appear in this room.

If you spared the Collector Base, the Human Reaper Brain will appear here.

Head forward down the catwalk to trigger the next fight. A Phantom appears close to you while reinforcements arrive further down the catwalk. The reinforcements consist of Assault Troopers, more Phantoms, and a Nemesis. Run forward and take down the first Phantom quickly, then get into cover before the Nemesis starts sniping you. When you're clear, proceed down the catwalk and up the ladder.

Two easter egg enemies may also appear at this point:

If you didn't do " Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation ", Jack will appear as a Phantom enemy.

If you sold Legion to Cerberus in Mass Effect 2 for 50,000 credits, you'll have to face them here as well.

On the next level, pick up some ammo, then continue your climb. Different level, same group of enemies. Do your thing, then climb up one last time to the end of the catwalk portion.

PDA - 5,000 credits. Before heading through the door, turn around and go to the far end of the catwalk to find this PDA on the floor.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Right next to the PDA described above.

Go back to the door and head through it. As you pass through, there are yet more goodies to find:

PDA - 5,000 credits. On the left-hand side of this walkway, next to a red ammo box.

Cerberus Video Log - Next to the PDA and Med Kit described above. This video log details the Illusive Man's use of Reaper implants in his troops thanks to the effects on Paul Grayson from the Mass Effect Books , and eventually put into himself.

Go through the door on the far side of the room, then up the ramp and through the door at the top.

In the cutscene in this room you'll enter another important conversation with the Illusive Man, just like on Mars and Thessia , As with those instances, your choices here are crucial to a scene later on in the game. Pick "So what is it?" when it shows up, then pick either...

"It's not too late to help me" Charm for +5 Paragon Points .

"You're in this for yourself" Intimidate for +5 Renegade Points .

You MUST pick the same Morality option as you did on Mars and Thessia.

Regardless of taking the above advice (which you really should), answer...

"You'll never change" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I can't help you anymore" for +2 Renegade Points .

The following conversation will be with the Prothean VI you found on Thessia, and you'll discover that the Catalyst is in fact the Citadel! Here, you can say...

"Why all the secrecy?" for +2 Paragon Points .

"It's a bit late" for +2 Renegade Points (this will change to "This is critical information" if you use the Investigate option on the left).

Unfortunately, Shepard's attempt to contact Hackett will be interrupted by the return of Kai Leng for one final dance.

The Kai Leng fight is broken up into several waves. At the very start of the first wave, Leng will grapple with you, and you'll need to mash the MELEE ATTACK button rapidly to throw him off. Immediately have EDI and anyone else with Overload use it on Leng. Hit him a few more times and his Shields will lock and you can do no more damage. He'll kneel down and summon Troopers. It may seem like you should enter the pit area opposite the Troopers, but if you keep moving around the perimeter of the room you have a better angle to take them out (the high ground and all that).

Use EDI's decoy and send your Squad to opposite sides of the room to spread out the enemy fire. In this wave, you can reduce Leng's Shields to one bar. Keep using Overload and hit him with Disruptor Ammo whenever you can. The Sniper Rifle Concentration Mod is a great asset here since you can slow time and nail him. You can also use melee attacks if your character is built for it. Leng's deadliest attack is a wave of energy that completely drops your shields. You can dodge this or take cover from it, but if you get hit, get ready to use a Med Kit.

When Leng goes down on one knee again he'll barely recover, but more Troopers will arrive. It's this third wave of enemies that's a problem: Phantoms are tough to deal with in the trenches, so be sure to head for the sides of the room. They are close-range enemies, so give them some distance between you and your squad. Hopefully you can continue to nail Leng from the sidelines: once his shield is gone, use your weapons to whittle away his health bar. One solid shot to the head from a Sniper Rifle can do wonders.

Finally, Leng will fall. In the next cutscene, you'll get a Renegade Interrupt as Leng attempts to kill Shepard. Take it, and Shepard will break Leng's sword, while ignoring it will have Shepard simply dodge it. They'll stab Leng with their Omni-Blade either way, and you don't get Renegade Points for taking it, so even Paragons can go for this one!

Once you've defeated Kai Leng, you'll have one final exchange with the Prothean VI. When he says it's too late, you have two options for how to conclude it:

You can pull the Renegade Interrupt for +5 Renegade Points .

If you sit through the Renegade Interrupt, you can use a Paragon Interrupt for +5 Paragon Points instead.

You'll reconvene with Anderson at the Vid Comm to let him know why the Citadel has suddenly appeared over Earth, before you can do one more tour of the Normandy.

Completing this Mission will have given you your final War Asset, a piece of the Reaper-Human. The piece varies depending on your choice at the end of Mass Effect 2: either the Reaper Heart or the Reaper Brain. This is your final War Asset, meaning that you Effective Military Strength is now locked-in.

Since the Citadel is now over Earth in the heart of Reaper territory, you can only buy stuff via the Procurement Terminal in the Normandy's Cargo Bay. This also the last time you can use the Weapon Upgrade terminal to upgrade any weapons.

CIC - Talk with Traynor, Joker, and EDI a few times. Joker's in particular visually references their first conversation at the start of Mass Effect 1 .

Crew Deck - Talk with your Virmire Survivor, Liara, Garrus ( +2 Reputation ), and your doctor. If you didn't Romance either Garrus or Tali, Tali will be with Garrus in the Main Battery.

Engineering - Talk with Javik, Gabby, Ken, Adams, Tali (if you didn't Romance her or Garrus), and Allers.

After talking with Allers, check your Private Terminal for the last email in the game.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

War Assets: Ex-Cerberus Scientists (25 TMS) Dr. Brynn Cole (25 TMS) Tap to Reveal (25 TMS) Tap to Reveal (25 TMS)

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: The Citadel 2 "

This Side Mission does not become available until after you complete " Priority: The Citadel 2 ". After it, return to the CIC, and Specialist Traynor will once again flag Shepard over for something important. It seems Cerberus' top scientists have cut ties, and Traynor has figured out where they might be hiding.

Location: Minos Wasteland - Arrae - Gellix

To start this Side Mission, head for the Minos Wasteland near the "western" border of the Milky Way, then travel west to the Arrae system. Land on the planet Gellix (marked in green) to begin the Side Mission.

While you're in Fortis, the Relay system, you may want to pick up these Search and Rescue items:

Squad Tactics: Garrus is a good choice for this Mission because of his Overload and Proximity Mine abilities, and his sniper rifle is great for his level's long sight lines. James is another solid pick for his Incendiary Ammo and Frag Grenade powers. If you save this Side Mission until after " Priority: Rannoch ", Tali is a great choice because she can Sabotage the Generators and Shield Pylons in this level, and her Energy Drain is useful for setting up Tech Bursts.

Garrus is a good choice for this Mission because of his Overload and Proximity Mine abilities, and his sniper rifle is great for his level's long sight lines.

James is another solid pick for his Incendiary Ammo and Frag Grenade powers.

If you save this Side Mission until after " Priority: Rannoch ", Tali is a great choice because she can Sabotage the Generators and Shield Pylons in this level, and her Energy Drain is useful for setting up Tech Bursts.

Unique Dialogue: Garrus and EDI provide the most unique dialogue for this level.

Garrus and EDI provide the most unique dialogue for this level.

Shepard's Loadout: Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will help deal with this level's Guardians. The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs. If you have the Citadel DLC and / or completed the Omega DLC , a Thermal Scope for your assault / sniper rifle helps see through both their smoke bombs and through walls!

Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will help deal with this level's Guardians.

The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs.

If you have the Citadel DLC and / or completed the Omega DLC , a Thermal Scope for your assault / sniper rifle helps see through both their smoke bombs and through walls!

A bullet exchange is already taking place between the survivors (including a very familiar face, if he survived the end of the second game) and Cerberus troops. A pair of Shield Pylons will fortify the enemy personnel with a shield, so take that out when you can. A lot of troops will drop down from above and soften their landing with jet boots, which leaves them wide, WIDE open to gunfire.

After the Cerberus foes are down, locate the man featured in the earlier cutscene behind the crate cover, and Shepard will grab a nearby communicator to Dr. Brynn Cole. There's two ways this can play out:

If Jacob Taylor survived Mass Effect 2, he'll be present in this scene and vouch for Shepard, prompting Dr. Brynn to open the door inside.

If Jacob died at the end of Mass Effect 2, you'll have Dr. Webber, who is too hurt to say anything. Dr. Brynn won't trust Shepard, allowing three more Cerberus troops to show up. After you gun them down, Brynn will be convinced and opens the door.

You'll now chat with Dr. Brynn Cole face-to-face, and if Jacob's present, he'll insist he's okay (although he clearly needs some patching up at the very least). Here you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "Running was smart" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Running took guts" for +2 Renegade Points .

After a comment from EDI, you can now explore the base. First, turn right to spot a Dr. Brown on the floor conversing with a fellow refugee. When they're done, talk to Dr. Brown for +2 Reputation .

Now head up the nearby stairs to find a door forwards. Working on a terminal to the right of the door is Dr. Gavin Archer. If you completed the Overlord DLC in Mass Effect 2, Shepard will NOT be happy to see him again. Notably, it's possible for Gavin to tragically die at the conclusion of this cutscene if you make certain choices:

Dr. Gavin Archer will take his own life in any of the following situations: You did not complete " Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation " before " Priority: The Citadel 2 ", causing it to expire. You DID complete " Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation ", but refuse to tell Gavin the fate of his brother by choosing "[Let him worry]". You didn't send David to Grissom Academy at the end of the Overlord DLC (or never did the Overlord DLC at all), then negotiated a peaceful resolution to " Tap to Reveal " before starting this Side Mission.

You did not complete " Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation " before " Priority: The Citadel 2 ", causing it to expire.

You DID complete " Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation ", but refuse to tell Gavin the fate of his brother by choosing "[Let him worry]".

You didn't send David to Grissom Academy at the end of the Overlord DLC (or never did the Overlord DLC at all), then negotiated a peaceful resolution to " Tap to Reveal " before starting this Side Mission.

Any other situation will result in Dr. Gavin Archer living.

If you completed the Overlord DLC and Gavin lives through this cutscene, he'll become a War Asset worth 25 TMS.

Once the cutscene has finished, you can begin scouring the base for goodies:

Datapad - 2,500 credits. On a table just past Gavin's terminal.

Datapad - On a table past the above datapad. Provides lore.

Assault Rifle Magazine Upgrade - Head through the door next to Gavin's terminal, then check to the right of the Weapon Bench up ahead to find this mod.

Medical Station - 25 XP. Head up the next flight of stairs and go through the door. Here, look for this Medical Station on the right-hand side of the next set of stairs.

When you get to the top of the stairs you'll meet back up with Brynn, and Shepard learns that not only are the ex-Cerberus scientists here, but their families as well. Cerberus is vengeful . Here, you can say...

"There's a lot on the line" for +2 Paragon Points .

"We can't let that distract us" for +2 Renegade Points .

After another chat with Jacob (again, assuming he's alive and present), your next task is to get up onto the roof. But first, it's time for loot and conversations (no better time than now, right?). First, talk to Brynn nearby to pick her brain on the available topics, then head off for goodies.

Datapad - 2,500 credits. On a science station to the left of Dr. Brynn.

Datapad - To the left of the Datapad described above. Provides some lore.

From the second Datapad described above, follow the wall left to find a doorway into a "Recovery-2" room, where the rest of the goodies can be found:

Kassa Fabrication Greaves - Standing in the doorway to "Recovery-2", look right to spot this in the corner of the room, atop some crates.

Medical Station - 75 XP. To the left of the doorway into "Recovery-2".

Datapad - 1,250 credits. On a table in the middle-left of the room (close to Jacob, if he's present).

Datapad - On a bed in the back-left corner of the room. Provides some lore.

You can now talk to Jacob if he's present, allowing you to catch up on what he's been up to since Mass Effect 2. After asking any "Investigate" topic, picking "Tell me about Dr. Cole" will lead you to some interesting revelations... especially if you Romanced Jacob in Mass Effect 2.

Now exit out of the "Recovery-2" room to get the last pieces of loot:

Datapad - Directly ahead on some crates at the top of the stairs. Provides some lore.

Turian Toxin Data - From the Datapad described above, head for the back-right corner of the room to find a microscope among some crates. Examine the microscope to pick up the Quest Item for " Citadel: Cerberus Turian Poison "!

Shotgun High Caliber Barrel - Return to the doorway into "Recovery-2" and face the stairs. Turn right to spot the door out, but before going through, check behind the crates to the left of the door to spot this weapon mod.

Once you're sure you've done everything here, exit out the door where the Shotgun mod was, then turn right and climb up the ladder to go through a loading screen. At the top, check the pipes on the left-hand wall to spot a Heavy Pistol, the M-6 Carnifex .

Cerberus have already occupied the roof when you arrive, but the first group don't realize you're there yet. Take them by surprise, being sure to take out the Shield Pylon first, as it reinforces the defenses of anyone nearby. After that, kill the Combat Engineer before he can plant a Turret and make your life even more miserable.

Head up the ramp at the back and then veer right to spot a lone Combat Engineer at the Telemetry Override: kill him, then kill all the Cerberus Troops who drop down from above (again, that leaves them incredibly exposed). Once they're down, the roof will be quiet for now, letting you grab some more loot:

SMG High Caliber Barrel - At the entrance to the side-area with the Telemetry Override will be a pile of crates on the side. Check behind these crates to find this mod.

Datapad - 2,500 credits. On the ground to the right of the telemetry controls.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Tucked in the shadows behind the Datapad described above.

We'll now sweep the rest of the rooftop for loot (it's easier to do this with no enemies shooting at you):

Med Kit - 50 XP. Face away from the Telemetry Override and climb up to the back level of the roof. Here you'll find a Med Kit on your left on top of some ducting.

Sniper Rifle Piercing Mod - On the rooftop with the Med Kit described above, head to the railing at the very back of the roof. Once there, turn right to spot this mod among the large cube container.

Datapad - 3,750 credits. From the Piercing Mod described above, climb up the ladders on the left-hand side of the roof to get to their highest point. At the top, head left and go forward until you mantle up a ledge. This Datapad will be directly ahead on top of some ducting, near the AA Guns.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Under the ducting where the Datapad described above was.

Shotgun Spare Ammo - From the Datapad and Med Kit described above, locate the nearby ladder and slide down it. Before you slide down the second ladder, check this small area for this mod. This is the last item!

Okay, now that you have all the loot in the level, return to the Telemetry Override and Activate it to continue the Side Mission. The next step is to reactivate the anti-aircraft guns manually. They're far across the way, and your advancement there will be punctuated by a myriad of enemies, including one on the mounted turret in the distance.

Take cover from the turret fire and inch toward it: your target is the left-hand structure, which has a pair of ladders that take you up to the AA Guns. Once you get to the shaded area at the back of the rooftop, you'll be safe.

When you reach the AA gun controls, assign any squadmate to conduct the repairs. Ideally the one you leave behind should be powerful and good with sniper rifles, so if you have Garrus, make sure he ISN'T the one to repair the AA Gun!

While the other squadmate is tied down, mount the turret and rain hell on the Cerberus enemies coming in from dropships. They should pose little problems for you if your aim is true on the turret, but make sure you take out any Phantoms, especially those dropped off on the same high rooftop as you're on.

After the repairs are done, you'll return to Dr. Brynn (and Jacob if present) back inside the base. If you missed anything in this upper floor of the base, you should pick "Not yet" to go grab them (with no effect on this mission's outcome), otherwise pick "Evacuate immediately" to initiate the final part of the Mission.

Things don't go smoothly, however, as Cerberus troops start to flood into the facility. You'll now need to fight your way out of the base to get all the way back to the landing bay where Cortez first dropped you off. Fend off the troops and defend the departing shuttles.

This is your LAST CHANCE to pick up the Turian Toxin Data ! If you miss it, you'll have to buy a similar item from Spectre Requisitions on the Citadel to complete " Citadel: Cerberus Turian Poison "!

The combat will get pretty heated back outside, so make sure to take out the Generators first so that the Shield Pylons no longer work! Annoyingly the shuttles now drop their troops off at elevated positions, so you can't just shoot them out like normal. And just when you think it's over, an Atlas Mech drops by, backed up by a Combat Engineer who repairs the mech sets up Turrets. Hunker down and keep behind cover!

After eliminating all the enemies on-site, you'll be automatically scooped up by Brynn. If Jacob is present, you'll have a chance for some Morality Points:

Pick "I understand" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I'm disappointed" for +2 Renegade Points .

After a debriefing with Admiral Hackett, you can do another round of the Normandy:

CIC - Chat with Traynor, Joker and EDI. Also make sure to check your email: you'll have requests from your Virmire Survivor, Miranda, Joker, Garrus, Liara and Javik.

Crew Deck - Listen to James and Garrus in the mess hall (you'll have to walk back and forth to hear all three parts before talking to Garrus), then pop by Liara and her Broker Terminal. You can also talk to your Virmire Survivor: Ashley is in the Port Observatory, while Kaidan is in the Crew Quarters ( +2 Reputation for Kaidan only).

Engineering - Chat with Javik and Allers.

Shuttle Bay - Talk to Cortez for a very small comment.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:
