articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastery Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

War Assets: Asari Commandos (20 TMS) Tap to Reveal (25 TMS)

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: The Citadel 2 "

Location: Nimbus Cluster - Mesana - Lesuss

This Side Mission is one that's unlocked automatically through the story. After you complete " Priority: The Citadel 2 ", you'll be pulled aside by Liara in the War Room: Asari High Command wanted her to pass along news that multiple asari commando squads have disappeared investigating a distress signal in Mesana. Liara thinks they're implying Shepard should do so themselves to find out more (a repetition of their task, as Kirrahe would say).

Mesana is the "northwestern" system in the Nimbus Cluster, with Lesuss being the first planet orbiting the star. While you're in the Nimbus Cluster, though, you may want to scoop up the following Search and Rescue finds:

Squad Tactics: Liara is an excellent choice for this level, as her Warp power will help with stripping Barriers from a new enemy type in this level. She also unlocks a handful of Morality Points too! James pairs very well with Liara thanks to his Carnage and Incendiary Ammo working great to set up fire explosion combos that Liara's Warp will detonate. Garrus is an interesting choice because of his sniper proficiency, taking advantage of this level's wide open spaces.

Liara is an excellent choice for this level, as her Warp power will help with stripping Barriers from a new enemy type in this level. She also unlocks a handful of Morality Points too!

James pairs very well with Liara thanks to his Carnage and Incendiary Ammo working great to set up fire explosion combos that Liara's Warp will detonate.

Garrus is an interesting choice because of his sniper proficiency, taking advantage of this level's wide open spaces.

Unique Dialogue: Liara and Garrus give the most unique dialogue. If you don't have Garrus, your replacement should be (in order of availability) Javik -> Virmire Survivor -> EDI.

Liara and Garrus give the most unique dialogue.

If you don't have Garrus, your replacement should be (in order of availability) Javik -> Virmire Survivor -> EDI.

Shepard's Loadout: If you don't mind re-specing Shepard in the Med Bay, Warp Ammo is a very handy Bonus Power for its ability to strip biotic Barriers.

If you don't mind re-specing Shepard in the Med Bay, Warp Ammo is a very handy Bonus Power for its ability to strip biotic Barriers.

You start out with a briefing in the Kodiak shuttle on the way there, and you discover why Asari High Command was so vague: this is an Ardat-Yakshi Monastery (roll credits!), where those with the condition live their lives in solitude. Here, you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "Bombs are a last resort" / "We don't know that" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Then neither do we" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then be dropped off on the Monastery's landing platform.

Shuttle - If you played Mass Effect 2 or the Genesis 2 DLC comic , there's a good chance a red shuttle will be visible on your right. It's still warm, meaning someone's arrived just recently...

Assault Rifle Stability Damper - To the left of the entry door, on top of some crates.

Head inside to find that the monastery had gone dark (in the most literal sense as well) for a reason. Climb your way down the elevator shaft to arrive in the darkened mess hall. With only your flashlight to see, scour this first area for a number of useful items and intel:, including an asari corpse that points the team toward the Great Hall.

Pistol Melee Stunner - From the elevator shaft exit, head all the way to the left to find a doorway into a messy room. This mod is on the floor in the doorway.

Gallae's Electronic Signature - In the back of the room with the Pistol Melee Stunner will be a laptop. Examine it to get some very good Intel!

PDA - 20 XP. From the messy room described above, exit it and check the left-hand side of the room for some tables lined with many chairs. On the corner of a table will be this PDA with an audio recording.

Console - A tall terminal in the middle of the room, close to the PDA.

Wall Safe - 7,500 credits. Return to the elevator exit directly across from the PDA described above, then turn left to find the entrance to another bunk room in the corner of the mess hall. The Wall Safe will be visible on the back wall.

Sniper Rifle Spare Ammo - Lying on a shelf to the right of the Wall Safe described above.

Computer - On a bedside table in the left side of the room with the Wall Safe. Provides some lore.

With everything collected, exit the bedroom with the Wall Safe and head directly forward to find an Asari Corpse... and a Cannibal's corpse. Examine the Asari Corpse to initiate a cutscene, where you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "It seems drastic" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I can't blame them" for +2 Renegade Points .

With the cutscene over, head through the nearby doorway, vault over the planter on the left, then go through the door. In the large window area, head right and Bypass the door at the far end to continue.

Now, if Samara survived the events of Mass Effect 2, she'll be present throughout the level, including now in an exclusive cutscene! If your game has been an imported Mass Effect 2 profile, you can get some Morality Points too:

Pick "We'll help search" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I'm blowing this place up" for +2 Renegade Points .

Whether or not you had the cutscene, make sure to check this upper balcony for a quest item:

PDA - 20 XP. After leaving the darkened mess hall and exiting onto a balcony, turn right to find the body of an Asari Commando. Next to her is a Datapad: inspect it to begin the " Citadel: Asari Widow " Side Mission.

Now exit out the door on the left-hand side of the balcony to arrive in an outdoor plaza area. Ready your weapons: this is a battle arena, a wide, expansive space with plenty of cover... and you're about to face one of the most formidible enemies the Reapers have to bear: Banshees .

These powerful foes are highly resistant to bullets and teleport all over, unleashing their own biotic powers upon their opponents.

Dispel the Barrier with Liara's Warp power, then whittle down the Banshee's Armor using any fire-based powers as quickly as possible.

Keep a safe distance from the Banshee to avoid getting caught by their sync kill move, which can insta-kill Shepard in almost any situation.

If you played Mass Effect 2 then you'll find the Banshees to be somewhat similar to Harbinger-possessed Collectors. Their biotic attacks are certainly similar: they'll knock you out of cover if they hit you, so make sure to duck back down to stay protected!

Soon after the destruction of the Banshee, Cannibals make their appearance from the door up ahead. Compared to the Banshee, these enemies will crumple after a few bullets.

Bypass the door and continue on to find an asari survivor: Falare, who will be saved by Shepard, or Samara if she's present (someone whose name starts with S either way). She'll reveal that her sister Rila has been taken to the Great Hall: you can get a few Morality Points here, although the wording depends on if Samara is present or not:

Pick "We won't" / "We can try" / "We'll help find her" for +2 Paragon Points . Strangely, if Samara is present and you pick "The Ardat-Yakshi are innocent?", then the "I believe you" option does NOT give Paragon Points.

Strangely, if Samara is present and you pick "The Ardat-Yakshi are innocent?", then the "I believe you" option does NOT give Paragon Points.

Pick "It's not a rescue mission" / "I don't have time" / "It's not a rescue mission" for +2 Renegade Points .

Whichever you choose, Falere will run off after you reveal the existence of the bomb and your plan to detonate it, followed by Samara if she's present.

Damaged Elevator - After the scene with Falere, head left to the far end of the balcony to find this door riddled with bullet holes.

Computer - 20 XP. Now head to the exact opposite end of the balcony (past the exit door) to find this laptop sitting on a coffee table with an audio log on it.

Chase after Falere using the traditional method of opening doors (specifically the exit door to the right of where the cutscene with her took place). Just on the other side of the door are a pair of Cannibals, backed up by a Marauder and another pair of Cannibals in a side-room to the right with a Barrier Engine inside. Gun them down, then duck into the side-room:

Serrice Council Shoulder Guard - Found in one the side room, on a table under the Barrier Engine up on the wall.

Disciple - On the ground of the side-room, very close to the Serrice Council Shoulder Guard described above.

Medical Station - 75 XP. On the far wall in the side room with the Barrier Engine inside.

Exit out of the room and continue anti-clockwise around the upper area. Ignore the stairs going down on the left and instead look for a doorway just past them for another side-room:

Computer x2 - 50 XP. Found in the small side-room just past the stairs down to the lower level.

Wall Safe - 5,000 credits. Found in the same side-room as the pair of Computers described above. There's also a Weapon Bench to the right of it.

Now descend down to the lower floor, and meet up with another Banshee and its retinue of more Cannibals (who attack during your Banshee fight now rather than waiting politely). There's a lot more this time too, and they emerge from protected areas in the back and sides of the room, so stay vigilant!

Once they're down, Bypass the door after the battle to enter another dimly lit area, to where Falere descended earlier. There's two things to find here: In the very center of the room, you'll find the remains of an asari commando.

Asari Corpse - In the middle of the room, slumped against a bomb and some crates.

Assault Rifle Precision Scope - From the Asari Corpse, head left to go up some steps and under the upper balcony. This will be on the ground on your left.

Proceed through the open door into the elevator and Activate it to reach the Great Hall. The bomb is intact, and both Ardat-Yakshi sisters appear to be as well. Before talking with them, you may want to locate / acquire the following before the fighting begins:

Medical Station - 75 XP. On the left-hand column when you enter the Great Hall.

Medical Station - 75 XP. On the right-hand column when you enter the Great Hall.

Med Kit - 50 XP. At the base of the stairs leading up to Falare, next to two dead Asari.

If you're playing the Wii U Special Edition, you'll find an M-597 Ladon on top of the bomb at the back of this room, on the right-hand side of the large window. Make sure to grab it BEFORE Examining the Bomb to start the next cutscene!

Examine the Bomb where Falere and Rila are to initiate the finale of the Mission.

When you attempt to activate the bomb, a pair of Banshees and an accompanying group of Husks crash the party. Take out the pesky Husks first. The pair of Banshees poses a huge threat to the squad, but be sure to focus fire on one at a time. Luckily, there are a couple of Medical Stations around the room that you can use to keep the squad and yourself healthy (assuming you didn't grab them earlier). Run laps around the big room if you need to keep your distance from the deadly enemies.

If you're on Wii U and grabbed the Ladon, now's the time to use it! However even on Narrative difficulty, the Ladon rarely kills both the Banshees and all the Husks at once, so instead use the TouchPad to make sure only the Banshees (marked with red diamonds on the map) are selected.

Once they're all down, return to Falere and Rila to find the detonator. As revealed in the cutscene, it turns out Rila had it... and like a true Asari Commando, she stays behind in order to ensure that both the monastery and all the Banshees inside it are destroyed.

When you return to the landing pad, you'll now have to decide how to handle Falere, the last Ardat-Yakshi in the monastery. How this plays out, and what Morality Points you can get, depends on if Samara is present or not.

Falere will tearfully ask why Shepard didn't try to bring Rila along and help her: Pick "She chose to save you" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "She was beyond help" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "She chose to save you" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "She was beyond help" for +2 Renegade Points .

Samara realizes that the Justicar Code demands she kill any Ardat-Yakshi not living in a monastery. Unwilling to kill her only remaining daughter, she turns her gun to her head: Pull the Paragon Interrupt to prevent her from taking her own life for +15 Paragon Points (allowing her to become a War Asset worth 25 TMS). After accepting Falere's loophole, Samara then promises to visit: Pick "You could stay, Samara" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "It's time to fight, Samara" for +2 Renegade Points . If you ignore the Paragon Interrupt, Samara takes her own life, leaving the fate of Falere in Shepard's hands.

Pull the Paragon Interrupt to prevent her from taking her own life for +15 Paragon Points (allowing her to become a War Asset worth 25 TMS). After accepting Falere's loophole, Samara then promises to visit: Pick "You could stay, Samara" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "It's time to fight, Samara" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "You could stay, Samara" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "It's time to fight, Samara" for +2 Renegade Points .

If you ignore the Paragon Interrupt, Samara takes her own life, leaving the fate of Falere in Shepard's hands.

If Samara has died (either in Mass Effect 2 or by taking her own life in this Mission), then Shepard will have to decide what to do with Falere.

If Samara died in Mass Effect 2, you can pick "Are you sure?" for +15 Paragon Points .

Pick "I can't let you live" for +5 Renegade Points . Pull the Renegade interrupt to gun Falere down for +10 Renegade Points .

Pull the Renegade interrupt to gun Falere down for +10 Renegade Points .

After debriefing the Asari councilor, you'll be able to do another sweep of the Normandy:

CIC - Talk to Traynor, Joker and EDI. Also check your email for Citadel meetups with Jacob and Samara, if available.

Crew Deck - Talk to Garrus and Javik in Port Observation (including a parting conversation), your Virmire Survivor, and Liara. Don't forget to use Gallae's Electronic Signature at the Intel Terminal for the Store Discount Bonus!

Don't forget to use Gallae's Electronic Signature at the Intel Terminal for the Store Discount Bonus!

Shuttle Bay - Talk to Cortez. Also if you completed either the Firewalker or Overlord DLCs in Mass Effect 2, you'll have an amusing exchange between him and James when you walk in!

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Rannoch: Admiral Koris - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Rannoch: Admiral Koris Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Rannoch: Admiral Koris Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

This Side Mission is actually rather important! If you didn't have a perfect run with Tali and Legion in Mass Effect 2, then not completing this Side Mission will lock out an ideal resolution to a later Mission. This Side Mission will also expire after " Priority: Rannoch ".

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Geth Dreadnought "

Location: Perseus Veil - Tikkun - Rannoch

This Side Mission is unlocked after you complete the " Priority: Geth Dreadnought " Mission. During that Mission, Shala'Raan mentions that Admiral Koris' ship was shot down and made a crash-landing on Rannoch, thus providing the setup for this Mission.

When you're ready, fly to Rannoch in the Tikkun system of the Perseus Veil, then highlight and select the "Quarian Escape Pod" marker on the southern hemisphere of the planet.

Squad Tactics: EDI is a fantastic choice thanks to her focus on tech-based powers. Garrus is also a solid option thanks to having powers to strip both Shields and Armor. Ashley will do well here if you have her, being proficient with Sniper Rifles and able to use Disruptor Ammo. Tali will also excel here, but won't make sense for story reasons.

EDI is a fantastic choice thanks to her focus on tech-based powers.

Garrus is also a solid option thanks to having powers to strip both Shields and Armor.

Ashley will do well here if you have her, being proficient with Sniper Rifles and able to use Disruptor Ammo.

Tali will also excel here, but won't make sense for story reasons.

Unique Dialogue: James has a great unique moment in this level. Ashley is a good compliment to James, if you have her. Tali is to be avoided, as she has a big story moment on Rannoch in a later Mission.

James has a great unique moment in this level.

Ashley is a good compliment to James, if you have her.

Tali is to be avoided, as she has a big story moment on Rannoch in a later Mission.

Shepard's Loadout: This level has wide open spaces that will help sniper rifles excel in combat.

This level has wide open spaces that will help sniper rifles excel in combat.

When you start, you'll be in the Kodiak shuttle in a conversation with Admiral Xen, who explains that Koris was shot down to destroy a Geth ground cannon, and since then the Civilian Fleet has taken significant losses without Koris' leadership. Here you can pick up a few Morality Points:

Ask "Why is Koris so vital?" to open the following options: Pick "I don't blame them" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "That's suicide" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "I don't blame them" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "That's suicide" for +2 Renegade Points .

Regardless of the above, you can progress the conversation with... "Protect your civilians" for +2 Paragon Points . "Koris could be dead" for +2 Renegade Points .

"Protect your civilians" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Koris could be dead" for +2 Renegade Points .

The first pocket of enemy resistance won't be too far from the starting point, being around a crashed escape pod. You'll likely face your first Geth Pyro enemy here, whose flames not only set Shepard on fire, but also stagger them repeatedly, so it's important you keep your distance from them. Once the Geth are dead and the music calms down, you can search the area around the escape pod for loot:

Geth Parts - 2,500 credits. Look for a path to the right of the escape pod that loops around the edge of the cliff overlooking the water. At the end you'll find an inactive Geth platform: take his parts! (isn't that like grabbing someone's organs...?)

Quarian Corpse - From the Geth Parts described above, drop down the ledge to find this right in front of you, who one of your squad mates may be examining with their omnitool.

Wreckage - 2,500 credits. Located to the right of the Quarian Corpse described above, next to some burning wreckage.

As you head forward, you may be tempted to pick up the Javelin weapon on the ground, but BEWARE! There's a Trip Mine that will detonate when you get too close. To avoid it, we actually recommend intentionally setting it off: when you get the "click-bweee!" sound, quickly pull the left stick back and tap the Sprint button to roll backwards, taking you out of harm's way.

Javelin - Just past the first Trip Mine, next to a dead Quarian.

If you look to your right, you'll see the flaming wreckage of the next crashed escape pod, with Geth picking away at the wreckage. With some rock cover provided, this is a fantastic spot to use your sniper rifle (such as your shiny new Javelin!). Once they're down, continue forward to face a second wave of Geth. Also beware of the Trip Mine placed in the crash site of the escape pod!

Down the clifftop path, you'll arrive at the first AA Gun, which is of course guarded by Geth. There isn't any great cover here as you approach, so be very careful, especially when the reinforcements show up!

Once all the Geth are gone, return to the short ramp leading up to the AA Gun to look for these goodies:

Geth Technology - 3,750 credits. Head up the middle of the short ramp to face a wide piece of cover. In the middle of the cover will be this, sitting on a metal structure. to be found south of the AA gun controls.

Geth Spitfire - A Heavy Weapon found on a metal structure on the railing to the right of the AA Gun Controls.

Locate the AA Gun Controls near the Geth Spitfire, and you'll have to pick a squad mate to disable it.

While the other squad mate goes to work, you'll need to stave off incoming Geth enemies from multiple fronts. You'll even have a Geth Prime on your hands. This is where you can put the Geth Spitfire to good use, but it's not as easy as it looks thanks to the brief spin-up, which can leave you quite exposed.

Once you kill all the enemies in the first wave, a second wave will show up. It's usually around now that you'll run out of Geth Spitfire ammo, so hunker down and assume normal combat operations. Be on your toes, as there's a cloaked Geth Hunter prowling around now!

Once all the Geth are dead (definitely not pictured above), you can grab some loot as you proceed forwards. Keep an eye out for a Trip Mine!

Assault Rifle Magazine Upgrade - Head up the slope where the two Geth waves came from, but make a left-hand U-turn onto a ledge overlooking the first AA Guns. You can find this mod there.

Med Kit - 50 XP. To the left of the Assault Rifle Magazine Upgrade described above.

Shotgun Shredder Mod - After the Trip Mine, you'll round a bend and spot some inactive geth platforms up ahead. Follow the slightly elevated path on the left-hand wall to find this mod at the end.

Geth Parts - 3,750 credits. From the Shotgun Shredder Mod described above, drop right off the elevated path to find this on the closest inactive geth platform.

From the Geth Parts described above, continue along the path and you'll eventually come across a mortally wounded Quarian named Dorn'Hazt , who barely manages to speak. You can pick up some Morality Points here:

Pick "Stay still" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Where's the admiral?" for +2 Renegade Points .

Whichever you choose, Dorn'Hazt will say that the Civilian Fleet didn't want this war with the Geth, and asks that you extract Koris out alive. He also asks you tell his son, Jonah, that he made it to the homeworld.

SMG Magazine Upgrade - After talking to Dorn'Hazt, mantle up the ledge to spot this in the shrubbery ahead, to the right of a dead Quarian.

Pretty soon you reach the general vicinity of the remaining two AA Guns. There's a split leading to one on the right and one on the left, but it doesn't matter which you go for first as both are heavily guarded by a number of Geth enemies. Like with the first AA Gun, you'll also have to let one squadmate sit out of the gunfight in order to disable the AA Guns (unfortunately, James has no further comedy if you ask him to do it).

Meanwhile, waves of Geth will spawn to disrupt your plans. Fortunately, a nearby Mounted Turret at each AA Gun will provide some great fun peppering any and all enemies that appear, including Primes and Geth Pyros . After the first AA Gun is disabled, a corridor will appear that lets you go straight to the other one... as well as a Geth Trooper and Geth Pyro.

Once you've killed the geth in the tunnel, head for the other AA Gun and kill its geth guards. Then, use this moment of calm to sweep for loot (the Mission automatically progresses once both AA Guns are down):

Armax Arsenal Chestplate - Near the right-hand AA Gun Controls, sitting on a metal structure sticking out of some cover.

Jamming Tower Data - At the left-hand AA Gun, go to the tunnel leading to the right-hand AA Gun and face toward the AA Gun. Head left down the ledge, and keep an eye out on the left-hand wall to spot holographic terminal: Examine it to find this item for " Citadel: Target Jamming Technology ".

With both AA Guns destroyed, Cortez can swoop in with the Kodiak to destroy the jamming tower, allowing you to finally come in contact with Admiral Koris. His current situation is rather dire: he's cut off from the rest of the civilians by Geth, who are heading to his position. To this you can say...

"We're on our way" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Hold them off" for +2 Renegade Points .

Koris however will urge you to save the civilians instead, leaving him for dead for their sake. You'll now be faced with a VERY important decision to make:

Pick the "We need a peacemaker" Charm to persuade Koris that Shepard needs to rescue him to end the Geth war peacefully for +15 Paragon Points .

Pick the "You're a coward" Intimidate to shame Koris into representing the Civilian Fleet for the sake of his people for +15 Renegade Points .

Pick "We'll save them" to save the civilians for +2 Paragon Points and +5 Reputation .

Pick "Your people will be proud" to save the civilians for +2 Renegade Points and +5 Reputation .

Whichever one you choose, Shepard will mount the Kodiak's own guns (dunno where they store that thing!) to help the escape of whom you chose to save. The Geth will initially be on the right, and after you've cleared them, a second wave will appear on the left. Fortunately, the enemies will explode the moment you hit them with a shot, but don't get complacent as Rocket Troopers will target the shuttle to down it.

After all the Geth are destroyed, Shepard will drop in for the rescue and will depart for the Normandy.

The scene in the Normandy's Comm Room will differ depending on who you chose to save:

If you chose to save Zaal'Koris, he'll reluctantly admit that Shepard was right to choose him, and the Civilian Fleet is in a worse state than he thought. He'll be able to join Shepard's forces as a War Asset worth 25 TMS.

If you chose to save the civilians, you'll be on call with Han'Gerrel, who'll say he's too busy to take responsibility of the Civilian Fleet and pass the job on to his aides. As a result, the Quarian Civilian Fleet War Asset loses -75 TMS.

If this was the first Rannoch Side Mission you completed after " Priority: Geth Dreadnought ", you'll by approached by Admiral Raan saying the Reaper Base has been located. You can get up to +6 Paragon Points / +11 Renegade Points depending on your choices. This scene will unlock the next Mission, " Priority: Rannoch ", but we HIGHLY recommend you complete the other Rannoch Side Mission if you haven't already!

You'll also have one of the two arguments listed below, depending on if this was your first or second Rannoch Side Mission after " Priority: Geth Dreadnought ".

After your first Rannoch Side Mission, there'll be an argument between Admiral Raan and Admiral Gerrel. Supporting Raan weakens the Quarian Heavy Fleet by -10 TMS, while supporting Gerrel will boost it by 25 TMS. You'll get +2 Reputation either way.

After your second Rannoch Side Mission, there'll be an argument between Admiral Tali and Admiral Xen. Support Tali for +2 Paragon Points , or Xen for +2 Renegade Points .

With all the scenes wrapped up, you can do another lap of the Normandy:

CIC - Talk to Admiral Raan about the Civilian Fleet, Tali for a slight new reply, Traynor, Joker and EDI.

Crew Deck - Talk to your Virmire Survivor, Garrus (for a harrowing walk-in scene), and Javik in the AI Core ( +2 Reputation ).

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

Up Next: Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons

articles.title: Kasumi: Stolen Memory - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Kasumi: Stolen Memory DLC Mission (also known as Stealing Memory), including how to access
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Kasumi: Stolen Memory DLC Mission (also known as Stealing Memory), including how to access and unlock it, how to recruit Kasumi, how to complete her Loyalty Mission, and how to get all the collectibles, including the Locust Submachine gun.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Original release: On Xbox 360, the Kasumi: Stolen Memory DLC is only available as a download via the Cerberus Network, which can be activated by going to your EA account and using the Redeem Product Code section. On PlayStation 3, Kasumi: Stolen Memory is available on-disc / in the initial download. On PC, most storefronts will label this version of the game as "Mass Effect 2 (2010)", which now includes Kasumi: Stolen Memory as part of the download.

On Xbox 360, the Kasumi: Stolen Memory DLC is only available as a download via the Cerberus Network, which can be activated by going to your EA account and using the Redeem Product Code section.

On PlayStation 3, Kasumi: Stolen Memory is available on-disc / in the initial download.

On PC, most storefronts will label this version of the game as "Mass Effect 2 (2010)", which now includes Kasumi: Stolen Memory as part of the download.

In the Legendary Edition of Mass Effect 2, the Kasumi: Stolen Memory DLC is automatically included.

Kasumi: Stolen Memory is available in-game as soon as Commander Shepard gains captaincy of their own ship after the " Freedom's Progress " Mission.

Location : Serpent Nebula - Widow - Citadel - Zakera Ward - Level 27 Dock

Recruiting Kasumi is one of the simplest tasks in the game, and can be done as soon as you complete the Freedom's Progress Mission and acquire the Normandy SR-2 . Set your sights for the Citadel in the Widow system. To your right will be an ad podium with Kasumi trying to talk to you. Interact with it to begin. Here you'll have a few opportunities to earn Morality Points:

Pick "Cut the crap" for +2 Renegade Points .

After this, you can progress the conversation again for more Morality Points. Oddly, picking "You and Cerberus" and then "What deal?" will replace these and lock out these Morality Points. Don't worry about picking them before "What deal?", as Kasumi will explain that to you anyway.

"Welcome Aboard" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Let's head out" for +2 Renegade Points .

Once you have her, Kasumi will set herself up on the Starboard Observation Deck in the Crew's Quarters. It's very much her space, so there's a bunch of objects you can interact with in there. As well, you can talk to Kasumi and hear three of her thoughts regarding recent events and things happening around the ship.

Location : Serpent Nebula - Boltzmann - Bekenstein

Your destination will be Bekenstein, the second planet of the Boltzmann system located in the Widow cluster (that's where the Citadel is!). You should head straight for the planet: since Boltzmann is a very established system, it only has Moderate and Poor amounts of Resources to Scan for.

When you install Stolen Memory, you receive a message at your terminal on the Normandy that Cerberus has contracted Kasumi Goto to join your team. At any point thereafter, you can visit the Citadel to find Kasumi waiting for you at the docks.

You begin with Kasumi in a skycar on the way to the party, and are debriefed on what the plan is, and why Shepard is in formal wear pretending to be a fictitious person. There's no Morality Points to earn here, so you can answer however you like in this conversation.

Next you'll arrive at the party, where the gold Saren statue is being scanned for delivery into the vault. Hock himself then shows up, but unfortunately he doesn't like the look of Kasumi and asks her to wait outside for the duration of the party (must be the hooded catsuit). Here, you can get some Morality Points:

Answer "Of course" for +2 Paragon Points .

Answer "If that's what it takes" for +2 Renegade Points .

Afterwards you'll discuss the matter with Kasumi. Luckily she has an invisibility cloak, so she'll just have to be covert while you go inside and do all the talking for her. You can get Morality Points here too:

Answer "What's the plan?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Answer "I can do this alone" for +2 Renegade Points .

Your first task is to scout out the party floor and find the entrance to Hock's Vault. You won't be able to do anything else here yet, although there are some ambient exchanges to overhear between some of the party guests. Several of these are actually contextual: they'll be different depending on where in the game you are.

To find the vault door, look in the back corners of the room for these large, white murals with glass bead curtains. They mark the location of stairs that will lead you right to it. Once in the vault, Kasumi will scope out its defenses. It has a DNA Scanner which you'll need some samples to get past, a Kinetic Barrier for which you'll have to cut the power to, and a Voice Lock Microphone that requires you to get both a sample of Hock's voice and the password itself to crack.

The closest of these to start is to shut down the kinetic barrier. Exit the vault into the hallway and look right to spot a Kinetic Barrier Power Cable. Examine it, and Kasumi will enhance Shepard's optics so that you can see the cable through the walls and floor.

You'll follow the cable upstairs, across the party floor, past Hock, and into a secluded library area. Locate the Statuette and Pull it to raise the digital fireplace, which allows Kasumi to cut the power to the kinetic barrier. Awesome!

The Voice Lock is the only security measure that has two steps: you'll need both a sample of Hock's voice to synthesize the password from, and the password itself. To start, locate Hock in the middle of the party floor near the koi pool.

The best way to get a voice sample is to use one of the Charm / Intimidate options on the left: this will send Hock into an extended filibuster about him and people like him, providing more than enough for Kasumi.

The requirements for these options are quite low, however if you can't pass them, you'll need to use one of the options on the right: this will provide a shorter sample, but give some more, less engaging white options as well as an Intimidate option with a lower requirement. These new right-hand options will get you enough of a sample, although Hock will be irritated that you wasted his time.

Now for the password. From Hock's position, look for a large, round, vault-like door at the bottom of one of the nearby staircases, labelled Security Room Door. Interact with it, and Kasumi will open it up for you. At the end of the corridor, you'll have to Bypass the second door to get inside the room itself.

Once you've done that you'll get into a gunfight. There's no good cover here, so use Shepard and Kasumi's Powers and take down the two guards as fast as you can. Once they're dead, look for the Datapad on the office table and Read it to get the password: "Peruggia".

Wall Safe - 7,200 Credits. On the right-hand wall of the office.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. On the right-hand wall of the office, next to the Wall Safe.

The last security measure is the most involved, as it requires you to get into Hock's Private Quarters. You can find the main entrance to it in a secluded library area, opposite the one where you disabled the Kinetic Barrier's power. Here will be an Eclipse Security Guard, but of course he won't let you in. Sounds like you need someone's proper authority to get in this way.

Your ways for getting past this both lie in the outdoor balcony area. First, locate the security guard in one of the back corners having some private time with an Asari. Read the Datapad next to him to learn about Chief Roe, who's so strict even these guys go out of their way not to piss her off. In the opposite corner meanwhile are some rusty Balcony Railings you can use to sneak into the Private Quarters without permission.

Those are your two methods for getting in. Our suggested method is to take the "Chief Roe" route: talk to the security guard, say you have authorization, and then cite Chief Roe. Kasumi will make sure he's successfully fooled, and you'll be let in. This route is preferred simply because you have authorization to be in there, and thus will be caught much less easily.

The Balcony Railing method is more exciting, but will force you into combat and also means you have more avenues of getting found out (plus Kasumi doesn't really approve of it by the end). If you decide to take this route, quickly take out the three guards in the lower area before going up to the window and shooting it.

However you got inside, you'll now be in Hock's Private Quarters and need to search for three DNA samples so that you have enough material to fool the vault's scanner. There's several things you can try for, and not all of them will gets results!

Your DNA positive objects are the Datapad , the Wine Glass and the Antique Weapons Collection . We suggest using the Papers first before the Datapad, as well as search one of the Couch Cushions for a credit chit. This is because once you have your three samples, you'll be unable to interact with any more items here (except for the Wall Safe), and the Papers and Datapad contribute to the story.

We suggest using the Papers first before the Datapad, as well as search one of the Couch Cushions for a credit chit. This is because once you have your three samples, you'll be unable to interact with any more items here (except for the Wall Safe), and the Papers and Datapad contribute to the story.

Couch Cushions - 1 Credit. The first couch cushion in the room that you Interact with will have a credit chit with 1 Credit on it. Score!

Objects that return no samples include the Plant , Keyboard , Pillows and Couch Cushions . The Papers don't either, but they do contribute to the story a little bit.

If you snuck in via the Balcony railing, avoid interacting with the Alarm Clock . This will alert the remaining two guards to your presence and you'll have to fight them.

Wall Safe - 7,800 Credits. Located near the fireplace at the back of the room: you can Bypass it at any time, even after getting the DNA samples. Be careful though! If you fail the Bypass by selecting the wrong node or running out of time, you'll alert the guards, even if you got in with Roe's authorization!

Once you have the three samples, you should head out by exiting out the door and going up the stairs.

Now, if you snuck in via the Balcony Railing and didn't interact with the Alarm Clock, there will be two guards at the exit who've noticed your earlier handiwork outside the window. Hide behind the pillar at the top of the stairs, then tell Kasumi to Shadow Strike one while you take care of the other. She'll say "what a mess" over how this part of the heist has gone down.

Now that you have everything, return to the vault entrance. The Kinetic Barrier is already down, so all you have to do now is use the DNA Scanner to pass that measure, then the Microphone to get past the Voice Lock. Then interact with the Secure Elevator, and you'll be into the vault, safe to reclaim your weapons and armor from the Saren statue.

Once you're inside the Vault, you'll need to search for Keiji's graybox. Use the Graybox Proximity sensor in the bottom-right corner of the screen to tell how far away you are from it.

There's a lot of good stuff in here though: examine the Statue of Liberty Head for a codex entry explaining what it's doing here. There's also the Creature statue, which is a statue of the Ogre enemy from Dragon Age: Origins.

M-12 Locust - Before you interact with Keiji's Graybox, make sure to pick up the Kassa Fabrications Locust sitting right next to it. Kasumi uses Submachine Guns, so it's worth picking it up so that she can use it now.

When you interact with Keiji's Graybox, you'll be met by Hock's hologrammatic head.

If you're feeling like an ass, you can use the Renegade Interrupt to shoot one of the art pieces for +5 Renegade Points .

Regardless, you'll get into your first proper fight of the Mission.

Among the Eclipse mercs who enter the room will be Chief Roe herself: she's a heavily-shielded engineer, complete with her own combat drones. Kasumi is very much a glass cannon, but her Shadow Strike is potent: Kasumi teleports to her target and backstabs them (often for an instant kill), then returns to her original position, all while being invulnerable. It's a good idea to let Kasumi use Shadow Strike of her own volition, as it does a lot to improve her very low survivability. You can also use it to take out specific high-priority targets, like Vanguards or Engineers.

Once you've dealt with Roe's squad, leave the vault via the entry door. Take cover near the entrance and pick off the footsoldiers one at a time, then open up on the YMIR Mech with your heaviest weapons. Just be careful if your final hit of the YMIR Mech is a headshot: this will cause it to collapse and eventually blow up in a colossal explosion. This does massive damage to everyone in the area, including you if you don't take cover!

As you head through the garage, Hock will close the doors in front of you. To get past, look for the ramp on the right-hand side to find a door to a side area.

PDA - 4,200 Credits. Across from the door you use to leave this area, among some crates.

The next room has a very neat alternate method of getting through. If you've got heavy shields, the Infiltration Cloak, or are on an easier difficulty setting, you can rush left across the room and up a ramp to fire a Mass Accelerator Cannon, which instantly kills every enemy in the room and opens the way forwards! Otherwise, you're better off dealing with the Eclipse and YMIR Mechs the old-fashioned way.

Once they're done, Investigate the grey Volatile Tanks: they can be used to clear the path forwards, but your on-hand weapons aren't powerful enough to puncture them. Head up the ramp directly across from them to get up to a vehicle's Mass Accelerator Cannon: fire it to blow up the tanks and open a hole in the wall. Before leaving, scout around for loot:

Spare Parts - 4,800 Credits. In a locker close to the bottom of the ramp up to the Mass Accelerator Cannon.

1,000 Refined Platinum - On top of a large crate right next to the ramp up to the Mass Accelerator Cannon.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. At the top of the ramp up to the Mass Accelerator Cannon.

Spare Parts - 1,200 Credits. To the left of the large white Volatile Tanks you blow up with the Mass Accelerator Cannon is a small room. Inside is a rack of LOKI Mechs with the Spare Parts to Salvage.

Your path takes you back into the first tunnel, where a bunch of Eclipse heavies and another YMIR Mech have taken up a position on the other end, while Engineers and normal troops try to flank you. Let Kasumi deal with as many of the distant enemies as you can while you take out the flankers. Once they're all down (including the truck that arrives at the far end), head up the left-hand ramp.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. At the top of the steps leading to the exit door, on the right-hand side near a stack of cube-shaped crates.

Eclipse Soldier - Tech Damage Research. Next to the exit door will be a dead Eclipse soldier next to a desk. Examine him to get some Research Data.

The next room will be a shipping garage with yet more Eclipse enemies in it. Take cover behind the crate immediately across from the door then get to work. If you can use Sniper Rifles, we highly recommend using it to take out the Vanguard on the opposite side of the room, but only after you've taken out the two Troopers who fire at you from a closer distance.

Once you're done, sweep the area for more loot:

Spare Parts - 1,800 Credits. On the left-hand side of the room are two shipping containers. Check between them to find a blue dumpster with Spare Parts to Salvage.

500 Refined Platinum - From the Spare Parts described above, turn right to find a box of Refined Platinum at the end of a cargo platform, near two round green-and-black canisters.

500 Refined Platinum - Found inside the shipping container to the right of where the Spare Parts were.

PDA - 1,800 Credits. In the bed of a yellow pick-up truck in the docking bay, to the left of the first box of Refined Platinum described above.

Storage Crate - 1,200 Credits. On the right-hand wall close to the exit door, underneath a section of wall with "AO- 181" written on it.

Now that you have all the collectibles, it's time to exit the building for the final showdown!

Hock has come after you in a shielded gunship, and alternates between firing its very powerful main gun and throwing out a pair of homing missiles. Standing out in the open while Hock is firing at you is a good way to get killed in seconds. If that wasn't enough, Hock constantly calls in LOKI Mechs and assorted Eclipse mercenaries to support him from the ground; the first wave comes from ahead of you as the fight begins, and subsequent groups appear on the far left side of the platform.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. From the spot where Shepard initially takes cover after the cutscene, turn around and you'll spot this to your left, in the corner next to a shipping container.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Among some crates and canisters in the middle-left of the battlefield.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On some crates in front of the ramp up to the elevated part of the battlefield.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. In the back-left corner of the battlefield, on top of a blue pick-up truck.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. In the elevated part of the battlefield. Head up the ramp and look to your right to spot some crates with the Med Kit on it.

Dispose of the mercs on the ground as quickly as possible so you can spend the maximum amount of time whittling away at Hock's gunship's shield. The first time you deplete it, he'll temporarily leave the fight, leaving you alone with the mercs for a second. Take this opportunity to grab ammo, including the power cells over by the mercs' backup spawn point, as Hock rejoins the fight with regenerated shields shortly thereafter.

When the gunship returns to the fray, Kasumi says she can take down its shields if she has a clear shot. So, clear out incoming waves of enemies so that Kasumi has her window. You'll see an awesome cutscene of her taking them out in style, then you'll be able to fight Hock's gunship one-on-one and finally take it down. Once it's destroyed the Kodiak shuttle will arrive, letting you depart the planet.

The finale of the level is a choice regarding Keiji's Graybox. As you discover, Keiji intends for Kasumi to destroy the Graybox due to the secrets it contains putting a target on her back, but as is obvious by now, Kasumi wanted the Graybox primarily to relive her time with Keiji.

Whether you choose to keep or destroy the graybox is up to you. There are no gameplay consequences either way, and the only story effects are present in Mass Effect 3 (see below for more on that). Regardless, here's what each of the options give you when it comes to the game's Morality Points:

Pick "Keep the graybox" for +5 Paragon Points .

Pick "It's what he wants" or "Destroy the graybox" for +2 Renegade Points . You can then choose one of the following: Pick "Let me do it" for +5 Renegade Points . Pick "Do it" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "Let me do it" for +5 Renegade Points .

The main effect of this end choice is felt in Mass Effect 3's Extended Cut DLC (included in the Legendary Edition). If you'd like to know now, click the spoiler tags below to learn what the effects are:

If you keep the graybox , Tap to Reveal .

If you destroy the graybox , Tap to Reveal .

As noted above, any choice ensures her loyalty, which gives her a new outfit and a new power, Flashbang Grenade. This is a low-radius explosion with a surprisingly long range that inflicts light damage and a stun on anything it hits. Perhaps most importantly, the party outfit that Kasumi gave you is now an option for wearing around the Normandy and other casual situations!

Once you're back on the Normandy, here's what you can do:

CIC - Walk through the bridge tunnel to hear the crew talk about FerrIs Fields, and visit Joker for more ambient comments and about how things are in the cockpit.

Crew Deck - Pop into the Crew Quarters room, and check in with Kasumi.

Engineering - Pop by Gabby and Ken, and talk to Zaeed for more stories.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:
