articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Normandy SR-2 hub level. In particular, details all the various areas of the ship, what you
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Normandy SR-2 hub level. In particular, details all the various areas of the ship, what you can do on it, and the people you can meet from your first visit after completing the Freedom's Progress level.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

When you first arrive on your new ship, the Normandy SR-2, you'll be in a cutscene with Jacob, Miranda, and a new surprise addition: EDI, the ship's on-board AI. You'll have more Morality Point opportunities here!

After EDI makes her presence known, you can respond with the following: "Joker won't like this" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "AIs are dangerous" for +2 Renegade Points . If you did the the UNC: Rogue VI Side Quest on the Moon in Mass Effect 1, it will be cited.

"Joker won't like this" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "AIs are dangerous" for +2 Renegade Points . If you did the the UNC: Rogue VI Side Quest on the Moon in Mass Effect 1, it will be cited.

Pick "Glad to hear it" when it first shows up for +2 Renegade Points . It'll disappear if you pick anything else.

Before we begin to assemble our team, you should first take the time to familiarize yourself with your new Normandy. This ship is, in many ways, an enlarged version of the original SSV Normandy SR-1 from Mass Effect 1, though it has far more to offer in many respects. The ship's four floors are accessible via a central elevator, one that will bring you to each floor rapidly (faster if you're playing on PS5 or Xbox Series).

The floors in question are the Captain's Cabin, Combat Information Center (CIC), Crew's Quarters, and Engineering.

We'll start on the CIC, also known as the Combat Information Center. Like with the original Normandy, this is where you can use the Galaxy Map to travel across the galaxy.

To the right of the Galaxy Map ramp is Yeoman Kelly Chambers. She acts as your personal assistant, letting you know if anyone wants to speak with you and if you have any new messages at your Private Terminal.

If you're Paragon, make sure to agree to call her Kelly by picking "Sure" when she asks you to.

Aside from new messages (which we'll get to soon), it seems that Joker wants to speak with you on the Bridge at the front of the ship.

Before doing that though, you should continue talking with Kelly. Kelly is a semi-important character for two reasons. First, she offers a key-but-cosmetic service for your Cabin by feeding your fish for you, if you befriend her. Secondly, she's your first Romance interest in the game, although she is considered a Fling (which means she won't jeopardize other Romances, at the expense of having no Romance Scene).

That aside, you can also pick "What do you think of Cerberus?" under Investigate, then follow it up with "Does Cerberus hate aliens?". Here, you can get Morality Points:

Pick "You are very loving" for +2 Paragon Points . (only available if you agreed to address her as Kelly instead of Ms. Chambers).

Pick "You're naive" for +2 Renegade Points .

Now tend to your Private Terminal, which are the pair of laptops on the opposite side of the Galaxy Map ramp from Kelly. You can do several things here:

Team Status - Review the status of your team, including Loyalty, unlocked Talents, and cycle Appearances. You can also view any unlocked Dossiers to learn more about future crew members.

Upgrades - Review all purchased Research Upgrades.

Unread Messages - All your unread messages. Here you can either delete them, or Archive them for later viewing.

Archived Messages - All Archived messages are stored here.

Advanced Combat Training - Three video tutorials that cover Squad Commands, using Powers, and Real-Time Control (using both at once without pausing the game). This is removed in the Legendary Edition.

Now head on up to the Bridge to talk to Joker, through the tube-like corridor on the far end of the CIC. Along the way, make sure to Examine these for Codex entries:

Controls - On the right-hand side of the tube corridor leading to the cockpit.

Flight Controls - On the right-hand side of the cockpit itself.

Talk to Joker to catch up with him, then talk to him a second time to get his thoughts about the state of the Mission, as well as the two Squad Mates you went ashore with most recently. You can also ask how things are going in the cockpit: this will update after you complete any Mission or Assignment.

You can also speak with EDI here and ask her about a wide variety of subjects. However literally everything regarding Cerberus has a Block that prevents her from answering about them at all. These will lift at a certain point in the story, and we'll let you know when they do.

Now return to the main CIC area and head for the door with the red light on it, to the left of the hologram podium in the middle of the room. This is where you access the Tech Research Lab, however it's locked at the moment since you don't have Mordin Solus yet.

Instead, cross over to the opposite side of the room and enter the Armory. Here you can find a Weapons Locker, which lets you sort out your Weapons Loadout. While you can do this when selecting your Squad, that only applies to Shepard and their two Squad Mates: the Weapons Locker lets you do it for your entire Squad.

You'll also get to talk with Jacob here. Talking with Squad Mates on the Normandy is an important facet of Mass Effect 2, because not only do you get to know them and what they're about, but also progress towards unlocking their Loyalty Missions , which are extremely important towards their survival of the game.

Here, when talking to Jacob on the Normandy for the first time, you can get some Morality Points:

At the outset, pick "Bringing you wasn't my choice" for +2 Renegade Points .

At the next Dialogue Wheel, when Jacob brings up his issues with Cerberus...

Pick either "Glad to have you aboard" or "I appreciate your honesty" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Do your job. Nothing more" for +2 Renegade Points .

The last place of the CIC level to explore is located between the Armory and the Tech Lab, and that's the Briefing / Comm Room. This room is unimportant from a gameplay sense, but similar to the Comm Room on the original Normandy, you'll frequently find yourself here after completing Missions, so it'll be helpful to know where on the ship you are since it's kinda buried on the CIC deck behind the elevator.

With that done, locate the elevator near the Galaxy Map and head down to the Crew's Quarters.

The Crew's Quarters is unique because it's the only deck of the ship that you exit backwards out of the elevator, meaning you'll be facing the opposite direction compared to the other three decks. To start, enter the door on your left marked Crew Quarters to overhear a conversation between two crew members. This updates every so often, so we'll keep you posted.

The other rooms around here are locked. The Starboard Observation requires the Justicar, Life Support requires the Assassin, and the Port Observation requires a Thief (who is a DLC character in the original release of the game). You can venture into both bathrooms: go into the one opposite your Shepard's gender to get an amusing comment from EDI.

Now head around the elevator into the mess hall, where the crew will be complaining to the cook about the quality of the food. Talk to the cook, Mess Sergeant Gardner, in the kitchen, and ask him "Need anything?" and then "How can I help?" to pick up the Normandy: Special Ingredients Side Quest, which you can progress on The Citadel.

Next, head into the room on the other side of the kitchen wall to find Miranda's Cabin. You can learn more about both Cerberus and herself here, but there's no Morality Points to earn. You should still talk to her though, again to progress towards unlocking Miranda's Loyalty Mission later in the game.

The last thing you'll want to do is cross over to the opposite side of the deck to the Medical Center. It's here that you'll meet an old friend: Doctor Karin Chakwas, survivor of the original Normandy.

Ask "Why are you here?" for +2 Paragon Points .

However you respond, make sure to ask her "Need anything?" and then "I'll get you another" to pick up the Normandy: Serrice Ice Brandy Side Quest, which you can progress on the Citadel.

Engineering is the second-smallest deck on the Normandy SR-2, so it won't take as long to explore it. First, you'll notice that both of the doors on the far sides of the hallway are locked. You'll need the Warlord to access the Port Cargo area, and the Veteran for the Starboard Cargo area (The Veteran is a DLC character in the original release).

For now, head through one of the doors next to the elevator and locate Gabby and Ken, your engine team. In the opening exchange, you can get some Morality Points:

Reply "Shape up!" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll also want to ask them "Need anything?" and then "What's the issue?" to pick up the Normandy: FBA Couplings Side Quest. You can progress that on Omega.

The final area of the ship is the Captain's Cabin at the top. This is a mostly cosmetic area of the ship, such as the fish tank. Any fish you buy on the Citadel will be displayed here, however the catch (ha) is that you must feed them after every Mission and Side Quest you complete, or else they'll die. While this is more feasible on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, the best solution is to befriend Kelly so that she'll feed them for you.

The office across from the fish tank has another Private Terminal, which works just like the one next to the Galaxy Map on the CIC. You'll also find the Medal of Honor here, where you can review your unlocked Trophies / Achievements and how close you are to meeting them. Lastly, if you Romanced someone in Mass Effect 1, there will be a picture of them on the desk between the two.

Here will also be a glass wall with a model of the Normandy SR-2 in it. This area displays various models that you can purchase from stores across Omega and The Citadel. This is purely cosmetic, but everyone likes model ships, right?

In the lower area of the cabin is the Armor Locker, which works just like the one on Minuteman Station. With it, you can customize Shepard's amour, including the various pieces and what colours they are. You can also choose a casual outfit, which is what Shepard will wear while on the Normandy and in other relaxed settings.

The final thing we'd like to point out is the Sound System clock, which lets you choose from a variety of tracks that were in the Mass Effect Original Soundtrack (and one from Mass Effect 2). Here's your tracklist selection, in order, and where they could / can be heard:

Virmire Ride (Virmire - opening Mako section)

Criminal Elements (Noveria - Port Hanshan Mezzanine bar)

Protecting the Colony (Feros - return to Zhu's Hope)

The Wards (the Wards areas of The Citadel)

Battling Saren (vertical run up the Citadel Tower)

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Dossier - The Professor - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Dossier: The Professor Mission on Omega, including how to get through all combat encounters,
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Dossier: The Professor Mission on Omega, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Research : Assault Rifle Damage Medi-Gel Capacity

Found Credits : 23,000 credits (Paragon) 25,000 credits (Renegade)

Resources : 1,000 Element Zero 2,000 Palladium 2,000 Platinum 2,000 Iridium

Location: Omega Nebula - Sahrabarik - Omega

This Dossier Mission is one of two that takes place on Omega, which is in the Sahrabarik system of the Omega Nebula . This is the system you started in after first acquiring the Normandy SR-2. If you've been doing this guide in order, this will be your third visit, after some shopping and picking up Archangel.

If you're interested in mining, here's the one Rich planet in the system Omega is in, Sahrabarik:

However chances are this may be your first visit, since the game suggests you recruit Mordin as soon as you get the Normandy SR-2. So, when you first arrive you'll be met by two emissaries (the first one is fake), who demands that you meet with the local head of the station, Aria T'Loak. There's no pressure to do this immediately despite his strong words.

Squad Tactics: If your interest is tactics, Zaeed and Grunt are good picks as they both have fire-based abilities to strip Armor, which you'll be doing a lot of here.

If your interest is tactics, Zaeed and Grunt are good picks as they both have fire-based abilities to strip Armor, which you'll be doing a lot of here.

Unique Dialogue: For story reasons, Grunt and Archangel have the most unique dialogue on this Mission.

For story reasons, Grunt and Archangel have the most unique dialogue on this Mission.

Once you've done some shopping and picked up Zaeed and Archangel (or not, it's ultimately up to you), you'll want to head into Afterlife and ask Aria about Mordin (if you put Archangel in your Squad, he'll respond to the news EDI delivers him.

If this is your first time in Afterlife, you can talk to a Batarian called Kylan in the entry hall and use Charm / Intimidate for some Morality Points. Inside the bar itself, you can go to the bar on the right side of the floor and order some drinks: order three to get intoxicated.

Head up the stairs in the back to meet with Aria. If this is your first time, she'll have her men check that you're really Shepard: your response will earn you Morality Points. However it goes, ask her about Mordin to find that he can be found in the Quarantine Zone (never a good pair of words to hear), helping out some sickly people there. She also lets you know that you travel there at your own risk, if you can even get there at all.

The Quarantine Zone entrance is at the southeastern end of the map, at the end of an alley just off the right-hand route to the Markets, although actually getting there won't be as easy as it seems. When you arrive at the door, you'll find a Turian guard arguing with a human woman. When you speak with him, you'll learn about the plague that's the reason for the quarantine. It doesn't affect humans (or Vorcha, for that matter), but members of just about every other race can be easily killed by it.

At this point, you can decide to get in using either the white options on the right side of the Dialogue Wheel, or with the coloured Persuasion options on the left. Here's how each will go for you:

If you Charm with "Let me in and I'll help", you'll get +5 Paragon Points , and the guard will radio ahead to let you through.

If you Intimidate with "I'm going in", you'll get +5 Intimidate Points , and the guard will radio ahead to let you through.

If you pick "I really need to get in" or "You can't stop me", Shepard will go in regardless. However since the guard didn't radio ahead about you, you'll have to gun down three Turian guards at the start of the level.

Now if you have Garrus and/or Grunt on your Squad, they'll talk to you before heading in about entering a Quarantine Zone with a plague that kills Turians and Krogan. This gives you the chance for more Morality Points:

Pick "Don't worry. You'll stay back" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I need you to come" for +2 Renegade Points .

Once inside the Quarantine Zone, all will be quiet... for now, anyway. Head forward down the initial corridor.

250 Refined Element Zero - Before going through the doorway on the right, check around the boxes at the end of this corridor for some valuable Element Zero. This is one of the rarest resources in the game so you'll want as much as you can find!

Now go through the doorway to meet the main barricade. If you used one of the Persuasion options with the Turian guard earlier to get in, the barricade patrol will let you pass peacefully. If not however they'll start shooting at you, and you'll be forced to kill all three of them.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. To progress forwards you'll have to go through a side corridor that goes around the barricade. In here will be the Medical Station, close to the exit door.

With the guards pacified and the Medical Station salvaged, head through the door to continue.

As soon as you enter this door, have your gun at the ready, because two Blue Sun mercenaries are up ahead. When you begin to walk into the room, to the left of the burning corpses there, they will open fire on you. Try to initiate hostilities here, aiming carefully and maximizing as best you can the damage dealt. There's plenty of cover around you to use, if necessary.

Once you've downed the enemies, search the area for goodies.

Bank Terminal - 5,000 Credits. To the left of the white-lit door the two Blue Suns troops were standing in front of, with "Mechanical Sciences" text above it.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. Head through the door next to the Bank Terminal described above, then go left around the column to find it sitting on a table.

If you Bypass the next door in the room the Power Cells are in, you can Examine a Turian Plague Victim on the ground, deceased, as well as use a nearby Computer Console to hear his four log entries. Things are, clearly, quite serious down here.

Exit back out to the main area and head left: you should spot a Batarian Victim on your right on the floor, near a floor lamp. Speak with him, and you'll get into a surprisingly deep, lengthy and thorough conversation with him.

You can get +2 Renegade Points for saying "Leave him". This won't back out of the rest of the conversation.

Whatever you pick, the Batarian's life will start failing after you advance the conversation, and you'll have two choices:

If you act fast and use the Paragon Interrupt, you'll apply some Medi-Gel and save his life, getting you +5 Paragon Points .

If you ignore or miss the Paragon Interrupt, the Batarian will die. He drops his Datapad in the process, which you can Examine to get 2,000 Credits. You get no Renegade Points for this.

If you were fast and decided to apply some Medi-Gel with the Paragon Interrupt, you can then respond with:

"I'm here to help" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I need information" for +2 Renegade Points .

After that, you'll be able to pick the Batarian's brain for more information about what's going on.

With the Batarian conversation over, continue down the corridor, but keep an eye out for a door on the right that you can Bypass (it'll have an "Apartments" sign above it). Do so, and you can head down the stairs and into a room with a dead Batarian on the bed. Play the Logs on the Datapad to find out what happened to him.

Wall Safe - 4,000 Credits. On the right-hand wall of the room with the dead Batarian in it.

Continue forwards into an area called Kokomo Plaza, with tables in the middle and a Blue Suns barricade on the far end. You're going to have to use cover here, because as you'll find out, you're going to be under assault from multiple angles. Try to use your special skills, as well as your squad members' skills, and this fight shouldn't be too long. What makes this battle difficult are the sheer number of Blue Suns Troopers you'll have to deal with, and not so much the strength of those soldiers.

While the tables provide good cover and keep you in range of the barricade, tactically your best bet is to run forward along the left side and up the stairs to the balcony, letting you flank them from above. If you're extra daring, you can run to the far side of the room and flank the soldiers at the top end of the area, using the nearby explosive barrels to devastating effect. Otherwise, be patient and pick off the enemies you encounter one at a time.

With all of the enemies around you dead (or most of them, anyway), you can explore this area.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. With your back facing the way you came, head to the left side of the area and go up the stairs. At the top you'll find the Med Kit on a round table overlooking the stairs.

Circuit Boards - 1,000 Credits. To the left of where the Med Kit is on the back wall.

Now head through the doorway to the right of the Blue Suns barricade and look for the white-lit doorway with "Apartments" above it. Head inside and ignore the occupants for now to get some goodies.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Hidden on a table behind the column at the base of the stairs going up to the slightly elevated area where the occupants are.

Wall Safe - 4,000 Credits. Head up the steps near the Med Kit and go to the back-right corner of the room. The Wall Safe will be here on the right above a seat next to the bed.

Now talk to the occupants, who were scared to ever let their presence be known here. Say "You should go to the Clinic", as this lets you then say:

"I'll help you get there" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Hiding here won't save you" for +2 Renegade Points .

Now head back outside and around the back side of the barricade.

Modified Assault Rifle - Assault Rifle Damage. On the other side of the barricade, face away from it to spot a lamp in the corner up ahead, with a Blue Suns corpse next to it. Scan his rifle. This is a VERY useful upgrade for Soldiers to have because Assault Rifles don't do that much damage, even on Easy Difficulty.

Up ahead will be the final battle area before you reach Mordin's clinic, where you'll be fighting Vorcha, Krogan and Varren. To get a leg up, head up the stairs on the right as you approach the battlefield to get to an upper balcony so you aren't stormed.

This is a surprisingly extended fight because more foes walk in just when you think you've gotten rid of everybody. As well, Vorcha heal automatically, so when you attack them you have to kill them all the way, or it'll be like you never attacked them at all after a few seconds. Once the battle is over, pick up all the Thermal Clips you need.

500 Element Zero - Check the left-hand side of the battlefield to find a door into a small room with this inside, on the shelves to the left of the next door.

Now go through the next door in the room the Element Zero was in to find another apartment, which currently has two looters in it (so no goodies for you).

Here, you can answer:"Who are you"?, then say "I don't like looters" for +2 Paragon Points .

Next, reply "I want you to stop" to get the following options:

Pick the "No... but someone will" Charm for +5 Paragon Points .

Pick the "If I have to" Intimidate for +5 Renegade Points .

Pick "Yes" to kill both of them for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "Forget it. I don't care" to drop the subject for no Morality Points.

Exit back out to the main area and look for a glowing red line on the ground. This will actually lead you around the corner and to the door that takes you to the Med Clinic! As you approach the clinic's front door, take heed of the Clinic Guard's warning when talking to him: If you try any funny business here, you'll have to deal with him an army of mechs. Luckily, Shepard and their squad will put away their guns when entering.

Explore the lobby to talk to the two Clinic Receptionists, the Turian Patient, the Batarian Patient, and the female Clinic Guard around the corner.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. Around the corner where the female Clinic Guard is, right next to her on the wall.

Now return to reception and head down the nearby hallway. Mordin is pattering away in the room on the right, but first explore the room on the left.

2,000 Refined Platinum - On the table on your left as soon as you enter the room, under a lamp.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On a medical bed towards the middle of the room.

2,000 Refined Palladium - On a table in the back-right corner of the room.

Research Station - Medi-Gel Capacity. Accessed via a computer on the same table where you can find the Refined Palladium.

Now head to Mordin's room, but before talking to him, pick up the following items:

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On the table on your left as soon as you enter the room.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. On a table in the back-middle of the room, on the other side of a medical bed.

500 Refined Element Zero - On a table to the right of where Mordin is working.

2,000 Refined Iridium - On the same table the Element Zero is on.

Now talk to Mordin, who is a very fast-talking character and a challenge to keep up with (we won't blame you for putting on subtitles). He at first tries to deduce who you are and why you're here:

You can pull the Renegade Interrupt for +5 Renegade Points .

However, if you're patient, the Renegade Interrupt will go away, and you'll get a Paragon Interrupt that you can pull for +5 Paragon Points .

Eventually, Mordin will ask you to go to the ventilation system to help disperse the cure:

Reply "I'll take care of it" for +2 Paragon Points .

Reply "Why can't anything be simple?" for +2 Renegade Points .

Right after the power cuts out. Mordin urges you to go, but also gives you a Side Quest: to find his missing assistant Daniel. Despite the Dialogue Wheel showing up, you don't get any Morality Points for whatever you reply with.

Lastly, if you healed the sick Batarian early into the level, you can say "I met a sick batarian" to send help out for him, netting you 40XP.

Now it's time to leave the clinic, and head towards the Environmental Control Center. This is where we'll get to use the good doctor's cure, in an attempt to heal all injured and sickly parties. Seek out the previously-locked door in the clinic near the Medical Station -- it will now be open.

Head up the stairs on the other side of the door, and immediately swing leftward. Hide behind the first piece of cover you find, and initiate hostilities on the Vorcha standing around: they should be completely oblivious to your presence until you open fire (unless you get too close).

A plethora of Vorcha, and some Krogan will assail your position, so pick them off as they draw near. Your party members should maneuver to areas that will serve them best, so worry only about yourself. Stay protected, revealing yourself to return fire on various foes as the opportunities reveal themselves. At the top edge of the room, begin working leftward towards long, thin staircase leading upward. More enemies will occupy that staircase, as well as the area around it, so stay alert!

Once all the enemies are down, explore the area for goodies, all of which are around the thin staircase.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. To the right of the thin stairs up to the next area.

Gambling Terminal - 3,000 Credits. To the left of the thin stairs, around the corner with the lightstand.

Bank Terminal - 5,000 Credits. A the top of the thin stairs in the back-left corner.

Continue into the next hallway and you'll see two doors: a close one to the left, and a locked one on the right. Enter the left-hand door and you'll discover Mordin's assistant Daniel has been captured by Batarians, who think that he's dispersing the plague itself rather than the cure for it. This is a delicate situation, which you can resolve in the following ways:

First, you have two options on the right that don't advance the conversation. Picking one of these will swap out both with different options:

If you're Paragon, open with "Everybody stay calm". This gets you a free +2 Paragon Points .

Picking "He's not my friend" doesn't reward anything.

Next, these are the options that conclude the conversation.

Pick "Let's talk this out" for +2 Paragon Points . Daniel will die.

Pick "[Signal Henchmen]" for +2 Renegade Points . Daniel will die.

Pick "No" won't give anything, and Daniel will die.

Use the "Nobody needs to die" Charm for +5 Paragon Points . Daniel will live.

Use the "Kill him, and you're next" Intimidate for +5 Renegade Points . Daniel will live.

If you used one of the two Persuasion options above, you get these two choices:

Pick "You can go" to let the Batarians go, to no further conflict.

Pick "No. I can't trust you" to kill the Batarians, to Daniel's horror.

If Daniel dies, you can Examine his body for some comments from your Squad Mates. If he lived, you can talk to him for one more parting comment.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. After the cutscene ends, this will be visible directly ahead, next to the couches and fallen plant.

Now return to the main hallway and head through the other door. Instead of going through the next door, take cover on the right: there are a few enemies to deal with here, all located on the far side of the room. Take them out before opening the door to reach the staircase, as you have plenty of cover to work with.

Once the enemies have been slain and the door has been open, dash down the stairs and toggle over to your sniper rifle, if you have one. As soon as you turn leftward through an open door, you'll see an enemy off in the distance on a balcony. This foe, with some friends, is shooting rockets from the safety of that location, and the only realistic way to deal with him is to use your sniper rifle to its fullest capacity. Rush forward and to the right a bit to get as close to him and his friends as possible so you can take them out.

You'll want to deal with them as fast as possible, because down below will be more enemies coming in through the ground floor. The balcony here is a very safe spot, so you'll have plenty of time to take out the Vorcha at your leisure before taking one of the stairs down and mopping up the rest. Surprisingly, while there's ammunition lying around for you post-battle, there are no items for you to gather otherwise.

When you're ready, press through the door that the Vorcha earlier poured out of; it has no green holo-button, instead it opens automatically when you get close. On the other side of the second door, you'll meet up with a few more Vorcha and Krogan. Take cover behind the door you came through when the enemies reveal themselves, as you'll be fighting in close quarters here, and can be easily felled if you aren't careful).

With those thugs down, explore a side area on the right-hand side here for goodies.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Sitting on the back wall directly ahead as you enter the right-hand side area.

Spare Parts - 1,000 Credits. In the back-right corner, to the right of the Med Kit described above.

Return to the central corridor, then head leftward and forward towards a series of uphill staircases. A Squad mate will comment that you're almost to the Environmental Control Center.

When you arrive in the Environmental Control Center, you'll find the Vorcha. These guys aren't too smart: they quickly let loose that they are, in fact, working for the Collectors. Here, you can answer:

"Why are you doing this?" for +2 Paragon Points .

The initial conflict you're faced with is quick to overcome: take cover and return fire on the few enemies that are guarding the main control panel. It's that control panel at the far end that will be used to insert the cure into the air supply throughout the Quarantine Zone, though placing the vial in the machine isn't even remotely all we have to do here.

Once you've killed the few enemies guarding the machine, dash up to it to place the cure within. That's step one. Unfortunately, there are two more steps to tend to before we're out of dodge.

Double unfortunately, there are far more enemies in the area who'll make themselves seen as soon as you place the cure to the disease within the central machine. Once that's done, make haste towards the nearest piece of cover, and stay there until things calm down.

When you get a moment, begin to return fire on the myriad enemies around you. The balcony above the door you entered from now has a few rocket-toting enemies, so break out your long-range weapon and take them out first and foremost.

Next, begin working your way to either side of the room, going down the stairs to reach parallel pathways (it doesn't matter which one you go to, since you need to go down both eventually). Once you've cleared the first corridor of enemies, run to the room they were guarding, then activate one of two fans. These fans must be turned on in order for the cure to make its way around the Quarantine Zone.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. In the fan control room, in the corner next to the door, farthest from the fan controls.

As for the other corridor, working your way to it will be more difficult than the approach (again, this is true regardless of which corridor/door you first breached). You'll need to not only fight your way back to the center of the room, but you'll need to fight a fresh force of Vorcha, and Krogan, AND elevated rocket launching Vorcha, once you approach the other yet-unexplored corridor. The fighting is furious here, so take your time, seek cover, and don't rush, or you'll meet an untimely death.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. As before, in fan control room the corner next to the door, furthest from the fan controls. MAKE SURE TO GET THIS BEFORE TURNING THE FANS ON, as you'll be taken back to Mordin's Clinic automatically!

Click the fans on to get taken back to Mordin's clinic, job done.

When you get back, the topic will quickly move to Daniel. The scene, and thus your choice of responses, will depend on if you saved Daniel, saved him but killed the Batarians, couldn't save Daniel, or even missed / skipped him altogether.

Rest assured that picking the upper-right option will give +2 Paragon Points .

And of course, the lower-right option will give +2 Renegade Points .

However this all went down, the cure to the Collectors' plague should now be dispersing through the Quarantine Zone. It's now time to invite the doctor to come along with you:

Pick "Will you join me?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Don't forget our deal" for +2 Renegade Points .

At this point, you can now decide whether to go straight to the Normandy, or to hang around in the Clinic. If you want to hear more remarks from people, you should decide to stay a while, especially if you're Paragon and have been telling everyone to go to the Clinic. You can talk to the Wounded Batarian, Daniel, the Turian Patient, the two apartment Refugees, the Batarian Patient, the Clinic Guard and both Clinic Receptionists. You can return to the Normandy by either of the doors, or by talking to Mordin again.

When you return to the Normandy, you'll be met with Mordin in the Comm Room. Here, you can answer...

"Cerberus hasn't changed" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Cerberus does good work" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then get not one but two Paragon Interrupts: pulling them won't give any Paragon Points, but if you ignore them you can say "You think this is fascinating?" for +2 Renegade Points .

Finally, your last options with Morality Points are:

"Stay focused, Professor" for +2 Renegade Points .

Now that you have Mordin, the Research Lab is now open. In addition to researching on Research Data you've found in the levels (as well as DLC armor and weapons for Legendary Edition players), every Squad Mate will have a Research Project to contribute if you ask them. Several of these will only benefit them specifically, but several characters like Jacob and Garrus will have projects that give upgrades to the Normandy's weapons and armor. If you have ANY interest in having a positive end mission, BUY THESE UPGRADES .

With Mordin on the team and the Research Lab unlocked, you can now talk to your various Squad Mates and ask about any Research projects they want to pitch you on. While several of these apply only to them, there are three that you'll definitely want to complete because they affect the final Mission of the game.

Here's what you need to know about them:

CIC - Talk to Mordin, Kelly, and Jacob about the Mission.

Crew Deck - There are new exchanges in the Crew Quarters room and the Mess Hall.

Engineering - If you bought Garrus' Thanix Cannon upgrade, Gabby and Ken will reference it in a new exchange. Zaeed will also have a story referencing Mordin, although you may have to spend a few Missions talking to him to loop to it.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Normandy - FBA Couplings - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Normandy: FBA Couplings Side-Quest, including where to find all the items, how to survive all
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Normandy: FBA Couplings Side-Quest, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

After you first board your new Normandy SR-2, you'll have the freedom to explore all four levels of the craft at will. If you head to the lowest floor, the Engineering area, then head through the pair of doors flanking the elevator, you'll find a couple of eager engineers that are ex-Alliance officers. These two are known as Engineers Kenneth "Ken" Donnelly and Gabriella "Gabby" Daniels, and they've been working together for quite some time. As you speak with them both, you'll learn that they know each other quite well, work together well, and have quite the history with one another.

But there's a problem: ask "Need anything?" and then "What's the issue?", and you'll learn that the FBA Couplings they're dealing with require incredibly frequent calibration (heh), while replacement couplings will make their lives much easier. This will add this Assignment added to your Journal, but you can further ask "Why don't you have them?" to learn more about why the T6-FBA Couplings are what they need (if you don't mind being bored with tech!).

Location: Omega Nebula - Sahrabarik - Omega - Kenn's Salvage

The discontinued T6-FBA Couplings aren't as difficult to track down as you might think, though knowing exactly where to go to look for them probably wouldn't hurt. Gabby suggested you can find some used FBA Couplings at the Omega Markets, so you should head there to begin your search.

While here, you may want to consider mining this planet Rich in resources:

When you arrive on Omega, pull up the map and locate the marker to the east called "($) Kenn's Salvage". This is where you can find the T6-FPA Couplings, but as you can no doubt tell by the map, it's not that intuitive to get there.

To find Kenn's Salvage, head to the exit door at the end of the main corridor to enter the main plaza. Here look to your right to spot two doors: you'll want to take the left-hand door labelled "lower section". This will take you down some stairs and directly in front of Kenn's Salvage.

Kenn is a Quarian desperately trying to get off Omega, which connects to an unrelated Assignment called " Omega: Struggling Quarian ". We actually recommend you talk to Kenn do this Assignment first, because you'll get a discount at Kenn's store if you do! But there's another way to get it: talk to Kenn and use one of the following Persuasion options:

Pick "Maybe we can cut a deal" to get a 12.5% discount and +5 Paragon Points.

Pick "Your prices are insulting" to get a 12.5% discount and +5 Paragon Points.

Regardless, to get what you need, interact with the Kenn's Salvage kiosk. Here you can buy the Nashan Stellar Dynamics T6-FBA Couplings . Its standard price is 500 credits, but with the discount it'll only cost 416!

Once you have what you need, return to the Normandy and back to the Engineering deck so you can give Gabby and Ken the good news. They'll be thrilled, as they cut back re-calibration time from everyday to every week -- a good deal indeed, one that will open them up to be able to do other things.

Excited, Donnelly will invite you to play a game of Skyllian-Five poker, which you can accept or decline. There's no reason not to accept, however, since you can earn credits by taking him up on the offer! Here's how to do that:

Pick "I'll play", then choose either the "Go easy on the new guy" Charm or the "Remember, I'm your boss" Intimidate to get 500 credits for winning Skyllian-Five poker.

Picking any other combination will get you nothing.

Unfortunately you can't actually play this form of poker. Bummer.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Namakli: Leviathan - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Namakli: Leviathan DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Namakli: Leviathan DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Mods: Assault Rifle Omni-Blade SMG High-Velocity Barrel SMG Mass Pulse Recoil System

Prerequisite: Complete " Citadel: Leviathan 2 "

Location: Pylos Nebula - Tap to Reveal - Tap to Reveal

Similar to the search for Dr. Garneau, your first order of business is to find the exact location of Ann Bryson, with how wide your search area being determined by how much search criteria you found back in " Citadel: Leviathan 2 ".

Unlike the hunt for Dr. Garneau, your search area will be only in the Pylos Nebula even in the broadest circumstance. If you'd like to narrow down the search however, you may still freely return to Dr. Bryson's Lab on the Citadel to look for more clues (which gives you some XP, by the way!). If you just want to get to Ann Bryson now, however, reveal the spoiler text below:

Even if you've got Ann's exact location, you'll want to explore the other systems in the Pylos Nebula, as they all contain their own discoveries to be made via the Search and Rescue mechanic. Use the chart below to help find them all!

Squad Tactics: Garrus is a very useful Squad Mate here thanks to his tank-like attributes and Armor-Piercing Ammo power. Having Overload is also helpful for the Marauders at the end of the level. James is similarly useful for being tank-like, with multiple powers focused on stripping Armor, as is being able to use assault rifles and shotguns. Ashley is also to be considered if you have her, especially if you don't have Garrus.

Garrus is a very useful Squad Mate here thanks to his tank-like attributes and Armor-Piercing Ammo power. Having Overload is also helpful for the Marauders at the end of the level.

James is similarly useful for being tank-like, with multiple powers focused on stripping Armor, as is being able to use assault rifles and shotguns.

Ashley is also to be considered if you have her, especially if you don't have Garrus.

Shepard's Loadout: You'll be facing a lot of enemies in tight quarters, so if you have to bring a limited selection of weapons, focus on close and mid-range weaponry . If you can spare one, however, a sniper rifle does occasionally come in handy. Due to the rather unique level hazard on this Mission, you may want to consider giving Shepard the Defense Matrix Bonus Power. This is unlocked after completing " Priority: Rannoch " and then talking to EDI; you can then assign it in the Medical Bay on the Crew Deck.

You'll be facing a lot of enemies in tight quarters, so if you have to bring a limited selection of weapons, focus on close and mid-range weaponry .

If you can spare one, however, a sniper rifle does occasionally come in handy.

Due to the rather unique level hazard on this Mission, you may want to consider giving Shepard the Defense Matrix Bonus Power. This is unlocked after completing " Priority: Rannoch " and then talking to EDI; you can then assign it in the Medical Bay on the Crew Deck.

Unlike the low-key and creepy Mahavid, the Namakli dig site is practically a war zone, being under constant bombardment and with high winds to boot. Kill the opening Husk that shows up, then dip into the building ahead on the right.

You may notice as you go through this level that Shepard will take fire from Harvester cannons, despite one not being present in the area. This is from all the ambient Harvesters flying around, and occurs after around 30 seconds to keep you moving. It can and will kill you. The only safe areas are inside the buildings: wait for the bombardment to let up and keep moving to the next area. This is why we suggested getting the Defense Matrix Bonus Power, as it instantly restores Shepard's shields.

As you enter the first building, Shepard will be contacted by Ann Bryson, and after a short discussion, Ann stays put while Shepard starts heading toward the elevator. When you approach the next building, it gets destroyed, forcing you to take an alternate route over its roof. Get used to this, it will happen multiple more times in this level!

Eventually you'll have to take a vertically zig-zagging route through an overturned building, after which you'll face the first Cannibals of the level. Kill them, then check the building for some loot:

AT-12 Raider - In the hand of a dead man, in front of the doorway into the building on the left-hand side that had Cannibals in it.

SMG High-Velocity Barrel - Head inside the building and check the left-hand wall of the back half of the building to find this, next to a counter.

Once you've gotten everything, approach the stairs to the elevator... only for a Harvester to blow them up. Damn. For an alternate route, check the back end of the nearby building and climb up the ladder onto the roof. Kill the Husk, then jump rightward onto the cliff.

Follow the path to some Bridge Controls and Activate it: the controls are down, so a Squad Mate will take the initiative to fix it. This leaves it up to you to defend them, at first from Husks, then from a Banshee once they're done with the repairs... in an area with no cover to speak of. Yeah.

Luckily there is something you can use to help: there are some olive green containers in this area that explode when you shoot them. They don't have a very wide blast radius though, so your victims will have to be very close in order to get damaged by them.

With the Banshee dead, wait for the rest of the platform to raise up so you can cross it. Climb up the ladder on the other end, run across the rooftop, then slide down the ladder on the far end. Kill the Husks that show up on the fallen roof of another building, then vault up onto it to get up to the elevator.

Use the Elevator Controls to summon the lift: use the View Prompt to watch it come down... and get stuck on some debris. Of course. Luckily Ann is able to help out: she opens up the door of the building to the level of the elevator, opening up an alternate route to a higher point of the lift so you can hop on there instead. Make sure to grab this item as you go:

SMG Mass Pulse Recoil System - Inside the building next to the Elevator Controls. Will be on the right-hand wall, on a keyboard under one of the wall monitors.

Head through to the end of the building, jump left across the gap to reach the stairs, then go up the stairs and vault up the ledges on the right. Here you'll be fighting some Cannibals, as well as the first Ravagers of the level. Take cover to avoid their cannons, and make sure to shoot the explosive container next to the Ravager up on the balcony to take out a chunk of its damage.

Data - 2,500 credits. Inside the building where the Cannibals were, on a keyboard under a wall monitor.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Climb up the ladder where the Ravagers were to enter a building. Kill the Cannibal in here, then grab this Med Kit from on top of the rusty PC towers objects on the right-hand side.

As you continue forward, Shepard will once again note that they're blocked thanks to a destroyed ladder. As before the solution is the same: turn around and climb up the ladder on the back end of the building you just walked past.

When you get to the top, make a U-turn to the left to get inside a destroyed building: vault over the overturned desk as Ann makes another call to Shepard regarding her injured workmate. As this happens, you'll fight a few Cannibals as to climb up ladders and walk across balconies.

After the second ladder, turn right to get to a unique battlefield among rows of columns. There's some Husks here that attack you from the start, but be aware that there's a Brute at the far end making its way to you. You can lure it next to the explosive containers in the middle here, but sadly they don't do quite as much damage as you'd hope.

The walkway above on the far end collapses, forcing you to divert around it on the right and down a ladder. Here you'll spot some Cannibals and Marauders on a balcony up ahead: stay on the balcony at the bottom of the ladder and snipe them from there. This is because moving forward will summon...

...a Harvester! Fortunately it doesn't have to be killed, just driven away, so focus fire on it to get it to fly elsewhere. That's not the end of it though: a Ravager will appear around the corner of the balcony to pot-shot you, and Cannibals when you head inside the building itself.

You'll have now cleared the way to the elevator, but make sure to collect these pieces of loot while you can:

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the inside corner of the balcony guarded by the Harvester.

Assault Rifle Omni-Blade - Inside the building, next to a countertop about halfway down the Harvester's building.

Damaged Machinery - 2,500 credits. On a terminal at the back wall of the Harvester's building.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Inside the wrecked building next to the Elevator Controls, next to some PC tower-like boxes.

Data - 5,000 credits. In the back-left corner of the wrecked building next to the elevator, under a wall monitor.

Use the Elevator Controls to ride it up and meet up with Ann Bryson in a cutscene. There's no Morality Points to be earned here (yeah, still!), and Ann takes you to the artifact... and a painting that implies that Leviathan is a rogue Reaper acting on its own. The artifact also takes control of Ann even as the Reapers try to find Leviathan's location through it, so Shepard's squad destroy it.

Of course the Reapers aren't just gonna let you leave with Ann just like that, and in addition to some Cannibals, that Harvester returns and makes a landing, preventing Cortez from picking you up. TAKE COVER!

Our preferred spot for this fight is the bridge where the artifact was: shoot the MANY explosive containers here, and the bridge will have a big hole in it. As a result, you'll now have an elevated position with some great cover, limited opportunities to be flanked, and you have the high ground!

Once the Harvester is destroyed, Cortez will be able to land, leaving you to mop up the remaining Marauders and Cannibals. Don't hop across immediately however! Return to the starting point and grab these items:

Med Kit - 50 XP. From the starting point, drop down the ledge, then look left to spot this on a corner desk.

Med Kit - 50 XP. From the starting point, cross over the battlefield and vault up into the open building on the other side. Here, look right to spot this on a corner desk.

Data - 2,500 credits. In the same building as the Med Kit described above. Will be a laptop in the back-right corner of the room.

Whether you grab the loot or not, you can end the level by running up the walkway where the shuttle is waiting. This will initiate the end of the level, even if there are still enemies in the area!

As this is a Leviathan DLC Mission, you can now get some more thoughts from your crew regarding the story so far:

Crew Deck - Talk to your Virmire Survivor, Liara and Garrus.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Prologue - Awakening - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Prologue - Awakening Mission on Lazarus Station, including how to get through all combat
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Prologue - Awakening Mission on Lazarus Station, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Weapons : M-3 Predator Pistol M-100 Grenade Launcher

Found Credits : Original release : 3,750 Legendary Edition : 7,500

At some point after creating your character, the station you're on will find itself under attack. You'll be alone here, but will receive instructions from an unknown woman via your comm. She'll instruct you to do three things here, in sequence.

The first is to pick up the pistol from the locker in the corner of the room.

M-3 Predator - In the locker in the back corner of the room. This is mandatory to progress the story.

Once you've grabbed it, you'll be able to work towards the door out of this room, where this mysterious woman will tell you to take cover, so that you aren't damaged by the subsequent explosion. Third and finally, you'll be told to pick up the pistol ammunition in the doorway before heading on your way.

If you've imported a Mass Effect 1 profile, pause and enter the Squad menu to distribute your available Squad Points. We highly recommend picking your class' unique Power (Combat Mastery for Soldiers) FIRST. This is because that ability will increase your total Paragon and Renegade points, making it easier to unlock the Charm / Intimidate dialogue choices for better story outcomes.

In the next room, you'll experience your first go with combat, though you'll only have a single, easy-to-destroy target to kill, a LOKI Mech. The game will first tell you to vault over the railing in front of you, and then quickly take cover behind a planter, while the robot you're going to be fighting storms into the room. Return fire on the robot and quickly take it out.

Mech down, head up the stairs it was one and through the door it emerged out of. You should be able to replenish your ammunition here via some Thermal Clips, as some should be strewn around on the floor.

In the following room, you'll again find yourself under attack, this time from seven or eight LOKI Mechs instead of just one. Thankfully, these foes aren't fast-moving or aggressive, nor can they aim exceptionally well, so you'll have plenty of time to deal with each one as they approach you.

Take cover and make sure to remain consistent in shooting these foes as they approach, since you can find yourself inundated and in serious trouble if they start to swarm your position. The good news is that, once all is quiet, you can find ammunition dropped by all of those enemies you killed. Very nice!

Head into the next room, where two scientists will be gunned down on the other side of the glass, then turn right to head into the next area, where you can pick up a new weapon:

Grenade Launcher - Next to the body of the Dead Soldier in front of the glass railing.

Take cover behind the glass railing, aim downwards, and take out the four robots that walk through the door with a single shot (they won't come through the door until you're armed and ready with the grenade launcher, so take your time).

Once the LOKI Mechs have fallen, you can switch back to your pistol and move towards the nearby elevator. Once you've taken the elevator down, follow more on-screen prompts. These will assist you in getting through the fire hazard ahead in one piece (you have to Sprint through it in order to survive).

The corridor you eventually encounter following the fire hazard will present you with what is, in essence, the very first fork in the road you'll face. While you need to turn right down the hallway to ultimately continue on with your quest, you should first go through the door ahead of you, which will lead to an isolated office with two crawling LOKI Mechs, and some goodies:

Wall Safe - 1,725 Credits. On the wall between the two Cerberus Laptops. In the original release, the Wall Safe must be bypassed, and only gives 975 credits.

In the original release, the Wall Safe must be bypassed, and only gives 975 credits.

Cerberus Laptop x2 - On the sides of this room, one on the left-hand corner desk, and the other on top of some shelves on the right.

Backtrack out of the office and continue down the corridor, heading up a staircase. At the top, look left for a man who gets blown up by a YMIR Mech on the other side of a window.

Public Computer - To the left of the window where the man gets blown up on the other side.

Head through the door at the top of the stairs and you'll be attacked by another crew of mechs from across a chasm on your left, but this time, you're going to have a little help in dealing with them (thankfully). A man named Jacob, who works on this ship, will be here to help you. Take out the LOKI Mechs, and you'll enter a conversation with him.

In this conversation with Jacob, you have three responses to pick from, with one on the left and two on the right. In general, left-hand responses will give longer replies, and will almost never give any Morality Points.

When the conversation begins, pick "I need answers!" for +2 Renegade Points .

After that, Jacob will take out another LOKI Mech and suggest you head for the shuttle. You'll again have the chance to get more Morality Points:

Pick "Just a few questions..." for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I'm tired of taking orders!" for +2 Renegade Points .

Eventually it becomes clear that you'll need to destroy the LOKI Mechs before you can have a decent conversation, and you'll be back in combat. As Jacob is a Biotic, you're able to command him to use his special skills in order to help you out in this conflict. In fact, you MUST use Pull on a Mech to stop any more from spawning in!

Once all is finally said and done, you'll be able to speak with Jacob at length about all sorts of topics, which will help shed some light on just what the hell is going on here. If you're curious, Jacob is the first permanent member of your team you've encountered.

Pick Jacob's brain about all sorts of other issues, and then, when you're ready, it's time to move towards the escape shuttles.

DataPad - Before leaving, check the seats here for a DataPad that gives yet more backstory.

At this point, Jacob is now officially part of your squad. If you've imported a Mass Effect 1 profile, you'll have some Squad Points to spend on him as well. We suggest focusing on Incendiary Ammo: it works great on Armor and organic targets, and can upgrade to Squad Incendiary Ammo at Rank 4, letting anyone on the squad use it (including Shepard!).

Head through the only open door nearby, and swing leftward down the next corridor. As you work down this hallway towards another door, Jacob will be in touch with his friend Wilson (a medical officer on the ship) who is trying to find an escape route for you and your new friend. When you walk into the next room, however, you'll have to deal with three LOKI Mechs before continuing.

As you head around the corner of this red room, you'll hear Wilson struggling remotely, as mechs get closer and closer to his location. Suddenly, he comes under fire. After giving you his location, everything goes quiet. We'll have to find our missing man before continuing. Exit and head down the corridor and up the stairs.

Cerberus Laptop - The way to Wilson is through the door on the right, but before doing that, head left to find a dead-end with another laptop with yet more backstory on the Lazarus Project.

When you finally head through the door, you'll find the man named Wilson. This is the guy that's been communicating with Jacob, trying to get you through to the shuttles, and ultimately to escape this under-siege station.

Pick "Let's get you out of here" for +2 Paragon Points .

However you respond, you're ultimately going to have to help him out with his leg injury.

In order to restore Wilson, you'll have to give him some Medi-Gel:

Medical Station - Look for the orange arrow that points you to the white-and-red Medical Station on the wall and open it.

Next, press the Right Bumper to open up the Power Wheel and then highlight Unity, then Use it. This will restore Wilson and start the next conversation.

During the conversation with the healed Wilson, you can some more Morality Points, first after Wilson explains why he was trying to fix the mechs:

Pick "It doesn't matter!" for +2 Renegade Points .

Later, Wilson accuses Miranda of being either dead or a traitor:

Pick "But she tried to help me" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Maybe, maybe not" for +2 Renegade Points .

Once this next conversation is over, more LOKI Mechs rush into the room. Wilson will point out some Explosive Crates for you that, once attacked, should take out the entire mech contingent with a single blow. In fact you must detonate the crates here to continue, as like with Jacob earlier the LOKI Mechs will keep appearing until you do. Wilson's Overload ability is a great way to do this.

With the mechs scorched, or otherwise downed, you'll get some answers from Jacob (though Wilson remains reluctant to give you any more information). Here, you can get yet more Morality Points when Jacob reveals who they all work for:

Pick "That sounds familiar..." for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "You lied to me" for +2 Renegade Points .

After that, Jacob says that he'll take Shepard to the Illusive Man:

Pick "I'll never work for Cerberus!" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "What are you after?" / "He'd better have answers" for +2 Renegade Points .

Datapad - 1,650 Credits. In the hallway after meeting Wilson, among some bodies. In the original release, you'll have to bypass the Datapad, and it only gives 900 credits.

In the original release, you'll have to bypass the Datapad, and it only gives 900 credits.

When you finally reach the hangar bay, you'll be near the escape shuttles, but you'll still have to fight through a mighty group of mechs. After dealing with the initial mech contingent upon entering the bay, you'll have two routes to choose from. You can either head left and up a ramps, or go rightward up some stairs.

We suggest taking the right-hand route, as this will have you only fight two groups of mechs rather than three. At the upper walkway, turn left and hide behind cover to take out the closest Mechs, then snipe out the mechs coming in from the distant room.

When the mech threat is nullified, it's time to do a little exploration. The room the mechs were pouring out of should be examined posthaste, before heading in the other direction to finish up the escape sequence.

Datapad - 1,720 Credits. Next to a dead officer in the room the mechs were coming out of. In the original release, the Datapad needs to be hacked, and only gives 975 credits.

In the original release, the Datapad needs to be hacked, and only gives 975 credits.

Wall Safe - 2,400 Credits. On the right-hand wall of the same room. In the original release, the Wall Safe doesn't have to by Bypassed, and only gives 900 credits.

In the original release, the Wall Safe doesn't have to by Bypassed, and only gives 900 credits.

The Wall Safe is the earliest point in the game you can do the Bypass minigame (in the Legendary Edition, at least). Here's how it works:

Your task is to link up four pairs of nodes using a cursor, before time runs out.

The node pairs are signified by symbols, which are revealed when you hover the cursor over a node.

Once you've selected a node, you'll have a few seconds to select the other one and complete the circuit.

If you make an incorrect connection, you'll be locked out and get no rewards.

If you select a node but are then unsure where its sibling is, wait a few seconds and the first one will be un-selected automatically, letting you try again.

It isn't too obvious, but the nodes and their connection lines trace along the circuit board background. You can use this to tell what the connections are in advance.

You technically have two timers. When the first timer runs out, you move on to the second one where the Credits are slowly drained, giving you less and less for when you do complete the Bypass. Once the second timer runs out, you're locked out of the object's rewards entirely.

If you're having trouble with the Bypass time limit, you can buy the Bypass Module from Serrice Technology on Illium for 30,000 Credits. You can visit Illium after completing " Horizon ".

With everything looted in the room, head to the room on the opposite side of the walkway (near where the right-hand path took you) and open the door to run into Miranda, who quickly shoots Wilson in the neck for betraying her.

Pick "I knew he was lying" for +2 Renegade Points .

However you respond, choose left-hand options to get the most information from her. When all is said and done, you'll need to board an escape vessel with both of them on board in order to bail out of here before it's too late.

On board the ship towards the vessel where the Illusive Man is located, Miranda will ask you a few quizzical questions, over the slight protests of Jacob, who thinks you should be left alone. The questions will be in regard to Shepard's backstory, so whatever you chose when you created them will be what you're asked about.

The specific responses you'll get for the background check varies depending on Shepard's Psychological Profile, but the mechanics are the same:

The upper-right response will always give +2 Paragon Points .

The lower-right response will always give +2 Renegade Points .

Picking "We're done here" (or any variation thereof) will end the interview entirely.

You'll next be asked about who you sacrificed on Virmire back in Mass Effect 1 (which will have been chosen for you if you started a fresh save and didn't do the Genesis DLC comic ).

Pick "It was a hard choice" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "It was that or die" for +2 Renegade Points .

You're now on another facility, Minuteman Station, owned and operated by the very same organization that revived Shepard -- Cerberus. Jacob and Miranda are both in your direct vicinity, but attempting to speak to either of them won't open up any sort of dialogue at this point. Rather, they'll tell you to go ahead and see the Illusive Man.

You won't meet face-to-face with the Illusive Man, because as he explains, that'd be too risky. Rather, he'll meet you via hologram, from an unknown location. It's all the same, though, since you'll be able to speak normally with him.

This conversation has a total of four pairs of responses that can give Paragon or Renegade Points when chosen. You can get eight Morality Points from this, and how many will be Paragon or Renegade depends on the responses you pick. For brevity, we'll group them by Morality rather than show all four pairs directly:

"You don't know me", "You're not my friend", "I'll need a lot of convincing" OR "Maybe I believe you" and "Do I have a choice? ( +8 Paragon total )

"I need some answers", "Skip the pleasantries", "Not bad" OR "Where do we start?" and "I'll find the evidence" ( +8 Renegade total )

Over the course of the conversation, the Illusive Man will inform you that he wants to ensure humanity's survival, and that it's currently under serious threat. He's revived you in order to ensure that you are the one who combats this threat, and tells you that step one is going to an Alliance colony that's under siege, a place called Freedom's Progress.

When your conversation with the Illusive Man has ended, and you've received your orders, you can head back to the previous area of the station. Now, when you attempt to speak with Miranda or Jacob, they'll actually have something to say to you. Be sure to speak with both, earning Paragon or Renegade points as you do.

Miranda is cold and calculated. She doesn't trust Shepard, and she thinks the Illusive Man made a mistake in retaining your free will upon your revival. She's all about the mission, and nothing else. While talking with her, you can get more Morality Points: up to +4 Paragon Points by picking the upper-right options as you go, or +4 Renegade Points for picking the lower-right ones.

Jacob, on the other hand, is far more personable, trustworthy and kind. You can speak with him about the mission as well, in addition to his past in the Alliance military (where Shepard hails from as well).

As with Miranda, you can get +4 Paragon Points via the upper-right options, or +4 Renegade Points for picking the lower-right ones.

When all is said and done, you can then approach the door on the far end of the deck to wrap up the first Mission of the game. Phew!

At this point, you'll see the Mission Complete screen, which is also where you'll be notified of any import bonuses! If Shepard also ever held 1,000,000 credits in Mass Effect 1, you'll also get +100,000 credits in Mass Effect 2.

The main bonuses however are based around Shepard's level, awarding XP, credits and Resources. How much you get depends on Shepard's level, as well as which version of the game you're playing:

There's also a second credit bonus, although which you get will depend on which version of the game you're playing:

Original release - If you got the "Rich" Achievement / Trophy and unlocked the Level VII Spectre Master Gear, you'll get 100,000 credits.

Legendary Edition - 10% of your credits will be carried over to Mass Effect 2, capping at 100,000 credits. For the maximum bonus here, you need to have at least 1,000,000 credits at the end of Mass Effect 1.

You can also get some additional bonuses for having a Mass Effect 2 save that's completed the main story, and best of all, three of them will stack with any Mass Effect 1 import bonuses! These include...

+25% XP for all Missions and Assignments.

Keep all Heavy Weapons. This is the only bonus that cannot apply to imported Mass Effect 1 saves: it only applies to imported Mass Effect 2 saves (aka "New Game +" runs).

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:
