articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Freedom's Progress level, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Weapons : M-8 Avenger (Soldiers only) M-23 Katana (Soldiers and Vanguards only) M-92 Mantis (Soldiers and Infiltrators only) M-4 Shuriken (all classes except Soldiers)

M-23 Katana (Soldiers and Vanguards only)

M-92 Mantis (Soldiers and Infiltrators only)

M-4 Shuriken (all classes except Soldiers)

On your transport ship to the colony of Freedom's Progress, you will learn that the Illusive Man has deemed Shepard to be the commanding officer, meaning that both the eager Jacob and the reluctant Miranda will have to take orders from you. During this opening conversation, you can get some Morality Points:

Choose "Someone could still be alive" for +2 Paragon Points .

Choose "Do whatever it takes" for +2 Renegade Points .

When you land on the planet, you can toggle through some new weapon options before heading out, although what weapons are available to you is subject to the Class you picked for your Shepard at the start of the game.

Once you've selected your weapon, it's time to investigate. The landing area your ship is resting on has nothing of interest on it, so head through the door adjacent to the ship. As you may have noticed by now, doors with a holographic green rectangle on them can be entered, so it's a good idea to look out for them to find discover areas of interest. Head through the door and you'll find yourself in some living quarters, eerily empty.

Push through to the back end and out the door to return outside. Swing leftward around the building and down a ramp. This outdoor area is adjacent to the ship's landing pad, though you couldn't access it earlier. To your right is a large stone wall with a wide door on it.

Spare Parts - 1,000 credits. To the left of the wide door in the large stone wall, on a stack of PC tower-like objects.

Now head through the wide door and immediately take cover from the mechs. Seeking cover to the left of the boxes, so that the boxes are on your right, is your best bet. This will cover you from both the enemies ahead, over the chasm, and the enemies storming your position to the right. You'll face a new mech type here, the FENRIS Mech. These dog-like machines will run across the battlefield to melee you directly, so you'll want to take them out quickly.

Once everyone is down, head up the stairs and then left through a door into an isolated room. It's completely dark in here, but there's some goodies at the far end near the doorway back outside.

Med Kit - 100 credits. At the back of this room in the especially dark area.

Wall Safe - 2,000 credits. On the wall near the Med Kit, between two bunk beds.

Exit the dwelling with caution, as there are two rogue mechs (a LOKI and a FENRIS) on the other side, waiting to eliminate you. Turn the corner quickly and take them both out as rapidly as you can.

Spare Parts - 1,000 credits. Standing back in the doorway and facing outside, these will be down the steps and on your left.

Now head across and into the next building to meet an old friend.

It's Tali! She's here with a team looking for a nervous Quarian, Veetor, although her kind have no love for Cerberus. Here's how this can go:

If you gave Tali the Geth Data in Mass Effect 1's " Tali and the Geth " Assignment, you can smooth things over by saying "I'll prove it's really me" for +5 Paragon Points .

Alternately, any player can pick "Don't point those guns at me" for +5 Renegade Points .

You'll have several more Paragon and Renegade point chances here as the conversation progresses and you team up with Tali's crew (whether you want to or not). They are:

Paragon : "I didn't have a choice", "We need to team up", and "Sounds like a plan" ( +6 Paragon Points total).

Renegade : "I did it to help humanity", "You think he's alive?", "We'll handle it from here", and "Forget it" ( +8 Renegade Points total).

With the reunion over, you'll be back to commanding the Commander. Exit the building and descend down the staircase and back into another building. Pull out a weapon, as there's a hidden LOKI Mech to the left of the countertop who can catch you by surprise.

Wall Safe - 2,000 credits. On the wall behind the kitchen sinks right where the LOKI Mech was.

Push rightward out of this room and back outside. As soon as you do, head to the left and take cover behind the guardrails. Myriad Assault and Rocket Drones will fire at you, flying at a good altitude above the chasm adjacent to you.

Jacob will recommend that you use Miranda's Overload on these enemies, and that will work just fine, though you could also use more conventional means to get the job done here too. Prepare for more than one wave of these enemies; they will come in droves and move quickly.

Med Kit - 100 credits. In the building marked with a 56, among the black couches in the back.

Head into the next building and down the winding ramp to encounter more Drones. Take cover behind the railing to keep safe so that you and your party can deal with the numerous Assault Drones and other robotic foes that show up here. Make sure to reload when needed, and shoot only when it's safe. There's really no way for the enemy to pincer you or hit your flank, so patience will pay off during this particular conflict.

At this point you're expected to head right to another large loading bay door for a Squad Positioning tutorial, but first, grab some loot!

Med Kit - 100 credits. At the top of the slope, on a crate.

Spare Parts - 1,000 credits. From the Med Kit, face away from the slope and head past the meal benches and concrete pipes to find this at the far end.

Loot in hand, head to the loading bay door and use the D-Pad to place Jacob and Miranda at the sides of the door, then take cover behind the low wall in the middle. This is an important skill, as you can place your Squad Mates strategically to help attack the enemy from multiple angles.

After witnessing the sheer destruction the YMIR Mech is capable of in a bloody and brutal cutscene, you'll have to do battle with it yourself. This foe packs a lot of firepower, requiring you to move around from cover to cover. Many pieces of cover can be destroyed if struck with enough rounds (like the large yellow-trimmed boxes), so be agile and ready to move if necessary.

The YMIR Mech has two lines of defense in the form of Shields and Armor. The Shield can be downed quickly with Overload and Disruptor Ammo, though you're going to need sustained strikes on the Armor to cut through it if you don't have Incendiary or Armor-Piercing Ammo. The YMIR has a LOT of firepower, so you should only attack it when it's not currently firing at you, otherwise you'll find yourself Shields down and on the floor incredibly quickly.

Once the YMIR Mech is down, it's time to explore the area for goodies.

Med Kit - 100 credits. In the building with a 25 with Tali in it, on some shelves.

Power Cells - 100 credits. In the building marked with a 95, close to the middle window and next to two black seats.

Wall Safe - 3,000 credits. On the wall between two bunks, in the same building as the Power Cells.

2,000 Refined Iridium - Near the disabled YMIR Mech, at the bottom of the steps that lead up to where Veetor is.

Damaged YMIR Mech - Heavy Weapon Ammo Research. The disabled YMIR Mech at the bottom of the steps leading up to Veetor.

Now that you have everything, head up the small ramp where the Damaged YMIR Mech was and enter the building to continue the story. Veetor is indeed in here, but he's still frantic and doesn't even seem to know you're in the room. You'll have two options here:

If you pick "You're safe now", you can then use a Paragon Interrupt to gently turn off his screens, gently alerting him to your presence. You get +7 Paragon Points total for these.

If you pick "Snap out of it!", you can then use a Renegade Interrupt to shoot at a screen and violently grab his attention. You get +7 Renegade Points total for these.

This will be your first experience with the Interrupt System, a brand new mechanic for Mass Effect 2. These button prompts allow Shepard to interrupt the conversation rather than waiting for the Dialogue Wheel to show up, and they align with either the Paragon or Renegade Morality. They're very action-based, so Shepard will often take direct action with them rather than using words like with the Dialogue Wheel. Interrupt prompts only appear on-screen for a few seconds, and outside of this instance with Veetor, you only get one chance to trigger them, then they're missed forever. Sadly, you don't get an indication of how long they appear on-screen for: that innovation wouldn't come until Mass Effect: Andromeda.

However you grabbed Veetor's attention, he'll tell you what he knows about the mysterious invaders, who Miranda and Jacob suspect are Collectors. You can use the Investigate options if you wish to learn more about them, then at the end of the conversation you can get some more Morality Points:

Pick "Thank you, Veetor" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "What a waste of time" for +2 Renegade Points .

That's not the end of it however! After Miranda tells you to grab Veetor and leave, Tali arrives and is very upset that Cerberus wants to take him away. This presents you with your first major choice in the game:

Picking "Veetor goes with Tali" will have Cerberus only use Veetor's Omni-tool data for +15 Paragon Points .

Picking "Veetor has to come with us" will have Cerberus take him for interrogation for +15 Renegade Points .

Whichever option you pick, you'll find yourself back at Minuteman Station in the virtual presence of the Illusive Man to discuss how the mission went down. Morality Points abound!

If you let Veetor go with Tali, you can pick "Having friends pays off" early on for +2 Paragon Points .

You can later pick "What aren't you telling me?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Towards the end of the conversation, you can choose these: Pick "I can't do it alone" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "Agreed!" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "I can't do it alone" for +2 Paragon Points .

When the conversation does end, the Illusive Man will introduce you to a long-lost friend, someone Shepard ensured had survived the explosion on the Normandy SR-1. Your old pilot, Joker, no longer works for the Alliance, and has come to lend his piloting talents and expertise to Cerberus (specifically you!). And he's going to pilot your brand new ship, a new, better, more advanced vessel. It is the SR-2, and Shepard and Joker waste no time in giving it a name: the Normandy.

Now that you've completed the three main Prologue Missions and gotten the Normandy, the galaxy has opened up to you. You can visit The Citadel, go to Omega, and explore various systems for Side Quests , and even start the Overlord DLC if you have it (although our walkthrough saves it until the end of the game).

That said, Mass Effect 2 does progress the story by using invisible countdowns that trigger story Missions, each with different requirements. The very first one is known as " Horizon ". Here's how activating it works now that you've completed Freedom's Progress:

The first mandatory story Mission, " Horizon ", occurs after you complete the core four Dossiers in the base game: " The Warlord ", " Archangel ", " The Professor " and " The Convict ". Once you have, you'll be locked out of the Galaxy Map and must " Horizon ". The two DLC Dossiers, " The Veteran " and " The Thief ", do NOT count towards this. As such we recommend you complete these early to expand your Squad Mate options.

The two DLC Dossiers, " The Veteran " and " The Thief ", do NOT count towards this. As such we recommend you complete these early to expand your Squad Mate options.

Mandatory story Missions like " Horizon " are always difficulty spikes, so it's useful to do as much OTHER stuff as possible to level Shepard and their Squad up for more Powers and Talents, earn Resources for Research Projects, and find / earn Credits to use in stores.

Dovetailing with the above, the second mandatory story Mission, " Tap to Reveal " unlocks after a post-" Horizon " countdown that ticks down with every Mission or Side Quest you complete, making it impossible to delay. That second mandatory story Mission is also one of the biggest difficulty spikes in the game, so it's actually better to prepare for it NOW since you can simply avoid the Dossier Missions to delay it as long as you need.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Dossier - Archangel - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Dossier: Archangel Mission on Omega, including how to get through all combat encounters,
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Dossier: Archangel Mission on Omega, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Research : Submachine Gun Damage Tech Damage

Location: Omega Nebula - Sahrabarik - Omega

This Dossier Mission is one of two that takes place on Omega, which is in the Sahrabarik system of the Omega Nebula . This is the system you started in after first acquiring the Normandy SR-2.

Now if you've been following this guide out of order and haven't been to Omega yet, when you first arrive you'll be met by two emissaries (the first one is fake), who demands that you meet with the local head of the station, Aria T'Loak. There's no pressure to do this immediately, despite his strong words.

If you're interested in mining, here's the one Rich planet in the system Omega is in, Sahrabarik:

Squad Tactics: Grunt is highly recommended for his Krogan Berserker power that lets him stand up to incredibly amounts of punishment. Zaeed is also great to bring along thanks to his Incendiary Ammo power to strip Armor, especially if you can upgrade it to Level 4.

Grunt is highly recommended for his Krogan Berserker power that lets him stand up to incredibly amounts of punishment.

Zaeed is also great to bring along thanks to his Incendiary Ammo power to strip Armor, especially if you can upgrade it to Level 4.

Unique Dialogue: Grunt and Zaeed uniquely have entire unique scenes in this Mission!

Grunt and Zaeed uniquely have entire unique scenes in this Mission!

Shepard's Loadout: If your Shepard isn't a Soldier or Infiltrator, you won't have access to a Sniper Rifle or Assault Rifle. If that's the case, you should HIGHLY consider equipping the M-5 Phalanx Heavy Pistol from " Dossier: The Professor " and / or the M-12 Locust from " Kasumi: Stolen Memory ".

If your Shepard isn't a Soldier or Infiltrator, you won't have access to a Sniper Rifle or Assault Rifle. If that's the case, you should HIGHLY consider equipping the M-5 Phalanx Heavy Pistol from " Dossier: The Professor " and / or the M-12 Locust from " Kasumi: Stolen Memory ".

Once you've done some shopping, and hopefully picked up Zaeed, you'll want to head into the Afterlife club. It's practically impossible to miss: it's the club with the huge display of dancing strippers above the main sign. The owner of the club, and of Omega, is Aria, and since she has many contacts with their ear to the ground, she's the best person to talk to to find out where Archangel is.

When you first enter, you can find Kylan among a group of Batarians on the left side of the entry corridor. Talk to them for some Morality Points:

Answer "Careful now" for +2 Paragon Points .

Answer "A dead man" for +2 Renegade Points .

The club itself doesn't have much to do within it, outside of a bar on the right side where you can order drinks. Drink three glasses, and Shepard will be intoxicated (for a few seconds, at least). You should head up the stairs in the back, which will lead you to Aria.

When you first meet with Aria, she has her men double-check that Shepard is in fact Shepard. More Morality Points can be earned here! First, when Aria has Shepard scanned:

Answer "Like hell" for +2 Renegade Points . This has to be chosen as soon as it appears.

Next, when Aria tells you the one rule of Omega:

Reply "Simple enough" for +2 Paragon Points .

Reply "I have similar rules" for +2 Renegade Points .

Aside from the Investigate options, you should stick to talking about Archangel for now: we'll tackle the Mordin stuff when we've put our sights on him. As you'll learn, Archangel is currently subject to the ire and firepower of all three Omega Gangs: the Blue Suns, Eclipse and the Blood Pack. You're going to have to sign up as a freelancer so you can infiltrate their operation and get Archangel out of there.

Descend the stairs from Aria, and you'll see the Batarian Merc Recruiter standing near some stairs: talk to him to start the cutscene.

If you're playing as a Female Shepard, you can use a Renegade Interrupt for +5 Renegade Points .

Regardless, the Batarian will have more information on Archangel, the mission, and all of the failures the mercenary groups have had in trying to deal with Archangel. It's the only reason the three main mercenary clans in Omega got together in the first place. Frankly, it seems like a suicide mission for any scrub out there, but of course, you aren't just any scrub.

You'll be signed up either way, but as you leave a teenager walks in intending to make a name for himself. More Morality Points here:

Answer "How old are you?" for +2 Paragon Points .

When the youth talks about his new gun...

Pull the Paragon Interrupt to send him away, getting you +5 Paragon Points .

Now that you're signed up, it's time to head over to the operation. Exit Omega and head right to the Transit Hub where all the Rapid Transit skycars are. Talk to the Blue Suns Driver and he'll take you over there.

When you arrive, yet another Batarian mercenary will brief you on the situation. Archangel has effectively barricaded himself inside a building, destroyed all conduits into it except a single bridge, and eliminated dozens of people trying to get him, including those unfortunate souls in a few gunships. You're on the team that will distract Archangel while a group of "elite" mercenaries flank his position. As you might guess, you'll use this to infiltrate yourself and give Archangel some backup so he can escape with you.

When you gain control of your party, run forward past the barricade on your right and enter the door. Here, you'll find some of the Eclipse sitting around the table. Talk to their leader, Jaroth, to learn a bit more about Archangel and why he's so invested in this.

Also in this room will be a Datapad, on a table to the left of the door out. You'll want to pick this up, as you'll start the " Omega: Archangel: Datapad Recovered " Assignment, and if you miss it, it's missed forever!

Once you leave the Eclipse room and turn left, you'll find yourself in another small corridor. Ignore the door straight ahead and instead go through the door to the left of it, in to a small closet. Do you remember EDI suggesting that hacking and messing with the mercenaries' machines might disrupt them in battle? Well, we're going to take care of that right now. Bypass the Friend or Foe ID of the Heavy Mech Diagnostic Station . Now when the Eclipse deploy the YMIR, it'll attack anybody!

Eezo Smuggling Accounts - 4,000 Credits. On the table on the left-hand side of the room.

500 Refined Element Zero - Also on the table on the left-hand side of the room.

Head back into the previous corridor and go through the only yet-unexplored door, then go straight through the door to find the leader of the Blood Pack, Garn. Talk to him here, and if you have Grunt in your Squad, you'll get a unique scene just for him.

When you work your way into the next area, you'll see a Vorcha get mowed down in front of you.

"Protection" Money Accounts - 6,000 Credits. Directly across the "sniper's alley" where the Vorcha just got shot, next to the body of another Vorcha.

From the Protection Money Accounts datapad, look left to spot a door with an orange holo-button. Bypass it to access a supply room with the following goodies:

Med Kit - 100 Credits. In the corner on your left immediately after you open the door.

Blue Suns Weapon Shipment - Submachine Gun Damage. On top of a white crate to the right of the Med Kit.

Blue Suns Gunrunning Accounts - 4,000 Credits. On the table to the right of the Weapon Shipment.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. On the table to the right of the Gunrunning Accounts.

Exit the supply room and continue down the wall and enter the door at the far end, near the holographic Utility sign.

Medical Station - 100 credits. At the far end of the hallway past the door.

Enter the door next to the Medical Station, then talk to Tarak for Morality Points:

Reply "Calm Down" for +2 Paragon Points .

Reply "What an ass" for +2 Renegade Points .

If you have Zaeed in your squad, you can additionally reply with "This should be good" for +2 Renegade Points again.

Once you've gotten everything, there's two last things to do. First, you can talk to the Freelancer hiding behind the corner just outside the Blue Suns hallway for a brief conversation. Second, if you hang around the central area with the view to Archangel's perch, you may find that they shoot you once to disable your Shields... and then nothing more. Interesting...

This is your LAST CHANCE to pick up the Datapad in the room with the Eclipse mercs from earlier! If you don't pick it up before talking the Sergeant Cathka, you'll miss out on two side quest Assignments!

Now cross over to the room with the gunship in it and talk to Cathka's assistant so that you can talk to Sergeant Cathka himself. During your conversation with him, you'll be interrupted by the beginning of the freelancer assault, so Cathka has to get to work. During this, Cathka will put away an electronic tool:

Take the Renegade Interrupt to zap Cathka out for +5 Renegade Points . Further, the gunship will show up later with half its health gone!

You'll now be in the assault on Archangel's base. If you didn't use the Paragon Interrupt to send the young freelancer away back at Omega, you'll see him be the first one killed here. Poor guy. The idea here is to get through the two-story structure ahead without getting Archangel killed.

Archangel's health meter appears on the screen below, and you'll have to do your best to protect him before he's outright killed (also keep in mind: he takes friendly fire from you!). Just be aware that once you fire your gun on one of them, the rest will know what you're up to and return the favor. Luckily, they're quite unprepared and should be a cinch for you to take down.

Once the freelancers are down, make sure to check the lower floor for goodies:

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Right in the middle of the room on the black shelving unit.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. In the back-right of the ground floor is a door under the staircase that is locked for now. Opposite the door will be this Med Kit on the shelves.

Omni-tool Power Boost X-Mods - Tech Damage. To the left of the stairs going up are some boxes, with this Research Data sitting on top of them.

Here's what you can find in the upper level:

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On the shelves at the top of the stairs.

Wall Safe - 4,000 Credits. From the Med Kit described above, turn left into the doorway. The Wall Safe will be on the right-hand wall here.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. From the Wall Safe, turn left again through another doorway and check the back-right corner of the room for a Med-Kit hidden behind the bed.

Now it's time to meet face-to-face with Archangel. After sniping an unsuspecting mercenary below, Archangel will remove their helmet and reveal their face. Wait... is that... Garrus?! That's right. It's your old friend Garrus. Well, assuming you recruited him in the first game. If you didn't, he'll remind you. But if you did recruit him in the last game, you can get some Morality Points!

Respond "It's good to see you" for +2 Paragon Points .

Respond "Is that you, Garrus?" for +2 Renegade Points .

Fed up with the red tape and not being able to make a difference in the Sovereign cleanup, Garrus traveled to Omega to punish as many evil persons as possible. And he's been so successful that previously-feuding Omega-based mercenary organizations have ganged up just to kill him. But now that you know that this is Garrus, getting him out of dodge is especially important. It's a good thing Garrus has a plan, then.

During this conversation, you can say "You shot me", which is why we asked you to stand around so that he could land at least one hit on you. You can also get some Morality Points:

While looking at the LOKI Mech, take the Renegade Interrupt to headshot it for +5 Renegade Points .

After that, you can end the conversation with... "They won't get through" for +2 Paragon Points . "Let's kick ass" for +2 Renegade Points .

"They won't get through" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Let's kick ass" for +2 Renegade Points .

For the time being, you're going to have to help Garrus survive this mercenary onslaught, which is easier said than done, especially on the higher difficulties. Your first task is the Eclipse assault over the bridge, which will be a sniper's paradise. The Incisor is especially great here if you have it, as you can take out multiple enemies between reloads.

Also, you can find some Thermal Clips among the furniture behind you. These don't disappear, so when you run out of ammo, use them to replenish your shots. This is what makes the sniper rifle such a viable option here.

Remember that YMIR Mech we had you hack earlier? If you did that, then the machine that appears here won't give you any trouble: it'll turn on the Eclipse and attack them instead. If you didn't hack the mech, however, you'll have to deal with it in addition to all of the freelancers and mechs (and after a few waves the YMIR Mech will revert to normal anyways). As always, keep an eye on Garrus' health throughout!

When that threat is finally nullified, it's time to speak to Garrus, but you should scout around for goodies first. Remember to pick up the Vindicator Battle Rifle if you didn't earlier!

Med Kit - 100 Credits. In the entry door to Garrus' area, look right to spot this Med Kid among the various objects on the floor.

Footlocker - 2,000 Credits. From the Med Kit described above, follow the wall away from the doorway towards the bunk bed. The footlocker will be behind it.

Once that's done, you can then talk with Garrus, during which the alarms sound. It appears that the mercenaries have finally figured out that there's an alternate route into the building. You can scurry off from here, but if you voice concern about leaving Garrus alone, you'll be able to leave one of your party members behind and get some Morality Points:

Pick "I'm not leaving you alone" to select a party member for Garrus for +5 Paragon Points .

Pick "You need help" to select a party member for Garrus for +5 Renegade Point s.

We recommend giving Garrus a partner, since if he's killed your mission will end in failure.

With Garrus (and one of your Squad Mates, preferably) left behind, it's time to take your other party member and head down the stairs and through the now-open door on the far end of the staircase. This will ultimately lead to a wide-open room with an open door straight ahead, and two closed doors flanking it. You'll be fighting the Blood Pack down here, which means Krogan, Vorcha and Varren.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. After going through the door under the stairs you'll see a Weapons Locker ahead of you. To its left will be this Medical Station, on a column at the top of the stairs down.

First things first -- run forward towards that middle door, clipping any enemies that might have appeared, and hit the green switch adjacent to the door jamb. Doing so will close the blast door nearby, but as you do this, a few enemies will appear ahead.

These guys are of the self-healing variety, so be sure to keep consistent fire on them to eliminate them, and be certain no one crosses the plane of the blast door, or you'll have to hit the switch once more. Concentrate only on enemies close enough that risk breaching the doorway.

Next head for the right-hand door, since it's the more difficult of the two remaining. It'll lead to a wide open, hangar-like room chock-full of hostile foes. You're going to have to move through this room slowly, since there are so many thugs trying to end you here. The mercenaries and their Varren allies are aggressive indeed, but you're going to have to hit the green switch at the far side of the hangar to end things.

Once the button is pressed, hold off any remaining enemies on the far side of the door for ten seconds, and the door will successfully close. Be sure to scour this wide-open area for much-needed ammunition.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. To the right of the security door will be some stairs blocked off by objects. Check the white crate here for the Med Kit on top.

Now all that's left to do is to get through the door on the left (make sure to grab the Med Kit to the left of the door there under the Utilities sign: you'll return to Garrus automatically once you're done here). We left this one for last because it's far easier to complete than the door on the right, though the problems here are far different in nature. Instead of a wide-open room, you'll have to fight within the confines of a thin, linear corridor.

Killing the foes you encounter here is pretty self-explanatory, though as you turn rightward at the corridor's only bend, you'll want to keep a keen eye out for a dangerous flamethrower-wielding enemy that can quickly eliminate you if you aren't careful. Otherwise, the same rules apply here -- dash forward towards the green door parallel to the door jamb and hit the switch. Then, keep all enemies away from the plane of the door for a full ten seconds. Successfully shutting all three doors will transport you back to Garrus' pad to fight the remaining forces.

Here you'll find that Garm and his best men have made it to Garrus' base, so you'll have to clear them out. Garm and his Berserker will make a break for the stairs to get to Garrus, so you need to do everything in your power to stop him. Once all the Blood Pack are down, you'll have to reunite with Garrus up on the second floor.

The final showdown with the Blue Suns is now, and they'll storm the building from via the windows, first on the second floor, then down on the ground floor. Post your party members at the balconies on either side of the second floor, then hide behind the column at the top of the stairs to guard the way up. The second wave of enemies, the Blue Suns, will be dropped from a gunship through various second floor windows. Here, it's VITAL that you keep Garrus alive: this is the last time you have to keep an eye on him, so make sure the Blue Suns don't concentrate on him.

Unfortunately, things get decidedly more difficult when it becomes clear that the gunship itself is going to attack. After brutally incapacitating Garrus, you and your Squad will be on your own to take out this threat. If you're playing on a higher difficulty you should use your Grenade Launcher Heavy Weapon to take chunks out of the gunship's armor, when it's not busy dropping off more Blue Suns. Luckily, you no longer have to worry about Garrus' health at this stage. Take down the Gunship, and it'll be mission accomplished (and you'll get +5 Paragon Points and +5 Renegade Points !).

With the gunship down, it's time to get off of Omega. Worry not, though -- you'll find yourself back in the safety of the Normandy automatically. Garrus was seriously injured in protecting his Archangel alter-ego back on Omega, and he's going to be worse for the wear. Or is he? As Jacob briefs Shepard on Garrus' injuries, the strong Turian himself shows up.

Here, you can reply "No worse than usual, buddy" for +2 Paragon Points .

After Jacob leaves the room, Garrus will voice his concern that you're working with Cerberus. Answer for some Morality Points:

Say "You've got my back" for +2 Paragon Points .

Say "Cerberus is right this time" for +2 Renegade Points .

Now it's time to catch up with everybody on the ship.

CIC : Talk to Kelly, then to Joker for thoughts on Garrus and four ambient comments. You may also want to talk to Jacob if you haven't reached the end of his conversations yet.

Crew Deck : You may want to talk to Miranda depending on if you reached the end of her conversations or not.

Engineering : Zaeed will have a comment about Archangel now that you've recruited him.

Garrus will have set himself up in the Main Battery, which is on the Crew's Quarters deck at the end of the Life Pod tunnel. There's a new EDI terminal here, and make sure to Examine the Monitoring Station on the left-hand wall for two new Codex entries. You should then talk with Garrus himself: he'll explain what he's been up to and how he managed to become the most hated and beloved man on Omega.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Horizon level, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Horizon level, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

The Horizon level is a mandatory story Mission, and marks the end of Act 2 in Mass Effect 2. Since Mass Effect 2's level structure is otherwise very open, it isn't obvious what the reasons are for triggering it. This is important because once it does, you're locked out of the Galaxy Map and must complete the Horizon level before doing anything else, and Horizon marks a difficulty spike that will punish those who are unprepared.

The Horizon Mission is triggered when you complete the original four Squad Mate Dossiers in any order :

" Dossier: Archangel " ( Tap to Reveal )

The two DLC Dossiers, The Veteran (Zaeed) and The Master Thief (Kasumi), don't count towards this progress.

Once you've acquired Grunt, Archangel, Mordin and Jack, then when you return to the Normandy, Kelly Chambers will tell you that the Illusive Man wants to see you in the Debriefing Room, and interacting with the Galaxy Map will only cause Joker to tell you the same thing. This means you are locked out of doing anything else until you talk to the Illusive Man, after which you're automatically taken to Horizon.

With that in mind, once you have one Dossier left to go, you'll want to start preparing for Horizon, since it represents a difficulty spike. For this guide, the last of the four Dossiers is The Convict, Jack. You can prepare by...

Assigning Talent Points to Shepard and their Squad Mates

Buying vital Research Projects from the stores on Omega and The Citadel

Spending Resources on Research Projects most useful to you in the Normandy's Tech Lab.

Research : Biotic Damage Heavy Skin Weave

While not a reward as such, after completing Horizon you can explore its system, Iera, in the Shadow Sea . If you're interested in mining, here's what you should look out for:

After you've gotten Grunt, Garrus, Mordin and Jack onto your Squad, you'll be told by Kelly (and Joker if you try to use the Galaxy Map) that the Illusive Man wants to talk to you in the Debriefing Room. That's the room with the long table located between the Armory and the Tech Lab. Use the Message Terminal on the table to get started.

The Illusive Man has urgent news for you: a human colony in the Terminus Systems, a place called Horizon, has just gone silent. If it's not under attack it will be soon, and you want to catch the Collectors in the act and save the colony. Almost as important is that your Virmire Survivor is there, so now you really want to get down there.

Following your conversation with the Illusive Man, Shepard will automatically see Dr. Solus in his lab on board the Normandy. Though little is said between the two, you'll see that the good doctor seems to have devised something that will help us avoid the paralyzing Seeker swarms while on the surface of Horizon.

The scene will then take us to the colony of Horizon. You'll witness this lush, green planet being quickly overrun by the alien Collector forces, its citizens paralyzed by the Seeker swarms. Then their leader, the Collector General, shows up by way of possessing one of his own soldiers. It seems he considers them and their harvesting of humans to be the "Harbinger of their ascension"... whatever that means.

Squad Tactics: Garrus and Zaeed are excellent choices because of their long-range prowess and high durability. Grunt 's proficiency with shotguns and his Incendiary Ammo power will see a lot of effective use during this Mission. Miranda is also a good choice because of her Warp power: many enemies in this level will be protected by Barriers, which Warp will strip. Kasumi is an interesting pick because of her Flashbang power. There's a powerful new enemy type introduced in this level that this power can immobilize, making them easier to deal with. She also has Shadow Strike, which can deal huge damage to a single ground-based target.

Garrus and Zaeed are excellent choices because of their long-range prowess and high durability.

Grunt 's proficiency with shotguns and his Incendiary Ammo power will see a lot of effective use during this Mission.

Miranda is also a good choice because of her Warp power: many enemies in this level will be protected by Barriers, which Warp will strip.

Kasumi is an interesting pick because of her Flashbang power. There's a powerful new enemy type introduced in this level that this power can immobilize, making them easier to deal with. She also has Shadow Strike, which can deal huge damage to a single ground-based target.

Unique Dialogue: For the most unique dialogue, bring along Garrus and Mordin .

For the most unique dialogue, bring along Garrus and Mordin .

Once the cutscene is over, you'll have control of Shepard. Move forward down the linear path and Dr. Solus will communicate with you (either from the Normandy, or in-person if he's in your Squad) about your suit upgrades, which should keep the Collectors' Seeker Swarms at bay. However we won't know for sure that it'll work until it's put to the test (don't worry -- it works).

As the linear path curves leftward, have your weapon-of-choice at the ready. You'll meet a detachment of Collectors amongst the boxes and crates in the middle of the path. Use the crates and pillars as cover as you eliminate these powerful, aggressive foes. What makes Collectors extra trouble is that they use truly alien weaponry that don't drop Thermal Clips: if you need more ammo, you have to rely on what you can find in the environment since the Collectors won't drop any!

When all is quiet, explore the lower area with the boxes and pickup trucks.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. In front of the back-most yellow pickup truck.

Datapad - 6,000 Credits. On a picnic bench behind the pickup truck where you found the Power Cells.

As you continue further down the linear pathway from the previous area, you'll lose communications with Joker back on the Normandy.

Eventually you'll come to a valley between colony dwellings: Collectors of all kinds will attack here, so seek cover and take them out one at a time. None of them are too powerful per se, but they are equipped with strong weapons and fight aggressively. Making matters even more mysterious here is that you'll be fighting Husks. For those who didn't play the first Mass Effect, Husks are like zombies and will swarm your position in groups, forcing you out of cover.

Once everyone is down, return to the entry of this area and then face the way forwards.

Datapad - 4,200 credits. Enter the right-hand building on your right (marked with a red 5 on the outside wall) to find this.

Dead Collector - Heavy Skin Weave Research Data. Walk through to the back of the building and exit it onto the balcony, then turn left and head down the steps and up the hill: keep an eye on your right for a Dead Collector you can Examine near a picnic table.

Continue uphill and take a right, and you'll run into a Dead Husk. Once examined, a brief cutscene will ensue with you and your chosen teammates. You can hypothesize about why the Husks are here, and why the Collectors are creating them. But one thing is for sure -- these Husks seem better... stronger... more evolved. At the end of the conversation, you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "Let's go save the colonists" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "We're wasting time here" for +2 Renegade Points .

Continue forward from the Geth corpse, and you'll end up in another valley between colony dwellings, this one with much more undulating terrain. You'll also pass by Collector Pods; remember these as we'll ask you to return to them after the battle. You'll see Collectors of various types walking around ahead, but if you work your way through the dwelling on the right side, you can get the jump on them. However, the gunfire will alert the rest of the powerful Collector contingent here to your presence.

Get ready to take cover and deal with the repercussions (or should we say REAPERcussions ?). The balcony at the far end of the trailer on the right is a great place to spring off from in order to deal with the enemies streaming out from the area directly in front of it, and you can try to count on your teammates to deal with the stragglers down in the courtyard area to your left. Your job isn't finished in the valley either: some more Collectors will show up in a raised plaza at the far end and to the left. Make sure to take care of them, too!

Once you're done, scour the area for goodies.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Return to area where the Collector Pods and face the way forwards. Look left to spot a dwelling with a glass awning above the entryway: the Med Kit is on a bed on the right wall.

Safe - 4,800 Credits. Return to the Collector Pods and this time enter the building on the right: the Safe will be on the right-hand wall, between a glass lab container and a medical bed.

Now continue through the level and across the raised plaza: here you can Examine some Stasis Colonists: humans frozen by the Seeker Swarms who have yet to be put in pods by Collectors. Head up the stairs nearby to find more, then enter the dwelling at the top.

Computer - 3,000 Credits. At the top of the stairs near the Stasis Colonists, head to the back of the room to find this on the bed.

Collector Particle Beam - Return to the Stasis Colonists, then go down the steps to the next "valley". Resting on a Collector Pod on the left is this Heavy Weapon.

Now head forward for a new cutscene, where things truly hit the fan. It seems the Collector General has recognized Shepard's threat and has come to settle matters personally by possessing one of his own men, transforming them into the unit known as Harbinger. Harbinger is a dangerous foe with formidable Barrier and Armor defenses, and is able to fire biotic attacks that deal heavy damage and knock Shepard out of cover, even when hitting the other side of what you're hiding behind. You'll want to prioritize killing his agent first, then killing any other Collectors before he has a chance to possess them and re-enter the battle.

Cover here isn't as plentiful as you'd probably like, but that's okay. Remain aggressive, and keep moving closer to the Collectors, as you bounce from cover to cover. The closer you get to the enemies, the easier they will be to fell, though being close in proximity to any enemy will also make it easy for them to storm your position and cause massive damage. This might be one of the more difficult battles you've faced so far, so remain persistent, overcome those pesky barriers, and lay waste to these vanguards of your destruction.

When all is said and done, return to looking for collectibles. Go back to the Collector Pod between the two dwellings where you picked up the Particle Beam.

Computer - 3,000 Credits. From the Particle Beam spot, look forwards to the giant AA Gun in the distance. On your right is a dwelling with a red 6 on the side: enter it and go to the far end to find the Computer on the round table in the corner.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. Return outside and face forwards to the AA Gun again. Head to the building in the back-left corner of the area with a red 9 on it: the Power Cells are inside next to the crates.

The next section marks the point of no return for Horizon. If there's any collectibles from earlier in the level you didn't get, make sure to grab 'em!

Now look for the blast door at the end of this area on the right: enter it to bump into a survivor, Delan. As you'll find out, he's a huge skeptic of the Alliance, so it's a good thing that Shepard keeps quiet about who they are and that they're still loyal to their Alliance roots. But he does bring up the AA Defense Towers, which you can use on the Collector Ship!

You can get some Morality Points during this conversation:

At the outset, answer "Calm down!" for +2 Renegade Points .

After the man frets over who the Collector's took, pick "Who are you?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Further in, you can say one of the following: "Wait here" for +2 Paragon Points . "We might need your help" and then "You're a coward" for +2 Renegade Points .

"We might need your help" and then "You're a coward" for +2 Renegade Points .

When you regain control of your party, check the room for loot.

Wall Safe - 6,000 Credits. On the wall directly behind Delan (as in the screenshot above).

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Right behind Delan the Mechanic in the right-hand corner.

2,000 Refined Platinum - In the opposite end of the room, on top of a crate next to the Weapon Locker.

Use the Weapons Locker to switch out the Collector Particle Beam if you'd prefer another Heavy Weapon. Just keep in mind that you'll need to re-apply your Ammo Powers and what your two "in use" guns are, since they'll have been reset by interacting with the Weapons Locker.

As you proceed forward from the door, make a note of your surroundings: this is a vast battlefield and we'll ask you to return to the entry point for collectibles later. Up ahead, you'll encounter yet another detachment of Collector foes. This fight introduces a powerful new form of Husk known as a the Scion: he fires Shockwave explosions that travel in a line. This travels straight over all cover objects, so being nimble to move to new cover is essential against them.

When things quiet down, you'll want to explore.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. Return to the entry of the battlefield and face the way forward. Look left to spot a building with a glass awning over the entry: head inside and walk straight through to the balcony on the opposite end. Once there, look left to spot the Power Cells on top of a crate.

Dead Collector - Biotic Damage. From the Power Cells, turn around and re-enter the building, then go through the left-hand doorway. Go across the balcony and straight through the small building, then turn left. Go up the small steps in front of you to find the Dead Collector on your right.

Computer - 3,00 Credits. Go to the blast door exit, then go either left or right through the corner buildings, then out and up the stairs to the upper area. In the middle of it will be the Computer.

When you enter this next region via the hacked door, dash to the right side of this large outdoor area and immediately seek cover behind the wall up the ramp there. Scions and weak Husks will appear in this area, and the latter will appear in great numbers. Don't forget that your character can use melee attacks on nearby enemies (the B button on Xbox, Circle for PlayStation), and you're likely going to need it with regularity if you find yourself inundated with Husks.

With the Husks downed, you can then concentrate on the Scions. These guys are powerful, so feel free to break out that special Collectors weapon we mentioned earlier (and that you found earlier) to take them out easily. If you're not quick in eliminating those foes, you could be in for a world of hurt. You've been warned!

With the initial wave of Husks and Scions killed, you're going to want to first run around this outdoor area and collect any ammunition you might need: this will be the last breathing point you have before the end of the level, and this next section is tough.

Power Cell - 100 Credits. On the far right of the Transmission Tower Computer, up some steps on the side of a building.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On the far left of the Transmission Tower Computer, on a slightly raised walkway.

After you've replenished your ammo, you can then Hack the Computer terminal in the center of the area. Doing so will begin the process of activating the Alliance defense system here, which will in turn be used on the Collectors' ship, hopefully destroying it. Unfortunately, as EDI will let you know, the defense system will take a little while to get online. And you know what that means -- plenty of enemy encounters in the meantime.

Harbinger will return here, so you're going to want to try and focus on him. You'll also need to deal with his crew of Husks. Remember -- these guys are quite aggressive and quite obnoxious, but also defensively weak, so try and take the time to eliminate them en masse before you focus on the Harbinger himself. As you know, the Harbinger takes a load of damage to bring down, so keep an eye on your health (and that of your Squad), and remain focused on thinning his shields and ultimately bringing him down. The two waves of foes you deal with come from separate sides of this courtyard, so adjust your positioning accordingly. Good cover is important: the area around the Computer is frightfully exposed.

The Collectors, at this point, have had about enough of your nonsense, and from their mothership comes the Praetorian, a bug-like Husk that's without question the hardest enemy in the level. In addition to multiple levels of shields and health, the Praetorian has a Barrier that refills itself automatically if it isn't damaged. after a while This complicates the battle and then some, especially when you consider how powerful the Praetorian's attacks are. And to make things worse the Praetorian will have a ground slam attack that not only releases a damaging shockwave, but can completely refill their Barrier.

Keep moving, keep your shields up, and heal if necessary. Then, when opportunities present themselves, lay into your foe (with heavy weaponry, if applicable), ultimately bringing it down to the ground. Once the mighty Praetorian has fallen, you'll witness a couple of mission-ending cutscenes. And if you're curious about the word Praetorian, yes -- it's from Roman times.

The ending cutscene will have you finally reunite with your Virmire Survivor: as noted earlier, this can be either the biotic Kaidan Alenko or the soldier Ashley Williams, depending on who you chose to save on Virmire back in Mass Effect or the Genesis DLC comic (if you started Mass Effect 2 totally fresh, you'll have Ashley). As such, we'll refer to them as the Virmire Survivor, a popular term for whoever you saved when they appear after the first game.

The conversation is pretty lengthy, and while it's clear that they're happy Shepard is alive again, they're beyond upset that Shepard made no attempt to contact them, and that they're working with Cerberus, a pro-human group so extreme that even Ashley doesn't like them at all. Your opening response can earn you some Morality Points, so here's what you can pick:

"You sound angry" or "It's good to see you again", the latter of which will give you +2 Paragon Points , which lets you choose one of these two responses. "I didn't want to hurt you" ( Romance ) / "Too much time has passed" for +2 Paragon Points . "I have important things to do" for +2 Renegade Points .

"I didn't want to hurt you" ( Romance ) / "Too much time has passed" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I have important things to do" for +2 Renegade Points .

"I was. We can't get into it" will give +2 Renegade Points .

After this, you'll have several more responses you can pick that will earn you Morality Points. As ever, here are your options grouped by Morality:

Paragon : "Cerberus isn't the enemy", "I'm not a traitor", "You're too emotional, [Ash/Kaidan]", and "Don't go. Join me" ( +8 Paragon Points total)

Renegade : "I don't work for Cerberus", "Get over it", and "Fat chance" ( +6 Renegade Points total)

Unfortunately, nothing you say will change your Virmire Survivor from being upset with Shepard, and they'll leave with a lot of bad blood in the air. Shepard will then call in Joker, having had enough of Horizon. You will get +5 Paragon Points and +5 Renegade Points for completing the Mission, at least.

After the conclusion of the events on Horizon, you'll be automatically transported back to the Normandy for a debriefing with the Illusive Man. It comes to light during your conversation that the Illusive Man set things up to draw both the Virmire Survivor and the Collectors to Horizon. It worked, even if two-thirds of the colonists were captured in the process. Apparently the Illusive Man considers that an acceptable loss.

During the conversation, you can again give various responses that will yield Morality Points. Here's your selection, per Morality:

Paragon : "I didn't save everyone", "No more colonies get hit", "My team is strong" ( +6 Paragon Points total)

Renegade : "I enjoyed the fight", "Let's go on the offensive", "Don't worry so much" ( +6 Renegade Points total).

Also, don't forget to mine the Shadow Sea for Resources!

Once you have full control of Shepard again, it's time to do your rounds. This is the earliest point in time where you can pick up a Loyalty Mission. Loyalty Missions are excursions that are optional, but are HIGHLY recommended you do because they go a long way to ensuring a positive outcome at the end of the game. Completing them is also required for initiating a Romance with them.

CIC - Talk to Jacob for his Loyalty Mission, then Kelly and Joker.

Crew Deck - There's a new exchange to hear in the Mess Hall. Talk to Miranda for her Loyalty Mission.

Engineering - Pop by Gabby and Ken: they'll likely talk about the Thanix Cannon or Silaris Armor if you've installed them. Also talk to Jack to learn more about her, and Zaeed for a comment on Horizon.

Completing Horizon is the earliest point in time that you can initiate the Arrival DLC. If you have this, then it's practically mandatory to at least get debriefed on it, since it happens automatically when using the Private Terminal (you may want to make a backup save before doing that so you can view its first cutscene again). For our guide, we save Arrival until the post-game for story reasons. There's no repercussions for doing this.

At this point, you'll now have a varied future ahead of you. You'll be given three more Dossiers to complete your Squad lineup, and you'll soon learn that you'll need to resolve personal matters with your Squad in order to make sure their minds are focused and they are Loyal to the mission, and Commander Shepard.

More importantly, there is now an invisible countdown in place for the next mandatory story Mission. The exact mechanics behind this are still not 100% understood, but in general there are three parts of the countdown you need to know about:

You need to have eight Squad Mates - Unless you deliberately ignored Zaeed, Kasumi, and didn't awaken Grunt, all players will only need to gain one more Squad Mate after Horizon to meet this.

You need to complete five Missions and / or Side Quests - This includes Dossiers, Loyalty Missions , N7 Side Quests , or DLC like Overlord and Lair of the Shadow Broker . Minor Side Quests that do not have their own level, as well as the Normandy Crash Site , do not count towards this.

You must be on the Normandy - Like with Horizon you'll be locked out of the Galaxy Map, but you can belay this via worlds that have more than one Mission on them, like Ilium or Tuchanka. This is because they return you to the planet's hub area rather than the Normandy. The only complication is completing Miranda's Loyalty Mission : if you also did Jack's Loyalty Mission, you'll be taken to the Normandy to resolve their fight.

The only complication is completing Miranda's Loyalty Mission : if you also did Jack's Loyalty Mission, you'll be taken to the Normandy to resolve their fight.

The Mission this takes you to is ultimately an excursion: you can return to business as usual afterwards. HOWEVER, completing it will unlock another Mission you can do which, although it isn't obvious, kick-starts the journey to the end of the game.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:
