articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Grunt: Rite of Passage Loyalty Mission on Tuchanka, including how to get through all combat
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Grunt: Rite of Passage Loyalty Mission on Tuchanka, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

To begin this optional (yet main story) quest, you'll need to speak with Grunt when Kelly says Grunt would like to speak with you. Grun's Loyalty Mission unlocks after Jacob, Miranda, Jack and Mordin's. You can progress through this list by completing Missions, DLC or the N7 Side Quests . You'll also need to have talked to Grunt at least once after awakening him from his tank.

You'll find Grunt in bad shape. He doesn't know what's wrong with him and has an uncontrollable urge to kill things, and doesn't know what to do about it. After a brief consultation with EDI, it's decided that it's to head to the Krogan homeworld of Tuchanka, the Krogan homeworld (after the Genophage, the Krogan aren't really willing to share any medical data with aliens).

Location : Krogan DMZ - Aralakh - Tuchanka

Now, it's time to head to Tuchanka itself. If you've been following this walkthrough to a tee (and we hope you have been), then you have just finished everything up on Illium and are visiting Tuchanka for the first time. In the Galaxy Map, the Krogan DMZ is located just "south" of the Serpent Nebula , where the Citadel is. Tuchanka will be in the Relay system you arrive in, Aralakh.

If you're interested in mining, here are the Rich planets in the Aralakh system:

Squad Tactics: Grunt is required to be on your squad, as this is his Loyalty Mission. You may want to consider upgrading his Incendiary Ammo to Squad Incendiary Ammo, so that everyone on the team can take advantage of it. Mordin is a good companion as his Incinerate can be used to strip Armor. Miranda is a slightly unconventional choice as her Warp ability also strips Armor!

Grunt is required to be on your squad, as this is his Loyalty Mission. You may want to consider upgrading his Incendiary Ammo to Squad Incendiary Ammo, so that everyone on the team can take advantage of it.

Mordin is a good companion as his Incinerate can be used to strip Armor.

Miranda is a slightly unconventional choice as her Warp ability also strips Armor!

Unique Dialogue: Garrus will come with the most interesting unique dialogue for this Mission.

Garrus will come with the most interesting unique dialogue for this Mission.

Shepard's Loadout: Consider getting the "side-upgrades" for Assault Rifles, Heavy Pistols and Sniper Rifles. Their "Armor Penetration" upgrades unlock after 2 damage upgrades, while 3 damage upgrades unlocks a unique one for each weapon type: Assault Rifles get "Assault Rifle Accuracy" after three damage upgrades. Heavy Pistols get "AP Heavy Pistol Critical" after three damage upgrades. Sniper Rifles get "Sniper Headshot Damage" after three damage upgrades.

Consider getting the "side-upgrades" for Assault Rifles, Heavy Pistols and Sniper Rifles. Their "Armor Penetration" upgrades unlock after 2 damage upgrades, while 3 damage upgrades unlocks a unique one for each weapon type: Assault Rifles get "Assault Rifle Accuracy" after three damage upgrades. Heavy Pistols get "AP Heavy Pistol Critical" after three damage upgrades. Sniper Rifles get "Sniper Headshot Damage" after three damage upgrades.

Assault Rifles get "Assault Rifle Accuracy" after three damage upgrades.

Heavy Pistols get "AP Heavy Pistol Critical" after three damage upgrades.

Sniper Rifles get "Sniper Headshot Damage" after three damage upgrades.

If this is your first time visiting Tuchanka, then as you go down the ramp from the Landing Platform you'll be intercepted by an Overcaptain, who says you should see the Clan Leader and give Grunt "The Rite" or put him down. Ignore that second request and head through door behind him and to the end of the tunnel.

Whoever the Clan Leader is, speak to them on their makeshift throne and pick "What's wrong with Grunt?". Grunt will explain his origins as a creation of Okeer, who turns out to be a rather hated name.

Here, you can pick the lower-right option for +2 Renegade Points (what it'll be depends on if the Clan Leader is Wrex or Wreav).

The Clan Leader determines that nothing's actually wrong with him: he's becoming an adult.

Grunt's strong urges to kill still need a focus however, something to represent, so the Clan Leader suggests they take The Rite to become a part of Clan Urdnot (which pisses off Gatatog Uvenk enough that he storms off).

Answer "His call" for +2 Paragon Points .

You'll then be told to speak with the Shaman.

To get to the Shaman, depart the Urdnot Throne area and head directly forwards; you'll find a staircase on your left. At the top will be the Shaman, but you can also find a Nakmor Ambassador you can talk to to learn more about Krogan clan politics (if you can use one of the Persuasion options, that is!).

Now talk to the Shaman, who is arguing with Gatatog Uvenk.

Reply with "We have permission for +2 Paragon Points .

Reply with "He dares stand in Grunt's way?" or "I want this crap over with" for +2 Renegade Points .

Regardless, Uvenk will still put up a fuss, and you can pull a Renegade Interrupt to headbutt Uvenk as a show of force for +5 Renegade Points . Ignore it, and you can do the following:

Say "You defy a shaman?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Say "Do you want to die, Uvenk?" or "Let's get this crap going!" at any time for +2 Renegade Points .

Say "What is your problem, Uvenk?". This lets you follow up with one of these (at the expense of the "You defy a shaman?" option): "You argue like an alien" Charm for +2 Paragon Points . "So you're fearful" Intimidate for +2 Renegade Points .

"You argue like an alien" Charm for +2 Paragon Points .

"So you're fearful" Intimidate for +2 Renegade Points .

Once you've finally convinced all parties involved that Grunt deserves to take the Rite, and that you and your Squad will stand with him as his krantt, you'll be transported to the location where the Rite is to take place. Are you ready?

When you arrive the location of the Rite, you'll see a green "Keystone" button that you can Activate. You'll actually want to ignore it for now as this area has a lot of loot that you'll want to pick up!

Turbine Parts - 3,600 Credits. To the right of the Keystone button.

Urdnot Corpse - 1,200 Credits. From the Turbine parts, turn around and head for the stairs on your left: at the top of the stairs is an Urdnot Corpse to Search.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Down the stairs from the Urdnot Corpse and to the right.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. Next to the Med Kit described above.

Urdnot Corpse - 1,800 Credits. Return to upper part of the arena and go to the rusty circular hatch in the middle.

Urdnot Corpse - 1,500 Credits. Near the Urdnot Corpse described above.

Med Kit - 100 Credits Near the Urdnot Corpses described above.

2,000 Refined Platinum - Standing on the rusty hatch, face away the from the Keystone button and you'll see this between two columns on your right.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Next to the Refined Platinum described above.

Urdnot Corpse - 1,500 Credits. Return to the rusty hatch and face the Keystone button. Turn left and head past the column: you'll find this at the top of the stairs here.

Turbine Parts - 3,300 Credits. Directly to the left of the Keystone button.

When you're done searching and collecting, hit the Keystone button to begin. The Rite occurs in three distinct, separate rounds, and the game will save for you after each one is successfully overcome. You can tell when a round is over by checking the Keystone button: it'll remain red until the round is over, after which it'll turn green.

The first wave you have to deal with is, not surprisingly, the easiest. Once you've struck the keystone, Varren will begin to appear from the raised staircases in the two corners opposite the Keystone structure. across the courtyard. These dog-like creatures will be familiar to Mass Effect 1 players: they have weak health but will storm your position to maul you, so you'll want to take them out fast.

Though they come in great numbers, they are always spread out, so as long as you're efficient in killing them, no more than three or so should be on the screen chasing you at once. You'll face three waves of Varren before the round ends.

The second wave of foes is decidedly more difficult to deal with. After hitting the keystone a second time, a huge flying beast known as a Harvester will land in. You can't damage it, instead it'll drop a pair of hellish-looking creatures known as Klixen. If you haven't fought these before, they're pure melee enemies that move surprisingly fast.

Shooting the Klixen from afar is a necessity because they explode when killed, knocking back and damaging anybody nearby. These guys are damage sponges, so feel free to use some heavy explosives to take them out en masse. Otherwise, dealing with them spread across the map, one or two at a time, is easy enough with your conventional set of weapons. You'll deal with a total of eight pairs of Klixen during this round.

After the Klixen waves have been felled, it's time to hit the keystone one final time, summoning a threat familiar to Mass Effect veterans will appear. This gigantic ground-based enemy, a Thresher Maw, can take you out in short order if you aren't careful. How dangerous are Thresher Maws? In the first game, we told almost all players to kill them while staying inside a tank!

You're expected only to survive this round, which will last five minutes. Doing this is difficult because while the Thresher Maw stays outside the arena, it uses a powerful acid shot attack that has an enormous splash radius. This attack is powerful enough that just three hits on Casual difficulty will kill you.

To avoid it, you'll have to make the Thresher Maw aim at the various columns in the arena. Most of these are flimsy and will be destroyed in a single acid shot hit, but there are four much sturdier ones that won't ever be destroyed. These stronger columns are the key to survival. There's two in the lower section of the arena that you can easily hide behind.

The rusty metal plate in the middle of the arena is surprisingly useful! If you stand just behind it, the Thresher Maw's acid shots will hit it instead and negate most of the splash damage!

If you stick behind the strong columns and rusty metal plate, as well as keep track of the Thresher Maw, you can easily stick it out for the whole five minutes and survive the round, netting you +5 Paragon and Renegade Points .

The real prize, however, is to kill the Thresher Maw. Not only will this win you the accolades of practically every Krogan on Tuchanka, but it'll also net you a whopping +15 Paragon and Renegade Points . To do that, you'll need to lay into it with your best Armor-busting weaponry whilst also keeping away from its acid shots, which is no easy feat. Luckily, this is ultimately optional, as not killing it will have no adverse effects on the game or its story.

Surviving the Thresher Maw marks the end of The Rite... but not your challenges. Gatatog Uvenk will now show up, and is willing to let Grunt join his clan instead of Clan Urdnot. This is of course is rather hypocritical, since a moment ago Uvenk wanted nothing to do with him: it's clear that Grunt's only use for him is as a show of political force. The end result will be the same, but your exact options depend on if you killed the Thresher Maw or not:

If you didn't kill the Thresher Maw, you can pick "This is sacrilege" for +2 Paragon Points or "This is just political" for +2 Renegade Points .

If you did kill the Thresher Maw, you can pick... "He's the ultimate krogan" and "Your call, Grunt" for +4 Paragon Points total. "Are you here to fight?" and "He can't join your clan" for +4 Renegade Points total.

"He's the ultimate krogan" and "Your call, Grunt" for +4 Paragon Points total.

"Are you here to fight?" and "He can't join your clan" for +4 Renegade Points total.

Grunt of course wants nothing to do with Uvenk, and as Uvenk admits, he wants Grunt whether he's dead or alive; he's valuable either way. And you know what that means -- fight!

There is however some very easily-missed loot hidden in this battle arena.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. From the starting area, to your right at the top of a short ramp of rubble.

Urdnot Corpse - 1,200 Credits. From the Med Kit described above, head down the rubble ramp and it'll be directly ahead of you.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Next to the Urdnot Corpse described above.

Urdnot Corpse - 900 Credits. From the last Urdnot Corpse, head forward and turn left up the steps: you'll find this in the back-right corner next to two turbines. This one may be risky to get to since Uvenk and his two Warriors start the battle here.

The fight with Gatatog Uvenk and his heavily-armored Krogan fighters is actually a lot easier than the cutscene suggests. You'll start behind some cover, which is good, and you can plan to spring your attacks from this very location for the duration of the battle. The only time you'll ever have to move is if you aren't aggressive enough.

Playing too defensively from your current position will allow your enemies to flank you and overrun your spot. Uvenk has a powerful Barrier in addition to his Armor and Health, so it will need to be whittled down with whatever you have on you. Your best bet is to take out all of his friends first, and then have the entire party focus on eliminating him at once.

Following the fall of Gatatog Uvenk and his crew of flunkies, you'll automatically be brought back into the presence of the Shaman, who will reward you with successfully passing the Rite. Grunt is now part of the Urdnot clan, earning him the name Urdnot Grunt. You can now finally speak with the Shaman about any number of issues, which you'll want to explore in-depth before heading on your way. In fact, if you talk with him twice more after that, you can brag about taking down a Spectre, Saren, and a Reaper, Sovereign!

When you regain control following this conversation, you may want to head to Fortack's Database in the Med-Lab and talk to Fortack: completing Grunt's Loyalty Mission will have earned you a discount on his stock!

On your way back to the Kodiak shuttle, you may find that many Krogan will have new things to say about Grunt passing the Rite, especially if you killed the Thresher Maw! Make sure to talk to the Clan Leader, the Mechanic, Fortack and Ratch (the two shopkeepers), the Overcaptain and the Blood Pack Recruiter all have new dialogue. There's also a humorous update from EDI in the tunnel to the Landing Platform if you killed the Thresher Maw.

Grunt of course will also have new dialogue back in his wing of Engineering. Here, reply with...

"Someday it'll end. It has to" or "No shortage there" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I can't have you going rogue" for +2 Renegade Points .

Talk with Grunt done, do another round through the ship:

Engineering - Talk to Zaeed about having to fight a Thresher Maw in the Rite of Passage.

Crew Deck - Talk to Miranda to learn more about her.

CIC - Talk to Joker regarding the leader of Clan Urdnot.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Dossier - Tali - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Dossier: Tali Mission on Haestrom, including how to get through all combat encounters, where
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Dossier: Tali Mission on Haestrom, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Before we start on the level itself, there are two things to note!

First, there's a difficulty-exclusive weapon available in this level, the Geth Pulse Rifle. It only appears at the end of the level on Hardcore or Insanity difficulties, and you must complete the entire level on one of them in order to unlock it. If you take one step in the level without being on either difficulty, it won't appear. You'll also need to physically pick it up in the level: it's still possible to miss!

Second, a great amount of unique dialogue can be attained if you bring along the Squad Mate from The Reaper IFF Mission. However this may be a problem if you intend to Romance Tali and also want a positive outcome at the end of the game. If that fits your playthrough, save this Mission and the Reaper IFF Mission until absolute last, with the Project Firewalker DLC Assignments to do on the side.

Weapons : Geth Pulse Rifle (Hardcore and Insanity only) M-9 Tempest

Geth Pulse Rifle (Hardcore and Insanity only)

Research : Assault Rifle Damage Heavy Pistol Damage

As shown above, this Mission is one of the few where the Mission Credits and total possible Found Credits aren't the same value!

To start Dossier: Tali, you'll need to travel to planet Haestrom. Get to the nearest Mass Relay from wherever you are, then go to the Far Rim , in the northeast edge of the galaxy. Once there, you'll be brought to a small system called Dholen with a gigantic red star, on the verge of going nova. If you want to, mine the following Rich planet:

Haestrom is found just south of the Mass Relay (yes, we realize there's no cardinal directions in space), and as you'll find out the planet is a Geth stronghold. Tali has infiltrated this place, and this is where we're going to find her.

Squad Tactics: Due to a high amount of synthetic enemies and wide open spaces, Garrus and Zaeed come highly recommended.

Due to a high amount of synthetic enemies and wide open spaces, Garrus and Zaeed come highly recommended.

Unique Dialogue: If you're more interested in unique dialogue, Grunt and / or Kasumi provide some amusing quips.

If you're more interested in unique dialogue, Grunt and / or Kasumi provide some amusing quips.

If you intend to get the Pulse Rifle at the end of this level, you MUST have the difficulty set to Hardcore or Insanity before doing ANYTHING on Haestrom. If you don't, it won't appear at the end!

Once you land, you'll see a little planetside critter getting fried in the sunlight. That's a hint to you to stay out of the light when you can, since the star dominating the sky is dying and has fried the magnetic field of the planet.

From the starting point, head forward and down the ramps, sprinting through the sunlight and to the shaded areas. You don't have to do this here as there are no enemies, but it's good to get in the habit. Unfortunately there's no Sprint meter like in the first game, so there's no way of knowing if you can sprint again until you give it a go.

At the bottom of the ramp, you'll see a huge blast door directly in front of you that, when examined, won't budge. Instead, you'll be forced to use the smaller door on your right to continue. Here you'll find a distress signal mentioning Tali is playing on a computer near the body of the Quarian.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On the stone block, to the right of the computer playing the message.

Damaged Geth - 3,000 Credits. The red Geth body to the right of the entry door.

Look to the left of the quarian computer to find the Gate Controls that lets you Open the Facility Gate, and progress to the first combat area. It's time to shoot Geth like it's 2183!

Circle around back outside and head through the now-open blast door. On the other side, run forward through the sun and quickly seek cover, as a Geth dropship shows up and lands some Geth baddies for you to deal with. Thankfully, this first wave of foes is easy enough to deal with -- just stay out of the sun (it appears the sun doesn't affect Geth Shields), and meticulously whittle down their numbers as you push forward. If you have it, Disruptor Ammo is a huge boon in this level.

If you have a Sniper Rifle on you, look for the ramp leading to the upper corridor on the right side of the area. This will draw all the Geth up to the far end of the corridor, making it almost trivial to pick them off with a Sniper Rifle, so long as your ammo holds out. No matter which route you took, as you head forward the blast doors at the far side of the area will deposit a lot of Geth Rocket Troopers. You're going to have to pick your moments to peek out of cover wisely so that you're not knocked out of cover and blown to bits!

Once all is quiet, you'll want to go to the elevated corridor we were talking about earlier for loot.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. In the middle of the elevated corridor on the right-hand side of this area. In the middle is a doorway leading to a ramp: the Medical Station is at the top of the ramp.

Customized Heavy Pistol - Heavy Pistol Damage. From the Medical Station, head down to the very bottom of the ramp to find this next to a dead Quarian leaning on the wall.

400 Refined Iridium - Return to the elevated corridor and now go to the far end closest to the exit of this area. Turn left and go down the ramp, then go straight forwards to the L-shaped drilling machine. The Iridium will be on it.

You'll find more Iridium on these and many more machines later, so keep an eye out!

With everything swept up, push towards the blast door at the end of this area. When you arrive at the blast door, it will be locked, so head rightward along the wall, and you'll come to a little opening where some Geth seem to be having target practice. You know what to do -- lay into these thugs before they know what hit 'em, quieting them down real quick.

Damaged Geth Hunter - 6,000 Credits. Ignore the Quarian Radio at the far end and instead look on the right-hand wall for a Geth Hunter body popping in and out of its invisibility cloak.

Tempest SMG - On a dead Quarian a little closer to the Quarian Radio from the Damaged Geth Hunter.

Pick up the Quarian Radio and you'll get in a conversation with Kal'Reegar, who tells you what he knows about the situation. It appears they are here to ensure Tali's safe exit from this hostile planet. At the start of this conversation...

Pick "I'm here to help" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "They're all dead" for +2 Renegade Points .

Kal wants to work with you, but when a dropship blocks the way forward with a Collapsed Pillar, you're implored to find some explosives to work your way through the debris. At the end of the conversation...

Say "What's your current status?" for +2 Paragon Points .

The two pieces of explosives we need are in two separate locations, but thankfully, they're pretty close to one another in the area up ahead. But this is also your first encounter with a Geth Hunter, a unit that is almost invisible until they appear in front of you and Shotgun you, making them a priority target.

Once you clear the initial group of enemies, your first destination is a room on the left-hand side. As you approach you'll be fired at by Geth Troopers, and when you get inside, many more will show up. You have an advantage here in that the Geth must go through the doorway first, so you can shoot the weaker ones like a bottleneck. Once that wave of foes is defeated, head into the room and play Tali's Journal , but ignore the Demolition Charge on the desk for now.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. Head up the ramp near the desk to find this at the top.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. Check behind the crates from where the Demolition Charge is.

When you pick up the Demolition Charge, Geth reinforcements will show up to try and block your exit out of the structure, so take cover in the back of the room. One of the foes here is a Geth Prime, a VERY formidable enemy who's like a YMIR Mech who doesn't shoot rockets but moves faster. They should be a high priority target for you as they have very high defenses.

When all is quiet, exit out of the room and head left to go towards the next Demolition Charge. Expect to be attacked by multiple waves of Geth as you head downhill towards a quarry room at the far end. As you get closer and closer to it, more and more Geth will attack, including the well-shielded Geth Destroyers, who are flamethrower units. Thankfully, there's a minimal amount of sunlight for you to dodge, and plenty of cover for you to utilize. Once you've eliminated them all, head to the far end of the area, then enter the room and turn left to find the second Demolition Charge.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. On the wall to the left of the Demolition Charge.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. On the concrete block, to the left of the Demolition Charge.

As expected, you'll be attacked by more Geth when you exit the room. Among them will be Rocket Troopers on the upper walkway: you'll want to take cover at a distance to make it easier to snipe them. You can optionally go leftward (with your back facing the room with the explosives) to find a ramp leading up to the second floor. You can Open the Shutters here to get some crossfire going, and take out the Rocket Troopers more easily.

After downing all the enemies in the area, you'll have the space to do some exploring.

400 Refined Iridium - Head forward to the room entrance to find another L-shaped drilling machine with this on it.

Medical Station - 100 Credits. From the Iridium, turn left and go up to the top of the ramp to find this.

Tali's Journal - From the Medical Station, head outside to the upper walkway and cross to the other side.

400 Refined Iridium - Return to the Collapsed Pillar you're about to use the Demolition Charges on and check the brown drilling machine near it for more Iridium.

Now go to the Collapsed Pillar, Plant the Explosives, and retreat to a safe distance before it blows up!

With the Pillar now in two pieces, head inside to find a Quarian holdout that's sadly been wiped out (although you can melee the crawling geth to avenge them). Don't forget Tali's Journal on the computer!

Damaged Geth - 6,000 Credits. Resting at the foot of the short ramp on your right.

Disassembled Geth Rifle - Assault Rifle Damage Research. Make a U-Turn up the short ramp on the right to find this on the table.

Damaged Geth - 3,000 Credits. At the closed door in the upper area where you found the Disassembled Geth Rifle.

Ancient Wall Safe - 6,000 Credits. To the right of the terminal where Tali is trying to contact base camp (the building you're currently in).

Now go and Activate the Communications Console to talk with Tali, who is in another building in the quarry. She pleads for your help, and naturally, you're going to assist her.

At the outset, say "No one else is left" for +2 Paragon Points .

Say "I came to help" for +2 Paragon Points .

Say "I'm recruiting you" for +2 Renegade Points .

Either way, you will need to eliminate Tali's geth problem to help complete her Mission so she can join you.

Tali will open the sealed door to your left remotely.

Medical Station - Through the door Tali opens for you, to the right of the doorway to the ramp.

You'll eventually emerge out from some concrete pillars, with Geth drones looking on. You'll have to deal with these hounding you while you fight two powerful Geth Primes, and unfortunately, the drones will periodically fly in until you destroy both Primes. A Pistol and an upgraded Overload ability are very good ways for you to dispatch them.

You'll have to kill several dozen of them, and while they can barely take any damage before falling hard to the ground and exploding, they still have the ability to do a plethora of damage to those unprepared. They work well as a team, and are fairly aggressive. Don't let their size fool you! Your best course of action in the early-going here is to stay in a stagnant position, dealing with the few Geth soldiers that appear, but more importantly drawing the drones towards your location, dealing with them en masse as they make themselves seen. Snipe the first Geth Prime if you can, then make your way across via the right-most route to stay out of the sun.

Once all is over, head for the exit door on the far side: there are no goodies, loot or collectibles in this large area. But, when you head through the door...

Ancient Wall Safe - 6,000 Credits. When you go through the door at the end of the large area, turn right to spot this on the right-hand side of the door frame.

Use the Security Console to Lift the Security Lockdown and continue.

As soon as you lift the lockdown, you'll witness a rather gigantic Geth platform, a Colossus, causing massive amounts of damage just outside of Tali's location. Shepard is just able to dodge its attack. It goes without saying that taking down the Colossus has become your number one priority!

Med Kit - 100 Credits. At the bottom of the last ramp, where the Quarian in red is squatting for cover.

You'll now bump into Kal'Reegar. Kal is the last of Tali's squad, and got his suit ruptured trying to make a break for her.

Answer "Is she safe?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Further into the conversation, Kal suggests that he draw the Geth's fire using his rocket launcher so that Shepard can take advantage. If you know anything about Quarians you'll know that this is a TERRIBLE idea, since Quarians don't have much armor at all. You'll be able to determine the path forward:

Answer "No. Stay down" for +2 Paragon Points , then use the Paragon Interrupt to ensure he stays in cover and get +15 Paragon Points more.

Say "Sounds like a plan" for +15 Renegade Points , meaning Kal will join you in the fight.

The battlefield up ahead is has three routes leading to the Colossus, but each has their own quirks as Kal explained earlier:

The right route is a sniper perch but is very exposed to sunlight, and when you get to the end, you can be attacked from behind by reinforcements. As well, the Colossus doesn't repair itself while you're on this route for some reason.

The middle route has lots of cover, but you can be pinched by Geth on both sides. It also leaves you exposed to the Colossus, who can easily knock you out of cover.

The left route has shade and cover, but you can be attacked by Geth from both the front and the back. It does however lead to Power Cells you can use to refill your Heavy Weapons.

Our approach is a mix of two: we'll stick with the middle route at first to clear out the Geth in your way, particularly Destroyers with their dangerous flamethrowers. Once you're dealing just with normal Geth, make your way right up the elevated walkway to make sure you're not flanked from that direction. Once you've made your way up there, take out your most accurate weapon and get to it.

When you get to the end of the walkway however, some Geth reinforcements will show up. The end of the walkway offers VERY little cover for shooting backwards, so your best bet is actually to backtrack down the walkway and back to the boxes past the ramp, letting you deal with them more comfortably. Make sure to stay crouched down though: as mentioned above this route has no shade unless you're behind the railing.

Once all the Geth footsoldiers have been dealt with, return to the far end of the walkway and take cover at the top, to mitigate the Colossus' height advantage. With the wide railing you'll have plenty of room to avoid being hit the Colossus' pulse rockets. Of course when it's not doing that it'll be using its machine guns on you, so you only have a few scant seconds to safely fire at it. Since you're up on the right-hand route however, the Colossus won't recharge its shields! This is invaluable when trying for the Pulse Rifle reward.

Following the destruction of the Colossus, you're free to explore the area for goods.

1,600 Refined Iridium - Split over four boxes of 400 Iridium each, these are on the four drilling machines in the outdoors portion of this area.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. On a block at the base of the corner column to the left of the door to Tali.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. On some cares to the right of the door to where Tali is, in the dark corner.

Damaged Geth - 9,000 Credits. The red Geth body right in front of you when you open the door to Tali.

Intact Pulse Rifle - On the right-hand wall of Tali's room is a sparking Geth with a Pulse Rifle. If you completed the entire level on either Hardcore or Insanity difficulty, you can take the Pulse Rifle!

If you intended to do that but forgot to change the difficulty to Hardcore or Insanity, you can Pause and use the Load menu to Restart the Mission, which also lets you choose your Squad and their Weapons again.

Now go and talk to Tali: at the outset of the conversation, say...

"Can you join me now?" for +2 Paragon Points .

"The quarians owe me" for +2 Renegade Points .

Speak with her at length in regard to what's happening here, and what her research on the sun at the center of the system has netted. If Kal'Reegar survived the battle with the Colossus, he'll show up here, still injured but alive. Here you can say to Kal...

"Do you need transportation?" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Tali's with me now" for +2 Renegade Points .

With her Mission complete, Tali will gladly join your squad, leaving Kal to head back to the Quarian fleet on his own. You'll get +5 Paragon Points and +5 Renegade Points for completing the Mission.

Following the conversation with Tali back on the planet surface, you'll find yourself automatically transported to the Normandy. As you may remember from " Freedom's Progress ", Cerberus was responsible for infiltrating the Quarian fleet and destroying one of the ships within it. Tali hasn't forgotten about it, and makes it completely clear that she's here for Shepard, not them. Here...

Say "I agree completely" for +2 Paragon Points , then "Feel free to study the ship" for +2 Paragon Points more.

You should now head down to Engineering and talk to Tali, at the station to the left of where Gabby and Ken are. If you ask how she is, you can say...

"I don't trust them" for +2 Paragon Points .

"They're on our side" for +2 Renegade Points .

Tali's Research upgrade is a super important one: Cyclonic Shields for the Normandy. Considering the ship has been a target for the Collector's ship in the past, it's a very good idea to purchase this. If you've gotten all three combat upgrades to the Normandy (the Cyclonic Shields, Silaris Armor and Thanix Cannon), you can talk to Joker again and ask about the Mission for a new line of dialogue.

Engineering - Pass by Gabby and Ken for their thoughts on Tali, then talk to Tali herself.

Crew Deck - Talk to Garrus to pick up his Loyalty Mission.

CIC - Talk to Kelly and Joker for their opinions on Tali, and ask Joker about the Mission if you've bought all three Normandy upgrades.

If you've been holding out on concluding the " Normandy: FBA Couplings " Assignment due to unique dialogue, now's the time to do it: Tali will join in on the poker game! Use the white options to win or lose 100 Credits, or use the Charm or Intimidate options to win 500 Credits.

Before doing anything else, head over to Omega to start the " Omega: Packages for Ish " Assignment in the main plaza. Once you've started that, we suggest you visit Ilium, which will have a LOT of new stores for you to peruse and some Side Quests to tackle as well. We cover this in the Illium - Shopping and Side Quests page.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: The Reaper IFF - Mass Effect 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the The Reaper IFF Mission in the Hawking Eta cluster, including how to get through all combat
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the The Reaper IFF Mission in the Hawking Eta cluster, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

The Reaper IFF Mission comes with the MOST amount of caveats that you should know about before starting it, particularly because the game doesn't tell you anything. Completing The Reaper IFF Mission will kickstart invisible machinations that may force your hand to start the end of the game, especially if you're trying to keep everyone alive in the Suicide Mission .

What will happen is that after completing this Mission, both an invisible Countdown and an invisible Journal Check will activate, and when either one hits 0, the Reaper IFF will be ready to install.

The Countdown is set to either 2, 3 or 4, although which are chosen aren't really known (more quests in your Journal does tend to increase number, though). The Countdown ticks down by 1 after completing any Mission , N7 Assignment , Lair of the Shadow Broker or Arrival . Once this hits 0, then when you next approach the Galaxy Map the Reaper IFF will be ready to be installed. The Overlord DLC is worth highlighting because it's technically comprised of four Assignments. This means that completing it will instantly ready the Reaper IFF!

The Overlord DLC is worth highlighting because it's technically comprised of four Assignments. This means that completing it will instantly ready the Reaper IFF!

The Journal Check scans your Journal for N7 Side Quests , as well as Dossier Missions and Loyalty Missions . If only the "Stop the Collectors" Mission remains when you next approach the Galaxy Map, the Reaper IFF will be ready to be installed. Notably, the Journal Check DOES NOT look at DLC , including Kasumi , Zaeed , Firewalker , Shadow Broker , Overlord and Arrival . So if you only have two Loyalty Missions and two Firewalker Missions , then do the Loyalty Missions first, that will trigger the IFF installation "early".

Notably, the Journal Check DOES NOT look at DLC , including Kasumi , Zaeed , Firewalker , Shadow Broker , Overlord and Arrival . So if you only have two Loyalty Missions and two Firewalker Missions , then do the Loyalty Missions first, that will trigger the IFF installation "early".

You'll know that the Reaper IFF is ready to be installed when EDI mentions it when you walk up to the Galaxy Map and enter the trigger zone in front of it (shown in the screenshot above as the orange box). Fortunately, walking down from the podium doesn't count.

When the IFF is ready to be installed, interacting with the Galaxy Map will trigger a mandatory Mission known as Joker's Jump , which introduces an urgent need to strike the Collector Base . While optional, waiting will put innocent lives on the line, and may force you to choose between building your team or striking now unprepared.

In short, The Reaper IFF Mission is secretly what will kickstart the end of the game. As such, you'll want to delay doing it until your team is as ready as can be (save for an empty Squad Mate slot on the left). We highly, highly, HIGHLY suggest you do this for the best possible outcome to the game. Having two or three Firewalker DLC Missions left on the side will be useful to help out with any Romances for characters you pick up late in the game, too.

Research : Heavy Skin Weave Shotgun Damage Sniper Rifle Damage

Location: Hawking Eta - Thorne - Derelict Reaper

Assuming you're following our guide in order, The Reaper IFF will be one of the last things you'll have left on your checklist as you approach the end of the game. Your destination is a Derelict Reaper, located in the Thorne system of the Hawking Eta cluster. It's not the "Relay System", so you'll need about 400 Fuel to head over there, and to travel back again once you're done.

If you're interested in mining, here's the one planet to take note of:

Squad Tactics: Tactically, Grunt and Zaeed are the best choices thanks to their ability to strip armor and their Concussive Shot abilities.

Tactically, Grunt and Zaeed are the best choices thanks to their ability to strip armor and their Concussive Shot abilities.

Unique Dialogue: For unique dialogue, Jacob and Tali are recommended picks.

For unique dialogue, Jacob and Tali are recommended picks.

After the Normandy passes through the local storm and within range of the Derelict Reaper, you'll board and begin inside the Cerberus Facility. Head through the door and take a left down the stairs. To your left is an alcove with a Work Log detailing the ominous start of this facility's operations.

Wall Safe - 2,000 Credits. On the left wall of the alcove, right next to the outer corner of the wall.

Terminal - 2,000 Credits. To the right of the Wall Safe, the middle of the three terminals.

Wall Safe - 4,000 Credits. Directly opposite the first Wall Safe on the right wall of the alcove.

Medical Station x2 - 200 Credits. At the end of the hallway to the left of the door forwards.

At the end of the hallway is a second Work Log to listen to. Head through the doors to the right of these objects, and you'll find that the Reaper, despite being dead, had put up kinetic barriers that prevents Joker from picking you up in the Normandy. The solution is to destroy the Reaper's Mass Effect core, but that means it'll also fall into the crushing gravity of the nearby gas giant. Great!

Head forward down the next corridor and, at the intersection, view another Work Log for a creepy conversation between two scientists. Continue to the right and you'll find explosive crates strewn around the area, a sure sign that you're going to be assaulted by enemies presently. Lo and behold, as you move forward, you're attacked by several waves of Husks.

You'll also encounter Abominations, red Husks that explode as they rush up to you or are killed. The best way to take out either is to shoot the legs, much faster than pumping their upper bodies full of lead. Once the lower section is cleared, check the left-hand side for a Work Log showing the scientists spiral further into madness.

As you get to the top of the next ramp, you'll see two Husks up ahead get sniped. Who could have done that? Mystery deepening, check the area to the right:

Power Cells - 100 Credits. To the right of the sniped Husks is an alcove, with this in the back-right.

2,000 Refined Platinum - In the back-left corner of the alcove, next to a Terminal.

Terminal - 3,500 Credits. In the back-left corner of the alcove.

Cerberus Rifle - Sniper Rifle Damage. To the left of the Terminal described above.

The next area is very tough, because in addition to a HUGE amount of Husks, you'll also be fighting a Scion. You fought these on " Horizon " and in the " Collector Ship ", but they're at their worst here because of the tight quarters (and explosive crates in the open plaza), making it very difficult to dodge their Shockwave attacks that can kill Shepard in three hits on CASUAL difficulty!

The only way to avoid these directly is to stand a long distance away and not be aiming to increase Shepard's movement speed. The best strategy here is actually to backtrack around the corner to the previous area: this lets the Husks funnel in to your position, and lets the wall block the Scion's Shockwave attacks. Take out the Husks first, then gang up on the Scion.

Once all is quiet, return to the main battlefield and explore the wide open plaza area. Along the left-hand side is another Work Log that shows more of the paranoia that gripped the facility. Then go to the rail:

Med Kit - 100 Credits. At the back rail overlooking the spikes, in the middle-right.

Research Terminal - Heavy Skin Weave. One of the two terminals on the right side of the rail, next to the Med Kit.

Also at the rail is an Altar, which will have extra dialogue if you have Jacob because he was on Eden Prime, and thus has seen these Dragon Teeth spikes before. Garrus and Tali can comment here too, but will be overridden by Jacob if he's present. Whichever of the three it is, you can reply for Morality Points, although the wording will differ depending on who you have with you.

Pick the upper-right option for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Nobody touch anything" for +2 Renegade Points .

To leave this area, look for the exit door on the right-hand side of the plaza, near the entryway. Bypass the door and head through the airlock to the exterior of the facility. Once you reach outside, you'll be met with a VERY interesting cutscene. The mystery sniper will reveal themselves to be someone VERY unexpected!

Take a step forward and you'll immediately be swarmed by Husks and an Abomination. You'll be facing a LOT of these, so you'll want to be quick and efficient in taking them out. Use the explosive crate on the right to take out any standing nearby.

The lower area that serves as the way forward will spawn in more Husks and Abominations, but to make things worse a Scion appears on the ramp ahead. This is VERY dangerous considering how little room there is down here, so we HIGHLY advise you to backtrack back up to the area where you fought the last batch of Husks. This will create a bottleneck for the Husks and keep you further away from the Scion, letting you dodge its Shockwaves more effectively. Just remember that if you can see it, it can hurt you since its Shockwaves can travel OVER objects!

Once everything here is dead, return down to the lower area and take the two ramps up.

Terminal - 3,000 Credits. At the top of the pair of ramps, you'll find this directly by taking a tight U-Turn to the left into an alcove with three Terminals. It'll be the middle one.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. A bit further down the dead-end route on the left, on top of some canisters in the back-left corner of it.

Now continue down the right-hand route and you'll eventually be attacked by more Husks and some Abominations. This is a very linear area, so a good strategy is to retreat to the opposite end and let them come to you.

Terminal - 3,500 Credits. Return to the top of the pair of ramps from earlier and face the way forwards. A few steps forward will be an alcove on your right with three Terminals, one of which will give Credits.

Next take the ramps down to another lower area with a familiar setup: Husks swarming in and a Scion in the distance putting you in extreme peril. As with the last time, you'll do well to backtrack to the last area, letting you funnel the Husks to you and keeping the Scion's Shockwaves well out of reach. Once all the Husks are gone you can focus on the Scion, but remember that avoiding the Shockwaves is best done when you're not aiming since that will slow Shepard's movement!

Cerberus Shotgun - Shotgun Damage. Head down the ramp into the lower area the Husks and Scions were coming from and make a U-Turn to the right. The shotgun will be in this small alcove.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. Next to the Cerberus Shotgun described above.

Terminal - 3,500 Credits. From the lower area, head forward up the next ramp. At the top, look right to spot three Terminals in the back-right corner: Access the middle one.

Head down the next ramp and you'll enter your next fight.

You'll have the advantage of height here as well as more open space, but to make up for that you'll now be facing TWO Scions, which is just a nightmare. The distance these guys show up at will hinder your ability to damage them, but they'll be able to obliterate your Squad Mates just fine. Thus you have to balance shooting at one of them from long range while defending yourself from Husks at close range. Focus solely on one Scion first, and then the other. Once both Scions have fallen, you can then run down the ramp, deal with any remaining Husks, gather ammunition, and then run up the ramp on the other side.

What will you find on the other side of the ramp? More Husks, more Abominations, and the last two Scions of the level. There's much less room to move about here, so use your earlier strategy and retreat towards the previous area to bottleneck the Husks and hide the Scions behind the wall so they can't Shockwave you. Once the Husks have quietened down, head back and fire on the Scions, while keeping a respectful distance away.

Power Cells - 100 Credits. Check the right-hand corner at the bottom of the arrival ramp to find these.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. As you approach the door ahead, this will be on the left, in front of some canisters and two white crates.

Now approach the door and Bypass it to open it up. In the hallway, ignore the Reaper IFF for a moment:

Wall Safe - 2,500 Credits. Easily missed, this is at the back of the tunnel on the right-hand wall. You should grab this now because if you forget and enter the next room, the door will lock behind you.

To enable the door forwards, pick up the Reaper IFF on the computer terminal. Now head through the door to the final area.

Here you'll see a cutscene showing the Geth Sniper get taking out by Husks, so you'll have to head in there and deal with them yourself. Luckily there are no Scions here, but to finish the level you need to shoot at the Reaper Core when it's unprotected. This only happens periodically, and the Husks and Abominations aren't polite enough to wait for you to shoot at it. You'll have to balance shooting at Husks and at the Reaper Core, at least while the Reaper Core is unprotected.

Laptop - 1,000 Credits. Located on the desk in the back-left corner of the Reaper Core. Grab it as soon as you can : destroying the Reaper Core will instantly conclude the level, giving you no chance to Access the Laptop if you forget about it.

Once you the destroy the Reaper Core, it immediately becomes unstable, and Shepard has to make a snap decision on whether to take the Geth Sniper with them to the Normandy. Shepard is insistent, and the team is able to fling it across to the Normandy and jump over themselves, escaping just before the Reaper falls away and is crushed by the local gas giant. You'll get +5 Paragon and Renegade Points for completing the Mission.

Back on the Normandy, Shepard conferences with Miranda and Jacob over the Geth Sniper. Shepard thinks it could be an ally on the basis that it briefly talked to them, while Miranda thinks it should be sold to Cerberus for a pretty penny. Jacob thinks that's not as much of a risk, but would prefer to just have it destroyed. Eventually you'll get to choose what to do with it:

Pick "I want to talk to it first" to keep it and get +15 Paragon Points . This will put the Geth Sniper in a limbo situation similar to Grunt: out of the picture until you decide to activate it.

Pick "Cerberus gets the geth" to get +15 Renegade Points . You'll also get a HUGE 50,000 Credits in return.

Once you've made your choice, it's time to do your rounds. Kelly will have a new comment to make, and Jacob will too if you ask him about his thoughts on the Mission ahead. You may also want to talk to Thane to progress your conversations with him.

If you decided to keep the Geth Sniper, head down to the AI Core next. Here, pick "I'm reactivating the geth", and Shepard will do so, in safety thanks to EDI's precautions. There's a bunch of Morality Points you can have here:

Paragon : "You want to work with me?" and "That works" ( +4 Paragon Points total).

Renegade : "Why not?", "All geth are the same", "I don't 'cooperate.' I lead" and "Quiet, EDI" ( +8 Renegade Points total)

As it turns out, the Geth Sniper is actually friendly and even wants to help, although talking with it is a bit tricky thanks to it being made up of thousands of Geth software. Eventually EDI will interject with an appropriate name for them: Legion .

You can converse more with Legion after it agrees to join you. Their Upgrade is actually for themselves: a VERY powerful Sniper Rifle known as the M-98 Widow, capable of one-shotting practically any regular enemy in the game on the lower difficulties. While you're here, don't forget to use EDI's terminal to learn more about the AI Core, and talk to Joker, who has a comment to make if you activated Legion.

Crew Deck - If you're following our guide in order, talk to Thane to progress conversations with him.

CIC - Talk to Jacob for a new thought if you ask him about the Mission ahead.

If you're following our guide in order, your next task will be to tackle Tali's Loyalty Mission: " Tali: Treason ".

If you've yet to recruit Tali however for unique dialogue, you should do " Dossier: Tali " first.

So now we get to the important discussion of the road ahead. By completing the Reaper IFF Mission, you have effectively kick-started the road to the end of the game by activating an invisible Countdown and an Journal Check . Here's how each of them works:

The Countdown is set to either 2, 3 or 4, although which are chosen aren't really known (more quests in your Journal does tend to increase number, though). The Countdown ticks down by 1 after completing any Mission , N7 Assignment , the Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC or the Arrival DLC . Once this hits 0, then when you next approach the Galaxy Map the Reaper IFF will be ready to be installed. The Overlord DLC is worth highlighting because it's technically comprised of four Assignments. This means that completing it will instantly ready the Reaper IFF!

Both of these are checked when you walk towards the Galaxy Map (walking down from the podium doesn't count). The image above shows the area around the podium that triggers this. If you can avoid it and earn a Loyalty Mission from a Squad Mate, then the Journal Check will see it and not trigger the IFF installation.

Here's what will happen after either of the two expire:

Once the countdown expires, walking up to the Galaxy Map will have EDI announce that the Reaper IFF is ready to install (walking down from its podium doesn't count). This is irreversible: once EDI says the Reaper IFF is ready, there's nothing you can do to change it.

Using the Galaxy Map will now start the Joker's Jump Mission. This is a small but very important Mission that results in Tap to Reveal .

As a result of the above, you'll have to choose between building your team and their Loyalty, or to strike now so that no innocents will perish (even doing ONE Mission or Side Quest will have consequences). This is why leaving the Reaper IFF Mission until last is so important: it gives you the time to build your team and their Loyalty consequence-free.

With that all in mind, you effectively have four more Missions and N7 Side Quests until the next mandatory story Mission. You'll want to prioritize Dossier Missions and Loyalty Missions first because those are, by far and away, the most important things to do.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Citadel: Shore Leave - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Citadel: Shore Leave DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Citadel: Shore Leave DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Mods: Pistol Power Magnifier Assault Rifle Ultralight Materials Sniper Rifle Ultralight Materials

The Citadel DLC is the "one last hurrah" of Shepard's adventures, and thus has many meetups with characters past and present. However the availability of these characters is dependent on completing their base game storylines in Mass Effect 3, which is important because the Citadel DLC assumes you'll be doing everything in one go.

To that end, make sure you've completed the following before starting the Citadel DLC:

Complete all Reunion Missions to unlock Tap to Reveal .

Complete " Citadel: Hanar Diplomat " to unlock Tap to Reveal .

Complete " Citadel: Volus Ambassador " to unlock Tap to Reveal .

Complete the personal storylines of your Squad Mates past and present in the base game areas of the Citadel, as covered on the Citadel Excursion 4 page. For Steve Cortez, this additionally involves talking with him in the Normandy's Shuttle Bay twice, then meeting him at Docking Bay: D24 , and then Docks: Holding Area .

For Steve Cortez, this additionally involves talking with him in the Normandy's Shuttle Bay twice, then meeting him at Docking Bay: D24 , and then Docks: Holding Area .

Complete " Priority: Rannoch " to unlock Tap to Reveal in the Citadel DLC's main storyline.

Complete " Priority: Horizon " to unlock Tap to Reveal .

If you intend to Romance someone, make sure you've locked in their Romance before starting!

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: The Citadel 2 "

Location: Serpent Nebula - Widow - Citadel - Personal Apartment

Once the DLC has been successfully installed (see Citadel DLC for details), get Shepard to a private terminal on the Normandy to check their e-mail. Among many others, you'll find a message from Admiral Hackett instructing Shepard and the crew to head to the Citadel to take some shore leave, as well as offering Shepard the use of Admiral Anderson's Apartment .

Head to the Galaxy Map and set a course for the Citadel and dock there. One of the options in the pop-up menu will be "Personal Apartment": choose it to begin!

Shepard arrives in Anderson's (immaculate) Apartment, and he immediately gifts it to Shepard, much to their reluctance. It's quite the sprawling place, with many different rooms to explore (particularly a seemingly endless amount of bedrooms!). There's a lot to explore here, which we fully cover in the dedicated Anderson's Apartment page, but here's a summary:

There are 10 datapads lying about containing interview snippets with Admiral Anderson, detailing various topics about his life. There's at least one in every room of the apartment, except the bathrooms and the master bedroom upstairs.

There's also an Anderson ANN Interview that you can listen to via the TV in the downstairs study.

The downstairs lounge, dining area, and mezzanine have Stereo Controls to play music. More can be unlocked after the Shore Leave storyline at the Castle Arcade claw game.

The downstairs study has a Catalog that you can use to change the appearance of various furniture types in the apartment, although you can't buy anything until you complete the main Shore Leave storyline.

The downstairs study also has a Private Terminal. You can use this to progress the Shore Leave storyline, and after it you can initiate meetups with your squad and crew in the apartment with it.

The master bedroom upstairs has an en suite Weapon Bench and Armor Locker, although you cannot reset Powers or assign Bonus Powers. Weapon choice won't be a factor for the next part of the Mission.

Needless to say, it's a far, far more luxurious place than Shepard's Apartment from the Pinnacle Station DLC in the original game.

Once you're all done exploring the place (or got overwhelmed and want to move on like we did), find the downstairs study under the stairs and use the Private Terminal, near the poker table. Here you'll have an email from Joker titled "Dinner at sushi place on me!". Read it, then exit the apartment and use the exit door around the corner.

Shepard will take a Rapid Transit skycar to Ryuusei, the sushi place on the Silversun Strip. The Silversun Strip is the bustling hub of the Citadel DLC, however you won't be able to fully explore it until after the Shore Leave storyline.

Joker will be at the very back of Ryuusei's, but you can optionally talk to the french Host at the entrance four times, overhear various conversations at the dinnertables, and talk to the Bartender in the middle counter area.

When you're ready, talk to Joker in the very back of Ryuusei, where he'll be a bit nervous about leaving the SSV Normandy SR-2 to some tech guys. Here you can respond for some Morality Points:

Pick "This is a vacation" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I don't like it either" for +2 Renegade Points .

As the conversation continues, it's discovered that Joker didn't actually send the invitation to have some sushi: he thought Shepard had invited him to Ryuusei's. They're soon interrupted by an Alliance Intelligence Office named Brooks, who informs them that someone has been stealing Shepard's personal info, and wants them dead. Here you can say...

Before long the place is under attack, Brooks is taken hostage, and Shepard must battle their way to her... after having grabbed a black Carnifex-looking pistol off a Merc Trooper called an M-11 Suppressor. Due to the circumstances, this and the Omni-Blade will be Shepard's only weapons for the Mission!

Your task is to fight through these new foes, called CAT6 Mercenaries, and revive Brooks similar to fallen Squad Mates. CAT6 Mercenaries are functionally re-skinned Cerberus troops, but luckily you only have to fight basic Merc Troopers for this battle. They have their own traits that make them stand out, however:

Merc Troopers deploy Disruption Drones, who get close to Shepard and explode to knock them out of cover and into enemy fire.

Merc Trooper grenades are also thrown in clusters: while they deal less damage individually, they cover a wider spread, again to knock Shepard out of cover.

Interestingly, their shot trails aren't as visible, making it more difficult to tell where they're firing from.

Don't try and whittle away all the enemies: there's an unlimited number of them! Instead, focus on taking out the current threats and moving forward through the restaurant to Brooks so you can revive her.

After reviving Brooks, she's almost immediately shot by a Merc Trooper who then shoots out the glass under Shepard, sending them through the fish tank and down into the underbelly of the Wards.

Once Shepard recomposes themselves, head out to the left, hop right across the gaps, then drop left onto a beam to slide down a ladder. Look for a Datapad on the second platform after the ladder. Drop down the next ladder, then use the View Prompt to spot a nearby Skycar lot called Cision Motors.

Drop down another ladder, then hang a right into the freezer full of fish (make sure to say "hey" to the Salarian taking a smoko in here). Climb up the ladder in the back of the freezer, take a left, then hop across the rooftops (you can spot a crowd of civilians on your left, all confused by the C-Sec lockdown).

The next ladder leads to a marketplace area with more CAT6 Mercs, which the hint pop-up suggests is a stealth area for the M-11 Suppressor. We'll be completely honest: the stealth doesn't exactly work, because the enemies don't follow patrol patterns that encourage it and they spot the bodies of their dead comrades from very long distances.

With that in mind you should be fully prepared to get into a standard gunfight, but you should still prioritize headshots, since that is what the Suppressor is good at after all. After downing the first enemies, you can read an optional Datapad at the Fresh Meat stall (aka EZ Meat).

After the initial few Merc Troopers, sneak down the right-hand side to get to the next area. In the store at the back of this next area you can spot a Merc Sniper (pictured above). These are similar to the Cerberus Nemesis sniper, except they can cloak like Phantoms when moving from cover to cover. By taking this route, you can headshot her before she causes you real trouble.

You can get some sneaky shots on one or two more Merc Troopers before you get detected: Take cover and wait patiently for them to expose their heads so you can drop them.

Once they're all down, you can continue onward, and get some loot along the way. The door pictured above will mark where the last loot is, and the way forward after that.

Pistol Power Magnifier - In the indoor storefront of the marketplace with the Ryuusei hologram above it. This will be on the back counter.

Terminal - 2,250 credits. On the same counter as the Pistol Power Magnifier.

Credits - 1,500 credits. Exit the marketplace via the alley in the back-left with the Value Added hologram. On the other side, check the stall in the corner to find this, next to an amusing Datapad .

Terminal - 2,250 credits. From the Credits described above, head left to the Bridge Control door that's the way forward. Turn around and head inside the store to find this on the right-hand side of the counter.

Bypass the triangular glass door with the Bridge Control to open the way forward to the next area, and the next fight. This fight is the same as the others - Merc Troopers with grenades and Disruptor Drones, plus some Merc Snipers so you don't get too complacent. Once they're all dead, search the stores on the right-hand side for loot:

Terminal - 1,500 credits. Inside the blue Kon-Junc-Tion store, on the countertop next to a Datapad .

Terminal - 1,500 credits. Inside the pink "Van Allen Belts" store with the round doorway, on the countertop with the Datapad .

Assault Rifle Ultralight Materials - Inside the teal "Cepheid Variable" store, on a shelf on the back wall.

Terminal - 1,500 credits. On the counter inside the "Cepheid Variable" store, next to another Datapad .

Terminal - 2,250 credits. Inside the store for Cision Motors where the exit door is. Will be the laptop on the island countertop.

Once you have all the loot, head through the door, take a left and open the glass door to progress the story.

You'll now be met with a Squad Mate at the Cision Motors lot. If you're Romancing one of your Mass Effect 3 Squad Mates, they'll be the ones to meet you here (what a treat!). Unfortunately the landing pad is behind the locked gate of Cision Motors, so you'll have to find a way to open it. While you're here, make sure to locate and Examine these:

Sniper Rifle Ultralight Materials - As soon as you regain control of Shepard, turn around to face the glass door they just went through. This will be on your right, in front of a door directly across form the Used Skycars. Sneaky!

Used Skycar x3 - The Skycars lined up on your right from when you regain control of Shepard. Each has its own unique and, uh, "passionate" description.

Terminal - 2,250 credits. A laptop in the right-hand seating area of Cision Motors, directly across from the door where the objective marker is.

Find the door in the seating area and try and open it: your companion will show Shepard a kinder, gentler way to get the gate controls open: this opens up the triangle shaped gates across the way.

Move into the area marked by the blue hologram ring for extraction... only for the shuttle door to open and reveal it's packed with CAT6 Merc Troopers. Luckily James will come to the rescue (or Wrex, if he's alive and you genuinely cured the Genophage in " Priority: Tuchanka "). Once they're done kicking ass, they'll hand Shepard a Geth Spitfire before the next wave arrives (marked by an explosion, what else).

In addition to the new weapon, Shepard also gets +2 Medi-Gel. It's a good thing too, because you'll now have to survive against the Merc Trooper onslaught for 60 seconds until Joker arrives. Fortunately, the Geth Spitfire is fully loaded with 1,000 ammo, so have fun! And don't forget to blow up one of the Skycars with it to hear the despairing cries of the Cision Motors owner.

In this fight Shepard doesn't need to worry about clearing every Merc - just staying alive for one minute and then getting to the marked extraction zone (look for the translucent grid). Once in the extraction zone, the transport will show up and take Shepard and company back to the apartment, where soon the whole Normandy crew will assemble.

You'll now arrive back in the apartment to debrief yourself on what the hell just happened. Brooks however is still panicking: you can reassure her with...

"You're doing fine" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "You need to focus" for +2 Renegade Points .

After Brooks explains what her actual job is and what she does, she also explains how she detected Shepard's personal information getting hacked. This is a BIG DEAL, considering Shepard's a Council Spectre and all. To that you can respond...

"This is critical" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Shore leave canceled. Again" for +2 Renegade Points .

At the end of the cut scene, the Priority Target Achievement / Trophy will unlock, Reputation points will be earned, credits will be awarded, and Shepard's journal will be updated with the next part of the adventure.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

Up Next: Silver Coast Casino: Infiltration
