articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Citadel Archives: Escape DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Mods: Assault Rifle Ultralight Materials Shotgun Ultralight Materials SMG Power Magnifier Sniper Rifle High-Velocity Barrel Sniper Rifle Ultralight Materials

After you chat with a Squad Mate or two around the apartment, EDI will inform Shepard that they can continue by talking to Brooks. Like with Liara earlier, you'll be allowed to delay the meeting and the start of this Mission if you want to.

Brooks will give Shepard the the run-down on what they've found on Khan's drives, and after Brooks gawks about the Normandy crew, Glyph will interrupt. It seems that the mastermind is now using Shepard's Spectre access codes to access the top secret Citadel Archives, a hush-hush area filled with the Council's sensitive historical information.

So its off to the Archives. And for once Shepard decides that everyone can join in on this fun. Hopefully with better results than in Joker's Jump ! (spoilers: Tap to Reveal )

Squad Tactics: You'll be facing CAT6 Heavies for the first time here, who work like Cerberus Guardians but use tech-based Omnishields... which can be disabled with Overload. This means Garrus , EDI and Kaidan are excellent choices. Pull also works, meaning Javik could be considered too! James is a good compliment for his armor-stripping powers, which will also see use here. Tali is as well since she has a lot of tech powers to set up Tech Combos. Wrex is a great choice if you're playing on a higher difficulty: he has so much health and damage output he can genuinely kill every enemy entirely on his own without needing to be healed! Just him running around is helpful because he'll cause CAT6 Heavies to turn their shields, exposing them to your gunfire!

You'll be facing CAT6 Heavies for the first time here, who work like Cerberus Guardians but use tech-based Omnishields... which can be disabled with Overload. This means Garrus , EDI and Kaidan are excellent choices. Pull also works, meaning Javik could be considered too!

James is a good compliment for his armor-stripping powers, which will also see use here.

Tali is as well since she has a lot of tech powers to set up Tech Combos.

Wrex is a great choice if you're playing on a higher difficulty: he has so much health and damage output he can genuinely kill every enemy entirely on his own without needing to be healed! Just him running around is helpful because he'll cause CAT6 Heavies to turn their shields, exposing them to your gunfire!

Unique Dialogue: Wrex provides amusing dialogue throughout. Garrus or Tali will also tease out some unique comments. If you're Renegade, Javik will provide a very unique quip.

Wrex provides amusing dialogue throughout.

Garrus or Tali will also tease out some unique comments.

If you're Renegade, Javik will provide a very unique quip.

Shepard's Loadout: MAKE SURE TO SET YOUR WEAPON LOADOUT! The adventures in the Wards and Silver Coast Casino means that Shepard hasn't had time to swap back. If you forget, pause and use the Reload Mission save file to start over. Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will help deal with this level's CAT6 Heavies. The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by CAT6 Snipers and Atlas mechs. Since you have the Citadel DLC , and possibly completed the Omega DLC , a Thermal Scope for your assault / sniper rifle helps see through both their smoke bombs and through walls!

MAKE SURE TO SET YOUR WEAPON LOADOUT! The adventures in the Wards and Silver Coast Casino means that Shepard hasn't had time to swap back. If you forget, pause and use the Reload Mission save file to start over.

Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will help deal with this level's CAT6 Heavies.

The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by CAT6 Snipers and Atlas mechs.

Since you have the Citadel DLC , and possibly completed the Omega DLC , a Thermal Scope for your assault / sniper rifle helps see through both their smoke bombs and through walls!

The Citadel Archives is a sprawling place, and you'll find yourself exploring three archive levels. We've segmented this guide by each level to help you keep track of where you are, which is helpful for the cramped library areas!

As soon as the long cutscene ends, be ready for an immediate battle. You'll be fighting CAT6 Snipers and CAT6 Specialists (who are actually the Merc Troopers from the first Citadel DLC Mission but now you know they're CAT6!), who now have Shielding to protect them (the CAT6 Snipers can drop smoke bombs too, in case you didn't find them annoying already).

After enough enemies have been cleared, a cutscene will launch, and its time to meet the mastermind behind Shepard's utterly ruined shore leave...

...Shepard's Clone?! To this utterly shocking revelation, you can say...

"We don't have to fight" for +2 Paragon Points .

"There's only one Shepard" for +2 Renegade Points .

The Shepard Clone appears to have all of the physical benefits of the resurrected Shepard, but none of the Charm (but plenty of Intimidate, heh). Shepard tries to prevent their Clone from stealing the Normandy by initiating a lockdown, but the Clone blocks the signal and fools Traynor to prep for departure instead. To this you can say...

"Nobody takes my ship" for +2 Paragon Points .

"You're going to die" for +2 Renegade Points .

After that, you can use a Renegade Interrupt to shoot the model Citadel above (but don't worry about missing it as a Squad Mate on the balcony will do it instead).

Either way the cutscene ends and immediately puts you into battle. This time however you'll also have to contend with the CAT6 Heavy, who like most CAT6 foes is a remix of a Cerberus enemy, this time the Guardian. There are some key differences however:

Rather than using a standard metal riot shield, they use a holographic Omnishield. This means that you can't use the Lash power from the Omega DLC to remove them, but luckily their new weakness is for more readily available: Overload! They're also susceptible to Energy Drain and Sabotage. Unfortunately the Omnishield is only disabled temporarily, so once they're gone, lay down the hurt!

CAT6 Heavies are poor choices to get the Mail Slot Achievement with because they have Armor instead of health. Because of this you should remove the Omnishield with a tech power and then strip their armor with a fire-based power.

As for biotic powers, their Armor protects them from Liara's Singularity, but they are still vulnerable to Pull, hence why Javik is a viable Squad Mate choice.

Once all the enemies are down, Team Mako and Team Hammerhead press onward, while you yourself can start getting some loot! Stand in the middle of the room where the four desks are, then face the exit door with the green hologram panel.

Shotgun Ultralight Materials - On the corner of the desk ahead on your right.

Medical Station - 75 XP. On the side of the column near the desk where the Shotgun Ultralight Materials were.

Terminal - 3,750 credits. Continue through the exit door and up the ramp. At the top, check the left side of the reception desk for this laptop.

SMG Power Magnifier - Continue forward through one of the security scanners on either side of the room. On the other side, check the desks in the middle for this mod.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the same table as the SMG Power Magnifier described above.

Through the next door you'll enter the giant vault storage area, launching a brief cutscene showing the vastness of this area. Continue forward along the walkways where Shepard tells Glyph to search for their Clone, and at the end you'll get into yet another fight that breaks out. Luckily it's only two CAT6 Specialists on a wide open platform.

To continue, follow your squad's suggestion and stand on the platform, then step inside the vault container.

M-7 Lancer - Inside the vault, sitting in a display box close to the "Vault" objective marker.

Once the vault stops moving again, move forward by following the objective marker, taking you right and up some stairs. At the top, head right and drop down on top of another vault canister. Start forward and it's time for another fight. There's plenty of cover here, but beware of the CAT6 Snipers!

After crossing over the second vault containers, you can get some loot:

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the back-most walkway of the vault container area, on top of a crate. If you're heading to where Team Mako is being attacked, TURN AROUND!

Shepard finds themselves above Team Mako, who are in trouble! While you can shoot some enemies up here, it's actually best to drop down the end of the walkway, initiating a cutscene that, um, quite handily resolves the situation with at least 47 bullets.

After the cutscene, you'll now be in a sort of library area of the Archives, and like the Library in Halo: Combat Evolved, this section involves repeating indoor environments, so it can be a bit difficult trying to figure out where you are in it. Thus, we've split this section up by the upper and lower floors.

Your start on the upper floor, facing directly towards an archival hologram. We count these as goodies because they're great contributions to Mass Effect's overall lore, and we don't want you to miss them:

Turian Interrogation - In the blue hologram room directly ahead after the gratuitous balcony fire scene, depicting thee very first conversation between Humans and Turians in the First Contact War.

Kredak's Attack On Council - From the Turian Interrogation hologram, head through the exit door nearby and through the orange corridor. At the bottom of the ramp, look left to spot this, showing the moment the Krogan Rebellions officially began.

From the Kredak's Attack On Council hologram, turn around to face a glitchy hologram room: head down the ramp to the left of it to enter the first actual library room, which is broadly shaped like an O, with a walkway in the middle. You arrive in the southeastern corner of the O, with the exit door on your right to the north.

There's a fair few enemies to clear here, but while Teams Mako and Hammerhead are on the balconies above like in the opening room, they still aren't to be relied upon: any assistance they give is a handy bonus at most.

Illegal AIs - In another hologram room, this one directly across from the entry door.

To continue, head through the exit door and down the ramp, then turn left to spot a lone CAT6 Specialist in a malfunctioning hologram room. Kill him! The room up ahead doesn't look it, but it's essentially laid out like a big U, with hologram rooms on the sides and a shortcut walkway in the middle. There's fewer enemies here than the upper level, but one of them is a CAT6 Heavy so don't get complacent!

Once all is quiet, search the area for goodies:

Medical Station - 75 XP. At the malfunctioning hologram room where the lone CAT6 Specialist was. From the original entry door, enter the room, then look left to spot this on the wall.

Battle of the Citadel - An actually functioning hologram room, connected to the malfunctioning hologram room with the Medical Station. As Shepard is currently a Spectre, their clearance unlocks an additional entry that reveals Tap to Reveal !

Terminal - 3,750 credits. Using your minimap, head for the southwestern corner of this floor (the thin diamond on the edge of the minimap indicates north). This laptop will be on the corner desk there.

Sniper Rifle High-Velocity Barrel - At the southern desks where the Terminal described above was. This is located in the middle arrangement of desks on this wall.

Med Kit - 50 XP. When you're ready to continue, locate the exit door illuminated in green with Glyph floating next to it. Go through it and down the ramp to enter a zig-zagging orange corridor. At this corridor's exit door, turn around to face away from it. Check the crates on your right to spot this Med Kit tucked between one of them and the railing.

Out the orange corridor you'll be back in a huge open vault container area, with Team Mako pinned down by an Atlas mech. All the rules that apply to the Cerberus Atlas mech apply to this one: take over and only pop out to shoot at it when it's safe and not firing at you.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On some crates at the bottom of the ramp heading up to the next area.

Continue up the ramp and along the walkway, then drop off the end and turn left to face the next contingent of enemies, whom Glyph identifies as Razor Squad. For best results, you'll want to climb up the ladder on the upper walkways, giving you the high ground (if you brought a sniper rifle, now's a great time to use it!).

The initial CAT6 Snipers will be backed up by no less than four CAT6 Heavies that arrive on the central platform, so make sure to use Overload and other powers liberally to expose them. Be aware though that unlike Cerberus Guardians, CAT6 Heavies ARE capable of climbing ladders, so make sure you know where all four of them are!

Med Kit - 50 XP. Sitting on the left-hand crates of the Razor Squad area, between the CAT6 Heavy platform and the exit door.

Head through the door to enter the next archive library area, Level 5.

Similarly to Level 3, Level 5 is also somewhat confusingly laid out, so we've once again split it in two. This time, you start out on the...

The lower floor is shaped like a large U, once again with a shortcut walkway in the middle, with only a handful of enemies towards the exit door. Mop them up, then return to the entry door: this area has a lot of good stuff!

Terminal - 3,750 credits. From the entry to the Level 5 Lower Floor, take the left-hand path at the split, where you'll look down a long walkway. Take a few steps forward and keep an eye on your right for some desks. Here you can find this laptop.

Krogan Genophage Deployment - From the Terminal described above, back up a bit and enter the first hologram room on your left, depicting the actual deployment of the Genophage.

Medical Station - 75 XP. At the Genophage hologram, turn right to look down the blue corridor. On the right-hand wall of the corridor will be this Medical Station.

Assault Rifle Ultralight Materials - Further down the hologram room corridor where the Medical Station is. This will be on a desk right next to...

Beelo Gurji the First Spectre - At the opposite end of the hologram corridor, depicting the induction of an STG operative as the first Spectre.

Sniper Rifle Ultralight Materials - Return to the open walkway area and locate the walkway shortcut crossing over to the opposite side of the room. This mod will be here on some crates.

Terminal - 3,750 credits. For this last item, face north towards the malfunctioning hologram terminal, then approach the desk to the left-hand side of it to find this laptop there.

Speaking of the malfunctioning hologram, if you return to where the Sniper Rifle Ultralight Materials mod was, look back at it to discover an "ancient religious artifact" from Earth, referencing another famous archive from the realm of film.

Having trouble seeing it? Check out this video .

To leave, locate the exit door and head up the ramp.

On the upper floor is another that's shaped like a U with a shortcut walkway in the middle. Here you'll immediately get into a gunfight with some CAT6 Heavies and three CAT6 Snipers, so vanquish them with your usual tricks and strategies. Once they're done, seek out the final two archive holograms:

First Citadel Landing - In the back-right (ie northeastern) corner of this floor, depicting the discovery of the Citadel by this cycle.

First Human Spectre - Continue via the exit and up the ramp to reach the upper -upper floor of Level 5. Here, turn right and you'll spot this across the way, depicting the deliberations around the first Human Spectre (that's you, chief!).

As you progress down the upper-upper floor, you'll get a call from Brooks saying that Hammerhead and Mako have gone on ahead to take on the Clone, but she's been hit and need assistance. Rush through the next door, through the scanner room, and to Brooks on the other side of the area requiring "Bio-Metric identification".

...or not. Turns out, it was a trap, and Shepard is now stuck. And on top of that, Brooks reveals that she was working for the Clone! Here you can optionally use Investigate, learning that Brooks was the one who gathered the two Dossier sets for the Illusive Man back in the second game. Here you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "I will end you" for +2 Paragon Points . After this, pull the first of the three Paragon Interrupts for +5 Paragon Points more.

After this, pull the first of the three Paragon Interrupts for +5 Paragon Points more.

Pick "I will end you painfully" for +5 Paragon Points . After this, pull the first of the three Renegade Interrupts for +5 Renegade Points more.

After this, pull the first of the three Renegade Interrupts for +5 Renegade Points more.

Verbal threats won't get Shepard out of a shielded iridium vault, however, allowing the Clone to replace Shepard's biometrics with their own. During this, they'll accuse their counterpart of growing soft by relying on aliens over the course of their career, which rings hollow for Paragon players, but if you've been Renegade since the first game, well, they kinda have a point...

Pick "They all matter" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "You've saved no one" for +2 Renegade Points .

After this, the Clone and Brooks head out for the Normandy, leaving Shepard and crew trapped in vaults, though not for long thanks to Glyph. During this, you have one final spot for Morality Points based on the Clone's parting words to Shepard:

Pick "Seriously, I sound like that?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I say much cooler things" for +2 Renegade Points .

At this point the Team Player Achievement / Trophy should unlock. The next cutscene marks the beginning of the next Mission of the Citadel DLC, so use the link in the box below to jump over to it.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

Up Next: Citadel Docks: Capture the Ship

articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Citadel: Party DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Citadel: Party DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters (pfft), and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

War Asset: +35 TMS to Alliance Frigate Normandy SR-2

"Citadel: Party" is considered the finale of the Citadel DLC, as the action you're expected to do after it is return to the Normandy to conclude her crew's shore leave and return to saving the galaxy.

As such, we highly, HIGHLY, HIGHLY recommend doing everything else at the Silversun Strip before you initiate the Party. Here are the various locations and activities you should do beforehand:

Personal Apartment - Can be customized by purchasing furniture in the Tiberius Towers lobby. Highly recommended so that the apartment can feel truly yours for any scenes that take place in it.

Character Meetups - The highlight of the Citadel DLC, these allow you to meet up with literally every available Squad Mate in the Mass Effect Trilogy. A few of these will also adjust the dialogue in the Party!

Armax Arsenal Arena - A combat arena similar to the first game's Pinnacle Station DLC , this has its own line of Side Missions that has great rewards.

Castle Arcade - An arcade with three games to play, each with their own rewards, including Weapon Mods and apartment music!

Silver Coast Casino - Allows you to play Quasar, Roulette and bet on Varren Racing, and is also where you buy the supplies for the Party.

Immediately upon concluding the Identity Theft storyline and returning to your Personal Apartment , Joker coerces Shepard into throwing a party. In order for this soirée to go down, preparations will need to be made. Glyph will act as a guide through the process, stating the two things that need to happen in order for the party to start:

The Party Supplies can be bought at the Silver Coast Casino , the venue for the earlier " Silver Coast Casino: Infiltration " Mission. To get there, exit the Apartment, then go down the hallway and onto the Silversun Strip. Turn right, then go to the red-lit area in the back-left corner of the strip, which marks the entrance to the Silver Coast Casino.

Here, take one of the curved stairs to the upper bar, marked with an 8 on the map screen (this is where you met with Brooks and you got the yellow wire-sensing lenses). Locate the Party Supplies terminal and buy some for 100 credits (does this terminal only sell Party Supplies...?). This will be subject to any store discounts, so you could be buying it for the low low price of only 90 credits!

Once the supplies have been purchased, return to the Apartment and head for Shepard's Private Terminal, in the study room under the stairs. Now that you've purchased the Party Supplies, there's a new "Send Invitations" option on the right. Shepard may choose to Invite All, only some, or none of the rest.

A selection of the Normandy's current crew have been automatically invited: Joker , Glyph , EDI , Cortez , Traynor , Liara , and James (if you're paying attention, these are all the guests who are guaranteed to be alive at this point!). The rest will need to be invited manually.

The as-yet uninvited Squad Mates all have prerequisites you must complete for them to become available, both to Invite to the Party and to meet on the Silversun Strip .

Mass Effect 2 Squad Mates are assumed to have been recruited and have survived the final Mission of that game.

You also do NOT need to complete any Character Meetups on the Silversun Strip to unlock someone to Invite to the Party, although doing so can adjust their dialogue at the Party in minor ways.

Here's all the specific unlock requirements:

Garrus Vakarian - Has no prerequisite outside of surviving the second game. Nice!

Grunt - Survived " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ".

Kasumi Goto - Completed " Kasumi: Stolen Memory " in Mass Effect 2, and then " Citadel: Hanar Diplomat " in Mass Effect 3.

Miranda Lawson - Survived " Priority: Horizon ". Miranda is the final Squad Mate you can unlock an Invitation to the Party for.

Mordin Solus - A very unique example. Tap to Reveal

Tali'Zorah vas Normandy - Survived " Priority: Rannoch ".

Thane Krios - Another unique example. Tap to Reveal .

Urdnot Wrex - Survived Virmire in Mass Effect 1, then genuinely cured the Genophage in " Priority: Tuchanka " in Mass Effect 3.

Virmire Survivor - Survived " Priority: The Citadel 2 ", then recruited as a Normandy Squad Mate.

Zaeed Massani - Secured Loyalty in " Zaeed: The Price of Revenge " in Mass Effect 2, then complete " Citadel: Volus Ambassador " in Mass Effect 3.

When you're ready, select "Throw Party" from the Invitations menu of the Apartment's Private Terminal. You will however still be able to opt out of the party if you need more time (for example, having more Squad Mates to unlock invitations for).

When you're ready, Glyph will ask you what type of party you'd like to throw. This ties into how the Party actually works:

Phase 1 - This will always have the same group layout. Quiet and Energetic only determines some character dialogue as well as the background music.

Phases 2 and 3 - These Phases are the ones that differ from each other when it comes to the layout of the groups, who's in them, and what they're talking about. HOWEVER, the mood you picked for Phase 2 will also be the mood for Phase 3! Quiet Party - A relaxed get-together that prioritizes thoughtful and reminiscent conversation. Energetic Party - A loud party with more opportunities to change how it goes later on. Group Photo - A little bonus at the end of Phase 3 for either Party.

Quiet Party - A relaxed get-together that prioritizes thoughtful and reminiscent conversation.

Energetic Party - A loud party with more opportunities to change how it goes later on.

Group Photo - A little bonus at the end of Phase 3 for either Party.

Investigate the Aftermath - The final phase takes place in the morning. Similarly to Phase 1, this is mostly the same no matter what type of party you threw, outside of some character dialogue.

Return to the Normandy - After the party has been thrown, you're asked to go to the Rapid Transit on the Silversun Strip to round everyone up on the Normandy to resume saving the galaxy.

Shepard's "job" is to roam the party and talk to the various groups of guests. If you're interested in hearing everything (and if you're playing this DLC, you probably are!) , here's how this can work:

Each phase will collect your guests into various groups in the biggest rooms of the Apartment: the open lounge, the bar lounge, the kitchen, the library study, the mezzanine, and the upstairs lounge.

Some characters will split off and can be encountered in one of the smaller rooms.

Each group will have "walk-in intros" to overhear, as well as "walk-in outros" you can hear after you've sat down with the group. You can "farm" these by walking out of range of the group and then back: you can tell you're done when you get either no response or a generic "Shepard" / "Hey" / etc when you get close.

After you've sat down with two, three or all four main groups, you'll be able to move things along by talking to Glyph.

Dialogue varies on if the Party is Quiet or Energetic.

In an Energetic Party, James will start making moves on Ashley, if both are present and un-Romanced during an Energetic Party.

You can talk with Liara and Traynor afterward. Traynor will explain why Dr. Chakwas isn't in attendance.

You can talk with Joker, EDI and Jacob afterward. Jacob's will be quite different if you Romanced him in Mass Effect 2.

Wrex can be talked to four times afterward, and Javik thrice.

If one Krogan is missing, the other and Zaeed will be with "Party Mood Comments", while Javik will be with "Normandy Small Talk".

When you next talk to Glyph, you can choose the theme of the party again. Do note that this will choose the theme for the rest of the party!

Will differ depending on if Wrex, Grunt or both are present.

Pick "Making Food" or "Mixing Drinks" to affect Quiet Phase 3.

You can talk to Jack and Cortez afterward.

Pick "Normandy SR1" or "Normandy SR2" to affect Quiet Phase 3.

In the downstairs bathroom under the stairs.

Grunt can be talked to thrice afterward.

Has two walk-in outros, which will differ if Zaeed isn't present.

The initial topic is determined by your choice in the library study in Quiet Phase 2.

You can talk to Ashley four times afterward, and Miranda twice.

After sitting down with all three main groups, you can return to the downstairs open lounge area to take the Group Photo .

Pick "Invite Up" to see for yourself, or "Turn Away" to reject them yourself.

Grunt can be talked to five times afterward.

Pick "Cortez" or "Joker" to affect the walk-in outros and Energetic Phase 3.

If Zaeed isn't present, Samara will be under the glass stairs near the entrance. If Samara isn't present, Zaeed is at "Target Practice?"

Pick "Support Conflict" to keep them throwing insults, or "Support Friendship" to have them give compliments.

If one isn't present, the other will be at "Brains or Brawn?".

Pick "Support Biotics" or "Support Physical" to affect Energetic Phase 3.

Has only one walk-in outro (thank goodness ).

At the statue at the end of the mezzanine.

At the display shelves in the upstairs lounge.

Pick "Support Sitting" for EDI to "help", or "Support Dancing" to force Joker to dance.

Pick "Support Cool It" for them to return to the mezzanine or "Support Hook Up" for them to, well, hook up.

If they Hook Up, has three walk-in outros.

Has six walk-in intros (that consist of, well, grunting).

Grunt can be talked to twenty-three times, ending just after the comment about clowns.

After sitting down with all four main groups, you can return to the downstairs open lounge area to take the Group Photo .

Once you've sat down with all the main groups in Phase 3, head to the couches in the downstairs open lounge and Use the Take Group Photo prompt. Doing this will unlock the Perfect Host Achievement / Trophy!

The morning after the party finds Shepard in the master bedroom, with an intimate guest accompanying them. There are three options as to who this guest will be:

If Shepard is in a locked-in Romance, that Romance partner will be with them in the bed.

If a female Shepard has no locked-in Romance, but flirted with James in his Character Meetup , he will be with her in the bed.

If neither of the above are true, the person in the bed with Shepard will be Tap to Reveal .

There may also be another bonus! If Mordin was present during the Tuchanka arc of the game, you can find a Datapad next to the bed in the master bedroom containing 7 archival recordings from him.

Here's where all the characters can be found across the Personal Apartment. Javik, Ashley and Wrex's comments vary depending on the party theme. What they say will differ from if Phases 2 and 3 were Quiet or Energetic; these crew members will be marked with an asterisk (*)

Upstairs: Javik * - In the en-suite spa of the master bedroom (2-3 comments). Liara* - In the upstairs lounge (2 comments). Garrus - In the upstairs lounge (2 comments). Samara - Under the tree outside the upstairs guest bedroom (4 comments). Tali - On the bed of the upstairs guest bedroom (6 comments). Kasumi - On the mezzanine (6 comments).

Javik * - In the en-suite spa of the master bedroom (2-3 comments).

Liara* - In the upstairs lounge (2 comments).

Garrus - In the upstairs lounge (2 comments).

Samara - Under the tree outside the upstairs guest bedroom (4 comments).

Tali - On the bed of the upstairs guest bedroom (6 comments).

Downstairs Bar Lounge: Joker - Slumping on the bar (6 comments). Wrex* - On the sofa (3 comments).

Joker - Slumping on the bar (6 comments).

Downstairs Open Lounge: Zaeed - On one of the sofas (2 comments). Cortez - On one of the sofas (4 comment). EDI - Standing at the window near the piano (3 comments).

Zaeed - On one of the sofas (2 comments).

Cortez - On one of the sofas (4 comment).

EDI - Standing at the window near the piano (3 comments).

Downstairs Guest Bedroom: Jacob - Doing crunches (3 comments). Jack - Doing pull-ups (4 comments).

Kitchen: James - Making eggs (2 comments). Ashley * - In the kitchen (2 comments). Miranda - In the kitchen (4 comments). Grunt* - In the kitchen (2 comments).

Traynor - In the library study (6 comments).

After talking with at least two guests at the party's aftermath, this becomes the objective. Exit the Apartment to the Silversun Strip, then use the Rapid Transit terminal between Tiberius Towers and the Armax Arena to wrap things up. You can actually still do whatever you want on the Silversun Strip, but Shepard will currently be unable to initiate any Character Meetups at the Apartment due to the Private Terminal being inaccessible.

Return to the Normandy via the Rapid Transit terminal to initiate a final cutscene. A fitting, memorable end... before the end. And, if you're a female Shepard who Romanced Thane in Mass Effect 2 and nobody else in 3, this scene will be a little bit longer than it usually is.

...now, Shepard can actually still return to the Silversun Strip and the Apartment anytime they want. The Apartment will no longer be full of party guests, their Private Terminal will be available again, and you can still initiate any Character Meetups you haven't done yet. Nice!

This wraps up your adventures in the Citadel DLC, and if you've been following our guide in order, it was the last thing you could do before the point of no return. If that's the case, your next task will be...
