articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Zaeed: The Price of Revenge DLC Mission, including how to access and unlock it, how to
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Zaeed: The Price of Revenge DLC Mission, including how to access and unlock it, how to recruit Zaeed, how to complete his Loyalty Mission, and how to get all the collectibles, including the Firestorm Heavy Weapon.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Original release: On Xbox 360, the Zaeed: The Price of Revenge DLC is only available as a download via the Cerberus Network, which can be activated by going to your EA account and using the Redeem Product Code section. On PlayStation 3, Zaeed: The Price of Revenge is available by downloading the "Cerberus Pack" for free via the PSN Store. On PC, most storefronts will label this as "Mass Effect 2 (2010)", which now include Zaeed: The Price of Revenge as part of the download.

On Xbox 360, the Zaeed: The Price of Revenge DLC is only available as a download via the Cerberus Network, which can be activated by going to your EA account and using the Redeem Product Code section.

On PlayStation 3, Zaeed: The Price of Revenge is available by downloading the "Cerberus Pack" for free via the PSN Store.

On PC, most storefronts will label this as "Mass Effect 2 (2010)", which now include Zaeed: The Price of Revenge as part of the download.

In the Legendary Edition of Mass Effect 2, the Zaeed: The Price of Revenge DLC is automatically included.

Zaeed: The Price of Revenge is available in-game as soon as Commander Shepard gains captaincy of their own ship after the " Freedom's Progress " Mission.

Location : Omega Nebula - Sahrabarik - Omega

Recruiting Zaeed is one of the simplest tasks in the game, and can be done as soon as you complete the Freedom's Progress Mission and acquire the Normandy SR-2. Set your sights for Omega in the Sahrabarik system.

If you're interested in mining, here's the one Rich planet in the system Omega is in, Sahrabarik:

At the far end of the entrance corridor will be Zaeed, railing on a Batarian. Talk to him to recruit him for your cause. Along the way you can pick up 6 Morality Points by giving Paragon or Renegade responses, depending on the options you pick. Here's your selection, grouped by Morality:

Paragon : "Welcome aboard", "No. He didn't", and "We can do that" ( +6 Paragon Points total)

Renegade : "Report to the Normandy", "There's always a catch", and "If there's time" ( +6 Rengade Points total)

Zaeed will take up lodgings in the Port Cargo Bay down on Engineering. These are very much his quarters, so he'll have a bunch of objects to interact with and will have two stories to tell after every Mission or Side Quest you complete.

Research : Heavy Weapon Ammo (Paragon) Assault Rifle Damage (Renegade)

Mission Credits : 30,000 credits (Paragon) 15,000 credits (Renegade)

Found Credits : 30,000 credits (Paragon) 24,000 credits (Renegade)

Resources : 2,000 Palladium (Paragon) 1,600 Palladium (Renegade)

Location : Ismar Frontier - Faia - Zorya

The main Loyalty Mission itself will take place on planet Zorya, which is in the Faia system of the Ismar Frontier (the Ismar Frontier is in the North-West area of the Milky Way). You'll need about 200 Fuel in order to travel to the Faia system from Aquila.

If you're interested in some mining, here's the Rich planets located in the Aquila and Faia systems, the two you'll be visiting in the process of getting to this Mission.

Squad Tactics: Miranda is a good pick for her Overload power to strip the Shields of enemies in this level, which she'll be doing a lot. While Zaeed is of course mandatory, it's a good idea to have him switch to his sniper rifle considering the very long sight lines in this level.

Miranda is a good pick for her Overload power to strip the Shields of enemies in this level, which she'll be doing a lot.

While Zaeed is of course mandatory, it's a good idea to have him switch to his sniper rifle considering the very long sight lines in this level.

Zaeed's Loyalty Mission begins with your party touching down on the jungle border of the Eldfell-Ashland Refinery on planet Zorya. As soon as you start moving forward through the linear passage between the cliffs, you hear a radio signal from Vido Santiago, the man that Zaeed has sworn to kill, calling for a squad to investigate your landing zone.

As you move forward, you'll find some bodies that you can Investigate, which will prompt Zaeed to make a comment on Vido's brutality. Continue moving through the passageway as the radio chatter intensifies. Vido's team definitely knows you're here at this point, and you're ambushed by a squad of Blue Suns not too far ahead.

The Blue Suns Troopers and Blue Suns Heavy are heavily shielded; take them down by staying in the first position of cover you see while flushing them out of their cover spots and picking them off one-by-one. Moving up, another squad of Blue Suns will attack you - this time with a mixture of Blue Suns Troopers, Blue Suns Heavy, Blue Suns Pyro and a FENRIS Mech that can deal serious damage to you at close quarters if you aren't ready for it.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. On the right-hand side of the area, on a metal floor at the base of a support column near the bottom of the rocky cliff.

PDA - 6,000 Credits. Next to a fallen over crate on its lonesome in the back-right corner of the area.

Just ahead, you'll reach a Bridge Control. Activate it, and you'll spark a dialogue between yourself and Zaeed as he gives you a rundown of why you're here. At this point, you can get some Morality Points:

Reply "You know this guy?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Reply "Vido sounds dangerous" for +2 Renegade Points .

As it turns out, Zaeed co-founded the Blue Suns with Vido 20 years ago, after which Vido betrayed him and shot him in the head, explaining the severe damage to Zaeed's face.

Continue forward across the bridge to the gatehouse. After going up the ramp on the other side of the bridge, keep an eye out for some goodies:

400 Refined Palladium - After going across the bridge and starting up the hill, you can find this on your left, on top of a small crate next to a large rock.

Up ahead you'll enter the gatehouse and have a meeting with Vido Santiago. Zaeed goes overboard and starts a chain reaction in the refinery to try and kill his archenemy, but Vido escapes. Here you can confront him over his actions for Morality Points:

Respond with "That was unnecessary" for +2 Paragon Points , after which you can finish the conversation with a Paragon Interrupt for +5 Paragon Points .

Respond with "Explain yourself!" or "Warn me next time", or ignore the Paragon Interrupt, and you'll get a different end to the conversation. See below!

If you didn't get or go for the Paragon Interrupt, you have more Morality Point opportunities (you won't get as many Paragon Points with this route). Your options are as follows:

Paragon : "We came to save these people" and "Keep to the mission, or else" ( +4 Paragon Points total)

Renegade : "You do what I tell you" and "If that's what you need" ( +4 Renegade Points total)

After the dialogue ends, you're thrown into combat against a small squad of Blue Suns Troopers, so quickly take cover via the short metal wall in the middle and gun them down.

400 Refined Palladium - Before moving on, look to your left to see the valve Zaeed bashed with his gun during the cutscene. The Palladium will be there.

Continue moving through the facility walkway, and eventually you'll come to a brief fork, with a door on your left.

400 Refined Palladium - At the fork, go right to find the Palladium. Make sure to grab it BEFORE interacting with the door, as that initiates a point of no return!

When you open the door, a refinery worker will desperately call at you for help, as they can't access the valve controls to turn off the fire. Zaeed doesn't care and has eyes only for Vido. At the outset, you can get some Morality Points:

Reply with "You suggest we leave them?" for +2 Paragon Points .

Reply with "You must really want him dead" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then have a big decision to make: whether to take the time to save the workers, or ignore them and head straight for Vido (kinda like Asteroid X57 in the first game!). Each option has its own path that has exclusive rewards, some of which aren't apparent until the end of the Mission:

Zaeed's Loyalty up to a Persuasion Check

Taking this option makes Zaeed quite upset that you aren't going after Vido immediately, but he's at least practical enough to know there's no arguing and you'd better get to it. After Shepard jumps down onto the platform below, move down the ramps and Bypass the door to get inside. Here, your path will be regularly blocked by fire, and you'll need to use Fuel Control panels to keep moving forwards. To start, move up the flight of stairs and through the door on your right.

Pass through the flames in the doorway and then activate the first Fuel Control panel to clear the ramp forwards. Cross over, then hit the second Fuel Control panel hidden away on the left, which will remove the fire blocking the next ramp. Cross over it.

Generator Pipe - 6,000 Credits. After going over the ramp formerly blocked by fire, check the back-right corner for this to Salvage.

Continue up the next set of stairs, and an explosion causes a metal beam to appear on the floor. Here on the right the workers will try talking to you. Heed their advice and hit the next Fuel Control panel to clear the last ramp. Move forward and up the next flight of stairs.

Continue along the walkway until an explosion blows up the way forward, forcing you up the detour ramp to your right. Move across it and back down onto the main path.

400 Refined Palladium - After going around the detour ramp, instead of turning left, continue straight towards the wall: you'll find this on your left.

After getting the Palladium, head into the next room via the nearby door.

Research Terminal - Heavy Weapons Ammo. In the room you just entered, the one with the Fire Extinguisher Systems.

Once you have the Research, use the Fire Extinguisher Systems to put out the fire. Move through the door and onto the next catwalk and then jump down onto the crates. This is where the Paragon and Renegade routes meet back up, so click here to continue through the rest of the level .

Fight Through the Refinery (Renegade Route)

Going directly to kill Vido will take you through a route that's almost entirely combat. As you move through this next section, you hear explosions and screams as the refinery is blown apart. Moving forward, you will need to fight another squad of Blue Suns Troopers. As you approach the walkway across the chasm, it'll be blown up by the refinery's chain reaction: you'll have to find another way across.

At this moment you'll get into another fight with more Troopers and a Pyro attacking from your right. Defeat them, then head through the same interior passage they ambushed you from for some goodies:

Servos - 6,000 Credits. Directly across from the door you just went through.

Research Terminal - Assault Rifle Damage. Up the ramp that's near the Servos.

Move through the next door and fight the moderately large squad of Blue Suns Troopers that storm at you. Be careful to pick off the enemies on the ledge as well. Next, move through the same door they came from and up the walkway through another door. You'll now be at the other end of the split, where the Renegade and Paragon paths meet back up.

The two paths merge in the hallway dripping with water and a tall pile of crates on the right-hand wall; Paragon players will have dropped down these crates.

400 Refined Palladium - To the left of the crate pile that, if you're Paragon, you just dropped down.

M-451 Firestorm - Through the next door you can find this Heavy Weapon on the floor, next to a Blue Sun Trooper crushed by a steel beam. If you miss it, you'll still get it at the end of the Mission courtesy of Zaeed.

In the next room on the right you'll be ambushed by two Blue Suns Troopers. Kill them! then grab the Power Cells next to the Weapons Locker. Use it if you prefer using a different Heavy Weapon to the Firestorm.

Servos PDA - 6,000 Credits. On a crate in the middle of the room (see note below).

The next room is the refinery core, where you will face off against a series of Blue Suns Troopers, Pyros, Heavies, and an YMIR Mech at the very end. The best strategy is to stay in cover and have both of your Squad Mates cover the two flanks while enemies ascend up the stairs on both sides. There isn't any good spot the camp down in the middle though, so you may have to improvise.

Also on both sides of the room are two loose fuel tanks that move forward and backward in a straight line. They fall to the ground and explode when shot at enough times, causing massive area damage that you can use to flush out enemy troop clusters hiding behind cover. You'll probably want to shoot them down anyway because their downward fire streams deal significant damage. If you're playing the original release however, their explosions also hurt you and your Squad, so you'll need to be careful when dropping them (this doesn't apply to the Legendary Edition).

After the fight is over, check the area for more goodies.

Med Kit - 100 Credits. At the corner of a ground pipe between the doors to the side-areas.

Various Industrial Bits - 6,000 Credits. In one of the side-areas where the Blue Suns troops were entering the room from.

Various Industrial Bits - 6,000 Credits. In the other side area where the Blue Suns Troops were entering the room from.

When you're ready to move on, head down the steps to the lowest platform, move across the bridge, and head out the door to your right.

Once you go through the door, you'll be at the finale of the level. This scene will differ depending on your choice before entering the refinery.

If you took the Renegade route, Zaeed will catch Vido before he can make it into his gunship. Vido attempts to run, but Zaeed shoots faster - nailing Vido in the kneecap and forcing him to the ground. Vido pleads for his life, and Zaeed responds by ejecting a Thermal Clip into the nearby fuel spill, causing an ignition that scorches Vido to death.

This ending will always result in Zaeed being Loyal to Shepard.

If you took the Paragon path however, things will be more complicated: Vido has enough time to escape in his gunship, and Zaeed is enraged at losing his chance to kill him. He's quickly humbled by his own hubris however, as an explosion pins him down via a steel beam. At this point, you can get some Morality Points:

"Are you hurt?" and "I don't want you on my ship" ( +4 Paragon Points total)

"You deserved that" and "Why should I trust you?" ( +4 Renegade Points total)

When Zaeed tells you to stop screwing around, you're given an important set of choices, as it's here where you determine if Zaeed will be Loyal to you when you leave and conclude the Mission:

The Charm option, "You brought this on yourself", will convince Zaeed to put the past behind him and secure his Loyalty to you. You'll also get +7 Paragon Points .

"You owe me big for this" and "Come on, Zaeed. Let's go" will award +2 Paragon Points , but WILL NOT secure Zaeed's Loyalty to you, putting him at risk at the end of the game.

"I'm leaving you here" is only available if you did this Mission AFTER the Suicide Mission and have at least two other Squad Mates. Shepard leaves Zaeed to die, not securing his Loyalty and eliminating him as a future Squad Mate and story character.

Here's what you can do on the Normandy now:

CIC - Talk to Kelly to hear about Zaeed after his Mission, and Joker about things in the cockpit.

Crew Deck - Talk Kasumi, and to Chakwas if you did the Serrice Ice Brandy last time.

Engineering - Talk to Zaeed for a post-mortem of his Loyalty Mission.

Since you completed his Loyalty Mission you can also use the Squad Menu to put Zaeed into a cleaner palette of armor modeled after the Blood Pack's colours rather than the Eclipse.

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.title: Treasure Maps - Red Dead Redemption 2 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are 11 treasure stashes hidden across the different regions and locations in Red Dead Redemption 2. This guide will provide a complete walkthrough for
articles.body:
There are 11 treasure stashes hidden across the different regions and locations in Red Dead Redemption 2 . This guide will provide a complete walkthrough for solving and finding all Treasure Maps , which will often reward you with lucrative Gold Bars .

Looking to find a particular Treasure Map? Click the links below to jump to...

Red Dead Redemption 2 (RDR2) Treasure Maps

Treasure Maps in Red Dead 2 show a drawing of an area with steps to reach the treasure. You can find maps on your own or purchase them from treasure hunters around the world.

Looking for a particular Treasure Map? Click the links below to jump to their individual page or continue scrolling below to find a complete list on this page.

The Jack Hall Gang , a band of outlaws from yesteryear, left their stash of gold somewhere in or around New Hanover .

You can purchase the first map in this treasure hunt from Maximo, a treasure hunter you can meet after starting Chapter 2 near Flatneck Station . He will offer to sell you the map for $5 if you decline, or you can kill him and take it off of his body. If you fail to collect the map from Maximo, it can be purchased from a Fence later on.

The first map to the Jack Hall Gang treasure can be purchased from Maximo, a treasure hunter found on the ridge overlooking the river north-west of Flatneck Station and north of Bard's Crossing , for $10.00.

The map depicts Caliban's Seat, a unique rock formation to the south of Valentine .

Scale the hill on the eastern side to reach the top.

Follow a path through the rocks from the top.

Move along the ledge, jumping across gaps and mantling over ledges, until you reach a large swath of white granite with a small hole in it.

You'll find the treasure - and another map - inside.

The second map to the Jack Hall gang treasure is found by finding the stash from the first Jack Hall map.

The location depicted in the map is Cotorra Springs , just east of the dividing line between the E and W Grizzlies in Ambarino . This is also the location of a Legendary Wolf , so tread cautiously in this area.

Head to the west end of the springs area, where you'll find a small circle of unique rock formations.

The treasure stash is inside the central stack of rocks.

Map number three leads you to the lake at O'Creagh's Run , just north of Three Sisters in the Grizzlies East region of Ambarino .

To get there, head directly north into the hills from Emerald Ranch .

You'll find the gang's treasure - two gold bars - under a rock on the small rocky island in the middle of the lake.

The High Stakes treasure can be started either during a random encounter out in the world, or later by purchasing a map from a fence if the player has missed the random encounter enough times.

To find the first of the High Stakes treasure maps , you'll need to keep an eye out for an older treasure hunter .

He won't willingly give up his map, so you'll need to either rob him at gunpoint, kill, or hogtie and then loot him. If those don't fit your fancy, just run into him hard enough and he will drop the map.

We've had the best luck spotting him at the top of a large rock to the north-east of Riggs Station, though he can also appear in various locations between Strawberry and Valentine .

Once you've collected the map, you'll find the first treasure stash at Cumberland Falls, west of Valentine .

Approach the base of the falls from the west, then swim across to the rocks on the south side of the falls.

You'll find a fallen tree allows you to get up to the side of the waterfall - climb up behind the falls to collect the stash and the next map.

The second High Stakes Treasure Map will lead you north, into the Grizzlies West .

This treasure stash is located above the frozen water of Barrow Lagoon , between Lake Isabelle and Widow Rock.

Head down onto the frozen lake and look for a tree bridging the ice-coated island and the rocky banks of the lagoon.

You'll find the treasure and the next map stashed in the knot of the log bridge.

This final High Stakes map will take you close to Fort Wallace.

It's on the large rock formation directly next to Ft Wallace to the north-east.

Ride along the path leading east around the front of the fort, then veer off to ride up the hill on the backside of the large rock face.

At the top you'll find a path leading down between the two peaks of the rock. Follow it down to the cliff side below and turn left.

Follow the ledge and then continue up the thin ramp that rises ahead of you, crouching to make your way around the corner.

There's a slight drop ahead of you - jump down, then turn around and drop to the next ledge down.

Jump across to the next ledge and crouch under the low overhang - you'll find three gold bars stashed in the rocks at the end of the overhang.

The Poisonous Trail is a unique set of treasure maps in that you cannot buy the starter map anywhere, nor will anyone tell you about it. Instead, you will have to stumble upon it in the wilderness, requiring you to journey across the lands in Red Dead 2.

To locate the first map, head up to the Grizzlies West where Chapter 1 of the game took place, and head southeast from the town of Colter you were holed up in, to the small Cairn Lake.

Enter the Cairn Lake Lodge, and look under the bed for a lock box you can loot - which will contain the Poisonous Trail Map 1.

The Map features an iconic looking rock face that looks like a head, with a path leading to the right winding past trees to the treasure.

You'll find this geographical feature in the state of Lemoyne , North of Rhodes , and North of the Hill Haven Ranch along the road up in the Scarlett Meadows.

Look for the Face Rock on the left side of the road as you go northwest of Hill Haven Ranch.

Consult the map and go right from the rock face past a tree and down a slope.

Here you will see a withered tree trunk, and a fallen log behind it.

Search behind the withered tree trunk to find a hole at the base which you can inspect to find the next map piece.

Upon finding the treasure map at the Face Rock in Scarlett Meadows, you will have your next clue. The map will feature a snake-like formation, and a mound with rocks where the treasure is located.

You can find this geoglyph in lower Roanoke Ridge in New Hanover , just to the west of the Van Horn Trading Post along the lower road going towards the Kamassa River .

Halfway along the road to the river past the train tracks, head south up the hill to find an abandoned tower you can climb.

At the top, look down on the hillside to spot the geoglyph of the snake, which Arthur will draw in his journal.

At the top of the hill is the circular end of the snake with a rocky mound in the middle.

Climb down into the mound and inspect the hole to get the next treasure map.

The final map you find at the Snake Geoglyph points to the location of treasure in a hidden cave. The map depicts a waterfall with a passage behind it, and a secret tunnel off to the right leading to treasure.

Move north of the Snake Geoglyph up to the Elysian Pool in New Hanover 's central Roanoke Ridge .

At the north end of the pool where the river empties out you will find a large waterfall.

Leave your horse behind and jump headfirst into the waterfall, where you'll find a secret passage into a large cave system on the other side.

As you move deeper past the initial cave tunnel, ignore the rest of the cave on the map, and look down on the right in the first large corridor for a small slope down to a pit.

At the bottom of the pit, check the wall on the right for a small hole to crawl through into a new area.

The next part has a crossroads with two paths - and by consulting your map you'll find that going right is the correct choice. You can also find an abandoned campsite here with a lock box that holds some valuables .

Moving past the campsite, you'll come out onto a ledge. Look to the left with your lantern to find a pit below you, and a lower ledge on the left that you must run to (tap the run button to build speed) and then jump across to land safely.

After landing on the lower ledge, look for a long slope on the other side to fall down to a dead end with some water, and a pile of rocks on the left.

Climb up and inspect the large rock pile to find at last the treasure of The Poisonous Trail - 4 Gold Bars , which sell for $500 a piece at your local Fence !

The Red Dead Redemption 2 Torn Treasure Maps are used to find the rare Otis Miller's Revolver .

To collect and use the Torn Treasure Maps you will have to locate and kill two unique Hermits that can be found in the world of Red Dead Redemption II. Each one contains one half of a treasure map that will lead to the unique pistol Otis Miller’s Revolver .

The order in which you collect the map halves does not matter. It will affect which map half is named " Torn Treasure Map 1 " and " Torn Treasure Map 2 " though.

The Male Hermit is found on the far eastern side of the map, north of the town Annesburg . Along the right-hand road north of Annesburg is Manito Glade. There you will find the hermit’s home surrounded by a fence and "Keep Out" signs.

When you approach, he will shout at you and threaten to shoot at you. Kill him to be able to enter the home and collect the unique shotgun simply called the Rare Shotgun . You must pick it up now, or you will not be able to collect it later. One half of the Torn Treasure Map is inside the house inside a drawer.

The Female Hermit is found on the western side of West Elizabeth . Her home is far northwest of Wallace Station. Follow Little Creek River into the mountains and her home is in the woods off to the right.

She will sick her three dogs upon you when you get close to her home. Kill all three of them and the hermit herself so you may safely collect the half of the Torn Treasure Map. The map piece is inside the house inside a drawer.

The two map halves will make the whole treasure map, pictured below.

Once you collect both halves of the Torn Treasure Map, head down to the town of Armadillo. Northwest of the town along the state line near Rattlesnake Hollow, you will find a small cave entrance.

Inside the cave is Otis Miller’s treasure. Open it up to collect the rare Otis Miller’s Revolver , as well as six "erotic photographs."

The Landmarks of Riches series of treasure maps aren't maps as such, more sketches hinting at where you need to look to find the stash. Here's where you need to go for each clue.

The first map for the Landmarks of Riches Treasure is found by exploring the wilderness. It is in the Big Valley region of West Elizabeth , near the western edge of the map.

Northwest of Lake Owanjila is the Obelisk . It is one of a handful of Points of Interest in the area. While you are there, take the time to inspect it and let Arthur sketch it in his journal.

Examining the plague on the western side of the Obelisk will reveal a hole behind the plague. Inside is the first map.

The map depicts a church with a large hand reaching down from the clouds. This clue leads to another Point of Interest in the swamps of Bayou Nwa.

Standing alone in the swamps east of Lakay is the Tiny Church . Climb onto the roof of the church and search the bell tower. Here you will find some loot and the second map.

The map depicts a sculpture of a turtle with a broken shell. This clue leads to yet another Point of Interest .

East of Donner Falls and Bacchus Bridge in the Grizzlies East region of Ambarino is the Mysterious Hill Home .

Painted onto the roof of the Mysterious Hill Home is a symbol of a turtle similar to the turtle shown in the map. Climb onto the roof of the home and search a broken window to find more loot and the third map.

This map shows a cannon that morphs into a fallen tree, pointing toward a tree stump. This clue leads to yet another Point of Interest .

South of Rhodes in the state of Lemoyne you will find Bolger Glade .

Bolger Glade is the site of a civil war battle. It features several discarded cannons and a network of reinforced trenches. Near the southern edge of the site is a tree stump surrounded by trenches, with a fallen log spanning one of the trenches. Search the tree stump to find the fourth map and some loot.

Map 4 of the series shows the sun rising over a mountain ridge with a clock face or sundial in the foreground. The number 7 on the clock face is highlighted.

Head to the stone sundial on Mount Shann. As you might expect, you are almost back where this treasure hunt started. The sundial is within sight of the Obelisk .

Approach the sundial from the west and examine the rock at the 7 o'clock position. Underneath the rock is the treasure - six gold bars worth $3000 at any fence . This concludes the mission.

Similar to the Landmarks of Riches, the Elemental Trail treasure maps use sketches as clues to help you track down the stash.

To begin the hunt for The Elemental Trail Treasure, you must find the first map by exploring the wilderness. The map is located at the western tip of New Austin , near the Sea of Coronado. New Austin is only accessible after Chapter 6 .

There is a body hanging by a rope from one of the canyon walls. When you get near, an "x" will appear on the map and mini-map showing the location of the body.

Shoot the rope to release the body, and loot the stranger's corpse to acquire the map.

The map has a sketch of a fireplace and chimney near a large body of water. This clue points to Greenhollow, a crumbled homestead near the shore of the San Luis River in southwestern Hennigan's Stead .

Search the fireplace to find the second treasure map.

The map shows a sketch of what appears to be a tower and a sloping elevated walkway or bridge.

At Benedict Point in the Rio Bravo region of New Austin , you will find a series of water towers connected by an elevated trough.

To access the trough, ride around to the top of the hill and jump onto the trough at the top. Then walk about halfway down the trough to find the third map.

The map contains a sketch of a steeple with an arrow pointing to the left, and a cross with an arrow pointing down.

Southeast of the town of Armadillo is Coot's Chapel.

To the left of the chapel is the cemetery. In the cemetery, underneath a tree, is a wooden cross marking a grave. Approach the grave and examine the large rock on it. Underneath the rock you will find one gold bar, the Crow's Beak trinket, and some horse medicine.

This completes the hunt for The Elemental Trail Treasure.

Looking for even more Red Dead Redemption 2 Guides ? Why not check out...

Up Next: Exclusive Digital Pre-Order Treasure Map

articles.title: Priority: Earth - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Earth Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Earth Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Squad Tactics: Squadmates with great health like Garrus and James will be preferable, as the Mission is all about surviving waves of Reapers.

Squadmates with great health like Garrus and James will be preferable, as the Mission is all about surviving waves of Reapers.

Unique Dialogue: This Mission has two points where you can select your Squad: one at the start and one in the middle. The first one has no instances of unique dialogue, even with Love Interests, so don't worry about that. That said, James is contextually a good choice for the opening squad selection, since he wanted to return to Earth badly at the start of the game. Kaidan / Ashley are also a contextually good story choice for similar reasons.

This Mission has two points where you can select your Squad: one at the start and one in the middle. The first one has no instances of unique dialogue, even with Love Interests, so don't worry about that.

That said, James is contextually a good choice for the opening squad selection, since he wanted to return to Earth badly at the start of the game.

Kaidan / Ashley are also a contextually good story choice for similar reasons.

Shepard's Loadout: A Level V Sniper Rifle with fast reloading will be of great help thanks to the large combat areas and the need to take down powerful enemies like Banshees and Brutes.

A Level V Sniper Rifle with fast reloading will be of great help thanks to the large combat areas and the need to take down powerful enemies like Banshees and Brutes.

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Cerberus Headquarters "

Location: The Milky Way - Local Cluster - Sol - Earth - London

You only have one place to go after " Priority: Cerberus Headquarters " -- Earth. It's labeled "Local Cluster" on the Galaxy Map (since that's where humanity started!). Once you enter the system, you'll go through a trio of cutscenes.

First, Admiral Hackett's ship will appear and he'll board the ship. He'll meet with Shepard before delivering a rousing speech to the forces you've assembled about the fight ahead. After this, you'll reconvene in the Vid Comm Room to talk with Admiral Anderson, who reveals that the Citadel's arms have been closed to prevent access.

The plan is this: while Shepard's fleets, known as Sword Team, engage the Reapers in orbit, the Alliance will send down Hammer Team, who will make a ground assault on the Conduit Beam the Reapers have been using the transport humans onto the Citadel. They'll use it to board the Citadel and open up the arms, which will allow the Crucible, protected by Shield Team, to dock with it and hopefully save the day.

The next cutscene is the arrival of Sword Team through the Sol Relay, headed by the Normandy, and followed by an uncountable number of fighters, Frigates, Cruisers and Dreadnoughts from all the races you've allied with, passing through it at once . If you spared the Destiny Ascension in Mass Effect 1, it'll appear here instead of a generic Asari Dreadnought. The fleets will report in, and you get an epic sequence of the forces engaging with the Reapers while the Normandy slips through thanks to its stealth drive and Reaper IFF.

You'll also get one final scene with Joker, where he salutes Shepard for the first time. If you're playing the Legendary Edition and were tolerant with him after Thessia, you'll have an alternate version of this scene which ends in a handshake.

As you approach the Forward Operation Base, the Reaper Hades Cannon takes out the shuttle with the team designated to take it out. The Hades Cannon is what prevents Hammer Team from landing, so Shepard tells Cortez to drop them off so they can recover the heavy weaponry and do it themselves.

Reaper forces start firing at you even before the Kodiak lands. Take out the Cannibal standing in front of the first bit of cover, then exit the shuttle. Once you're on the ground, watch out for Cannibals and Marauders trying to flank you. Thin out their ranks and make your way up the hill. Time when you come out from cover carefully. Ammo can be found on a few pieces of concrete at the top of the hill if you need it.

As you reach the top, a Brute appears on your right, along with more Cannibals, Marauders, and another Brute in the distance. When you hear the closer Brute start to growl, retreat a little ways down the hill so the Cannibals and Marauders can't hit you, then focus on taking out the Brute as quickly as possible. Once they're dead, switch to a long range weapon, then snipe at the remaining enemies from cover. Just make sure you don't forget about the second Brute.

Follow the stream of incoming enemies to a ramp made out of rubble on your right. The enemies will pour in constantly, so it's best to head up the rubble to the objective rather than try and kill them all, since you can't. You may want to stock up on ammo before you leave the area, though-- there's some in the buildings on the right, before the ramp, and on a piece of broken concrete as you start heading up the ramp.

A few things await you at the top of the ramp: more Cannibals and Marauders, a Ravager , the crashed shuttle, a med kit, and a M-920 Cain -- a big missile launcher that you can use to destroy the Hades Cannon. The M-920 is set as a nav point.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Next to the M-920 Cain will be this Med Kit, right next to the crashed shuttle.

After taking out the enemies, pick up the M-920 Cain and aim it at the big Reaper-looking Hades Cannon, then hold down the fire button until it fires. As the Hades Cannon comes crashing down, see if you can locate another M-920. Each M-920 only has one shot, so it can't be used again, but it'll definitely come in handy. If you can't find the other M-920, just switch back to a normal weapon.

At this point, a bunch of enemies will appear, including a Banshee . Take cover with the downed shuttle and take out the Banshee as quickly as possible, then pick off the Cannibals while you slowly make your way forward toward the extraction point.

Note that the shuttle actually has two M-920 Cains: one next to a column, and the other on the edge of the rooftop. You can pick up the second one to deal with the Banshee.

After a bit more radio chatter, a shuttle will appear. You have a limited amount of time to get to the shuttle, so take cover to charge your shields, then make a run for it. If you have Tactical Cloak, you can simply use it and run straight to the shuttle.

On board you'll have a surprise conversation with Admiral Anderson: pull the Paragon Interrupt for +5 Paragon Points .

Either way, you can ask "How did you last so long?", where you can then say... "You did more than hold on" for +2 Paragon Points . "We expected nothing less" for +2 Renegade Points .

"You did more than hold on" for +2 Paragon Points .

"We expected nothing less" for +2 Renegade Points .

You can end the conversation with either... "Everyone's prepared for this" for +2 Paragon Points . "They know it's do or die" for +2 Renegade Points .

"Everyone's prepared for this" for +2 Paragon Points .

"They know it's do or die" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then land that the Forward Operating Base, or FOB. Anderson and your two Squad Mates will go on ahead, and you'll have a conversation with Major Coats. Reply with...

"They shouldn't need me" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then be free to roam the FOB with absolutely no time pressure, so take as long as you need here to talk with the military leaders, squad and crew that you've come to know over the course of Commander Shepard's journey. Who you can talk to is detailed in the list below, although keep in mind that there are a few ambient radio communications you can listen to along the way too.

James Vega - Just across the street from the building you started out in ( +2 Reputation ).

Virmire Survivor - Facing the Conduit Beam, Kaidan / Ashley on the right-hand side of the street, at the corner of the building with the green entry panel.

Communications Tech - Inside the corner building where the Virmire Survivor stands. Allows you to talk with friends not at the FOB if they're alive, including Jacob, Miranda, Grunt, Jack, Zaeed, Cortez, Samara and Kasumi.

Primarch Victus - Head up the ramp of rubble near the Communications Tech building and into the next room. You can talk to Victus multiple times.

Garrus Vakarian - In the room with Primarch Victus ( +2 Reputation ).

After talking to Victus and Garrus, you'll cross over a bridge, where you'll partake in a turret minigame. The idea is that you're supposed to defend the FOB from a Reaper ground force attack, but you don't actually have to do anything. After 45 seconds, an Alliance fighter flies by and bombs them all, allowing you to proceed.

Liara T'Soni - In the room right after the turret minigame ( +2 Reputation ).

Med Kit x2 - 50 XP each. In the room Liara is in, there are two Med Kits under some stretchers.

Datapad - This disturbing Datapad can be found in the small room after Liara, on a table to your right.

Javik - In the next room with the Krogan Leader barking orders to his men ( +2 Reputation ). This conversation differs depending on if Javik looked into the Memory Shard after " Priority: Horizon ".

Krogan Leader - Wrex or Wreav will be on top of a rubble pile in the same room as Javik. If you sabotaged the Genophage with Wrex as the Krogan Leader, nobody will be here.

Med Kit - 50 XP. In the final room, where Admiral Anderson is, on a fallen column on the right-hand side of the room.

Tali'Zorah vas Normandy - In the final room, to the right of the table Anderson is at ( +2 Reputation ).

EDI - In the final room, to the left of the table Anderson is at ( +2 Reputation ).

In the final room will be a table with Admiral Anderson. You can talk with him to begin the final assault, however you will have a chance to hold off on it if you've forgotten anything at the FOB.

As Anderson explains, a Reaper Destroyer is guarding the Conduit Beam, so Hammer Team will escort tanks equipped with Hydra Missiles through a dense cluster of buildings towards it, then use them to take out the Destroyer (thanks to your actions on Rannoch, you know that the firing chamber is a weak spot). Once the Destroyer is down, it'll be a rush to the Conduit Beam.

Before setting out, Shepard will make another customary speech to their squad. Here's what each option will earn you:

Paragon - "Comrades...", "Remember what you fight for" and "Be fearless..." ( +6 Paragon Points total)

Renegade - "Soldiers...", "Victory or death!" and "Be rutheless" ( +6 Renegade Points total)

Squad Tactics: The fighting ahead will be similar to the first half, but with the highest amounts of overwhelming enemies in the game. As such, the earlier advice applies here: Garrus and James with their health, and powerful sniper rifles for Banshees and Brutes.

The fighting ahead will be similar to the first half, but with the highest amounts of overwhelming enemies in the game. As such, the earlier advice applies here: Garrus and James with their health, and powerful sniper rifles for Banshees and Brutes.

Unique Dialogue: If you have a love interest in your squad, we HIGHLY recommend you bring them with you if you have the Extended Cut DLC . This will be pre-installed in the Wii U and Legendary Editions.

If you have a love interest in your squad, we HIGHLY recommend you bring them with you if you have the Extended Cut DLC . This will be pre-installed in the Wii U and Legendary Editions.

To start, kill the first two Cannibals with a power, then take up their position behind cover and kill the rest of the Cannibals and Marauders. Ammo is available on a table in plain sight. Follow the Mako until it gets taken out, then take cover. Shoot some more Cannibals and Marauders, then make your way through the open doorway on the right.

As you approach the next Mako, it starts driving away. A Harvester appears, along with more Cannibals and Marauders. At some point a Banshee appears too, just in case it was a bit easy. Keep your distance and take out the Harvester, then work on the ground forces. There is plenty of ammo scattered about, so be sure to load up before you leave through the door in front of the Mako.

A group of Husks attack you in the parking garage: if you stay in the open, you and your squad mates should be able to take them out before they get too close. As you get to about the middle of the garage, more Husks and two Brutes lumber in. Back up and take them down before they get close enough to attack. If they charge, run or roll out of the way -- just make sure you keep track of where you are in the garage so you don't back yourself into a corner.

When things are quiet, climb up the ladder at the far end of the garage. Climb up the rubble, then take up positions on either side of the open doorway on the right. Clear the room of the Cannibals, Marauders, and the Ravager.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Under a stretcher bed near the exit of of the apartment room.

Computer - On a desk near the Med Kit described above.

Med Kit - 50 XP. In the bathroom to the right of the exit door, on the vanity next to the shower.

Exit through the door and take out the surprise Husks before they get too close and overwhelm you. Once they're down, head down the rubble and back outside. Get out a long-range weapon and take down the handful of Marauders. As you press on, a Ravager and a Brute appear.

Once they're history, approach the broken store window on the right and duck behind the ledge for cover. Take out a few Cannibals and Marauders, then vault inside. You can easily flank the rest of the Cannibals in the store by sneaking around the right side of the shelves. Equip a short-range weapon, use powers, or just melee. Alternatively, just stay ducked behind the ledge and shoot them from there. There is some ammo on one of the shelves if you need it.

Med Kit - 50 XP. When you get to the wide countertop at the back end of the store, turn around. You'll spot this on some shelving on your left.

Once all the enemies are dead, exit the store and drop down into the crater that used to be an intersection. As you cross to the opposite side, Cannibals appear. You should be able to take them out from a distance without too much trouble. More Cannibals and Marauders await inside the building.

For some variety, try positioning your squad mates at one window while you shoot at the distracted Reaper forces through the other. Alternatively, crouch under the ledge of the broken window, wait for a Cannibal to get too close, then grab and melee.

When the coast is clear, proceed through the next door.

This door opens slowly -- there is some radio chatter as the door mechanism spins. Use this time to back away from the door and take cover, as there are a lot of Cannibals and Marauders bunched up just behind the door. Once you've cleared out this first group, make your way past the booths to the part of the restaurant with the tables. Duck behind the tables and clear out any enemies inside the restaurant, then switch to a long range weapon and take out the enemies outside across the street.

Medical Station - 75 XP. In the restaurant you passed through, to the left of the open window you vault through with a piece of tall artwork between it and the Medical Station. You may want to save this until after you clear out the alleyway up ahead.

Try to get a feel for the layout of the alley outside the restaurant before stepping outside. When the Brute appears from the adjoining alley, you'll need to know where you can back up and where you can run to. If you're fast, you can kill it before it gets to the restaurant.

Go down the alley where the first Brute appeared, but be ready. Two more Brutes crash through the wall on your right. Run back to the restaurant area where you'll have a little more room to maneuver. When the Brutes have been dealt with, go back down the alley and go through the hole in the wall. You'll find some ammo and a Datapad on the shelf on the right. The exit door is at the far end of the room.

Through the door is the biggest battle of the game -- three rounds of survival with enemies of increasing strength, with the Reapers throwing EVERYTHING they've got at you. Are you ready?

After an uplifting cut scene where many of your allies get vaporized, the door opens and you're asked to secure the missile battery. Take out the handful of Cannibals and Marauders, taking care to conserve ammo and health. The enemies are spread out throughout the area, so check your radar after you kill a few to figure out where the rest of them are. You can also use your radar to make sure they don't flank you.

Once the first wave is over, take some time to get familiar with the area before you open a link from the Normandy to the missile systems: enemies won't appear until you do. Using the Conduit beam and the Reaper Destroyer as "north" (which is actually how the map is oriented on Wii U!), you can find the final pieces of loot in the Mass Effect trilogy:

Medical Station - 75 XP. In the Northwestern Store, on the northern wall close to the road going north to the Conduit Beam.

Med Kit x2 - 50 XP each. In the Southwestern Store, one on the the middle shelves, and one on the western shelves behind the counter.

Hydra Missile Launcher - In the Southwestern Store, on the shelves under the counter (pictured above).

Medical Station - 75 XP. In the Southeastern Store, on the eastern wall, between a painting and some corner couches.

If you're playing the Wii U Special Edition, you can also find the last M-597 Ladon in the game in the Southeastern Store with the paintings, specifically on the cashier counter.

ONLY PICK UP THE HYDRA / LADON WHEN YOU NEED THEM . While you can move them by picking them up, walking and then pulling out another weapon, they'll despawn five minutes after you pick them up, which is too short even when mowing down enemies on the Casual difficulty. It's better to go grab them when you actually need them.

When you're ready, deactivate the Firewall Controls on the rear set of missiles to continue. The next wave is similar to the first, but a few Husks have been added to the mix. The first group comes from the "North" of the area (in the direction of the Conduit beam). Take cover behind the concrete barricades between the two missile trucks and shoot the incoming Reaper forces from a distance. As you finish up, another group comes in from the South, so watch your radar via the Weapon / Power Wheel.

When things go quiet again, you'll hear some radio chatter indicating Reaper forces are coming in from the West. Take cover, switch to a long-range weapon and try to kill as many Cannibals and Marauders as you can before the two Banshees show up. The arrival of the Banshees is a fantastic time to use the Hydra Missile Launcher to take them both out in one move. After you kill the Banshees, mop up the rest of the Reaper forces. Remember that the side room has ammo if you run out during the fight.

Once all the enemies are dead, go stock up on ammo and Medi-Gel in the stores one more time before you activate the Missile Launch Controls . Unfortunately, the Reaper Destroyer is still too close to the Conduit beam for the Thanix Missiles to hit it, and they'll swerve wildly off course. The Destroyer will practically be right on top of you in the third and final wave.

Now the Reapers will throw everything they've got at you: a wave of Brutes is followed by a Harvester, which is followed by a wave of Banshees, Cannibals and Marauders. Watch your radar and your ammo (on Wii U you'll have to use the corner radar: the Destroyer took down your GamePad Minimap!), and listen for radio chatter indicating when the second set of missiles are ready for launch: the wave will be endless unless you hit the switch.

When you get the go-ahead, rush to the Northern set of missiles to fire them, which will take down the Destroyer.

Anderson will now finally catch up with Shepard and what remains of Hammer Team. Unfortunately, Hackett has let Anderson know that several Sovereign-class Reapers, including Harbinger itself, have broken off from the fight with Sword Team and are heading right for the Conduit, just as the Crucible has made its way into the Sol system.

While in the ride in the truck to No Man's Land, you can say...

"I'm proud of all of you" for +2 Paragon Points .

"No one hold back" for +2 Renegade Points .

Unfortunately the truck is hit before it can start crossing No Man's Land, and it's at that moment that Harbinger arrives. Here, it'll be a straight charge to the Conduit beam. There's only one thing for it: RUN.

During the charge, several vehicles will flip dangerously close to you and your Squad Mates. There are two outcomes to this:

If your EMS is very low, Harbinger will then fire a laser at your Squad Mates and vaporize both of them instantly.

If your EMS is isn't very low, the Mako will explode and injure your Squad Mates. Shepard calls the Normandy in for an emergence evac, and they say their last words to their Squad (if your Love Interest is present, it will always be to them).

Once this scene is over, Shepard will attempt to get to the Conduit Beam, but Harbinger fires one last shot at them. Just barely hanging on, you'll now have to press on to the Conduit beam with only a Carnifex pistol. If you're playing on Casual difficulty or higher, you'll soon be charged at by three Husks: shoot them down quickly using headshots. As you get close to the beam, a Marauder will pop out behind some rubble and shoot you: take him out quick , as he's much better armed than you and can kill you fast.

When Shepard gets close, they'll enter the beam and be warped up onto the Citadel.

After this point, you will proceed to The Finale of the Mass Effect Trilogy. This is a very important and unique section of the game, so it's been split into its own section:

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about exploring the Citadel in the opening act of the game, just before you do "Priority:
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about exploring the Citadel in the opening act of the game, just before you do " Priority: Tuchanka ". Here we'll guide you to all the various Side Missions you'll hand in and character interactions you can fulfill.

The purpose of this page is to make sure you've completed all possible interactions before you do " Priority: Tuchanka ". Completing that Mission will refresh the Citadel, and many character interactions and Side Missions will be replaced with new ones. As such, there are a few notes we'd like to make first:

We highly recommend that you first go through the Citadel Excursion 1 page and make sure you've done all the major interactions in it , if you haven't already. You'll pick up a great many Side Missions that you'll be able to hand in at this point.

This page expects that you've done " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ", " N7: Cerberus Abductions " and " N7: Cerberus Attack " - All of these have items that you'll hand in on this page to complete Side Missions. We also expect that you've picked up the " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe " Side Mission from Engineer Adams.

We also expect you to complete the Search and Rescue section below - This is again because you'll get items that you'll hand in to complete Side Missions here. The Ismar Frontier cluster unlocks by picking up the " Ismar Frontier: Prototype Components " Side Mission at Huerta Memorial Hospital.

Finally, we assume you've kept up with Steve Cortez's personal storyline , where he's emotionally ready to say goodbye to his husband Robert.

Before we start with exploring the Citadel, you should complete the Search and Rescue table below to get Credits and Quest Items for Side Missions that you'll be handing in further down the page.

The Ismar Frontier requires you to pick up the " Ismar Frontier: Prototype Components " Side Mission at Huerta Memorial Hospital.

The Vular system in Kite's Nest requires you to negotiate with the black market seller on the Citadel rather than kill General Oraka in " Aria: Blue Suns ". The only item there is that Side Mission's quest item, so if you opted to kill General Oraka, you're not missing out on anything (unless you really like the planet descriptions).

Head through the security walls and then turn left to find Cortez at the memorial area. Talk to him to continue his storyline and get +2 Reputation .

There's a Paragon Interrupt during this scene, but you get no Morality Points for using it.

Head into Cargo Hold: C and talk to the Batarian Preacher to hand in " Kite's Nest: Pillars of Strength ", which will give you 15,000 Credits, +5 Reputation and bolsters the Batarian Fleet War Asset. If you didn't get it, you can find it on Khar'shan, the second planet in the Harsa system in the Kite's Nest cluster.

Go to Cargo Hold: B and talk to Kelly Chambers to catch up with her. If you've been following this guide correctly, then in this scene she'll confess that she sent reports about you to the Illusive Man as part of her job in Mass Effect 2. At this, you can say...

"You did what?" for +2 Renegade Points , which severely traumatizes Kelly.

Exit the elevator and go left to find Dominic Osoba at the window. If you found the Dog Tags of his son during " N7: Cerberus Abductions ", you can hand them in here to complete " Benning: Evidence " for +5 Reputation and 90 XP. If you missed them, you can buy them at Spectre Requisitions .

Head to Udina's office to catch this easily-missed conversation where he discusses your Virmire Survivor accepting the position of Spectre. Here you can reply...

"Good for her / him" for +2 Paragon Points .

"This won't end well" for +2 Renegade Points .

None of his Investigate topics have updated dialogue, unfortunately.

If Dr. Michel isn't aboard the Normandy, you can check in with her in the corner of the first room to learn about the current condition of your Virmire Survivor.

Now head inside and talk to the Virmire Survivor themselves about accepting the position of Spectre, and how they're feeling. Aside from giving you +2 Reputation , this meeting is again important in helping your Virmire Survivor reconcile with Shepard later.

Head through the door opposite the room your Virmire Survivor is in to hand in " Ismar Frontier: Prototype Components " for 90 XP. If you didn't grab them, you can find them by scanning Metaponto, the fourth planet in the Aquila system in the Ismar Frontier cluster.

From the elevator, head left and up the stairs to talk to Barla Von behind the far desk to cash in " Citadel: Barla Von ", giving you 120 XP and +5 Reputation . If you didn't pick up the Shadow Broker Wet Squad that Barla Von is looking for, you can find them by scanning Rothla, the fourth planet in the Dranek system of the Krogan DMZ .

At Barla Von's post, access the Elkoss Combine Arsenal Supplies store and buy the GX12 Thermal Pipe (called "E-Gel Thermal Conduit" in in the storefront itself, for some reason) for 1,000 credits, progressing the " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe " Side Mission for Engineer Adams. It's quite cheap, so don't feel bad about buying it without the full 10% discount.

In the Apollo's Cafe area you can find Matriarch Aethyta serving drinks, who Mass Effect 2 players may recognize from Illium . Talk to her and you'll begin a very interesting conversation. When she mentions keeping an eye on Liara, say...

"You should talk" for +2 Paragon Points .

"You shouldn't spy on her" for +2 Renegade Points .

During this conversation a Paragon Interrupt will pop up: pull it for +5 Paragon Points . A Renegade Interrupt will also appear here: pull that for +5 Renegade Points .

After this, find Liara at the balcony and talk to her. If you pick "[Make her talk to her]", the strength of the Asari Second Fleet will be increased by 25 TMS.

You can then head back to the cafe bar and hear a 10-part conversation between Liara and Aethyta that will be very interesting for those who played the first Mass Effect. To move to the next part of this conversation, walk to one of the nearby staircases and then walk back to them.

Now go to the lowest balcony with the two stores and talk to Ereba at the Nos Astra Sporting Goods storefront, which will complete " Citadel: Krogan Dying Message ". You MUST have picked it up during " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ", otherwise this Side Mission cannot be started, let alone completed.

Handing in the message will give you +5 Reputation and 90 XP.

If you went the Paragon route with the " Aria: Blue Suns " Side Mission and talked to Krannik, you should now head upstairs to the Cipritine Armory kiosk and talk to Kannik to continue that Side Mission (if you had General Oraka killed, click here to skip to the next section of this page ).

This will have you hand in Black Market Artifacts, appeasing Krannik into giving General Oraka the black market weapons he's asking for, netting you 210 XP, 5,000 credits, and bolstering the Terminus Fleet by +50 TMS. If you don't have the Black Market Artifacts, you can find them by scanning Vana, the third planet in the Vular system of the Kite's Nest cluster.

With Kannik appeased, return to General Oraka at the bottom of the steps just across from Apollo's Cafe. Talk to him to conclude the Side Mission for +5 Paragon Points .

In the exterior area of Purgatory, talk with the human woman in the dress at the railing just outside the entrance door to conclude " Citadel: Improved Power Grid " for +5 Reputation , 30 XP, 1,000 Credits and strengthening the Alliance Fifth Fleet by 8 TMS.

If you missed the power grid schematics from the " N7: Cerberus Attack " Side Mission, you can buy them from Spectre Requisitions for 1,000 credits.

If you completed " Aria: Eclipse ", " Aria: Blue Suns " and " Aria: Blood Pack ", you can talk to Aria again to get her reactions to fulfilling her requests. You can ask her about your new task force, as well as about each individual mercenary gang.

With the Citadel now completely done for now, here's what you can do on the Normandy:

CIC - Check your Private Terminal to read an email from Cortez, which gives you 375 XP and the Rogue Fighter Pilots War Asset, worth 20 TMS.

Crew Deck - Swing by Liara's Intel terminal for the Intel you picked up. You should have the following: Weapon Upgrade Kit - +5% Ammo Capacity or +5% Weapon Damage. Advanced Biotic Implants - +5% Power Damage or +5% Power Recharge Speed.

Weapon Upgrade Kit - +5% Ammo Capacity or +5% Weapon Damage.

Advanced Biotic Implants - +5% Power Damage or +5% Power Recharge Speed.

Engineering - Talk to Engineer Adams, as well as Gabby if present, to progress " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe ".

Shuttle Bay - Lastly, talk to Cortez for some post-memorial thoughts.

Want more Mass Effect 3 help? Check out the following pages:

articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 2 wiki guide is all about the Overlord: Vulcan Station DLC Assignment, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Squad Tactics: Garrus and Zaeed are great picks for this section, as you'll need their ability to strip both Armor and Shields!

Garrus and Zaeed are great picks for this section, as you'll need their ability to strip both Armor and Shields!

There is no unique dialogue for this section.

To get to Vulcan Station from Hermes Station, head directly forward and follow the left-hand cliff until you get to a tunnel: enter it to transition to Vulcan Station, where it's time to start playing with lava!

The lava river ahead can be jumped over, but be aware that the lava in this area isn't anywhere near as dangerous as it appears. You can actually hang around in it for a bit before the Hammerhead blows up, giving you a window to get yourself out of trouble.

On the other side, head into the building on the right-hand wall and pass over the steam vents when they aren't venting (you'll be shot up into the ceiling if you're not careful!). At the end however, the Hammerhead's VI suggests doing the opposite : hang around the vents and, combined with the vehicle's own jump thrusters, you'll be able to get to the tunnel up top.

At the top you'll encounter a Cerberus Turret. Even this one turret is enough to quickly down the Hammerhead, and there's not a lot of room to evade in this tunnel, so keep your distance, and if the vehicle is in a bad way you should retreat out of the turret's range.

400 Iridium - Just past the turret will be a split in the tunnel. Head down the left-hand route to find some Iridium to extract at the end.

Out the other end of the tunnel will be another, much wider river of lava. The vehicle's VI helpfully points out that the slabs of rock floating on it are enough to let it cross. What it doesn't tell you however that they can only barely do that: sitting on them makes them sink, so quickly hover away again before you take a lava bath.

On the other side, use the vent to the right to ascend up the cliff. The next vent however is inactive, which halts your progress. To enable it you'll have to go into the nearby building: approach the garage to get the prompt to exit the Hammerhead and enter the facility.

Inside, head up the stairs and through the doors, then immediately take cover behind the pipes on the right-hand side: there's three LOKI Mechs in here! Once you destroy them, head through the next door, then check the left-hand wall for some Research Logs , and Valve A3 Controls to Bypass, enabling the vent for the Hammerhead!

To get up, hover the Hammerhead over the vent until it reaches maximum altitude, then engage its vertical thrusters to get up on top of the cliff. In this chasm you'll have to destroy another Cerberus Turret, which is guarding...

400 Iridium - Extract this from the base of the Cerberus Turret described above.

At the end of the chasm you'll drop down to another river of lava. You'll need to be careful here as the rocks move in the same direction you do, meaning you may not be able to reach the rock you were hoping for! As you go, keep an eye out on your left for the path forward.

Vulcan Station will be visible directly ahead, but first extract some Iridium!

400 Iridium - Use the vent on the right-hand wall to get on top of the cliff. This site of Iridium will be among the rocks here.

800 Iridium - Up the top of the left-hand cliffs. This will be guarded by two Cerberus Turrets, so employ hit-and-run tactics by dropping down to the middle level so the Hammerhead can recover.

Once you've done all the looting required, you'll now need to go upstream along the third and final lava river to reach Vulcan Station. This river is rather narrow, so you'll likely have to land on every rock on your way to the station's garage.

Head through the door at the top of the garage, then...

Datapad - 1,125 credits. As soon as you exit the garage, take a right to go down a side-path to Valve D4 Control . Bypass it to shut down the valve, letting you go down a slope to a dead officer with this Datapad.

Return to the main path and continue forward to find it blocked by a metal pipe section. To clear it, shoot the Explosive Container on the machinery to the left of it: the machienry will vent enough steam pressure to blow the metal pipe away!

Med Kit - 100 credits. Partway up the next steps, turn left to spot this.

At the top of the steps you'll encounter three LOKI Mechs: shoot the Explosive Containers on the machinery to the left of them to instantly destroy them! You can use this trick on the beams at the back of the arena itself to destroy the flying Assault Drones.

Once everything is quiet, head to the back-right of the fighting area to find a walkway that leads to two silver pipes you can walk up. At the top, vault up onto the walkway, then turn left into the side-room for some goodies:

Wall Safe - 1,500 credits. On the left-hand wall of the side-room.

Research Log - On the right-hand wall of the side-room, next to the holographic monitor.

Return to the main walkway and now turn left to go through the open doorway.

Medical Station - 100 credits. To your right after going through the open doorway.

The last room of Vulcan Station is an awkward fight against LOKI Mechs, Assault Drones, and eventually a YMIR Mech too! Don't be afraid to retreat back through the doorway: this serves as a helpful bottleneck between you and the mechs. Also try to take advantage of the Explosive Containers in the back corners of the room when the Assault Drones perch there.

Computer - 2,625 credits. On a table in the front-left corner of this room (ie on your left when entering through the doorway).

When all the enemy mechs are down, head up the stairs in the back-left corner of the room to release the security lockdown. As you do you'll get a Renegade Interrupt: it doesn't give any Morality Points, and if you don't pull it a squadmate will fire the killing shot themselves, so Paragons may as well!

Want more Mass Effect 2 help? Check out the following pages:
