articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the main Omega: Aria T'Loak DLC Mission of the Omega DLC , including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Unlike the Leviathan and Citadel DLCs , once you start this Mission, you'll be committed to it and can only leave by completing the DLC!

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Phaeston (if not acquired in " Tuchanka: Turian Platoon ")

Mods: Assault Rifle High-Velocity Barrel x3 Pistol Heavy Barrel x3 Shotgun High-Velocity Barrel x3 Shotgun Omni-Blade x3 Sniper Rifle Thermal Scope x3

War Assets: Omega Eezo Hoard (300 TMS) Omega Raiding Fleet (75 TMS) Tap to Reveal (30 TMS) / +30 TMS to Alliance First Fleet

Tap to Reveal (30 TMS) / +30 TMS to Alliance First Fleet

Prerequisite: Complete " Citadel: Aria T'Loak ".

Location: Serpent Nebula - Widow - Aria's Fleet

Sadly, the Omega DLC doesn't add the Omega Nebula cluster to the Galaxy Map. Instead, you begin by traveling to the Widow system of the Serpent Nebula. If you did the " Citadel: Aria T'Loak " prelude, you'll find Aria's Fleet to the "west" of the Citadel: rendezvous with it to begin the DLC in earnest.

As established in " Citadel: Aria T'Loak ", Shepard doesn't bring their usual Squad Mates along for this Mission, so instead this section will focus primarily on Aria and Shepard's Loadout:

Squad Tactics: Make sure you upgrade Aria's Lash ability to Level 6 and choose " Shield Penetration ", which allows it to bypass Shields and Barriers and tear off the metal shields used by Guardians. You should also upgrade Aria's Flare power to Level 6 and choose " Improved Damage ", increasing its damage to Shields and Barriers by 75%. This will be useful on this DLC's Phantoms and a new enemy type it introduces.

Make sure you upgrade Aria's Lash ability to Level 6 and choose " Shield Penetration ", which allows it to bypass Shields and Barriers and tear off the metal shields used by Guardians.

You should also upgrade Aria's Flare power to Level 6 and choose " Improved Damage ", increasing its damage to Shields and Barriers by 75%. This will be useful on this DLC's Phantoms and a new enemy type it introduces.

Shepard's Loadout: Shield-stripping powers will be scarce in the Omega DLC, so if possible you'll want to make sure Shepard develops their Disruptor Ammo , Energy Drain and / or Overload powers to help cover this problem on their own. Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will help deal with the many Guardians you'll be fighting, as well as the new enemy type that appears in this DLC. The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs. You'll be picking up Sniper Rifle Thermal Scopes throughout this DLC, which help you see through both their smoke bombs and through walls! If you have the Citadel DLC , an Assault Rifle Thermal Scope also sees through smoke bombs and walls!

Shield-stripping powers will be scarce in the Omega DLC, so if possible you'll want to make sure Shepard develops their Disruptor Ammo , Energy Drain and / or Overload powers to help cover this problem on their own.

Piercing, Shredder or High Velocity mods , as well as the Venom Shotgun , will help deal with the many Guardians you'll be fighting, as well as the new enemy type that appears in this DLC.

The Sniper Rifle Enhanced Scope is very helpful for seeing through the smoke bombs used by Centurions and Atlas mechs.

You'll be picking up Sniper Rifle Thermal Scopes throughout this DLC, which help you see through both their smoke bombs and through walls!

If you have the Citadel DLC , an Assault Rifle Thermal Scope also sees through smoke bombs and walls!

Shepard arrives on Aria's captured Cerberus cruiser and gets a basic run-down of her plan: pretend to be an allied ship, strike a surprise blow, then call in the rest of the fleets. Here you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "It sounds risky" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "I like it" for +2 Renegade Points .

Whichever you say, Aria will end the discussion with a line that is, quite frankly, hilarious if you know anything about how Mass Effect 3 itself ends.

Aria will then initiate the attack, but before it gets too far, they're hailed by General Oleg Petrovsky himself. Aria reveals her ace in the hole (that's you, chief), and Oleg says he's heard great things about Shepard. Here you can say...

"I can't say the same" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Not from your boss" for +2 Renegade Points .

After a bit more chit-chat, Aria reveals she plans to infiltrate Omega... by ramming it . Unfortunately Petrovsky's threats were no bluff, and Omega's new laser cannons quickly down the cruiser. Luckily, unlike the last time a ship blew up on them , Shepard is able to make it to the escape pod and onto Omega.

The escape pod makes it too! With the cruiser ramming plan a failure, you'll have to get to the Defense System Station to shut down Omega's outer defenses manually, before the rest of Aria's fleet is blown to bits. Aria then tells Shepard that in combat, what they say goes, to which you can reply...

"Why am I skeptical?" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Glad to hear it" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll now have to shoot your way through Hangar Bay 28, filled with the first of a great many Cerberus soldiers you'll be fighting. You'll be facing Assault Troopers and Centurions in here, and while there's a fair bit of cover in this area, that works for both you and Cerberus.

Once everyone's dead, Aria will station herself near the far end of the Hangar Bay, and you can grab your first items of the DLC:

Med Kit x2 - 50 XP each. Just in front of where Aria stations herself will be these two Med Kits, close to some tire channels on the left and right sides of the Hangar Bay.

In front of Aria will be some Blast Door Controls : Use them to lower the blast door up ahead: take cover, as there's a Centurion and a Guardian on the left and right sides. This is a great time to use Aria's Lash ability: if you were able to upgrade it to Level 6 and picked "Shield Penetration", it'll rip the shield right out of the Guardian's hand!

When they're both dead, head down the right-hand side of the fighter launcher track to locate the exit. But first, grab these two items:

Tools - 3,000 credits. On top of a crate next to the wing of the Cerberus fighter.

Assault Rifle High-Velocity Barrel - See above.

Head through the door opposite of the loot and use the Elevator Controls to continue. When able, head out the elevator and veer left to arrive at a long hallway, with storefronts on the right and a view to space on the left. There's more Cerberus troops in here too, including two Combat Engineers who you should gun down ASAP.

After killing them, head to the back-right corner of this long room to find the exit door: Examine it to re-pressurize the next room.

Medical Station - 75 XP. To the right of the exit door.

Initiating this process will call upon Cerberus reinforcements, including Centurions and a Nemesis sniper. Take cover and treat the Nemesis with respect so that you aren't gunned down yourself. Once they're all dead, the depressurization will conveniently be done and you can proceed to the next area.

Head through the hallway with the burning escape pod and Bypass the door at the end to get to the Defense System Station. Take cover on your left, as more Cerberus troops will drop in, including two Guardians and a Combat Engineer. Kill the latter before he can set up a Turret, then get to work on the rest.

Once all is quiet, use the Defense System Controls towards the middle of the room to disable the defenses, letting Aria's fleet dock and offload their forces.

Aria then begins explaining the details of their rendezvous point, including its location and capabilities... right as Shepard locates a security camera. There's a Renegade Interrupt to shoot it out, which Paragons can take as it doesn't give Renegade Points! Regardless, Petrovsky now knows where the rendezvous is and deploys forces to take it out.

Before exiting, sweep the room for these goodies:

Medical Station - 75 XP. From the Defense System Controls, turn around to face away from the window. Check the wall on the right-hand side to find this.

Med Kit - 50 XP. In the back-left area of the room, near-ish to the exit door.

Head through the exit door and enter the right-hand elevator. Examine the Screen overhead if you wish, then hit the Elevator Controls to move forward (well, upward). As soon as you exit, quickly grab this item:

Wall Safe - 3,000 credits. On the left-hand wall as soon as you exit the elevator.

You'll be faced by some Cerberus soldiers ahead, three Troopers and a Centurion. Take cover where you can and drop 'em when they expose themselves. When they're all dead, head through the blue security scanner wall (no wait times, yay!) then use the Garage Door Controls on the right-hand side to open the door.

You'll now emerge outside: after Aria takes in the, erm, "wonderful" Omega skyline, use the View Prompt to take notice of the orange Force Field up ahead. We'll get properly introduced to them in due time. In the mean time:

Tools - 1,500 credits. Salvage these up ahead, next to a Batarian corpse in front of a red skycar.

Pistol Heavy Barrel - To the left of the Tools described above, at the back end of the red skycar.

Control Screen - To the left of the Pistol Heavy Barrel. Use this multiple times to hear four different public announcements.

Locate the door jammed with a crate to the left of the Control Screen and vault over it to proceed. Take cover, as you'll be facing Guardians and a Centurion that are bolstered by a Shield Pylon that's out of sight. Remember to use Aria's abilities to strip these Shields and take them down. Also remember that it works both ways: the Shield Pylon will top up Shepard's Shields too!

When everyone's down, make sure to grab this loot:

Med Kit - 50 XP. About halfway down the left "lane" of this area, to the left of the first Shield Pylon.

Graffiti - On a panel on your right as you exit the next elevator.

Scrap Metal - 2,250 credits. Continue past the Graffiti described above to find this at the end of the hallway, just a bit past the exit door on your left.

Drop down the side of the next walkway, and you'll observe one of Aria's men getting ambushed by Omega's new enemy type: the Rampart Mech. While they may look like simple recolors of Mass Effect 2's LOKI Mechs, these guys have been upgraded to be far more formidable:

Rather than only being able to walk, Rampart Mechs can run like any good foot soldier.

They can pass through the orange barriers around Omega, letting them ambush Shepard from areas they cannot access.

They also possess powerful Omniblades that can deal serious damage if you get too close.

Killing a Rampart Mech isn't the end of it: they dissolve into sparking, burning cinders on the ground that will hurt Shepard if they walk over them, similar to Ravagers.

You'll therefore want to be very careful: never get close to them, and after they're killed, remember where they fell to make sure you don't accidentally walk over their corpses and suffer damage.

As you walk up to the Force Field to help Aria investigate it, don't forget to grab these:

Med Kit - 50 XP. In the lower area in front of the orange Force Field where the Vorcha got killed.

Shotgun High Velocity Barrel - Follow Aria left to a Door Control panel that lets you vault inside a store. Here, check the island counter to find this on the right-hand side.

Medical Station - 75 XP. In the back-left corner of the store Aria leads you into.

When Aria reveals the secret ladder inside the storefront, slide down it to initiate a cutscene, where you'll meet one of Aria's old friends... (wait, Aria has friends? ). This is Nyreen Kandros, and you can get some Morality Points here:

When Nyreen explains she's been using Aria's secret tunnels... Pick "You two must be close" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "You're getting sloppy, Aria" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "You two must be close" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "You're getting sloppy, Aria" for +2 Renegade Points .

When Aria offers to lead Nyreen to safety... Pick "You look capable" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "Just try to keep up" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "You look capable" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Just try to keep up" for +2 Renegade Points .

Nyreen now joins the Squad, allowing you to upgrade her various powers. Overload is an obvious choice to help strip Shields, but also put some in Lift Grenades, as grenade pickups are plentiful across Omega. Biotic Protector is also a good one as it projects a bubble shield that halts all damage and can even explode after it expires.

Make sure to grab these items as you head forward:

Scrap Metal - 3,000 credits. On the right-hand side, in the approximate middle of the dark room.

N7 Valkyrie - On the ground towards the back of the dark room. This isn't present in the original release of the game if you have the N7 Warfare Gear DLC.

Datapad - 2,250 credits. At the very back of the dark room, on the bed of the yellow pickup truck.

Bypass the door at the back-left corner of the room to continue into the next area. On the right-hand wall is a Weapon Bench , which you can use to customize Nyreen's loadout and apply the new mods you've been picking up, if you wish.

Head right past the Weapon Bench to go down the tunnel, then turn right at the end to find a ladder in the back-left corner that takes you back up.

At the top you can use a View Prompt to spot an Atlas mech land in the distance (immediately bolstered by a Shield Pylon, fantastic ), and Aria asks why the cannons aren't operational. Bray explains that something's jamming them, but first you'll have to get in there and clear the area.

Medical Station - 75 XP. After climbing up the ladder, turn left to spot the exit window you can vault through. Before doing that, however, check behind the fire on the left-hand side of the window to find this easily-missed Medical Station on the wall.

In addition to the Atlas mech, there'll also be multiple Rampart Mechs prowling the area, as well as a pair of Centurions. Take cover and eliminate them, preferably from a distance so you're not gunned down out in the open. Also make sure to destroy the Shield Pylon: it'll be right under an enemy spawn point, so it'll help your enemies far more than it'll help you.

Once they're dead, Bray calls in to let you know that there's a Cerberus Engineer somewhere in the area who's hacking the cannons, so you'll have to find and eliminate them. Before you can do that however, more Cerberus forces start pouring in from the back-left and back-right balconies of the area to make things difficult.

When you're ready to find the Combat Engineer, locate him by either clicking R3 on consoles (pushing the right analog stick into the controller) or pressing the V key by. This marks him with the blue objective diamond. Take cover after killing the Combat Engineer, as a second Atlas mech drops in right where the first one was. Remember that if you can shoot out the glass and its pilot, you can commandeer it for yourself!

Once you destroy the second Atlas mech, sweep the area for these items:

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the right-hand side of the area, on an upper area between an orange Force Field and a Shield Pylon.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the left-hand side of the area is a storefront you can enter, with a wide window you can vault through flanked by two doorways. This Med Kit will be on the sill of the wide window.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Close to the second Med Kit described above, on the column between the wide window and the left-hand doorway.

Now that you've topped up your medical supplies and / or gotten some XP, use the Cannon Controls to finish up, deliver some serious pain to Cerberus, and enter the bunker.

In the arrival cutscene, you'll have multiple opportunities to gain Morality Points during the discussion between Aria and Nyreen:

Paragon - "I'm concerned too", "We could use Nyreen's help" and "You better control yourself" ( +6 Paragon Points total).

Renegade - "Do you have another plan?", "She could be a spy" and "I won't stand in your way" ( +6 Renegade Points total).

You'll now have free reign to explore the admittedly rather limited area of Aria's Bunker. There's various conversations you can overhear if you wish, but we'd like to point out the following in the main control room area:

Near the back-left exit will be a Weapon Bench and Armor Locker so you can adjust Shepard's gear (Aria and Nyreen aren't currently considered part of your Squad at the moment).

Close to the Weapon Bench and Armor Locker will be a Batarian in white agonizing over tech issues. Talk to him to learn he needs a Kehri Power Inverter for " Omega: Assist the Mechanic ".

On the opposite side of the control room is a human Hacker at a control panel. Talk to her to learn you can help her by activating Cerberus Terminals on your travels for " Omega: Assist the Hacker " (although note that this gives zero rewards outside of 30 XP for each Terminal).

When you're ready to continue, talk to Aria at the window next to the circular hologram display. Talk to her to lay down a plan for your next move. Aria's losses were significant and she's begrudgingly looking to recruiting the Talons, the only remaining merc band, to fill in the missing ranks. Here you can say...

"We'll negotiate an alliance" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Mercs only respect strength" for +2 Renegade Points .

After the conversation, you can actually talk to Aria a second time to get more information about her plans forward, Nyreen and Petrovsky. When you're ready to move on, use the exit by the Weapon Bench and Armor Locker.

You'll start this section with Aria explaining that the Talons rose to power around the time of the Plague in 2185 , thanks to Shepard eliminating the Omega branches of the other three mercenary bands in their quest to recruit Archangel . Aria makes it clear that she only intends to use the Talons as cannon fodder for her war to reclaim her throne. To this you can say...

"I don't use people" for +2 Paragon Points .

And wouldn't you know it, Cerberus is in the area. To start, head directly forward and Examine the Red Sand crates blocking the doorway for an interesting observation between Shepard and Aria. Continue right and climb up the tall ladder, then make a right-hand U-Turn into a control station.

Now technically you can use the Air Lock controls to open the way forward, but instead you can grab some goodies for an alternate route.

To start, find the Lift Control : Using it will try to raise a platform in the distance, but it's blocked. Shoot the canisters on the platform to clear the way: this lets you use the Lift Control again the lower the platform so you can get onto it. Then, grab some loot!

Terminal - 30 XP. Activate this next to the Lift Control to contribute to " Omega: Assist the Hacker ".

Datapad - 1,500 credits. Exit out of the control room and look right to find this to the right of the locked door.

Assault Rifle High Velocity Barrel - Slide back down the tall staircase and then get onto the platform on your right (the one you lowered with the Lift Control). Use the Lift Control button on the platform itself, then turn left at the top to spot this mod next to the crates. From here, you can vault over the white crates to get back onto the main path via a shortcut!

From here, you can vault over the white crates to get back onto the main path via a shortcut!

When you get to the end of the tunnel, you'll enter a wider space with some walkways. There's one goodie here:

Datapad - 1,500 credits. Head directly forward and past the intersection to find this in front of some crates at the dead end.

Return to the intersection and take the other path this time. You'll find an Air Seal , but it's useless without any power. Head left to find a Datapad on some crates, then turn left again to go past a Terminal and find a Generator at the end. Reactivate it to restore power (and use the Terminal you just walked past!). Use the Air Seal again to open the way forward.

At the end of the tunnel you'll emerge back outside, and see a Cerberus shuttle crash into a walkway leading into the Talon Outpost. Slide down the ladder, but look out for some loot as you go:

Salvage - 1,500 credits. When you slide down the ladder, turn left and head past the stairs on your right to arrive at a door lit in white. Follow the wall rightward to find this near some dumpsters.

Salvage - 1,500 credits. Continue down the stairs, and when you get to the bottom, make a rightward U-turn to find this between the stairs and white container tank.

Now locate the door and proceed down the stairs to enter a control room. There's a Combat Engineer here as well as a Shield Pylon: take these out first before you get overwhelmed by the Troopers and Centurion who come in from the back door here.

When you're done, face the windows to start grabbing some loot:

Terminal - 30 XP. Head down to the right-hand side of the windows to find this and contribute to " Omega: Assist the Hacker ".

Datapad - 1,500 credits. In the small office room directly opposite the windows, you can find this on a desk with three laptops on it.

Medical Station - 75 XP. Visible through the doorway where the Troopers and Centurions entered the control room from.

Through the next door you'll enter a hallway guarded by a Trooper and another Combat Engineer, who comes out of the first side-room on the right. As ever, kill the Combat Engineer first before he can deploy any Turrets. Grab this loot while you have a moment of calm:

Datapad - 1,500 credits. In the first side-room on the right, look right to find this on top of a low book case.

Injured Talon - 60 XP. In the second side-room you'll find a Turian slumped in the back-left corner. Revive him to get some XP.

Terminal - 30 XP. Behind the Injured Talon will be this Terminal: Activate it to once again contribute to " Omega: Assist the Hacker ". This is the last one, but again be aware that you don't get any rewards for your good deeds.

Return to the room with the Datapad in it and this time use the laptop to Deactivate the Cerberus Lockdown . This will open the door forward... allowing a Guardian and two Rempart Mechs to enter. Use Aria's Lash to remove the Guardian's shield, and be careful of where you walk in this enclosed space, lest you get damaged by a fallen Rampart Mech.

Head down the elevator at the end of the hallway, then turn around to go down... another hallway, which leads to an open cargo hangar, both of which have enemies. Great! The cargo space has a Combat Engineer, so if possible shoot him down first before his Turrets become a problem. Oh and there's three Shield Pylons here too!

Things only get worse when you get to the back, as more Rampart Mechs show up just as a Cerberus shuttle arrives to drop off more Assault Troopers, and another Combat Engineer. Destroy their Shield Pylon first to make the job easier on you. Once they're all down...

Medical Station - 75 XP. Turn around to face the doorway into the cargo hangar, then check the right-hand wall. Here you'll find the Medical Station under a spotlight and yellow "Cargo Hangar 04" text.

Head up to the landing pad where the Cerberus shuttle was and head left to go down to another landing pad. Another Cerberus shuttle shows up and drops off a pair of Centurions and an Assault Trooper, but luckily there's some deployable cover to protect you. Before you move on, make sure to get these:

Med Kit - 50 XP. At the base of the rubble on the right-hand side of the landing pad.

Injured Talon - 60 XP. Hidden very well under the back of the crashed Cerberus fighter on the edge of the landing pad.

Injured Talon - 60 XP. Slumped at the nose of the crashed Cerberus fighter.

When you go through the next door, you'll enter a very cool cutscene where you reunite with Nyreen, and learn just what her role is on Omega these days. Here, you can pick up some Morality Points:

Pick "Let us help" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Not a chance" for +2 Renegade Points .

At this point, Nyreen comes back into your squad, so if you've levelled up in the time she's been away, head into the Squad menu to see if there's anything you can improve. Then, sweep this room for loot!

Medical Station - 75 XP. To the right of the door out that Shepard faces after the cutscene ends.

Phaeston - If you don't have this Turian assault rifle yet, you can find another one next to the Medical Station described above.

Shotgun High Velocity Barrel - From the Medical Station, turn around to face into the command center. On your left will be a dead Cerberus Assault Trooper at the bottom of a platform with a crate on it. This mod will be next to the Assault Trooper.

Datapad - 1,500 credits. From the Shotgun High Velocity Barrel described above, cross over to the opposite side of the room to find this behind some large crates.

Now exit the room and use the Elevator to continue along. You'll enter the very open Cargo Processing area, where some Rampart Mechs enter from the left-hand side. Destroy the nearby Shield Pylon before killing the Rampart Mechs post-haste, and eventually an Atlas mech will show up along with another wave of Rampart Mechs. Kill the latter enemies first, then locate one of the two M-560 Hydras in the middle of the room and use it to quickly destroy the Atlas mech.

Once the room is nice and quiet, check it for the following loot:

Med Kit - Return to the elevator and face into the Cargo Processing area. Walk forward, but before you go down the walkway to the central area with the burning vehicle, look left to spot this next to some crates.

Salvage - 1,500 credits. From the Med Kit described above, turn right and cross over to the other side of the area to a corner lit by a light overhead. Here among the detritus will be this Salvage.

Med Kit - 50 XP. From the Salvage described above, turn left and hop over the gap to get to a burning Alliance heavy vehicle with a Shield Pylon in front of it. Check the back of this vehicle to find this Med Kit.

Now head to the exit door and ride the elevator up, although Cerberus ensures you won't get very far. Shoot the Latch of the electricity box to the side of the entry door, then Activate the Emergency Access to drop a ladder you can use to get out of the cab.

Datapad - 1,500 credits. When you climb out of the elevator cab, vault up the yellow pipe, then go clockwise around the outside of the shaft to find this on the ground.

To progress, head counter-clockwise around the elevator shaft and slide down any ladders you come across. After the second ladder, you can find the exit on your right.

Eventually, you'll exit out onto the walkway that connects to the Talon Outpost. This is a very open catwalk area, but you may first want to quickly collect these three items:

Med Kit - 50 XP. On your right at the corner of the opening walkway when you exit the elevator shaft.

Salvage - 1,500 credits. From the Med Kit described above, turn left and go to the far end of the catwalk to find this in front of a fire.

Assault Rifle Thermal Scope - From the Salvage described above, backtrack towards the Med Kit and turn left to cross over to the opposite side of the catwalk. Turn left and head forwards to find this mod at the nose of a crashed Cerberus shuttle.

Now to do battle on the catwalk. This will be the first time you'll battle Phantoms in this DLC, who are protected by Barriers. Luckily, Aria's Reave ability can drain these defenses. Once you kill them and their compatriots, a shuttle will drop off some more enemies, including Centurions and a Nemesis sniper.

With them down, head to the door at the far end of the walkway to discover it locks up tight, thanks to being glitchy. Nyreen orders a tech to fix it, but in the meantime you'll have to hold the position while the door is bypassed. This will take 60 seconds, and its progress is indicated by the meter in the top-right corner of the screen. In the meantime, turn around and take cover: Cerberus will be attacking you from the upper walkway!

You'll be attacked by Assault Troopers, lots of Centurions, and the occasional Nemesis sniper. Fortunately you won't have to face any Phantoms or Combat Engineers.

On easier difficulties the best approach is to gun them down before they can drop down from the upper level

On harder difficulties the above may not be a viable option as you can't kill them fast enough. Instead, employ the usual strategy of firing at them while they briefly hover over the ground before landing.

When two Atlas mechs show up you may panic, but don't worry: this happens the exact moment the door is bypassed, and the roof is closed to prevent the mechs from dropping down to you.

When the roof is closed, the glitchy door will open, letting you proceed. Phew! As you proceed through the corridors, keep an eye out for a...

Med Kit - 50 XP. After you turn left, head to the very end of the corridor to find this in the back-left corner, next to an ammo box across from the exit door.

At the next door you'll now arrive at the Talon Outpost itself. Here Shepard leans about Adjutants, Reaper enemies that Aria has fought before (back in the Mass Effect: Invasion comic). You can get some Morality Points from your response here:

Pick "You overcame a lot" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Shake it off" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll now be set loose to freely explore the Talon Outpost. Be sure to grab the following loot:

Talon - Optional, but on a bed to your right will be a Turian Talon member who'll thank you for rescuing him (assuming you saved at least one Injured Talon on your way here).

Shotgun Omni-Blade - From the Talon described above, turn right to spot this on top of some ammo boxes near the wall.

Kehri Inverter - From the Shotgun Omni-Blade described above. Turn around and cross over to the other side of the room. On your left will be some crates in netting: check behind them near the floor like to find the Kehri Inverter needed for " Omega: Assist the Mechanic ".

Datapad - Find this to the left of Nyreen, on the hologram console she's observing. This gives a bit of lore regarding what Nyreen was doing right when you crashed onto Omega in the escape pod.

Talk to Nyreen, and Aria will state her intentions to take over the Talons from Nyreen, despite being told about their undying loyalty to their current leader. You can get some Morality Points here:

Pick "That's enough, Aria" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Don't be blind, Nyreen" for +2 Renegade Points .

Whichever you choose, Aria has her techs hook into the entirety of Omega so that she can make a broadcast motivating the station's populace to retake their home soon, which Nyreen of course strongly objects to. You'll then have control of Shepard returned to you: head to the pair of biotic bubble barriers and exit via the right-hand door.

Through the next door, you'll arrive at the landing pads. There will be Assault Troopers and Centurions in here, bolstered by Shield Pylons. After taking them down an orange Force Field is raised, signalling the arrival of Rampart Mechs. Try and take out the Shield Pylons if you can so that your opponents aren't harder to kill than they need to be.

Once they're down, Nyreen calls and asks for your assistance back at the outpost's main entrance. Before you run off, make sure to tend to these:

Injured Talon - 60 XP. At the back of the landing pads, turn around to face back towards the entrance. On the right-hand side will be this Turian Talon slumped on the guardrail, next to a large white, yellow and red crate.

Injured Talon - In the back-left corner of the landing pads, directly across from the entrance door.

Now backtrack to the Talon Outpost to find Cerberus firing everything they've got down the catwalks on your right. BUT BEFORE YOUR START, make sure you grab...

Med Kit x2 - 50 XP each. From the entrance of this open battlefield, turn right to spot these two Med Kits at the side wall, next to a pile of ammo boxes.

Okay, now that you've done that, start killing the Cerberus Assault Troopers and Centurions. You can do this on foot, but if you look left you'll spot a Mounted Turret on top of a truck that you can use to make literal mincemeat out of the troopers and quickly cut down the Atlas that shows up in their wake.

Once all the enemies are dead, you'll automatically move to the next cutscene (which is why we told you to get the two Med Kits before joining the fight!). Nyreen offers to join the fight, but calls out right away that she's aware of Aria playing her. Here you can say...

"[LIE] No, not at all" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll now be returned to Aria's Bunker, where Aria makes it plain that Omega's people will cause a million problems for Cerberus to sort out, spreading them thin so Aria can take out Petrovsky. To this you can reply...

"That's manipulative" for +2 Paragon Points .

"I'm impressed" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll now get to explore the bunker, although by now it's under siege and you can't access the vehicle bay anymore (not that there was anything in there to collect). Make sure to pop by these areas:

You'll be verbally flagged over by a nearby Elcor, who you may have spotted walking in during the earlier cutscene. This is Harrot, a merchant who Shepard will remember if you got a discount from his store back in Mass Effect 2 . He requests Shepard keep an eye out for Aria's couch on their travels ahead. Reply with "Why not?" to accept the " Omega: Assist Harrot " Side Mission. If you pick "No thanks", the Side Mission is PERMANENTLY declined and you'll miss out on its rewards!

If you pick "No thanks", the Side Mission is PERMANENTLY declined and you'll miss out on its rewards!

Next to Harrot you'll find the kiosk for Harrot's Emporium, which sells two upgrades of each weapon mod introduced with the Omega DLC. These will be affected by the store discounts, which is why we had you wait until after " Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastery " to start this. Don't worry if you can't buy all of these mods right now: any remainders will appear at Batarian State Arms after you finish the DLC.

Don't worry if you can't buy all of these mods right now: any remainders will appear at Batarian State Arms after you finish the DLC.

Talk to the Mechanic near Harrot to conclude " Omega: Assist the Mechanic " for 1,500 XP and +5 Reputation !

Now talk to Aria at the hologram table to progress the story and have Nyreen appear. She'll want to accompany Aria because, well, she doesn't trust her former partner. Despite the appearance of the dialogue wheel, though, there's no Morality Points to be gained here. Afterwards, you can do a few more things:

Talk to Aria and you can question her about the Force Fields and Nyreen's Commitment, and Petrovsky again.

You can talk to the Hacker if you wish, although you technically don't get any rewards for giving her access to the three Terminals in Talon Territory. Bummer.

Lastly, Nyreen will ask to speak with you in the Med Bay, which you can do if you want to learn about about her and her relationship with Aria.

Once you're done, head for the exit near Nyreen to proceed to the next level.

You'll begin in a very dark space on the way to Omega's Element Zero mines. It'll be pitch black in the original release, but if you're playing the Legendary Edition this area is lightened up a bit to ease navigation.

When you get to the end of the long catwalk littered with massacred Assault Troopers, turn left at the end and go down some steps. Here, turn right and head forward to find the huge door to the cargo lift elevator, marked with black and yellow chevrons.

As Aria says, you'll need to find a master circuit breaker somewhere in here so you can restore the power to this area. But before continuing, make sure to grab...

Credits - 2,250 credits. From the cargo lift elevator door, follow the left-hand wall leftwards, where you'll walk along an outer balcony. At the end of it, overlooking the large tankards of Eezo below, will be a crate with this on it, surrounded by round orange canisters.

To locate the master circuit breaker, return to the cargo lift elevator door, then look right to spot the Elevator Control terminal with "Warning: Low Power" written in red text, and some piping with glowing red lights on it. Follow the piping rightward until you come across a ladder: climb it!

At the top you'll need to navigate across the piping, including having to drop down and divert right over a gap to keep going. Eventually, you'll climb up onto an outer balcony. The doorway into the control room is on your right, but first...

Credits - 1,500 credits. Head past the doorway and turn right at the corner of the balcony. On the end of the balcony will be this, sitting on top of the crates.

Head through the doorway and slide down the ladder to enter the control room, then locate the Power Module on the right-hand side of the room to Reactivate the power.

After an exchange between Nyreen and Aria, an Adjutant smashes through the window and attacks. This is a unique Reaper enemy, so here's what you need to know to defeat it:

The main move used by Adjutants is their biotic arm cannon, which fires a projectile that explodes into a Singularity-like vortex that staggers Shepard out of cover. On top that that, they'll remove Shepard's shields and prevent them from recharging for as long as you're in range of the vortex.

These enemies also have a leaping attack, but fortunately it's rather predictable: they always use it when Shepard is at a set distance, and they crouch very low onto the ground before jumping. Roll out of the way!

While Adjutants have no sync kill move that instantly kills Shepard, their normal melee attack is still very powerful, so try to keep your distance.

The blue sacks on the Adjutant's back are weak points, but are protected by their tall head crest. Attacking from the side or rear removes this issue, as will any Piercing mods or weapons that naturally pierce like the Javelin or M-98 Widow .

Adjutants are completely silent as they move, so aside from their growling, there's no way to tell one may be sneaking up on you. Pay attention!

Adjutants are protected by very strong Barriers and Armor. Using Aria's Flare power is highly recommended, and in fact Adjutants are the reason why we asked you to pick "Improved Damage" when you evolved it to Level 6, as that increases its damage to Barriers by 75%!

Once you kill the Adjutants, locate the door behind the ladder you slid down here with and Bypass it to open the way back into the dark room you navigated earlier. Only now it's lit up, much better! Once you return to the main area though, a second Adjutant appears. Kill it using the tactics from the first one, then beeline it to the main elevator.

When you get there, Aria will let you know that two more Adjutants have shown up. Locate the Elevator Control terminal to the right of the elevator door and Use it to get the cargo lift elevator down here, then turn around to engage the Adjutants. With three on the prowl, you'll have to be extra-careful you don't get jumped by the ones you're not currently shooting at.

You'll know you're done when the music stops, so when this happens, return to the cargo lift elevator and use the Elevator Control terminal a second time to open the door. Step on and use the Elevator switch in the back-left corner to ascend into the mining complex itself.

Once at the top, head all the way down the long thin catwalk to enter the ore processing area. There's two items to find here:

Med Kit - 25 XP. On the platform at the end of the long walkway will be two white crates. Check behind them to find this Med Kit.

Assault Rifle High-Velocity Barrel - From the Med Kit described above, head through the gateway nearby with the glowing yellow text above it. Here on the left is a white crate against the guardrail with this mod on top.

You'll now come under attack from Cerberus, who have situated themselves in the various processing areas. While it's only Assault Troopers and Centurions, this area has plenty of cover, and there's a Shield Pylon helping them out too.

When you get to the back of this processing area, you'll want to head left across a short catwalk. When you do you'll get a View Prompt, where Aria will point out a maintenance elevator rising up in the distance that you can use to get to the next area. However as you approach the next catwalk to get to it, it blows up, courtesy of Cerberus sabotage.

To start on the alternate route, look for a ladder to the right of the destroyed catwalk and jump down it, straight into another gunfight. The troops here will mostly stick to the upper walkways, especially the Nemesis pair, forcing you to get into a sniper duel with them. If you're having trouble reaching them, use Nyreen's Lift Grenades to get a clearer shot at them.

Once they're down, locate the Door Control in the back-right that leads into a maintenance area. Through the gate will be loot:

Pistol Heavy Barrel - Through the gate, check the back corner to find this among the disheveled lockers.

Medical Station - 25 XP. On the right side of the column directly in front of you after you slide down the ladder.

From the Medical Station, turn left and sprint down the walkway to get right to the next battle. A Combat Engineer will be setting up a Turret here, so try to take him out before the Turret comes online and gives you all of the grief. This isn't as easy as it looks because of the two Shield Pylons, Rampart Mechs and even a Nemesis, but if you time it right you can shoot the Turret while the Combat Engineer is holding it so that it blows up in his face!

At the far end of the walkway, turn left and use the Door Control to exit the maintenance area, then climb up the ladder on your right. At the top, ignore the stairs on your right for now and instead head left to enter a Triage Area to find the following loot:

Tools - 1,500 credits. When you enter the Triage Area, turn right to look down the side of the main area. On your right will be a line of cabinets with three microscopes; check next to the closest microscope to find this.

Sniper Rifle Thermal Scope - From the Tools described above, continue forward to the back corner of the Triage Area. You can find this here on the cabinet.

Datapad - From the mod described above, turn right and cross over to the other side of the Triage Area. You can find this amusing Datapad here, to the left of the middle microscope.

Ignore the ladder in the Triage Area and instead return to the staircase from earlier and head up it. There's a battle in the upper area, and you have much better cover protection at the top of the stairs than the top of the ladder. Here you'll fight some Assault Troopers, a Nemesis and some Rampart Mechs, so be on your toes.

When they're dead, head to the far end of the area to find that you're now on the other side of the catwalk that Cerberus blew up earlier. So from here, make a U-turn to your right to find the maintenance elevator: hit the button to ride it up!

At the top of the maintenance elevator, turn right to head through the door and spot a lone Combat Trooper on your right. Gun him down, then check this area for loot:

Shotgun Omni-Blade - Inside a locker on the opposite wall from the Combat Engineer.

Chakram Launcher - Facing the locker with the mod described above, follow the wall left to find this at the base of a wall riddled with bullets, next to a human corpse and under a red light. In the original release of Mass Effect 3, this weapon does not appear if you already acquired it via the Kingdoms of Amalur Crossover .

In the original release of Mass Effect 3, this weapon does not appear if you already acquired it via the Kingdoms of Amalur Crossover .

Medical Station - 25 XP. From the Chakram Launcher described above, turn around and locate the open doorway with "Pedway Access" above it in yellow text. Stand in this doorway, then look right to spot this Medical Station on the wall, with a dead soldier underneath who tragically couldn't use it before he died.

Dead Trooper - 1,500 credits. Standing in the open "Pedway Access" doorway, turn right to spot a dead Assault Trooper jammed in the doorway. Take his wallet!

Tools - 3,750 credits. Head through the open doorway across from the "Pedway Access" doorway to get onto the outer balcony with no guardrails. On your left will be a tool cabinet next to a spotlight, with these Tools on top.

From the Tools listed above, head right and slide down the ladder, with the exit elevator visible across the way. Follow the catwalk (even as it partially buckles from under you) to the end. Climb up the next ladder, then locate a...

Dead Trooper - 2,250 credits. After climbing up the ladder, turn left to spot this guy slumped against the guardrail.

Head onto the elevator and hit the Elevator button to progress up to the main reactor for Omega.

At the top, don't head for the back of the reactor just yet. Instead, get this loot item while you can:

Equipment - 2,250 credits. Head clockwise around the outer walkway that goes around the reactor. At approximately the "11:00" position, you can find this on top of a crate with some Thermal Clips.

When you get to the back of the reactor walkway (at the "12:00" position), some orange Force Fields show up. Yeah... it was a trap. You'll get into a one-on-one conversation with General Petrovsky, who reveals he gave you no choice but this route. Here you can say...

"You're a smart man" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Stop stroking your ego" for +2 Renegade Points .

Aria will then attempt to rip an escape through the Force Field, so while she gets to work, you'll have to defend her from oncoming Rampart Mechs. Thus for the only time in this DLC, you'll have just Nyreen to help you out as a squad mate.

This area doesn't provide a lot of cover, and the Rampart Mechs will approach you from both sides, so watch your six. Remember that you can bring up the minimap to get a glimpse of where the surrounding enemies are!

Once all the Rampart Mechs are down, you'll get a cutscene where Aria successfully opens up a hole big enough for Shepard to pass through. You'll now have to make it to the control room to save Aria and Nyreen. But first!

Med Kit - 25 XP. As you go down the catwalk, take the first left up the steps to find this Med Kit at the top.

Okay, important stuff done, continue down the curved walkway and locate the zig-zagging stairs up into the control room. There's actually no time pressure here, so feel free to take your time to down the Assault Trooper and his Rampart Mech buddies.

Once they're down, head up the stairs into the control room and head right to find the Reactor Controls , which initiates a cutscene. Here Petrovsky appears again to inform Shepard that the reactor is powering life support to thousands across Omega, but Aria doesn't care and urges Shepard to shut it down. Nyreen instead asks Shepard to try re-routing the power, which they'll start attempting.

You'll now have an important Interrupt situation on your hands:

If you take any of the three Renegade Interrupts, you'll hit the Overload button to save Aria and Nyreen, killing thousands on life support for +15 Renegade Points .

If you ignore all three Renegade Interrupts, Shepard successfully re-routes the power to save Aria and Nyreen, avoiding the deaths of thousands on life support for +15 Paragon Points . If your Shepard is an Engineer class, you have a special situation! If you ignore the first Renegade Interrupt, Shepard activates their Omni-tool and a Paragon Interrupt will appear: pull it to have Shepard instantly re-route the power for +15 Paragon Points !

If your Shepard is an Engineer class, you have a special situation! If you ignore the first Renegade Interrupt, Shepard activates their Omni-tool and a Paragon Interrupt will appear: pull it to have Shepard instantly re-route the power for +15 Paragon Points !

With the reactor rebooted, all the orange Force Fields across Omega go down, and all hell officially breaks loose. You'll then reconvene with Aria and Nyreen in the control room, and Aria will soon berate Nyreen for being scared of the Adjutants.

Pull the Paragon Interrupt that appears here to tell Aria to lay off Nyreen for +5 Paragon Points .

Regardless, you'll follow Aria into the elevator to begin the final section of the DLC.

In the elevator, Nyreen gets news that all the Force Fields are down, and once again she and Aria butt heads over the inevitable civilian casualties as a result. You can pick up some Morality Points here:

Pick "Keep civilians safe" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Focus on the enemy" for +2 Renegade Points .

Bray then radios Aria to let her know that he's spotted engineers moving explosives to Omega's central columns. If they go off then nobody will be able to reach Afterlife where Petrovsky is headquartered, so Shepard and Aria break off to deal with them while Nyreen leads the Talon offensive itself.

Straight out of the gate, you can get some items when you exit out the elevator into the next room:

Sniper Rifle Thermal Scope - On top of some box objects next to the steps, directly across from the Weapon Bench.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On some crates on the other side of the steps where the mod listed above was.

Head up the steps and take cover in the doorway so that you can down the Rampart Mechs attacking Aria's men. Once they're down, head through the doorway and to the back wall, then turn left. As you go you'll be attacked by more Rampart Mechs, backed up by two Centurions and a pair of Shield Pylons.

As you get to the far end of the water treatment area, the bridge across will explode to hamper your progress. To un-hamper it, enter the control room on your right and locate the Dam Control panel, extending a new bridge across in the form of a dam.

After crossing over the dam, grab the following items:

Datapad - 1,500 credits. After crossing the dam, head left to the pile of crates to find this Datapad sitting on top of them.

Couch - 1,800 credits. To the right of the dam, slide down the ladder, then look left to spot a pile of couches. If you talked to Harrot earlier, you can Examine them to complete " Omega: Assist Harrot " and get +5 Reputation (although Aria rather spoils the task by noticing them!).

Medical Station - 75 XP. Climb out of the waterway and head through the doorway on your right labeled "Central Support". Up ahead is a locked door labeled "Doru District": check to the right of it to find this Medical Station.

Head left from the Medical Station described above to find a door to Bypass, which takes you into a cramped corridor filled with Guardians. If you have Piercing mods / weapons, they won't be too much of an issue, but if you don't you'll have to use alternatives like Aria's Lash ability (assuming you upgraded it to Level 6 and chose "Shield Penetration".

When you see the next door to Bypass, STOP! There's an item nearby:

Equipment - 1,500 credits. At the final corner of the cramped Guardian corridor is a door you can open. In this side-room you can find some Equipment on one of the tool shelves on the right-hand side.

Bypass the next door, then look to the left of the "Primary Ventilation Systems" door to go down a one-way slope. Deactivate the Fan Control on your left to open the way to the Support Column room.

Ignore any goodies for now and head for the middle of the room where the Cerberus soldiers are. There'll be Assault Troopers and a Combat Engineer: kill the latter first so you don't have any Turrets ruining your day.

Once you're done, head to the middle of the room and Activate the Access Panel Controls . This exposes the bombs... but also arms them, and of course more Cerberus appears to make this task difficult. Here's how this works:

You have five minutes to defuse all four bombs.

Cerberus enemies will continuously spawn into this area, so don't bother trying to clear them all out first.

It takes Shepard four seconds to defuse a bomb, during which they'll be unable to defend themselves. Luckily, Shepard getting hit does not cancel them out of defusing a bomb.

Get as close as you can to a bomb before trying to defuse one: Shepard crouches down as they do this, and the terminals flanking the bomb do provide a little bit of protection.

If you see a Combat Engineer, KILL HIM FIRST!

While Aria says she'll handle the enemies for you, in actuality she behaves as normal and doesn't explicitly try to cover you while you make a run for a bomb.

Once all the enemies are clear, reconvene with Aria to get an update from Nyreen, before Aria opens the way forward to the next objective. Before you leave, however, make sure to sweep the area for four Med Kits, located at each side of the room. For navigation, the the giant spinning fan Aria just took out is "North".

Med Kit - 50 XP. At the "North" side of the room, on top of a black tool shelf on the right side of the giant fan.

Med Kit - 50 XP. On the "East" side of the room, on top of a crate to the left of a locked door.

Med Kit - 50 XP. At the "South" vent you arrived here in, on top of a black tool shelf.

Med Kit - 50 XP. At the "West" side of the room, on top of a crate lit by a spotlight.

Jump over the gap to get under the giant fan, then Bypass the door to open continue forwards. Climb up the first ladder it in red, then scout around for loot:

Shotgun High-Velocity Barrel - To the left of the second ladder, at the foot of a yellow crate.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Climb up the second ladder, then turn left to head towards a second, broken ladder in the corner. Before you get there, keep an eye on your right for this Med Kit.

Equipment - 1,500 credits. From the Med Kit described above, turn left and head to the far end to find this Equipment on top of the black tool shelf in the corner.

Return to the top of the second ladder and now head right and climb up the ladder ahead. Through the next door, you'll spot an Adjutant massacring two Cerberus Assault Troopers, prompting Aria to ask Azz to lock the doors behind you as you go. You'll then arrive in a room littered with dead Cerberus, and a looping radio log. Ignore it for now and go for goodies:

Locker - 1,500 credits. From the entry point, look to the back-left corner for a door labeled "Doru District". Head through and check the back-left corner of this room to find this Locker.

Video Log - Continue down the walkway to get to the ground floor. Here, look left to spot a glitchy video log terminal for some lore. The log you listen to when you arrive is actually the third entry!

Datapad - 1,500 credits. From the Video Log described above, head down the right-hand path to find this Datapad on top of some crates.

Datapad - 1,500 credits. Return to the Video Log and this time head down the left-hand path and through the door into the airlock room. On the long back wall will be a dead Assault Trooper with this Datapad next to him.

In the next big room up head you'll fight yet more Cerberus troops, including an Atlas mech and two Nemesis snipers. Take Aria's advice and focus on the Atlas first, then mop up any remaining soldiers. That clears the room nice and quiet so you can get more collectibles:

Med Kit - 50 XP. Return to the entry point and head rightward along the walkway. Keep an eye out for this Med Kit in the first alcove on your right.

Med Kit - 50 XP. From the Med Kit described above, cross over to the opposite side of the room (going down and then up some steps in the process). At the opposite wall, turn right and start heading towards a ladder lit in white: this Med Kit will be near the bottom of it.

Equipment - 1,500 credits. From the Med Kit described above, climb up the nearby ladder and head through the door on your right. This will be at the back of the room, at the foot of an unlit spotlight.

Once you've grabbed the above, return to the ground floor and exit the room via the door labeled "Gozu District" that you have to Bypass, then climb up the ladder. Here Shepard will note that this area looks familiar, and Aria will make a comment regarding Mordin Solus.

Datapad - 1,500 credits. When you get to the top of the ladder, turn left to spot this on top of a crate in the corner.

Pistol Heavy Barrel - Through the next doorway, drop down to the lower area to find this mod at the bottom.

Cerberus Trooper - 1,500 credits. Head through the next doorway to enter a room with a crashed Cerberus shuttle. Check the back side of the shuttle, past a fire, to find this poor soldier. Take his money!

Through the next doorway, you'll arrive at the start of the main Gozu District route from " Dossier: The Professor " in Mass Effect 2, only you'll be going backwards. A Combat Engineer has already set up a Turret, so take cover and destroy it, then focus on the Engineer himself and his Cerberus buddies that drop in. They'll be backed up by a Shield Pylon that may be just out of view for you.

Med Kit - 50 XP. Sitting on a countertop on the right-hand side of the room, right next to the Shield Pylon.

Junk - 1,200 credits. From the Med Kit described above, continue up the stairs and Bypass the door at the top to return to the old quarantine checkpoint area. Ahead on your right will be the checkpoint wall: check behind the stack on PC towers on its right-hand side to find this.

Lab Equipment - 1 credit. From the junk described above, locate the door you can open to get into a side corridor. Talk to the Civilian if you wish, but check the left-hand side of this corridor to find this, between a bench and a trash fire.

Shotgun Omni-Blade - From the Lab Equipment, exit out the door next to the Weapon Bench and continue past the Batarian Preacher down the hallway with the Civilian in it. At the end of this corridor you have to turn left, but you should first get this mod from the stack of crates being used by the Talons as a barricade.

With your loot in hand, head into next Elevator to proceed to the final area. Nyreen will call over the radio that she's going to "check something out", and is going radio silent. After talking with some Talons, Aria realizes the inevitable: Nyreen is heading for Afterlife!

After a cutscene involving Cerberus, civilians and Adjutants, Aria is now more motivated than ever and charges into her old nightclub. Before you go after her though...

Datapad - 1 credit. Wait, loot? Really? NOW?!? Yes indeed! Turn around to face away from Afterlife and towards the door the Adjutants came in from. To the right of that door will be a pile of crates next to a skycar: this Datapad will be on them. Worth it!

Head into the entry hall of Afterlife where Aria quite literally clears the room, then Bypass the door at the end to enter the nightclub itself. Unfortunately, Aria falls right into Petrovsky's trap, and you'll be tasked with freeing Aria whilst fighting a horde of angry and obedient Adjutants and Cerberus soldiers. Here's how this final battle works:

Your task is to find the four Stasis Generator Controls in the upper corners of Afterlife to release Aria.

Aria's health will gradually deplete over time: you have roughly five minutes before she dies and you get a Critical Mission Failure.

Like with the Support Column bombs, the Adjutants will spawn indefinitely, so don't try clearing them all out first. Instead you should concentrate only on those who are an immediate threat to you.

Each Override console will have a Shield Pylon nearby. You should actually leave these alone: having your Shields topped up is very handy, and Adjutants can't have Shields and Barriers at the same time!

Once you Override one of the consoles, it'll open up a Shield Generator near Aria: shooting it will allow Aria to unleash a massive Flare that kills nearly everyone in the room.

Because of the glass walls, you can't just shoot the Shield Generators from the Override console: you'll have to return to one of the stairs up here in order to get a clear shot. The exception is if a gun can pierce through the glass!

Once Aria has cleared the room with a Flare, beeline it to the next Override console before too many new enemies show up.

When you've destroyed all three Shield Generators, Aria will be freed and officially rejoin your squad. You'll now have to secure the area, which will be whatever enemies you haven't killed yet and extra waves of Cerberus soldiers dropping in. Stay on your toes and don't get complacent: you don't want to die now!

Once they're all dead, don't head up to the balcony just yet! The last few items are in the nightclub:

Med Kit x2 - 50 XP each. At the highest areas on each side of the Afterlife nightclub. They'll be at the rough middle point between where each Override console is. Both are on coffee tables, one against the outer wall, and the other against the railing.

When all forces are dead, you'll get your rewards and Petrovsky will order all of his forces to surrender. Meet him at Aria's old balcony, and Aria will very quickly start to strangle Cerberus' top General. There's actually a number of permutations to this scene, based on your choices regarding Aria throughout the DLC.

If you've been either Renegade or mixed during the Omega DLC, Aria will strangle Petrovsky with the intent to kill. Here you can do the following:

If you take the first Paragon Interrupt, you'll get +2 Paragon Points . If you ignore the second interrupt, Aria will kill Petrovsky for +15 Reputation . If you take the second Paragon Interrupt, you'll stop Aria from killing Petrovsky for +15 Paragon Points .

If you ignore the second interrupt, Aria will kill Petrovsky for +15 Reputation .

If you take the second Paragon Interrupt, you'll stop Aria from killing Petrovsky for +15 Paragon Points .

If you ignore the first Paragon Interrupt, Aria will kill Petrovsky for +15 Renegade Points .

If you've been primarily Paragon during the Omega DLC, Aria will strangle but spare Petrovsky, after which you can do the following:

Take the first Renegade Interrupt to strike Petrovsky for +2 Renegade Points . If you ignore the second Renegade Interrupt, Shepard will spare Petrovsky for +15 Reputation . If you pull the second Renegade Interrupt, Shepard will kill Petrovsky for +15 Renegade Points . After this, you can then say "You need to reform" for +5 Paragon Points .

If you ignore the second Renegade Interrupt, Shepard will spare Petrovsky for +15 Reputation .

If you pull the second Renegade Interrupt, Shepard will kill Petrovsky for +15 Renegade Points . After this, you can then say "You need to reform" for +5 Paragon Points .

After this, you can then say "You need to reform" for +5 Paragon Points .

Unless you were Paragon and only took the first of the two Renegade Interrupts, you'll then be able to end the scene with the following two opportunities for Morality Points:

Pick "Take care of the people" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Time to pay up" / "I'll leave you to guess" for +2 Renegade Points .

Aria will then address the people of Omega, and the nature of her speech will depend on your Morality throughout the DLC.

If you were Renegade / mixed, Aria will order her people to kill all Cerberus invaders and end with "Don't fuck with Aria".

If you were Paragon, Aria will ask her people to cast out Cerberus so they can mourn their dead, for "We are Omega".

You'll then be returned to the Normandy, you'll have your War Assets updated. In addition to Aria's contributions, you'll have an additional contribution based on the fate of General Oleg Petrovsky:

If you spared Petrovky, he'll be his own War Asset worth 30 TMS.

If you killed Petrovsky, then his intelligence will bolster the Alliance First Fleet by +30 TMS.

Now you should do a sweep of the Normandy:

CIC - Talk to EDI. Also check your Private Terminal for a message from Aria regarding Petrovsky's chessboard. If you're playing the Legendary Edition, this is when you'll get the Reckoner-Knight Armor and the N7 Defender Armor added!

If you're playing the Legendary Edition, this is when you'll get the Reckoner-Knight Armor and the N7 Defender Armor added!

Crew Deck - If you've been following our guide in order and completed both " Citadel: Medical Supplies " in Mass Effect 3 had a drink with Chakwas after " Normandy: Serrice Ice Brandy " in Mass Effect 2, you can talk to her now for +5 Reputation , and optionally have another drink with her.

Engineering - Javik has a small comment to make.

Shuttle Bay - Cortez and James have a conversation to overhear when you walk in.

Lastly, if you check your Private Terminal you'll have a message from Aria saying she had Petrovsky's chessboard sent to the Normandy. You can find it in the Captain's Cabin at the desk near Shepard's bed.

articles.title: Desponia: Leviathan - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Desponia: Leviathan DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Desponia: Leviathan DLC Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Mods: Assault Rifle Omni-Blade Pistol Cranial Trauma System Pistol Ultralight Materials

War Assets: Tap to Reveal (400 TMS) Ann Bryson (20 TMS, only if you didn't use the second Renegade Interrupt in " Citadel: Leviathan 3 ")

Ann Bryson (20 TMS, only if you didn't use the second Renegade Interrupt in " Citadel: Leviathan 3 ")

Prerequisite: Complete " Citadel: Leviathan 3 "

Location: Sigurd's Cradle - Tap to Reveal - Tap to Reveal

Similar to the search for Dr. Garneau and Ann Bryson, your first order of business is to find the exact location of Leviathan, with how wide your search area being determined by how many Renegade Interrupts you took back in " Citadel: Leviathan 3 ".

Unlike the hunt for Dr. Garneau, your search area will be only in Sigurd's Cradle even in the broadest circumstance. Unlike the search for Garneau and Ann, however, you CANNOT return to Dr. Bryson's Lab to narrow things down, as Ann is currently out of action. So if you just want to get to Ann Bryson now, however, reveal the spoiler text below:

Even if you've got Leviathan's exact location, you'll want to explore the other systems in Sigurd's Cradle, as they all contain their own discoveries to be made via the Search and Rescue mechanic. Use the chart below to help find them all!

Squad Tactics: James is a very good pick thanks to his high health shotgun, and armor-stripping powers with splash zones. Garrus is another fine choice for similar reasons, and can help with enemies at long distances with his sniper rifle. Ashley is also to be considered if Garrus isn't available and she is, since she's a mix of both of them.

James is a very good pick thanks to his high health shotgun, and armor-stripping powers with splash zones.

Garrus is another fine choice for similar reasons, and can help with enemies at long distances with his sniper rifle.

Ashley is also to be considered if Garrus isn't available and she is, since she's a mix of both of them.

Unique Dialogue: If you have a locked-in Romance with Garrus, Kaidan, Tali, Liara, James or Ashley, you'll get unique dialogue if you bring them along on this Mission. Pick them first in the squad menu for the scenes to make the most sense. While it's very minor, Tali has the most interesting comments for this Mission.

If you have a locked-in Romance with Garrus, Kaidan, Tali, Liara, James or Ashley, you'll get unique dialogue if you bring them along on this Mission. Pick them first in the squad menu for the scenes to make the most sense.

While it's very minor, Tali has the most interesting comments for this Mission.

Shepard's Loadout: All combat will take place on terrain that rocks back and forth, making it a huge pain to aim with sniper rifles. A viable alternative is to use Garrus and / or Ashley as Squad Mates and let them handle that instead. If you're lucky enough to have the Adas Anti-Synthetic Rifle , its semi-homing shots will help mitigate the need for precision aim on the rocking terrain, as will its staggering splash damage. Despite the name, it works as good on organics as it does on synthetics. The downside is its extreme weight. Soldier-class Shepards should make liberal use of the Concussive Shot power, as it has a very useful homing trait that also mitigates the rocking terrain that throws off aim. Other classes may instead want to use James' Carnage Bonus Power, which is slower in both speed and recharge time, but deals high splash damage and also homes in on targets.

All combat will take place on terrain that rocks back and forth, making it a huge pain to aim with sniper rifles. A viable alternative is to use Garrus and / or Ashley as Squad Mates and let them handle that instead.

If you're lucky enough to have the Adas Anti-Synthetic Rifle , its semi-homing shots will help mitigate the need for precision aim on the rocking terrain, as will its staggering splash damage. Despite the name, it works as good on organics as it does on synthetics. The downside is its extreme weight.

Soldier-class Shepards should make liberal use of the Concussive Shot power, as it has a very useful homing trait that also mitigates the rocking terrain that throws off aim.

Other classes may instead want to use James' Carnage Bonus Power, which is slower in both speed and recharge time, but deals high splash damage and also homes in on targets.

Spoiler alert: the landing doesn't go as planned! A pulse hits the Kodiak shuttle and sends it crashing onto one of the ships floating in Desponia's ocean. Shepard and squad exit the ship while Cortez starts repairs.

So... here's the thing about this area. There are a TON of items to find, but enemy forces will eventually show up and draw you into an area further down the ship, after which things quieten down again. So what we're going to do is list all the items you can find in both this area (going clockwise around it), as well as the second area that opens up during the fight, with the understanding that you'll be interrupted by said fight and have to come back later. Okay?

For clarity, we'll refer to the shuttle as being at the "6:00" position, with the sun in roughly the "12:00" position.

Datapad - 150 XP. On a crate next to a black tarp, close to where you drop down from the crashed shuttle.

M-55 Argus - On a crate to the left of the Datapad described above.

Assault Rifle Omni-Blade - On the same crate as the M-55 Argus.

Skeletal Remains - Inside the small ammo box room with a black tarp roof next to the M-55 Argus.

Datapad - 150 XP. Inside the small ammo box room next to the M-55 Argus.

Star Charts - 2,250 credits. On a blue crate outside the ammo box room.

Pure Eezo Samples - 2,250 credits. From the Star Charts described above, head left towards the ocean to find this on top of a blue crate on your left.

Pistol Cranial Trauma System - From the Pure Eezo Samples described above, look towards the ocean, then look right to spot this on a metal structure that slopes into the sea. You'll get a View Prompt about the surrounding ships as you approach it.

Pure Eezo Samples - 2,250 credits. Return to the first Pure Eezo Samples, then look for a blue crate in the middle of this area with this item on it.

Med Kit - 50 XP. From the Pure Eezo Samples described above, face "12:00", then look left to spot a lower area covered by a blue tarp roof. It'll have this Med Kit inside, and a Leviathan Artifact.

Datapad - 150 XP. In the lower area with the Med Kit described above.

Damaged "Triton" ADS - 150 XP. A red mech at the "12:00" position of this area, partially covered by a red burgundy-coloured tarp.

Datapad - 150 XP. From the Damaged "Triton" ADS, look for the lower area covered by red burgundy tarps. You can find this Datapad here, along with an ammo box and another Leviathan Artifact.

Survey Data - 2,250 credits. From the Datapad described above, back out of the lower area and continue clockwise: you'll slot this on your left, on top of a metal block object next to some cables.

Datapad - 150 XP. From the Survey Data described above, continue anti-clockwise to find another lower area with an ammo box and a Leviathan Artifact. This will be sitting atop a crate in the middle.

Survey Data - 2,250 credits. From the Datapad described above, check to the right of it to spot this on top of a yellow crate, to the left of the Med Kit at the very top of this list.

Med Kit - 50 XP. In a lower area to the left of the Datapad at the very top of the list.

After around a minute and a half, one of your Squad Mates will spot a Reaper appearing in the area, which you can look at yourself with a View Prompt. Cannibals and Husks will appear at the "10:00" and "12:00" parts of the area, eventually followed up with two Brutes, and Marauders. Not helping matters is the swaying of the ship that throws off your aim: if possible use your squad mates to try and engage enemies at long range.

Around about when the Brutes are nearly down, Cortez will have repaired the shuttle and begins to assist you with some cover fire, one-shotting most enemies. But when another group of Marauders show up, he's hit with another pulse and crashes further down the ship, knocking down a structure in the process. Fight your way through the Marauders and Cannibals to get to him!

Before you talk to Cortez though... loot! In addition to the remaining items in the starting area, you can now get a few items in this second area. Start by returning to the gap you leapt over to get here and face the shuttle

Mining Equipment - 1,500 credits. From the gap facing the shuttle, look right to spot some blue crates: this will be on top of them.

Pistol Ultralight Materials - Continue towards the shuttle and get over the big metal block that crosses laterally over this area (there's a set of ramps that let you do this without vaulting). On the other side, immediately turn left towards the sea and head towards it: you'll find this mod on your left just before the ground slopes down into the sea.

Med Kit - 50 XP. At the base of the ledge in front of where the Kodiak shuttle landed, behind where Cortez is standing.

Talk to Cortez to learn the rather unique task before you: you'll need to carry some power cells from the shuttle on your back and take them to one of two ports on the deck of this ship and charge them up to power a nearby Triton mech, going through enemy forces all the while.

Here's how this part of the level works:

There are two charging ports on the deck: one on the left near the very wide window, and another on the right near the sea. We recommend the first one because it's much safer and faster to get to!

We recommend the first one because it's much safer and faster to get to!

Each power cell will contribute around 40% of the total power needed, taking four seconds for each charge. This means you'll have to make at least three runs to get enough juice for the Triton mech.

You'll slowly lose your power cell charge, so don't take too long fighting the enemies!

The enemies aren't infinite, but they will take up a lot of your time, especially the Brute. We recommend using the Hydra next to the ammo box where the shuttle is to quickly take them out, greatly easing your travels.

Once you're done, the cargo bay window at the highest point of the deck will open!

Before you hop into the mech, make sure to grab one last loot item!

Salvaged Xenotechnology - 2,250 credits. On some white crates to the left of the red Triton ADS you get into.

Once you're in the Triton ADS, a LOT of Brutes show up, letting you flex a little bit. Since this Triton wasn't shot to near-death like the ones you hijack, you'll have a lot more health to play with. The standard cannon will one-shot most enemies, but Brutes will still take a couple of shots to take down with it, so use the rockets instead if you're able.

Once all enemies are dead, Cortez will ask you to walk to Triton over to him to check it over. Doing so ends this section, so MAKE SURE you've collected everything before you do that!

After a systems check, and some words from your love interest if present, Shepard will dive into Desponia's depths. This unique underwater section is nonetheless linear: follow the trail marked by the underwater flares Shepard shoots out to make it the last 200 meters.

After you make an incredibly long drop down, head forward to have a very lengthy meeting with Leviathan, who turns out to be far more important than they first seemed!

Once the discussion is over, Shepard will return to the surface, with Leviathan helping out against the Reaper forces in an impressive show of strength. If Ann wasn't briefly knocked out during "Citadel: Leviathan 3", she'll commune with Shepard over the video display, confirming that she's been added as a War Asset!

After Shepard has a chat with Admiral Hackett over their discoveries, you'll now be able to do one last sweep of the Normandy for this DLC's comments:

Crew Deck - Talk to your Virmire Survivor, Liara and Garrus.
